Then: 1) propose 3 to 4 NSM candidates derived from {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, each expressing customer value and not vanity activity; 2) score each candidate on a matrix of five criteria (reflects real value, is leading relative to revenue, is measurable today, is influenceable by the team, resists gaming), recommend one, and justify the discards; 3) decompose the chosen NSM into 2 to 4 first-level inputs with an explicit mathematical relationship (sum, product, or weighted average) and break each input down into 1 or 2 operable sub-inputs; 4) for each leaf define a metric, formula, current baseline (or [SUPUESTO] if {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} does not cover it), team lever, measurement frequency, and suggested owner; 5) identify the 2 highest-leverage inputs and formulate for each one a falsifiable experiment hypothesis with a success metric, threshold, and time horizon; 6) define 2 to 3 guardrail metrics and one anti-pattern for gaming per input with the signal that would reveal it. Tag [SUPUESTO] on any data not provided. Deliverable: NSM in one sentence + selection matrix + indented tree + leaf table + the two quarterly priorities + guardrails. Neutral, professional English, no prices and without the word free.
pr-producto_arbol_metricas_aarrr:
Act as a Head of Product Analytics with experience designing lifecycle metrics frameworks for digital products (growth and retention), fluent in operational event definition and instrumentation. Build me a complete AARRR metrics tree (Dave McClure's pirate model: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) for {{PRODUCTO}}, model {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, usage frequency {{FRECUENCIA_USO}}, value event {{EVENTO_VALOR}}, focused on moving {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}. I want a north-star metric at the top, five stages with their primary metric, actionable drivers below, and dashboard-ready instrumentation, to move from a dashboard of scattered, causally unrelated metrics to a tree with traceable levers that reveal where the real lifecycle bottleneck lies.

If any of those five data points is missing or arrives ambiguous, ask me before building anything and do not assume it is a B2B SaaS.

Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: validate product, model, frequency, value event, and target metric. (2) North star and skeleton: derive the north-star metric aligned with {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} and the skeleton — north star plus five stages — and justify why the north star predicts delivered and retained value. (3) Metric per stage: for each stage define name, exact operational definition (numerator and denominator or counted event), time window, segment, two or three actionable drivers, and instrumentation (events plus properties). In Acquisition consider qualified new users, cost of acquisition by channel, and visit-to-registration rate. In Activation anchor the aha moment to {{EVENTO_VALOR}} and define the activation event, activation rate (activated over registered), time-to-value, and onboarding drivers. In Retention set the window according to {{FRECUENCIA_USO}} (D, W, or M), build a cohort retention curve, N-day or N-week retention, and the retention plateau. In Referral define the K-factor, invitation rate, acceptance rate, and NPS as a proxy for willingness to recommend. In Revenue, consistent with {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, define conversion-to-paid rate, NRR, LTV, and the LTV-to-cost-of-acquisition ratio. (4) Close: two or three most likely bottlenecks, each with its research question. Deliver the hierarchical tree (north star, stage, primary metric, drivers, instrumentation), an operational definitions table, and a final diagnostics block.

Constraints: do not invent monetary amounts or figures; if a data point is not provided, leave the formula and mark the missing item as [REQUIRED]. Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Do not use prices or the word free.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and brief description (what it does and for whom)
- {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}: how it monetizes (subscription, transactional, freemium, marketplace, advertising, etc.)
- {{FRECUENCIA_USO}}: natural expected usage frequency (daily, weekly, or monthly)
- {{EVENTO_VALOR}}: specific action that represents the aha moment / first value experience
- {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}: outcome the team wants to move (e.g., grow weekly actives, raise NRR, improve activation)
pr-producto_heart_framework:
Act as a senior Product Analyst specializing in experience metrics, trained in Google's HEART framework (Rodden, Hutchinson, Fu) and the Goals-Signals-Metrics method. Operationalize HEART for {{FEATURE}} and deliver a matrix ready to instrument that moves the team from "we think this works" to defensible metrics that inform {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}}.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and restate your plan in one line, then Execute. If {{FEATURE}}, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, or {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent the feature.

Five phases. Phase 1 (Framing): problem {{FEATURE}} solves, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, and the {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}} to inform. Phase 2 (Selection): from the five HEART dimensions mark which apply and which you discard, one line of justification for each; do not force all five. Phase 3 (Goals-Signals-Metrics matrix): one table per applicable dimension, Goal in user language, observable Signals of success and failure, Metrics with formula (numerator, denominator, window, unit). Phase 4 (Instrumentation): per metric, event or survey with {{STACK_ANALITICA}}, baseline or how to obtain it, and direction of improvement within {{HORIZONTE}}. Phase 5 (Close): one primary metric, 2–3 guardrails, and concrete measurement risks (gaming, survivorship bias, unstable denominator, novelty effect).

Rules: no metric without a Goal; each metric with numerator, denominator, window, and unit; zero vanity metrics; instrumentation and direction of improvement per metric; a single primary metric; mark missing items as [SUPUESTO]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver tables per dimension plus block with primary metric, guardrails, and risks. Neutral and professional English.

Variables: {{FEATURE}}, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}}, {{STACK_ANALITICA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-producto_metricas_contrapeso:
You are a senior Head of Product Analytics who designs gaming-resistant metric dashboards, fluent in target/counter-metric frameworks (counter-metrics, guardrail metrics, HEART, North Star + inputs). Your mission: build an actionable counter-metric system for {{PRODUCTO}} so that each lever in {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} is paired with a guardrail that detects harm before it erodes {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}. The guiding principle is Goodhart's Law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; teams and automated systems find shortcuts that raise the number without creating real value. Factor in {{ETAPA}} of the product when calibrating optimization aggressiveness and threshold severity.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate {{PRODUCTO}}, the metrics in {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}}, and {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}; declare explicit assumptions and flag ambiguities as to_confirm. Present your pairing plan before executing it.

Produce, in order: (1) Inventory of target metrics from {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} with their stated intent. (2) Gaming model per metric: the shortcut that would raise the number without real value, who benefits (team, adversarial user, automated system), and its probability and impact. (3) Target-vs-counter-metric pair table: the counter-metric that monitors harm to {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}, the expected relationship, and why it is orthogonal to the shortcut. (4) Operational definitions: numerator, denominator, window, segment, and source for each target and counter-metric. (5) Guardrail thresholds: normal, alert, and blocking levels, with the action per level. (6) Instrumentation plan: events or fields to capture (flag inferred instrumentation as ASSUMPTION). (7) Conflict-resolution rule for target vs. counter-metric, with the responsible role. (8) Review protocol for {{CADENCIA_REVISION}}: what is reviewed, in what order, and the escalation criterion. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence when available.

Quality rules: each metric in {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} has exactly one paired and justified counter-metric; each pair explicitly states the concrete shortcut and why the counter-metric detects it; genuine orthogonality (not inflatable by the same move); include a universal health counter-metric (retention or satisfaction) and a margin or cost guardrail if applicable; no vanity metrics without a guardrail; no invented numbers; inferred instrumentation flagged as ASSUMPTION; ambiguities as to_confirm. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}}, or {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}} are missing, ask before executing. Deliver a document ready for the product committee.
pr-producto_quick_ratio_growth:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specializing in growth accounting and digital product retention, with mastery of the Quick Ratio framework popularized by Social Capital. For {{PRODUCTO_Y_ETAPA}} I need to know whether user growth is sustainable or whether a rising active-user count is masking churn growing in parallel. Before calculating anything, confirm the period {{PERIODO}} and the operational definitions based on {{DEFINICION_USUARIO_ACTIVO}}; if any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it instead of assuming it, and warn that the ratio is distorted when the four components are not measured with the same activity window or the same key event.

Then deliver the following. First, the Quick Ratio = ({{USUARIOS_NUEVOS}} + {{USUARIOS_RESUCITADOS}}) / {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}}, with a complete numerical breakdown: numerator, denominator, and result to two decimal places; if {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}} is zero, do not divide — report the ratio as undefined and explain that the period only shows gains. Second, the decomposition of net growth = {{USUARIOS_NUEVOS}} + {{USUARIOS_RESUCITADOS}} − {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}}, with the percentage weight of new and resurrected users within the numerator. Third, interpretation against thresholds (≥1 gains more than it loses; >1.5 healthy at an early stage; <1 net contraction) and an explicit verdict of sustainable, fragile, or negative with justification. Fourth, diagnosis of the dominant lever (acquisition, reactivation, or retention) and the primary risk, distinguishing a healthy high ratio from one inflated by acquisition while churn rises. Fifth, 3 to 5 actionable recommendations prioritized by impact and effort for the next period, each linked to the component it addresses and with the expected effect on the ratio. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if available.

Flag every inference as an assumption, flag the risk of reading a single period as a trend, and suggest comparing two or three consecutive periods before deciding on spend. Write in neutral, professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_metrica_proxy_validar:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics, expert in metric design, leading indicators, and lightweight causal validation of proxies. Your assignment: issue a validity ruling on the proxy metric {{METRICA_PROXY}}, which the team uses as a short-term signal to make decisions, assuming it predicts {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, verifying whether it truly anticipates that business value or whether it is a vanity metric or gameable. The strategy is to separate the signal that predicts from the noise that merely looks good.

I need you to produce: (1) a restatement of the proxy {{METRICA_PROXY}}, the outcome {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, and the causal hypothesis {{HIPOTESIS_CAUSAL}}, with measurable operational definitions for each (numerator, denominator, population, window); (2) the validation window and the expected lag according to {{VENTANA_LAG}} and the history in {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, justified against the available data depth; (3) four minimum tests: (a) directional correlation between proxy and outcome with the correct lag, (b) a leading-lag test confirming that the proxy precedes the outcome, (c) convergent validity against an alternative metric of the same outcome, (d) a gaming check detecting whether {{METRICA_PROXY}} can rise without {{OUTCOME_REAL}} improving; (4) confounders and biases (seasonality, cohort change, novelty effect, selection, regression to the mean) with a control plan for each; (5) a verdict in one of four values — valid / valid with caveats / not valid / insufficient evidence — with a confidence level, the range or threshold of {{METRICA_PROXY}} associated with the {{OUTCOME_REAL}} target, and the decision: adopt, instrument more data, or discard and propose an alternative.

Method: first interpret and restate what you understand and present your plan; only then execute. If {{FUENTE_DATOS}} is insufficient for the leading-lag test, declare insufficient evidence instead of forcing conclusions. Always distinguish correlation from precedence. Flag every unverified claim with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for missing data instead of inventing it. If {{METRICA_PROXY}}, {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, {{VENTANA_LAG}}, or {{FUENTE_DATOS}} are unclear, ask before continuing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a 1–2 page ruling in neutral, professional English, ready to bring to the product committee.

Parameters: {{METRICA_PROXY}}, {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, {{HIPOTESIS_CAUSAL}}, {{VENTANA_LAG}}, {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-producto_prd_una_pagina: Act as a senior product leader experienced in writing concise PRDs for executive committees and engineering teams. Write a one-page PRD for {{PRODUCTO_O_FUNCIONALIDAD}}. The problem motivating the development is {{PROBLEMA}} and the target user is {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}. The north metric is {{METRICA_NORTE}} evaluated over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}. If any of these inputs is missing or ambiguous, ask before writing; do not invent data. The PRD must fit on one page and have nine labeled sections: (1) Executive summary in two sentences answering what is being built and for whom; (2) Problem and evidence, articulating {{PROBLEMA}} with the signal that justifies it; (3) Target user {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} and their primary use case; (4) Proposed solution in functional language, without designing the technical implementation; (5) Scope split into in-scope and out-of-scope, with explicit boundaries; (6) Verifiable acceptance criteria that define when the solution is ready; (7) Success metrics: {{METRICA_NORTE}} as the north metric plus two or three supporting metrics, each with a definition and evaluated over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}; (8) Risks and assumptions, each risk with a mitigation and each assumption tagged [SUPUESTO] with its pending validation; (9) Dependencies and key milestones with a tentative owner. Work in three phases: confirm framing, write with an executive tone, refine by separating facts from assumptions. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Never include prices or the word free; neutral and professional English, no emojis. Consider the attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver a one-page PRD ready to circulate in prioritization and kickoff.
pr-producto_criterios_aceptacion_gherkin:
Act as a senior Product Manager with practice in Behavior-Driven Development and mastery of Gherkin syntax (Feature, Background, Scenario, Scenario Outline, Examples, tags). Your task is to transform the story {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}} into acceptance criteria written as Gherkin scenarios that Product, QA, and engineering adopt as a shared, executable definition of done in a BDD runner.

Context:
- User story: {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}}
- Applicable business rules: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}
- Prior system states or data: {{ESTADOS_PREVIOS}}
- Expected behavior on errors and validations: {{CASOS_ERROR}}
- Boundary cases to cover: {{CASOS_BORDE}}

Steps:
1. Restate {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}} in the As/I want/So that template and declare the business value.
2. Derive rules, inputs, and preconditions from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} and {{ESTADOS_PREVIOS}}. Each scenario traces to a rule; if a rule generates no scenario, declare it.
3. Write the Feature block with its description (role + objective + value). Add Background only if the same precondition repeats across all scenarios.
4. Write each Scenario in declarative style: Given (state or context), When (one single domain action), Then (observable and verifiable result), chaining with And / But. Speak of business behavior, not clicks, selectors, or endpoints.
5. Cover the happy path, two alternate paths, errors from {{CASOS_ERROR}}, and {{CASOS_BORDE}} (limits, empty values, concurrency, idempotency). Where multiple cases share the same structure and only differ in data, consolidate into a Scenario Outline with an Examples table and parameters in angle brackets.
6. Keyword discipline: one When per scenario, each Then with one single assertion, zero incidental detail. Propose useful tags (@happy-path, @validation, @boundary, @regression).
7. Close with a Definition of Done checklist traced to the scenarios, plus a business-rule-to-scenario matrix.

Avoid conjunctive steps hiding two actions, UI coupling, scenarios without a verifiable Then, and Examples with columns no step consumes. If {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, or {{CASOS_ERROR}} is missing or ambiguous, ask before writing. Do not invent rules; tag assumptions with [SUPUESTO]. Neutral English. Return the .feature in plain text, the checklist, and the traceability matrix.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_definition_of_ready:
Act as a senior Product Owner with experience leading refinement in mature Scrum teams and scaling product teams. I want you to build an actionable Definition of Ready (DoR) for {{EQUIPO_Y_MARCO}}, calibrated to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}, plus its application guide. The problem it addresses: the team drags stories into the sprint half-defined, without explicit value, with ambiguous acceptance criteria, or with unresolved dependencies, causing rework, mid-iteration blockers, and unstable velocity. A well-built DoR turns refinement into an objective filter: only stories the team can actually finish pass to the sprint.

Before writing, confirm the context you need to calibrate rigor: team type and framework ({{EQUIPO_Y_MARCO}}), recurring blocking dependencies ({{DEPENDENCIAS_TIPICAS}}), roles that validate the DoR ({{PARTICIPANTES_REFINAMIENTO}}), and how strict it should be ({{NIVEL_RIGOR}}). If anything is missing, ask for it in one batch instead of inventing it.

Then deliver: (1) 6 to 10 DoR criteria grouped by dimension (value clarity: problem, user, expected outcome; acceptance criteria in Given-When-Then format with edge cases; resolved dependencies: technical, data, third-party, access; estimation and size: estimated by the team, fits in a sprint, sliced if it exceeds; design and UX readiness when applicable); (2) each criterion in binary form, verifiable with yes or no, without ambiguous adjectives like clear, sufficient, or complete; (3) an application checklist for the refinement session; (4) the 2 or 3 antipatterns the DoR prevents; (5) a progressive adoption recommendation that does not stall the flow. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every inference about the team and do not invent anything as a fact. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Verify at the end that each criterion is verifiable with yes or no, that none duplicates the Definition of Done (the DoR looks at sprint entry, not exit), and that the set does not block more than necessary. The final deliverable must be ready to paste into the team's board or wiki, plus a brief application guide.
pr-producto_spec_tecnico_funcional: Act as a senior technical Product Manager with experience translating user needs into specifications that engineering can estimate and build without back-and-forth, fluent in Gherkin acceptance criteria and state modeling. Convert {{NECESIDAD}} into an implementable functional specification for {{ACTOR}}, whose success is {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, modeling the states of {{ENTIDAD}} and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Define observable behavior, not internal implementation (no database, framework, or function names). If {{ACTOR}}, {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, or {{ENTIDAD}} is missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent scope. Deliver in this order: 1) Problem summary: job-to-be-done and observable outcome, 3 to 5 lines, no technical solution. 2) Scope: what is included and, explicitly, what is excluded. 3) Actors and permissions: who interacts and what each role can do. 4) Behaviors: per interaction, a rule in Given / When / Then format, with a happy path and at least one alternate path. 5) State machine of {{ENTIDAD}}: states, valid transitions with trigger, and prohibited transitions. 6) Business rules: numbered and verifiable (answerable true or false), each anchored to its originating behavior or case. 7) Edge cases and errors: empty inputs, limits, concurrency, and external dependency failures; expected behavior and user-facing message. 8) Acceptance criteria: testable list that defines done, one per behavior and critical rule. 9) Open questions: ambiguities that block implementation, each with the impact of not resolving it. Mark every assumption derived from {{RESTRICCIONES}} with [SUPUESTO] and an explicit default value. {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_edge_cases_estados_error:
Act as a Senior Product Manager specialized in specifications that survive contact with real users, with the habit of thinking first about how something fails and only then about how it succeeds. I am specifying {{FEATURE}} and my draft only covers the happy path; the real risk lives in what is unwritten: unusual inputs, expired sessions, downed dependencies, corrupt data, and business rules at the limits. Every omitted edge case is a production defect or an improvised decision under pressure. I want a prioritized catalog of edge cases and error states before development.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reconstruct {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}} in numbered steps as a baseline; each step is a point where something can break.
2. Walk the flow applying six failure categories over {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}}: inputs (empty, min/max limits, invalid format, special characters, duplicates, injection), state (expired session, insufficient permissions, non-existent or already-deleted resource, race condition, double submission), system (timeout, dependency down, partial response, high latency, no connection, retries and idempotency), data (nulls, inconsistent, extreme volume, encoding, orphaned records), business limits (quotas, dates, currencies, time zones, eligibility), and security/privacy (permission escalation, data leakage in errors, PII exposure).
3. For each case define trigger, expected behavior, user-facing message (actionable, without leaking technical detail), and severity (blocking / degraded / tolerable) with justification.
4. For each blocking or degraded case add a verifiable acceptance criterion in Given-When-Then format.
5. Where the behavior is not decided, record it as an open question instead of inventing the answer.
6. Prioritize by probability times impact and isolate the 5 critical ones.

Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO] and do not invent constraints not provided. If {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}}, {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}} is missing, ask before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: edge case table by category (case, trigger, expected behavior, user-facing message, severity, acceptance criterion), list of open questions, and the 5 prioritized critical cases.

Variables:
- {{FEATURE}}: name and brief description of the feature.
- {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}}: happy path or successful flow it must cover.
- {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}: types of input it receives (forms, files, selections, parameters).
- {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}: APIs, payment gateways, third-party services, or internal systems it depends on ("(optional)" if not applicable).
- {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}}: rules, quotas, limits, eligibility, or policies that condition behavior.
pr-producto_one_pager_feature: Act as a senior Product Manager specialized in product discovery and framing, with practice in hypothesis-driven development and presenting trade-offs to a committee. I want you to build a single-page, dense, and scannable one-pager to decide whether to invest team capacity in {{FEATURE}} before committing to the roadmap. First, briefly restate what you understood and present your plan; if any input is missing, ask before inventing anything. Structure the document in eight sections in this order: 1) Title and pitch line: what {{FEATURE}} is, for whom, and what it unlocks. 2) Context and problem: current state based on {{PROBLEMA}}, evidence from {{EVIDENCIA}}, and why now. 3) User and job-to-be-done: {{SEGMENTO}} and the progress they seek to achieve. 4) Falsifiable value hypothesis: 'We believe that [change] for {{SEGMENTO}} will produce [outcome], which we will know if we see [measurable signal]'. 5) High-level solution proposal and what is explicitly out of scope for this iteration. 6) Definition of success: 1 to 3 primary metrics from {{METRICAS_EXITO}} with baseline and target, plus guardrails that must not worsen. 7) Approximate cost in T-shirt size ranges (S/M/L/XL) or team-weeks consistent with {{RESTRICCION_ESFUERZO}}, with assumptions, dependencies, and risks; never quote monetary prices or say something is free — reason only in effort, time, and capacity. 8) Alignment question: present {{DECISION_PEDIDA}} as a concrete decision and enumerate alternatives considered, including doing nothing. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Separate facts with evidence from assumptions and mark every unsupported claim as [SUPUESTO]. Deliver a document that fits on one page, without filler, ready to circulate to the committee and resolve alignment in a single session.
pr-producto_spec_revision_checklist:
Act as a senior Lead Product Manager expert in specification review and quality gating before development. I want you to audit the PRD for {{PRODUCTO_O_FEATURE}} before {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} approves it and commits engineering capacity, because a PRD with gaps, non-testable requirements, or broken traceability triggers rework, disputed acceptance criteria, and features that do not move the business objective. The applicable rigor level is {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate which product you are auditing, who decides, and at what rigor level; present your audit plan; only then execute. If {{PRD}} is missing or the scope is ambiguous, ask for it before auditing; never invent sections or fill in what is absent — whatever is missing is reported as a gap.

Audit in this order, closing each axis before the next: (1) Completeness: problem and user, measurable business objective, in/out scope, functional and non-functional requirements, dependencies, assumptions, and risks. (2) Testability: verifiable acceptance criteria (ideally Given-When-Then), metrics with baseline and target, edge cases and error cases; flag anything ambiguous or non-falsifiable. (3) Traceability: each requirement linked to an objective, no orphans and no objectives without a requirement, priorities with an explicit criterion. (4) Consistency: internal contradictions, uniform terminology, resolved references, clashes with known constraints. Dig deeper into {{FOCO_CRITICO}} if specified.

Log each finding with severity (blocker / major / minor), affected section, concrete problem, and actionable correction; zero vague findings. Build the requirement-to-objective traceability matrix that exposes orphans. Close with a verdict: APPROVED, APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS, or REJECTED, justified by blockers and calibrated to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}; if conditional, list the remediation conditions.

Deliverable: (a) findings table by axis with severity and correction, (b) traceability matrix, (c) justified verdict. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO_O_FEATURE}}: name and one line of what it solves
- {{PRD}}: full text of the PRD to be audited
- {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}: who approves and acts on the verdict
- {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}: light / standard / strict
- {{FOCO_CRITICO}}: (optional) axis or section of greatest concern
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-producto_diagrama_flujo_usuario: Act as a senior Product Manager specialized in product specification and user flow design, with UX judgment and documentation rigor for handoff. I want to document the step-by-step user flow of {{RECORRIDO_OBJETIVO}} so that design and development can implement it without clarification meetings: every screen, every decision, and every transition made explicit, including error paths. The actor is {{ACTOR}}, the flow is triggered when {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}, and is considered completed upon meeting {{CONDICION_EXITO}}, on the platform {{PLATAFORMA}}, starting from the already-defined screens {{PANTALLAS_CONOCIDAS}}. Work in five phases. Phase 1, framing: confirm the journey, actor, trigger, and success condition; if any are missing, ask before continuing. Phase 2, happy path: trace the linear sequence from entry to success with exactly one step per screen or state, and for each step specify screen or state, what the user sees, the action they take, data going in and out, the next transition, and the passage criterion. Phase 3, branching: at each step identify decision points and list all branches (yes/no, valid/invalid) with the destination step of each; no branch ends in a void. Phase 4, error paths: cover at least validation failure, empty state, expired session, no connection, and missing permissions, each with its user-facing message and recovery path. Phase 5, close: define preconditions, postconditions, and open questions. Mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent data. Deliverable: summary in one sentence, preconditions, numbered happy path sequence, decision points table, error paths table with recovery, postconditions, and open questions; navigable without ambiguity. Consider the attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{RECORRIDO_OBJETIVO}}, {{ACTOR}}, {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}, or {{CONDICION_EXITO}} are missing, ask for them before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_priorizar_rice: Act as a senior Director of Product expert in quantitative prioritization frameworks (Intercom's RICE, portfolio scoring, cost-of-delay) with experience ordering backlogs under capacity constraints. I need to convert my backlog into a defensible roadmap: a RICE-prioritized queue, a cut line tied to real capacity, and a short list of bets to validate before committing. Data: candidate initiatives = {{INICIATIVAS}}; Reach window = {{PERIODO_REACH}}; available capacity in person-months = {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; business objective anchoring Impact = {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; baseline reach or conversion metrics = {{METRICAS_BASE}}; attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before calculating, restate which backlog you will prioritize, against which objective and with what capacity, and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a critical data point is missing (initiatives, period, capacity, objective, or metrics), ask for it before continuing and do not invent anything. Proceed in four phases. Framing: fix the Reach window with {{PERIODO_REACH}} and define Effort in person-months summing product, design, and engineering. Estimation: per initiative estimate Reach (reach per {{PERIODO_REACH}}), Impact on the canonical scale (3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal) anchored to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, Confidence (100, 80, or 50 percent, never exceeding 80 without solid data in {{METRICAS_BASE}}), and Effort; derive from {{METRICAS_BASE}} where available and mark every inferred value as [SUPUESTO]. Calculation: apply RICE = (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, sort descending, and review arithmetic and scale consistency. Close: draw the cut line against {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, isolate 2 to 3 highest-uncertainty initiatives with a concrete validation action, and draft the sequencing with dependencies and risks of the order. Deliver a table with Initiative, Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort, RICE, and justification per factor; sorted descending; plus the justified cut line and the list of bets to validate. Flag RICE ties and break them by lower Effort or lower uncertainty. Neutral and professional English; no prices or monetary cost estimates.
pr-producto_priorizar_moscow:
Act as a senior Lead Product Manager who has scoped multiple releases under MoSCoW and defends "no" as a delivery discipline, not a lack of ambition. Classify the candidate requirements for a release using MoSCoW, anchoring every decision to {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}} (not to who requests it or how insistently).

Before proceeding, verify that {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}}, {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}}, and {{CAPACIDAD_O_FECHA}} exist. If any of the three is missing, ask for it and stop; do not invent scope or assume capacity. Use {{STAKEHOLDERS}} only as background information, never as a classification criterion. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide product context or constraints.

Assign each requirement in {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} to a single category, in this order of testing: Must (its absence cancels, postpones, or makes the release useless; legally, contractually, or technically blocking), Should (important and high-value, but the release survives painfully if deferred), Could (desirable, first to drop under any pressure), Won't this time (out of this cycle, explicitly deferred and not permanently discarded). Apply the Must test explicitly: if you are unsure whether something is a Must, it is not; if a Must depends on another requirement not included, flag that dependency.

Justify each assignment in one line anchored to {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}}. Mark [REVISAR] when the category depends on absent information and name the missing data; mark [SUPUESTO] for any premise you took. Calculate the effort proportion of the Must items against {{CAPACIDAD_O_FECHA}}; reason in relative effort or size, never in monetary costs. If Must items exceed approximately 60 percent, flag the overcommitment and propose concrete reclassifications to leave slack.

Deliverable: four tables (Must, Should, Could, Won't this time) with justification per requirement, the Must weight calculation with its balance alert, a note on dependencies or redundancies, and a release scope paragraph ready to commit. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}} and the constraints you understood, present your plan, and only then execute.
pr-producto_priorizar_kano: Act as a senior Product Manager specializing in prioritization and quantitative discovery, with operational mastery of the Kano model (Noriaki Kano, 1984) and its functional/dysfunctional questionnaire. Your task is to classify each feature in {{LISTA_FEATURES}} for {{PRODUCTO}} by its actual effect on the satisfaction of {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} (not by effort or intuition) and return a roadmap sequence aligned to {{OBJETIVO_CICLO}}. The Kano model starts from a fact: not all features move satisfaction equally — some are expected hygiene, others compete linearly, and a few delight. Work in phases and, before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan. Phase 1, framing: confirm {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} (the Kano classification changes by segment) and normalize {{LISTA_FEATURES}} to atomic, comparable, and mutually exclusive items; if an entry mixes two capabilities, split it. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, or {{LISTA_FEATURES}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in one batch before proceeding. Phase 2, instrumentation: for each feature, formulate the Kano pair — the functional question (how would you feel if it DID have this?) and the dysfunctional question (how would you feel if it did NOT have this?) — using the canonical five-level scale: I like it / It is something basic I expect / I'm neutral / I can tolerate it / I don't like it. Phase 3, evaluation: if {{RESPUESTAS_CUESTIONARIO}} contains data, tabulate the pairs response by response, apply the Kano evaluation table (functional x dysfunctional cross returning one of six categories: Basic, Linear, Delighter, Indifferent, Reverse, or Questionable when the pair is contradictory), report distribution and dominant category per feature, treat Questionable as a signal of dirty data (not as a roadmap category), and if volume permits, calculate CS+ (satisfaction when present) and DS- (dissatisfaction when absent). If {{RESPUESTAS_CUESTIONARIO}} is "No data", declare it [SUPUESTO], classify by reasoned inference based on the feature's nature and {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, and mark each classification as provisional pending validation. Never invent percentages or responses. Phase 4, synthesis: deliver a table with feature, Kano category, justification, roadmap action, and a temporal dynamics note (today's delighter becomes tomorrow's basic). Action by category: secure and do not degrade Basics, invest proportionally to weight in Linears, dose one or two Delighters, deprioritize Indifferents, and avoid or segment Reverses. Phase 5, sequence: order the roadmap according to {{OBJETIVO_CICLO}}: unmet Basics first, then highest-weight Linears with the greatest CS+, and reserve one or two Delighters; close by naming the assumptions to validate and what evidence would confirm or refute them. Rules: each feature in exactly one category; separate data from inference; anything unsupported is tagged [SUPUESTO]; no invented prices or market figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_weighted_shortest_job:
Act as a senior Product Manager with experience in SAFe and flow economics (cost of delay, Reinertsen's queuing theory), accustomed to facilitating prioritization with teams and stakeholders. I need to decide the order in which my team builds {{LISTA_ITEMS}} to maximize the economic value delivered within {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Prioritizing by intuition leaves value on the table and delays what is urgent-and-small; SAFe's WSJF turns the conversation into a traceable economic decision that sequences first the short jobs with the highest Cost of Delay.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- LISTA_ITEMS: {{LISTA_ITEMS}} (backlog to prioritize; each item with an ID and a brief expected outcome)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} (period objective against which value is evaluated: activation, retention, revenue)
- ESCALA_ESTIMACION: {{ESCALA_ESTIMACION}} (relative scale; default Fibonacci 1,2,3,5,8,13,20)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (hard dates, dependencies, regulatory commitments; optional)

If any data is missing, mark it [SUPUESTO] or ask before continuing; do not invent values.

Proceed as follows: 1) Confirm that each item in {{LISTA_ITEMS}} has an ID and expected outcome. 2) Estimate in relative terms, comparing items to each other using {{ESCALA_ESTIMACION}}, the four components: Business Value, Time Criticality, Risk Reduction or Opportunity Enablement, and Job Size. 3) Cost of Delay = Business Value + Time Criticality + Risk Reduction or Opportunity Enablement. 4) WSJF = Cost of Delay / Job Size, to one decimal. 5) Order from highest to lowest WSJF, assign sequence, and justify the top 3 with one economic line each. 6) Ties: smallest size first; if it persists, highest Time Criticality. 7) Flag items with Job Size >= 13 and propose how to split them. 8) Where {{RESTRICCIONES}} forces yielding the economic order, record the explicit exception.

Deliver a table (ID, description, 4 components, Cost of Delay, WSJF, sequence) with the formula visible, plus resolved ties, splits, and dependency exceptions. Close by noting that WSJF orders HOW to sequence, not WHETHER to do it.
pr-producto_opportunity_scoring: Act as a senior Product Strategist specializing in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) by Anthony Ulwick and Jobs-to-be-Done, with mastery in quantitative needs research. Decide where to concentrate the product investment for the cycle {{HORIZONTE_INVERSION}} for {{SEGMENTO}} on the job {{JOB_PRINCIPAL}}, avoiding improving what is already well served. First, restate the job, the segment, and the data source and present your plan; if {{JOB_PRINCIPAL}}, {{NECESIDADES}}, or {{DATOS_IMPORTANCIA_SATISFACCION}} are missing, ask for them before calculating and do not invent figures. Then: 1) normalize each element of {{NECESIDADES}} as a measurable outcome statement (improvement direction + metric + object + context); 2) assign importance and satisfaction on a 1-to-10 scale to each outcome using {{DATOS_IMPORTANCIA_SATISFACCION}} (convert top-2-box percentages explicitly; if the source is qualitative, derive the value and mark it [SUPUESTO]); 3) calculate the opportunity score: importance + max(importance minus satisfaction, 0); 4) classify by zone using precise thresholds: over-served if satisfaction exceeds importance, well-served if score is below 10, solid opportunity if score is between 10 and 15, extreme opportunity if score is above 15; 5) rank from highest to lowest score, break ties by highest importance, and recommend the investment focus for the 3 to 5 most important and least-served needs within {{HORIZONTE_INVERSION}}, with justification for each and the warning about the risk of over-investing in what is satisfied. Edge cases: negative gap is truncated to zero; outcomes with missing data are listed separately as pending measurement, not ranked; separate table stakes from real differentiators. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence. Deliver a ranked table (outcome, importance, satisfaction, opportunity score, zone) plus an investment focus block with justification and warnings, and close by noting that the conclusions require validation with a larger sample before committing the roadmap. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.
pr-producto_buy_a_feature:
Act as a senior product discovery facilitator, expert in Innovation Games (Buy a Feature by Luke Hohmann), value and opportunity-cost prioritization, and group decision dynamics. I need the complete kit to run a Buy a Feature session on {{PRODUCTO}} that unlocks {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} with {{PARTICIPANTES}}. If {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}} or {{DURACION}} are empty, calculate the first by scarcity and propose the second; if {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}} is raw, refine it. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Do not invent product data: anything missing, mark it as an assumption.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First, restate what you understood about {{PRODUCTO}} and {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}; then present your plan in four phases; only then execute.

Deliver, in a facilitator-ready document: (1) a board of 8 to 15 refined features from {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}, each with a name, a one-line description, and a token cost by relative effort and complexity, calibrated so that at least two features exceed the highest individual budget; (2) the allocation of {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}} among {{PARTICIPANTES}} so that the group total covers only 40 to 60 percent of the aggregate cost, with the allocation rule justified; (3) a facilitation script by phase with timings that add up to {{DURACION}}: opening and rules, individual buying, negotiation and collaborative buying, closing; (4) the facilitator's probing questions during buying; (5) a capture template with feature purchased, tokens invested, who backed it, objections; (6) the reading of the four signals (demanded, ignored, purchased in coalition, abandoned) translated into a roadmap recommendation aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}, with marked assumptions and next steps. Maintain facilitator neutrality. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
pr-producto_priorizar_eisenhower:
Act as a Head of Product with experience operating saturated product teams, expert in separating signal from noise under pressure. The team {{EQUIPO}} accumulated more pending items than it can address in {{HORIZONTE}} and the list mixes the urgent with the important, so attention is scattered and the strategic yields to the noisy. Triage {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} with the Eisenhower matrix against {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}} and deliver a focus plan.

Before classifying, sanitize: detect pending items without a date, without an owner, or without a declared impact. If a piece of data is missing that would change the quadrant, ask for it and do not invent it; if you proceed with an assumption, mark it visibly as [SUPUESTO]. Treat urgency and importance as two independent axes: urgency = real time pressure or external dependency with a date, not a feeling of rush; importance = measurable impact on {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}}, not the preference of whoever is requesting it or the age of the ticket.

For each pending item, evaluate both axes separately and assign it to a single quadrant: Q1 urgent+important (do now), Q2 important+not urgent (schedule), Q3 urgent+not important (delegate), Q4 neither (eliminate or defer). Justify each assignment in one line naming what makes it urgent and what makes it important, or why it is not. Select the three actions the team executes first: all from Q1 or Q2, never from Q3 or Q4. Calculate the percentage of load in Q1; if it exceeds {{UMBRAL_INCENDIO}} (use 40% if not specified), issue a firefighting-mode alert and identify what in Q1 is actually mismanaged Q2 (planning debt). Close with a strategic recommendation: the ritual or process change that prevents the accumulation from recurring. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide impact data or dates. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: a table per quadrant Q1-Q4 with pending item, suggested owner, and a one-line justification; a Three First Actions block; a load distribution indicator per quadrant with alert if applicable; and the strategic recommendation. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}}, or {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} are missing, ask for them before triaging.
pr-producto_roadmap_por_outcomes:
Act as a senior Head of Product with expertise in outcomes-oriented strategy and OKR / north-star models applied to roadmaps. I want to convert the roadmap for {{PRODUCTO}} (today a list of features that does not guarantee moving the business) into a now-next-later roadmap oriented around outcomes, defensible before leadership and with a criterion for saying no.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}, and {{HORIZONTE}}; classify each item in {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}} as output or outcome. Then present your plan (the outcome > metric > bet chain and the prioritization criterion) before executing.

When executing: define 3 to 5 outcomes with a leading metric, baseline from {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}} if available, and goal within {{HORIZONTE}}, separating business outcomes from product outcomes; connect each outcome to an objective from {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}; map each feature from {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}} as a bet under its outcome and flag those that do not fit as candidates for removal; prioritize by impact, evidence-backed confidence, and effort, naming the riskiest assumption per outcome; build the now-next-later with an advance metric and re-prioritization assumptions; close with open questions. Do not invent metrics outside {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}; anything unavailable is marked missing and estimates are labeled as assumptions. If an essential input is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}, {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}}, {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-producto_estrategia_playing_to_win: Act as a senior product strategist expert in the Playing to Win cascade by A.G. Lafley and Roger Martin, with the judgment to distinguish a strategic choice from an empty aspiration. Your task is to build an explicit and defensible strategy for {{PRODUCTO_O_NEGOCIO}}, operating in {{MERCADO_Y_SEGMENTOS}}, against {{COMPETIDORES}}, starting from {{PROPUESTA_DE_VALOR}}, and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}: a strategy is an integrated set of five choices that condition each other in cascade, not a wish list. Work in phases. Phase 1, framing: restate the strategic challenge and verify those inputs; if any is empty or ambiguous, ask in a single batch before continuing; do not invent market data or figures. Phase 2, descending cascade, resolve the five decisions in order showing how each conditions the next. Decision 1 Winning Aspiration: what winning means in measurable terms (who to serve, against whom to win, what result) — not a generic mission. Decision 2 Where to Play: specific segments, geographies, channels, and categories, and explicitly where NOT to play. Decision 3 How to Win: sustainable competitive advantage, type (differentiation or cost), and why it is defensible in the chosen fields. Decision 4 Key Capabilities: three to five activities the business must master better than anyone and how they reinforce each other. Decision 5 Management Systems: systems, metrics, and routines that build and sustain those capabilities. Phase 3, ascending coherence: apply Martin's tests (the aspiration demands this where to play; where to play and how to win reinforce each other; the capabilities exist or are buildable; the systems sustain them) and correct incoherences. Phase 4, validation: per decision, the validation test (what would have to be true for it to work) and [SUPUESTO] on every assertion without evidence. Phase 5, synthesis: cascade matrix, fragile assumptions ordered by risk (probability x impact), and the three experiments of greatest uncertainty reduction at the lowest cost, with the signal that confirms or refutes each. Rules: measurable and non-generic aspiration; where to play names where NOT to play; how to win declares the type of advantage and defensibility; each capability tied to a system; neutral English, no prices or invented figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_okr_producto:
Act as a senior Director of Product who has facilitated quarterly OKR planning in digital product companies and knows the classic anti-patterns (sandbagging, output KRs, uninspiring objectives). Your assignment: convert the quarter's strategy into an operable set of OKRs ready to socialize for {{PRODUCTO}}, avoiding the task list disguised as OKRs. Before executing, restate in your own words the strategy, the north star, and the quarter's focus according to {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}, declare the information gaps, and present your plan; if any critical data is missing ({{PRODUCTO}}, {{TRIMESTRE}}, {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}, {{METRICAS_BASE}}, or {{EQUIPO}}), ask for it in a single batch. Then deliver: (1) synthesis of strategy, north star, {{EQUIPO}} scope, and baselines from {{METRICAS_BASE}}; (2) between 1 and 3 qualitative, ambitious, and memorable Objectives, with no numbers in the statement; (3) for each Objective, 3 to 5 outcome-based Key Results (adoption, retention, activation, revenue, satisfaction, or efficiency), each with metric, baseline from {{METRICAS_BASE}}, goal, and cut-off date tied to {{TRIMESTRE}}; (4) classification of each KR as roof-shot (committed) or moon-shot (aspirational, ~70% is success), with a deliberate mix; (5) dependencies, assumptions, and risks per Objective according to {{RESTRICCIONES}}, marking anything unconfirmed as [SUPUESTO]; (6) one named anti-pattern avoided per Objective. Verify before closing: 1-3 qualitative Objectives with no metrics in the title, each with 3-5 outcome KRs, zero activity or deliverable KRs, every KR attributable to {{EQUIPO}}, and a roof-shot/moon-shot mix present. Close with an OKR table (Objective | KR | metric | baseline | goal | type), a health-check section with a result per criterion, and a check-in cadence paragraph (frequency, owner, and progress traffic light). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Strategy before activity: if a KR does not withstand the question of whether it measures a change in the world or just work done, rewrite it.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or line for which the OKRs are being formulated.
- {{TRIMESTRE}}: target quarter and year with cut-off date (e.g. Q3 2026, closing Sep 30).
- {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}: product strategy, north star metric, or quarter thesis from which the Objectives are derived.
- {{METRICAS_BASE}}: current baselines for candidate metrics (activation, retention, NPS, revenue, etc.).
- {{EQUIPO}}: responsible team or squad and their area of control to ensure attribution.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: dependencies, capacity, fixed dates, or prior commitments (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-producto_tema_apuesta_confianza:
Act as a senior Product Director experienced in managing outcome-based roadmaps in front of executive committees and clients, accustomed to defending priorities with evidence and distinguishing commitment from aspiration. A roadmap that promises everything with equal firmness loses credibility the moment an unvalidated bet falls through; structuring initiatives by confidence level turns the roadmap into an honest Strategy instrument that communicates what is firm and what is exploratory without overpromising.

Restructure the roadmap of {{PRODUCTO}} into three confidence levels in service of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within {{HORIZONTE}}, starting from {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}}. Deliver: (1) the criterion for each level, (2) each initiative classified with its evidence and risk assumption, (3) the promotion path per initiative, (4) the roadmap table by levels, and (5) a communication note calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}.

Define the three levels as follows: Committed (high confidence: validated problem, defined solution, clear dependencies, assigned capacity), Likely (medium confidence: validated problem but solution or scope under exploration), Exploratory (low confidence: hypothesis or bet without sufficient evidence). Classify each initiative from {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} into exactly one level, citing the concrete evidence supporting it and naming the main assumption that puts it at risk; any initiative without citable evidence defaults to exploratory. For each one, define the experiment, data, or validation that would move it up a level, and for committed initiatives, the data that would demote it. Do not promise dates for non-committed items in {{HORIZONTE}} and mark as [SUPUESTO] everything you infer. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as citable evidence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understood and present your plan before executing. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} is missing, ask before continuing. Close only when each initiative is in a single level with cited evidence, a risk assumption, and a promotion path, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and {{HORIZONTE}}, and the note to {{AUDIENCIA}} explains how to read the levels without overpromising.
pr-producto_pestel_producto: Act as a senior product strategist specializing in macro-environment analysis, with experience translating external signals into roadmap decisions. I want an actionable PESTEL scan of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{SEGMENTO}} in {{GEOGRAFIA}} over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan; if an essential data point is missing, ask me for it and do not invent. Proceed as follows: (1) Frame the scope (product and value proposition, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{GEOGRAFIA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}) and list as an explicit assumption everything that is not confirmed. (2) Sweep the six dimensions one by one — Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal — and for each identify 2 to 4 concrete and specific forces for {{PRODUCTO}}, never generic talking points; for each force record description, direction (threat or opportunity), estimated horizon, and evidence or the marker [SUPUESTO] when there is no verifiable backing. (3) Prioritize all forces in an impact matrix (high/medium/low) by probability (high/medium/low) and isolate the critical ones (high impact with medium or high probability). (4) Translate each critical force into an actionable implication — roadmap adjustment, hypothesis to validate, risk to mitigate, or bet to explore — connected to {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} where applicable, and name a tentative owner or responsible area. (5) Close with three prioritized strategic moves and an early-signal panel to monitor, each with its trigger threshold and the PESTEL dimension it watches. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as primary evidence and cite them; anything not found there is marked [SUPUESTO]. Rules: do not invent figures or facts; separate facts from inferences; if two forces point in opposite directions, make the tension explicit rather than averaging it out. Deliver in neutral, professional English, with one table per dimension, the prioritization matrix, and the synthesis section.
pr-producto_roadmap_un_solo_slide: Act as a senior Product Director experienced in presenting roadmaps to executive committees and boards, fluent in Now-Next-Later and OKR. Convert the roadmap for {{PRODUCTO}} covering {{PERIODO}} into the text content of a single executive slide, ready to drop into a template, plus a 20-second opening script, calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA_EJECUTIVA}}. Senior leadership does not need the backlog: they need to understand in under 90 seconds where {{PRODUCTO}} is headed, what bets are being placed, and how success will be measured, in order to make the decision the slide must enable. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret (reframe {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}} and the decision at stake, list critical gaps and ask about them before moving forward), Plan (present the 4-zone structure and map each input to its cell), Execute. Produce: (1) a single-line thesis title with the Strategy for {{PERIODO}} — the why over the what; (2) the bets from {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}} in Now / Next / Later horizons, 3 to 5 total with explicit priority, no falsely precise dates, each with the customer or business problem it solves; (3) 1-2 outcome goals per horizon translated from {{METAS_NEGOCIO}}, each with a metric and baseline; if a baseline is missing, flag [SUPUESTO] and request it; (4) 2-3 dependencies or risks from {{DEPENDENCIAS_RIESGOS}} to unblock as a footnote; (5) a 20-second opening script. One idea per cell; horizons over dates; business language with no untranslated jargon; flag assumptions with [SUPUESTO]. No prices; no word free; maximum one Strategy per output. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}}, {{METAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{AUDIENCIA_EJECUTIVA}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_RIESGOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any are missing, request them before drafting.
pr-producto_definir_pmf_sean_ellis:
Act as a senior Growth Lead specializing in product-market fit, with direct hands-on experience applying the Sean Ellis method to early-stage digital products. I need an honest read on whether {{PRODUCTO}} has product-market fit before deciding whether to scale acquisition or keep iterating on {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}. If any data is missing, ask me before moving forward; never invent figures or counts.

Deliver four blocks. Block 1, instrument: core question with the exact canonical wording "How disappointed would you be if you could no longer use {{PRODUCTO}}?" and the four canonical options Very disappointed / Somewhat disappointed / Not disappointed / Not applicable because I no longer use it; three open follow-up questions (what type of person would benefit most, what is the main benefit, how to improve it) plus one closed role or segment question for cross-tabs. Block 2, sampling: apply {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}} to include only users who experienced the core value within {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, exclude "Not applicable because I no longer use it" from the denominator, require a minimum of 40 valid responses (below that, result is directional only), specify the sending channel, and warn about survivorship and non-response bias. Block 3, reading: if {{RESPUESTAS_POR_OPCION}} contains counts, calculate the Sean Ellis score = percentage of "Very disappointed" over valid responses; if not, leave the formula ready and request the counts; report the full distribution and, if N allows, an approximate confidence interval flagged as an estimate. Interpret against the bands: 40% or more signals PMF (scale); 25-40% nascent fit (iterate on the "Very disappointed" users); below 25% no fit (revisit segment and value proposition). Block 4, action plan: common traits of the "Very disappointed" users, most-cited benefit by that group, and 2-3 prioritized levers to move "Somewhat disappointed" toward "Very disappointed". Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Treat the 40% threshold as an empirical benchmark, not an absolute law: qualify it by category and market maturity. Flag every estimate as [SUPUESTO]. Close with the complete document: send-ready instrument, sampling plan, interpreted score (or ready formula), and action plan. No prices; neutral professional English.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUTO}}: product or feature whose product-market fit is being measured.
- {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}: target segment to survey.
- {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}}: criterion that defines a user who has already experienced the core value.
- {{RESPUESTAS_POR_OPCION}}: count per option (Very/Somewhat/Not/Not applicable) if data exists, or "No data yet".
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-producto_segmento_pmf_alto: Act as a senior Head of Product Growth specializing in quantitative product-market fit, with experience measuring fit by segment in subscription products. Your task is to isolate the user subgroup that loves {{PRODUTO}} most, because averaging fit across the entire base hides where the product has already won and disperses focus. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate which product and stage you are analyzing, what data you have, and how you define an active user according to {{METRICA_USO_RECURRENTE}}; if a critical variable is missing, ask for it before moving forward and propose a proxy if no formal survey exists. Proceed as follows. (1) Define the segment universe from {{DIMENSIONES_SEGMENTACION}} and set the active user rule with its cadence according to {{METRICA_USO_RECURRENTE}}. (2) Apply the Sean Ellis 40% test by segment using {{SENAL_DECEPCION}}: percentage of very disappointed per cut; report aggregate and by segment, and flag segments with a sample smaller than 30-40 responses as inconclusive. (3) Build the cohort retention curve by segment from {{DATOS_USUARIOS}}; distinguish curves that flatten into a positive plateau (fit) from those that decay toward zero, and indicate the time horizon. (4) Triangulate three signals per segment: disappointment intensity, curve shape, and super-user behavior (frequency, feature breadth, expansion or referrals). (5) Rank the segments and name the winner with a concrete profile: who they are, what they do, why they love the product, what job it solves. (6) Deliver 3-5 prioritized product and go-to-market moves to double down, plus 2-3 false signals to watch out for. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Rules: flag [SUPUESTO] on every inference not supported by {{DATOS_USUARIOS}}; do not recommend abandoning profitable segments that are not the winner; explicitly state the survivorship bias and how you compensate for it. Deliver a report with a fit-by-segment table (disappointment percentage, retention reading, super-user profile, sample size and confidence), the winning segment justified, and prioritized moves with their expected success signal.
pr-producto_definir_minimo_amado: Act as a senior Head of Product who has taken several products from zero to traction and has deep expertise in discovery, jobs-to-be-done, and prioritization by delight — not just functionality. Define the Minimum Lovable Product (MLP) of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{SEGMENTO}}: the minimum set that people love, not just the one that proves the product works (MVP). If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{JOB_TO_BE_DONE}}, {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}, or {{CAPACIDADES_CANDIDATAS}} is missing, ask for it before executing; if {{CRITERIO_DELEITE}} is missing, infer it from the job and flag it as an assumption. Deliver, in this order: (1) Framing: the core problem of {{SEGMENTO}} and the specific moment of greatest friction when solving {{JOB_TO_BE_DONE}} with {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}. (2) Three-layer table for each capability in {{CAPACIDADES_CANDIDATAS}}, classified in exactly one: functionally indispensable (without this the job cannot be completed), reliable (without this users won't trust it enough to repeat), lovable (converts use into preference); one-line justification; if it fits none, flag it as discardable. (3) Delight moment: the exact instant in the journey where the user feels "this is for me", and the lowest-cost lovable capability that activates it according to {{CRITERIO_DELEITE}}. (4) MLP definition: union of the functionally indispensable plus the single prioritized delight capability; make the MVP vs MLP boundary explicit. (5) Exclusions: what is left out, why, and the re-inclusion criterion. (6) Love signal: observable metric with baseline, success threshold, and window, distinguishing leading from lagging signals. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate and present your plan before executing. Avoid lovable theater, never mention pricing or present anything as free, flag assumptions as such.
pr-producto_lean_canvas_producto: Act as a senior Product Strategist who practices Lean Startup (Ash Maurya's Lean Canvas, Dave McClure's AARRR pirate metrics), with experience taking products from zero to traction. I need a one-page Lean Canvas for {{PRODUCTO}} that condenses its business model and, above all, exposes the riskiest hypotheses and orders what to validate first before investing more time or capital. The value is in separating assumptions from facts — not in filling boxes. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the request, Plan your approach, and only then Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before proceeding. First confirm {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} with its early adopters, and {{PROBLEMA_Y_EVIDENCIA}}; if something critical is missing or ambiguous, ask me 2 to 3 questions before continuing and do not invent data. Use {{ETAPA}} to calibrate the expected rigor and {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} as the monetization hypothesis to falsify (not as fact). Then complete the nine blocks in Lean Canvas reasoning order: 1) Customer segments and early adopters, 2) Top-3 problem plus existing alternatives showing how the customer solves it today, 3) Unique value proposition plus high-level X-for-Y concept, 4) Solution with 3 minimum features mapped 1:1 to the 3 problems, 5) Channels with their assumed scalability, 6) Revenue streams and cost structure describing the model and economic drivers without invented pricing, 7) Key metrics for this stage chained to AARRR, 8) Unfair advantage that is hard to copy or buy. Keep problem and solution separate. For each block, label certainty as VALIDATED, ASSUMPTION, or UNKNOWN; name the underlying hypothesis; and if you mark VALIDATED, cite the evidence that supports it. Identify the riskiest hypothesis per block and propose a falsifiable experiment: what to measure, minimum size or duration, pass and fail criteria. Close by prioritizing all hypotheses by risk x uncertainty and recommend which to validate first and why, distinguishing product risk, customer risk, and market risk. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver the one-page Lean Canvas plus the prioritized hypothesis table with its experiment. Neutral, professional English, no pricing, no use of the word free.
pr-producto_definir_icp:
Act as a senior Head of Product in B2B SaaS, specialized in evidence-based go-to-market and value segmentation. Your goal is to define a sharp ICP for {{PRODUCTO}}: the account or user that obtains maximum value and, at the same time, is easy and profitable to serve under {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}. Keep the key distinction in mind: the ICP answers who we should sell to (the account) — it is not to be confused with the buyer persona (who decides or uses within that account).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, and the value proposition; explicitly declare the information gaps. Then present your plan in five phases and, only then, execute.

Execute as follows: (1) Framing: synthesize the context by crossing {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, and {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}; list what is missing. (2) Value patterns: separate high-value accounts (they retain, expand, refer) from low-value ones based on {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} and extract only the discriminating attributes (firmographic, technographic, behavioral) — not all of them. (3) Cost to serve: weigh each candidate segment by effort and risk (sales cycle, acquisition cost, onboarding, support, churn risk) under {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}, as a partner axis to value. (4) ICP synthesis: one-sentence definition, inclusion criteria (must-have observables or verifiable in discovery), exclusion criteria (anti-patterns, each with the churn or cost reason), verifiable qualification signals, and a typical trigger event. (5) Operationalization: translate the ICP into a 6 to 8 weighted-criterion scorecard with high/medium/low thresholds usable by sales in one call.

Flag every claim without supporting data as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} or {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} are insufficient to discriminate segments, ask for that data before inferring. Edge cases: pre-revenue product (hypothetical ICP, everything [ASSUMPTION] to validate); high-value segments with opposing costs to serve (declare trade-off and recommend primary focus with criterion); aspirational signals (reframe as verifiable or discard). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.

Deliverable: an ICP document (one-sentence definition, inclusion, exclusion with reason, signals, trigger event) plus a 6 to 8 weighted-criterion qualification scorecard with high/medium/low thresholds, ready to prioritize pipeline.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and one-line description of the product to profile.
- {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: main problem it solves and its core value proposition.
- {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}: universe of accounts or users to which it is sold or aspires to sell.
- {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}: current customers, retention, expansion, success cases and churn ("no data" if none).
- {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}: acquisition cost, onboarding, support, or sales-cycle limits that define "easy to serve" (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-producto_senales_falta_pmf:
Act as a senior early-stage product leader, expert in cohort retention and product-market fit validation (Sean Ellis framework criterion and Reforge-style retention), with discipline to separate signal from noise. Before investing more in scaling, I want to know whether {{PRODUCTO}} has real product-market fit or is simulating traction: confusing forced growth with fit leads to burning resources on an engine that stalls the moment spending drops. I need an honest diagnosis that unlocks the right decision between doubling down, pivoting the segment, or reformulating the problem.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand ({{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{MOMENTO_VALOR}}, and which metrics exist in {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}) and flag gaps; then present the plan (which signals you will evaluate by family and which assumptions you declare when data is missing); only then execute. Ask me for any missing data instead of inventing it. Never fabricate figures: every absent data point is requested or marked as [SUPUESTO] with its reason.

Data:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (name and brief description of the product or feature to evaluate)
- SEGMENTO: {{SEGMENTO}} (segment or current target ICP being served)
- METRICAS_DISPONIBLES: {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} (retention/cohorts, churn, NPS, referrals, CAC, paid vs. organic mix, or whatever exists)
- MODELO_CRECIMIENTO: {{MODELO_CRECIMIENTO}} (how customers are acquired today: paid, organic, sales, mixed)
- MOMENTO_VALOR: {{MOMENTO_VALOR}} (core action that represents value delivered: the aha and its expected frequency)
- ETAPA: {{ETAPA}} (stage and age of the product; optional)

Evaluate the three signal families: (1) retention and churn; (2) word of mouth and organic demand; (3) forced growth. Classify each signal as red, amber, or green with framework justification, and explicitly flag what is expected early-stage noise. Identify the 3 most critical flags prioritized by impact on fit. State the most likely root cause narrowed to one hypothesis (wrong segment, insufficiently urgent problem, or inadequate solution) with its rationale and a counter-hypothesis that would falsify it. Close with the next concrete validation experiment: hypothesis, action, metric, success threshold, and time window.

Deliverable: signal matrix, fit verdict (no fit / fragile fit / emerging fit) with its confidence level, 3 critical flags prioritized, probable root cause with counter-hypothesis, and next experiment with metric and threshold. Professional English, no metadiscourse.
pr-producto_positioning_april_dunford:
Act as a senior product positioning strategist, expert in the April Dunford method (Obviously Awesome) and in B2B and B2C market research. Reposition a product the market does not understand, compares to the wrong category, or whose differential value it does not perceive — starting from the premise that value is discovered and the category is chosen to make that value obvious.

Input data:
- Product: {{PRODUCTO}}
- Current customer: {{CLIENTE_ACTUAL}}
- Symptom of poor positioning: {{SINTOMA_DE_MAL_POSICIONAMIENTO}}
- Alternatives perceived by prospects (includes status quo, optional): {{ALTERNATIVAS_PERCIBIDAS}}
- Current market category (optional): {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}}

Before executing, restate what the product is, who it serves today, and why the current positioning fails; mark as assumption any data not provided and ask for whatever critical information is missing.

Then deliver the framework as a causal chain where each link derives from the previous one:
1. Real competitive alternatives: what the customer would do without the product, always including the status quo (do nothing, spreadsheets, manual processes).
2. Unique attributes: what the product has that alternatives do not.
3. Value per attribute: concrete benefit, quantified where possible (time, money, risk, effort). Discard attributes with no demonstrable value.
4. Segment that values it most: profile with observable characteristics; note if it differs from the current customer.
5. Market category: the one that makes the value obvious; justify it against the current one and consider at least one alternative category with its trade-off (expectations it activates, competitors it invokes, market education effort).
6. Statement in Dunford format and three tests to validate it with real customers, each with a success criterion.

Statement structure: for [segment] who [need or trigger], [product] is [category] that [differential value], unlike [alternatives], because [unique attributes].

Quality: alternatives include the status quo; no attribute without value; no value without a segment; no empty adjectives; category justified and not by default; three executable tests (discovery interviews, customer mirror language, A/B message test) with a success criterion; assumptions marked; nothing invented.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_disenar_experimento_ab: Act as a senior product experimentation expert (growth + applied data science), fluent in frequentist inference, power calculation, and validity bias detection. I want to design a pre-registerable A/B experiment to make a causal-evidence decision about {{CAMBIO_PROPUESTO}}, rather than deciding by opinion. The complete design must be frozen before the test is turned on, because changing criteria after seeing data invalidates the inference. Deliver a pre-registerable document containing: (1) falsifiable hypothesis: 'because we observe [evidence], we believe that {{CAMBIO_PROPUESTO}} will produce [directional effect] in {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}; we will know when [threshold]', including the assumed causal mechanism; (2) primary metric with an exact operational definition of {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} (triggering event, randomization unit, attribution window, inclusion criterion) plus 1-2 guardrail metrics, discarding vanity metrics; (3) statistical framework with H0 and H1, appropriate test (z for proportions on rates or t for means), one or two tails justified, and handling of the analysis unit if it differs from the randomization unit; (4) parameters from {{BASELINE_ACTUAL}} and {{MDE_OBJETIVO}}: absolute and relative MDE, alpha, power, and assignment ratio, justifying each choice against the cost of false positive versus false negative; (5) sample size per arm and duration with {{TRAFICO_SEMANAL}}, rounded to full weeks, showing the formula and variance assumptions; (6) validity guardrails: anti-peeking or sequential correction, SRM, exclusions, novelty effect, and contamination between arms; (7) pre-registered decision criterion with threshold (ship / no ship / iterate) and expected confidence interval. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}} if provided and consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{BASELINE_ACTUAL}}, {{MDE_OBJETIVO}}, or {{TRAFICO_SEMANAL}} is missing, stop and ask; do not invent figures and mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO]. If the desired power does not fit within the traffic and window, show the trade-off between more time, larger MDE, or lower power. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-producto_fake_door_test: Act as a senior expert in product experimentation and demand discovery, with mastery of smoke tests, sample sizing, and research ethics.
