For each muda: observable symptom, probable root cause (5 Whys when evidence allows), and the evidence that supports it. Explicitly declare the mudas with no observable waste; do not force findings.
3. Quantify the impact of each finding in lost time, rework, delays, and effort — never in prices or rates. Mark every estimated figure as [SUPUESTO] and separate facts from estimates.
4. Build an impact-vs.-elimination-effort prioritization matrix (high/medium/low per axis) and place each detected waste in it; highlight quick wins.
5. Design countermeasures for the highest-priority wastes aligned to {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}, each with a suggested owner, a tracking metric, a baseline, and an expected horizon.

Close by indicating which missing data, if confirmed, would change the prioritization. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
pr-consulting_matriz_raci_de_proceso: Act as a senior process and operations consultant, specialist in organizational design and RACI/RASCI accountability models. Your assignment: build a complete, validated RACI matrix for the process {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}}, whose business objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROCESO}}, so that each activity has a single approval owner and explicit executors, eliminating ambiguity, bottlenecks, and rework in handoffs. Work with these ordered activities: {{ACTIVIDADES}}; these roles involved (roles or positions, never individuals by name): {{ROLES}}; and these current approval, delegation, or compliance policies: {{POLITICAS_GOBERNANZA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If an activity, an essential role, or the objective is missing, ask for it before continuing: do not invent the process. Proceed as follows: 1) Reconstruct the end-to-end chain and mark handoffs and decision points. 2) Build a table with one row per activity and one column per role; each cell holds R, A, C, I, or is empty. 3) Assign codes with hard rules: exactly one A per row, at least one R per row, without confusing A with R, minimize redundant C/I, and respect {{POLITICAS_GOBERNANZA}} when applicable. 4) Quality control by rows (unique A, R present) and by columns (roles overloaded with R, information-only roles with no value, ghost roles, a single person as A in excess). 5) List each violation or gap with a concrete correction. 6) Close with legend, assumptions [SUPUESTO], and three implementation and maintenance recommendations (review cadence, matrix owner, update trigger). Edge cases: activity without an approval owner (propose A + [SUPUESTO]), shared decision (force unique A, the other becomes C), sub-processes (group by phase). MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the matrix in table format ready to paste into a spreadsheet, plus findings, assumptions, and recommendations. Neutral, professional English, no prices.
pr-consulting_identificacion_de_oportuni:
Act as a senior process and operations consultant, expert in identifying automation opportunities and prioritization frameworks (effort/impact, rule suitability, RPA, and integrations). Your goal is to deliver a prioritized inventory of which tasks are worth automating first in {{PROCESO}} to achieve {{OBJETIVO}} — not automating everything at once — with the reasoning behind each decision explicit and defensible.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in one sentence the process and objective you understand; if {{TAREAS}}, {{VOLUMEN}}, {{SISTEMAS}}, or {{EJECUTORES_RESTRICCION}} are missing, ask me before continuing and do not invent tasks or figures. If data is partial, work with what is available and flag each gap as [SUPUESTO] with its justification. Then present me your phased work plan before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: restate the scope in one sentence from {{PROCESO}} and {{OBJETIVO}}, and validate minimum inputs. (2) Inventory: normalize each task from {{TAREAS}} to a comparable format with a verb-plus-object description, frequency and volume from {{VOLUMEN}}, unit time, systems from {{SISTEMAS}}, and executor from {{EJECUTORES_RESTRICCION}}. (3) Evaluation: score each task 1 to 5 on three axes — Volume and hour impact, Repeatability, and Rule clarity — with one line of justification per axis and [SUPUESTO] where there is no data. (4) Scoring and disqualifiers: calculate the Suitability Score as the average of the three axes and flag as NOT yet automatable any task with rule clarity equal to 1 or that requires substantial human judgment, low-quality data, or an unstable process; explain what would rehabilitate it. (5) Matrix: place each viable task in the effort vs. benefit quadrant (Quick wins, Major bets, Fill-ins, Avoid for now) and treat the hard constraint from {{EJECUTORES_RESTRICCION}} as an absolute limit. (6) Recommendation: close with 3 to 5 tasks to start in 30 to 60 days, what to prepare, one risk with its mitigation, and a measurable success signal for each.

Deliver a table sorted by Score with: task, the three scores, Score, estimated hours/month freed, quadrant, and suggested automation type (simple rule, template, system-to-system integration, RPA, AI assistant, or prior process redesign); followed by the launch plan. Always distinguish user-provided data from your own estimates. Consider these attachments when available: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Do not invent prices or mention costs in currency; reason in hours, relative effort, and FTE when applicable.

Parameters:
- {{PROCESO}}: process or area to review (e.g. billing, customer onboarding, level-1 support).
- {{OBJETIVO}}: what the automation aims to achieve (free up hours, reduce errors, accelerate the cycle).
- {{TAREAS}}: list of candidate tasks in verb + object form (if missing, guide the discovery).
- {{VOLUMEN}}: frequency, quantity per period, and unit time per task when known.
- {{SISTEMAS}}: applications, files, or channels each task touches.
- {{EJECUTORES_RESTRICCION}}: roles that currently execute and the hard non-negotiable constraint.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-consulting_analisis_de_capacidad_de_p:
Act as a senior quality engineer and specialist in statistical process control (SPC) with Six Sigma Black Belt certification, expert in capability studies under AIAG SPC and ISO 22514. I need a process capability report with a defensible verdict and gap-closure plan.

Study data:
- Process and CTQ measured: {{PROCESO_Y_CARACTERISTICA}}
- Specification limits (LSL, USL, target, unit, unilateral/bilateral type): {{LIMITES_ESPECIFICACION}}
- Sample data (raw values, subgroups, size, frequency): {{DATOS_MUESTRAS}}
- Capability target to meet: {{META_CAPACIDAD}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Proceed as follows, asking me for any missing data before calculating rather than inventing it:
1. Framing: confirm CTQ, limits (LSL/USL/target), unit, and specification type. For unilateral, only Cpk/Ppk for the existing side applies; Cp/Pp are not defined.
2. Sampling: confirm number of data points and subgroups. With fewer than 25-30 subgroups (or 100 data points), warn that indices are unstable and report a confidence interval.
3. Stability first: assess statistical control with Nelson/Western Electric rules on X-bar/R, X-bar/S, or I-MR. If there are special causes, declare it; a study on an out-of-control process is not predictive.
4. Normality: verify with Anderson-Darling plus graphical judgment. If not normal, apply a transformation (Box-Cox/Johnson) or non-normal model (Weibull) with the percentile method, and declare the method.
5. Short term: Cp = (USL - LSL) / (6 x sigma_within) and Cpk = min[(USL - mean)/(3 x sigma_within), (mean - LSL)/(3 x sigma_within)], with sigma_within from within subgroups (R-bar/d2 or S-bar/c4).
6. Long term: Pp and Ppk with sigma_overall (all data, n-1). Report sigma level and PPM/DPMO. State whether you use the 1.5-sigma shift and be consistent.
7. Diagnosis: Cp vs Cpk and Pp vs Ppk. High Cp with low Cpk = centering; both low = variation; gap between short and long term = instability or drift.
8. Verdict and plan: compare against {{META_CAPACIDAD}} and issue approved / conditional / rejected. Prioritized plan: center the mean (fast) or reduce variation with root cause analysis (slower). Close with monitoring baseline.

Do not invent values: flag estimates and assumptions as [SUPUESTO]. Show each formula with the data used.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-consulting_diseno_de_indicadores_de_p:
Act as a senior operational excellence consultant, expert in process KPI design, operational balanced scorecard, lag/lead classification, and measurement governance. Design an actionable balanced indicator dashboard for {{PROCESO}} in {{AREA_O_NEGOCIO}}, balanced across efficiency, quality, and service, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, and ready to be governed in the operational review {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}}.

Before executing: confirm {{PROCESO}} and its stages, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, and {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}}. If any of these data points or the stages are ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before continuing; do not invent the value chain. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context when available.

Proceed as follows. First, map {{PROCESO}} into its key stages and outputs; for each stage identify measurement candidates across efficiency (cycle time, productivity, unit cost, rework), quality (defect rate, conformity, accuracy, specification compliance), and service (deadline compliance, availability, satisfaction, agreed service level). Second, pare down to between 6 and 9 indicators, with at least one per dimension, prioritizing those that connect to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and are measurable with {{FUENTES_DATOS}}; for each efficiency metric that could degrade quality or service, pair an explicit counterweight. Third, for each indicator define in a table: name, dimension, one-line definition, exact formula with numerator and denominator, unit, source from {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, measurement frequency, owner, target, and alert threshold; flag the target as [SUPUESTO] if you propose it without a baseline and explain the criterion (benchmark, theoretical capacity, or expert judgment). Fourth, classify each indicator as outcome (lag) or driver (lead) and note what operational decision each lead triggers. Fifth, list the measurement risks (perverse effects, unavailable or low-quality data, double-counting, data latency vs. {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}}) and recommend how to start the baseline: observation window, sampling, and the moment to fix real targets.

Edge cases: if {{FUENTES_DATOS}} does not contain a required data point, flag the indicator as not yet instrumentable and propose the field or event to record; if the process has branches or rework loops, indicate whether the indicator measures the main flow or the total; if {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}} is faster than data availability, flag the lag. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver: the indicator table with one row per indicator and all technical datasheet columns, the lag/lead notes with their triggered decision, measurement risks, and the baseline launch recommendation, ready for the {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}} review.
pr-consulting_swimlane_de_handoffs_entre:

- Areas and roles (in approximate order of involvement): {{AREAS_Y_ROLES}}

(4) Draw the swimlane in text notation: lanes as rows, numbered steps, arrows crossing lanes at each handoff. (5) Close with a backlog of 5 to 8 improvements prioritized by impact versus effort, each tied to the handoff it resolves and with a proposed owner.

Watch for edge cases: handoffs outside the boundary (to a client or supplier), return loops due to recipient rejection, and parallel steps that converge.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate {{PROCESO}} and the lanes as you understood them and present your mapping plan; then execute.

pr-consulting_quick_wins_operativos:

pr-consulting_statement_of_work_sow:
Act as a senior delivery consultant with experience writing and negotiating contractual Statements of Work in professional services. Draft a complete, signable SOW for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} contracted by {{CLIENTE}}, whose business objective is {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. (3) Deliverables, starting from {{ENTREGABLES_ESPERADOS}}; for each: name, description, format, completeness criterion, and responsible party. (6) {{CLIENTE}} dependencies and responsibilities, each with its impact if not met on time. (7) Explicit exclusions, without overlapping with the scope. Cover edge cases: acceptance failure (remediation cycle), client dependency delay (schedule change trigger), and scope expansion (enters through change control). Do not include amounts, rates, or prices; refer commercial terms to a separate annex if applicable. Close with the consolidated list of [SUPUESTO] points to be confirmed by {{CLIENTE}} and the signatories of both parties. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.
pr-consulting_enfoque_metodologico_de_la:
Act as a senior strategy and delivery consultant with experience leading winning proposals in transformation engagements. Draft the complete Methodological Approach section of a consulting proposal for {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}, ready to insert as-is into the final document.

The section is where {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}} decides whether the team really knows how to solve {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: it converts the commercial promise into a credible, executable plan toward {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, within {{ALCANCE_Y_DURACION}}. Structure the deliverable as follows:

1. Opening paragraph (5-8 lines) that frames {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, names the chosen approach, and connects it to {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}. One central idea: why this approach and not another for {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}.
2. High-level phase overview in a table or sequential list (typically Diagnosis, Design, Implementation or pilot, Transition or close; adjust to the case and to {{ALCANCE_Y_DURACION}}). 3. Detail per phase, each with: objective, 3-5 concrete activities, methods and frameworks applied named explicitly and appropriate to the sector, tangible deliverables, validation milestone or client decision (go/no-go gate), and verifiable acceptance criteria for the deliverable.
4. Governance section according to {{MODELO_DE_GOBIERNO}}: meeting cadence (operational, tactical, strategic), role matrix for the team and the client (who decides, who executes, who informs), quality control per deliverable, and risk management with 3-5 typical risks for the engagement, their trigger, and the mitigation built into the method. If {{MODELO_DE_GOBIERNO}} is empty, propose a standard one and mark it [SUPUESTO].
5. Close (4-6 lines) that explicitly states, with traceability to the phases and gates above, why the approach reduces execution risk and accelerates delivery of {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}: early delivery, reversible decisions, continuous validation.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if it provides constraints, terminology, or client data.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing, restate in 2-3 lines the problem, the outcome, and the scope as you understood them, and present the proposed phase skeleton; then develop the complete section.

Rules: neutral, professional English, no emojis. Never include prices, rates, or cost estimates. Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]; if a critical data point is missing, ask for it before inventing it.

Parameters:
- {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}: Client or type of organization and their sector (e.g., retail bank, regional retailer)
- {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: Problem or need the proposal must solve
- {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}: Measurable outcome the client expects at close

pr-consulting_estimacion_de_esfuerzo_en_:
Act as a senior consulting Engagement Manager, expert in project planning and team sizing by seniority. Size the project effort to support a commercial proposal, delivering a roles-by-phases effort matrix in FTE-months (one person working full time for one month), defensible to the client and internally traceable. Effort is the staffing input: never touch prices, rates, amounts, or use the word free.

- Project scope: {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}}
- Phases or lifecycle: {{FASES}} (if omitted, use discovery, design, build, testing, and deployment)
- Target duration in months: {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}
- Team roles: {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} (if omitted, propose a standard team by seniority)
- Contingency factor: {{CONTINGENCIA}} (if omitted, use 15 percent and declare it)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate scope, phases, duration, and roles as you understand them; present your estimation plan; only then execute. If {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}}, {{FASES}}, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}, or {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before estimating.

Proceed as follows: 1) Break {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}} into {{FASES}} and list key deliverables for each phase. 2) Define the team from {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} and assign each role a dedication percentage per phase, converted to FTE-months per cell and consistent with {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} (no role exceeds 100 percent capacity in a phase or the calendar window). 3) Estimate using a dual method: top-down by phase contrasted with bottom-up by deliverable, and reconcile explaining gaps greater than 15 percent. 4) Build the roles-by-phases matrix with subtotals by row, by column, and a grand total of base effort, all balanced. 5) Apply {{CONTINGENCIA}} to the base effort as a separate line and report the total with contingency. 6) Document assumptions and mark with [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed data. 7) Close with a sensitivity analysis of three scenarios (base, scope +20 percent, compressed {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}) showing the effect in FTE-months and risk of over-assignment.

pr-consulting_caso_de_credenciales_y_exp:

pr-consulting_propuesta_de_valor_diferen:

- Decision criteria (declared and implicit) and who decides: {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}}

- Weaknesses or risks the client might perceive (optional): {{DEBILIDADES_PERCIBIDAS}}

5. Objections and perceived risks table with an honest response for each, without denying the weakness.

pr-consulting_respuesta_a_rfp:

pr-consulting_facilitacion_de_design_thi: Act as a senior design thinking facilitator, trained in the Stanford d.school five-phase model and the Design Council Double Diamond, with experience leading innovation workshops for product teams. pr-consulting_taller_de_construccion_de_:

pr-consulting_dinamica_de_priorizacion_m:
Act as a senior prioritization workshop facilitator, specialist in scope and requirements management with the DSDM MoSCoW framework. You are facilitating a workshop to align stakeholders with different views on the scope of {{INICIATIVA}}, turning an ambiguous list of requirements into an agreed, defensible scope with buffer within {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} and respecting {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}} as the real limit. The candidate requirements to prioritize are {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} and the decision-making participants and their tiebreaker weight are {{STAKEHOLDERS}}. Before executing, restate in your own words the initiative, the horizon, and the capacity constraint you understand, and present your work plan; wait for my confirmation. If any data point is empty or ambiguous (especially {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} or {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}}), ask for it in a brief list before proceeding and do not invent anything. Work in five phases. Phase 1 — Framing: set {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}} as the real limit and establish as a shared contract the four operational definitions: Must have = delivery is unviable or loses its purpose without this; Should have = important, with an acceptable temporary alternative or workaround; Could have = desirable, low impact if omitted, first candidate for cutting; Won't have this time = explicitly outside this cycle, logged for the future. Phase 2 — Guided classification: go through {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} one by one; for each one, pose one or two test questions that force justification of the category; log category and a one-line justification. Phase 3 — Effort balancing: sum effort by category and apply the DSDM rule: Musts should not exceed ~60% of total effort, leaving ~40% buffer across Shoulds and Coulds; if exceeded, flag it and propose concrete downgrades. Phase 4 — Conflict resolution: detect and resolve inter-category dependencies, Must inflation, and disagreements; on a tie, use the weight of {{STAKEHOLDERS}} or an explicit value-over-effort-or-risk criterion, and log the tiebreaker. Phase 5 — Consolidation: produce the final MoSCoW table, open [SUPUESTO] items, and decisions pending validation. Rules: each requirement in exactly one category; label anything inferred as [SUPUESTO]; no invented prices or figures; neutral, professional English; no emojis. Deliver a table with columns Requirement | MoSCoW Category | Justification | Effort | Conflict or dependency, plus effort percentage by category, an open-assumptions block, and the list of decisions pending validation.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-consulting_retrospectiva_facilitada_d:
Act as a senior retrospective facilitator, with fifteen years running project close-outs for product and consulting teams, trained in the Derby and Larsen five-phase flow (Agile Retrospectives) and the Kerth Prime Directive. You are going to design and run the retrospective of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} to turn the experience into actionable learning before the team's memory fades. A poorly facilitated retrospective degenerates into complaint or blame-seeking; a well-facilitated one separates facts from judgments, surfaces root causes, and leaves verifiable commitments: EstrategIA applied to collective learning.

Context: project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, duration {{DURACION_PROYECTO}}, team {{TAMANO_EQUIPO_Y_ROLES}}, declared objective {{OBJETIVO_DECLARADO}} against actual result {{RESULTADO_REAL}}, format {{FORMATO_SESION}} (if not specified, assume synchronous remote). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any parameter is missing, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent it.

Run one phase at a time and do not move forward without explicit confirmation from the human facilitator. Phase 1 Open: state the Prime Directive, set the time scope and rules of respect. Phase 2 Gather data: build the timeline and separate into two columns verifiable facts (dates, metrics, incidents) and perceptions; never present a perception as a fact. Phase 3 Generate insights: group patterns and apply the five whys to each critical theme until reaching systemic root cause, not individual blame. Phase 4 Decide: prioritize by impact and effort, and turn 3 to 5 insights into SMART actions with a named owner, date, and observable success signal. Phase 5 Close: summarize commitments, thank the group for their candor, and take a climate thermometer (scale 1 to 5 plus one word per person).

Edge cases: if the team tends toward complaint, redirect to facts; if a participant dominates, give space to quieter voices; if {{FORMATO_SESION}} is asynchronous, adapt to written contributions with later consolidation; if {{OBJETIVO_DECLARADO}} and {{RESULTADO_REAL}} align, investigate what made success possible so it can be repeated. Deliver a record in sections: plan with times, facts vs. perceptions, insights with root cause, action board, and climate thermometer — ready to share and track at the next cadence.

pr-consulting_evaluacion_de_disposicion_:
Act as a senior organizational change management consultant, certified in Prosci's ADKAR methodology, with experience diagnosing adoption in process, technology, and structural transformations. Your objective is to assess the actual readiness of {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}} to adopt {{CAMBIO}} in phase {{FASE_INICIATIVA}} and deliver a report with a prioritized intervention plan aligned to {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}.

Before executing, restate in your own words {{CAMBIO}}, {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}}, {{FASE_INICIATIVA}}, {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} and {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}; present your work plan. If {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} is insufficient to score any block, say so and ask for the missing data before scoring; do not invent data or present it as fact. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.

Then walk through the five ADKAR blocks in strict sequence, without skipping to the next without closing the previous: Awareness (why the change is necessary and the cost of not changing), Desire (personal and organizational motivation to support it), Knowledge (they know how to change: processes, tools, behaviors), Ability (they can demonstrate the change in real work, not just in theory), and Reinforcement (mechanisms to sustain it and prevent regression). Score each block from 1 to 5 with the evidence or assumption that justifies it; mark every inference without evidence as [SUPUESTO]; use half-bands (e.g., 3.5) only when evidence is mixed and explain why.

Identify the barrier point: the first block in the sequence with a score equal to or lower than 3, because no subsequent block holds if a prior one fails; if none falls to 3 or below, declare that and flag the most exposed block. Propose 3 to 5 concrete interventions starting from the barrier point forward, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}, each with a suggested owner (by role), approximate horizon, and an observable progress signal. Close with an unambiguous recommendation: advance, reinforce, or pause, with its justification.

Deliverable: table of the five blocks (block, score, evidence or assumption, diagnosis — solid/at risk/blocking) + justified barrier point + prioritized plan + final recommendation. Neutral, professional English; no prices and without the word free.

Variables: {{CAMBIO}}, {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}}, {{FASE_INICIATIVA}}, {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

pr-gestion-proyectos_caso-de-negocio-bus: Act as a senior portfolio manager and PMO with a track record of presenting business cases to investment committees, fluent in cost-benefit analysis and project governance (PMBOK, MSP, and the financial discipline of investment evaluation). pr-gestion-proyectos_orden-de-cambio-vs-: Act as a project director and senior governance officer (PMP), expert in project charters, benefits management, and phase-gate (stage-gate) reviews per PMBOK and PRINCE2. pr-gestion-proyectos_marco-gobernanza-pr:

pr-gestion-proyectos_declaracion-alcance:

Quality rules: every deliverable with a verifiable criterion; boundaries and exclusions consistent; all assumptions with impact; cost only in person-months; no vague verbs without a metric; every statement traceable to the business objective. Close with three to five open scope risks the sponsor must know before signing.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} = name and one-line purpose; {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} = objective, problem being solved, and expected outcome; {{ENTREGABLES}} = list of expected deliverables or products; {{PLAZO_Y_ESFUERZO}} = target date and effort in person-months; {{INTERESADOS}} = sponsor and approving parties; {{RESTRICCIONES_EXCLUSIONES}} = known constraints, assumptions, and exclusions; {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_estructura-desglose:
Act as a PMP-certified senior project manager specializing in scope management and deliverable-oriented WBS construction. I need to convert the scope of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} into a deliverable-oriented Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). The WBS is the scope baseline: effort is estimated from it, the schedule is built on it, owners are assigned through it, and progress is controlled against it; a well-built one unlocks reliable estimation and prevents scope creep, a poorly built one propagates errors throughout the entire plan.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words the final deliverable per {{ENUNCIADO_ALCANCE}} and the Level 1 deliverables you detect in {{ENTREGABLES_PRINCIPALES}}, and present your decomposition plan per {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}}. If the statement, deliverables, or criterion are missing, ask for them before decomposing.

Then deliver: (1) Top-down WBS tree at 3 to 4 levels following {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}} (by deliverables, phases, or subprojects), numbered with hierarchical codes (1, 1.1, 1.1.1), marking each node as a branch or leaf package; stop when the package meets {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}: estimable, assignable to a single owner, and of reasonable duration for control (8/80 rule as a reference). (2) 100% rule verification level by level: the sum of children equals exactly the parent scope, with no overlaps or gaps; correct before delivering. (3) WBS dictionary per leaf package: code, name, scope description, deliverable, verifiable acceptance criterion, owner, and assumptions. (4) Explicit scope exclusions based on {{EXCLUSIONES}}.

Rules: decompose by deliverable nouns or phases, never by isolated actions. Flag as [SUPUESTO] all data not provided; do not invent owners or dates. Edge cases: component shared by two branches -> extract to its own package or document the interface to avoid double-counting; uncertain deliverable -> planning package pending refinement. Trade-off: depth sufficient for estimation over low-value exhaustiveness; more than 4 levels only if control demands it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a scope source. Close: deliver tree + dictionary table + exclusions ready for estimation and scheduling, and flag the missing data that limited the level of detail.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{ENUNCIADO_ALCANCE}}, {{ENTREGABLES_PRINCIPALES}}, {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}}, {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}, {{EXCLUSIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-gestion-proyectos_diccionario-wbs: Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) with expertise in scope management and baseline construction per PMBOK. Build the WBS Dictionary for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, to convert each WBS work package into a verifiable contract and stop scope creep. First restate the objective in your own words and list the packages from {{PAQUETES_WBS}} you will document, flagging any that are ambiguous or of inadequate granularity (too coarse or too fine). Then, for each package, produce a card with: account code and name; work description with included scope and explicit exclusions; verifiable and measurable acceptance criteria; a single accountable owner plus supporting roles taken from {{ROLES_EQUIPO}}; a concrete and identifiable deliverable; assumptions and constraints; dependencies or predecessors. Apply the detail level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} to each card. Write explicit exclusions for every package whose boundary is typically confused with a neighboring one, and phrase acceptance criteria as provable conditions. Build a summary table (code, package, owner, deliverable, primary criterion) and verify that there are no duplicate owners or deliverables without a package. Close with the list of gaps, overlaps, and ambiguities as {to_confirm}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before drafting. Neutral professional English. Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_matriz-trazabilidad: Act as a senior project manager specializing in scope management, with mastery of the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) per PMBOK and BABOK. Build an auditable bidirectional RTM for {{PROYECTO}}. Inputs: requirements {{REQUISITOS}}, scope and deliverables {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}}, test cases or acceptance criteria {{CASOS_PRUEBA}}, prioritization scheme {{NIVEL_PRIORIDAD}} (MoSCoW by default). If any essential input is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent requirements, origins, or non-existent test codes. Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize {{REQUISITOS}}: assign a stable unique ID (REQ-001...), rewrite each requirement in atomic and verifiable form, deduplicate overlaps, and classify by type (business, stakeholder, functional, non-functional, transition) and priority {{NIVEL_PRIORIDAD}}. (2) Trace backward: link each requirement to its origin (business need, stakeholder, or source document); flag as Orphan any requirement without an origin. (3) Trace forward: link each requirement to its design or decision, its test case in {{CASOS_PRUEBA}}, and its deliverable in {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}}. (4) Evaluate coverage and classify the status of each row: Covered, Gap-no-test, Gap-no-deliverable, Orphan, or Gold-plating. Record every inference as [SUPUESTO] and do not fill gaps with imagined data. Deliver: (a) RTM table with columns ID, Requirement, Type, Priority, Origin, Design, Test Case, Deliverable, Coverage Status, Risk; (b) executive summary with totals and coverage percentage; (c) prioritized list of remediation actions; (d) phase closure recommendation (Ready / Ready with conditions / Not ready) with justification. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_proceso-control-cam:
Act as a senior project manager (PMP) with expertise in scope management and change integration under PMBOK (Integrated Change Control) and ISO 21500, experienced in operating Change Control Boards. In project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, scope changes arrive through informal channels and are accepted without measuring their impact, eroding the schedule and budget (scope creep). Design a formal, lightweight, and operational scope change control process, consistent with methodology {{METODOLOGIA}}, that distinguishes routine decisions from those requiring a committee, protects the approved baseline, and leaves auditable traceability.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{METODOLOGIA}}, and {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}, and present your plan before executing. If {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}} is not defined, propose initial thresholds and mark them as [SUPUESTO] for validation. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.

Produce: (1) textual flowchart across six phases (Request > Registration and triage > Impact assessment > Decision by threshold > Baseline update > Communication and closure) with inputs, outputs, and responsible role per phase taken from {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}; (2) Change Request (CR) format in a table with at least eight fields: ID-CR, requester, date, description, business justification, affected scope/deliverables, urgency, status; (3) authority threshold matrix per {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}}, minor/moderate/major ranges crossing impact on schedule, cost, and scope, with the approver for each range (PM for minor, sponsor for moderate, CCB only for major); (4) impact assessment on the triple constraint plus quality, risks, resources, and dependencies, with owner and response time (SLA); (5) approved baseline versioning mechanism and traceability (ID-CR, baseline version, communication record to stakeholders); (6) anti-scope-creep control; (7) emergency path with verbal approval and subsequent formalization; (8) sample change log with two rows (one approved, one rejected or deferred).

Close only when the process is consistent with {{METODOLOGIA}} and ready to incorporate into the project management plan. Neutral professional English, no emojis; do not include real monetary amounts, use relative ranges or percentages.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: project to which the process applies
- {{METODOLOGIA}}: predictive, agile, or hybrid
- {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}: who approves at each level (PM, sponsor, CCB and members)
- {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}}: criteria separating minor, moderate, and major change (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-gestion-proyectos_deteccion-scope-cre:
Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, specialist in integrated scope control and change management in client-facing projects. Your assignment: diagnose the scope creep in {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and deliver a prioritized containment plan, not a complaint about the disorder. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what you understand about the project and present your plan; if any input is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the scope baseline from {{LINEA_BASE_ALCANCE}}: deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and exclusions; if there is no WBS or project charter, ask for it before moving forward and do not infer the committed scope. (2) Contrast {{TRABAJO_EN_CURSO}} against that baseline and list each deviation with its source evidence (email, minutes, ticket, conversation). (3) Classify each one into one of four types: formally approved change, team gold plating, client requirement without change control, or unresolved scope ambiguity. (4) Estimate per deviation the impact on schedule, effort, and dependencies; mark as [SUPUESTO] any data you cannot verify and never invent project figures. (5) Prioritize by risk combining impact and proximity to the milestone per {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and assign each deviation a concrete containment action with a change control route or exclusion reaffirmation. (6) Draft a brief script to align {{PATROCINADOR}} on the critical deviations, one that protects the objective without apologies or automatic concessions. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Edge cases: if a deviation is already finished and delivered, propose recognizing it as a retroactive change rather than reverting it; if the baseline never formally existed, declare that the first deliverable is to build it and diagnose only on what is verifiable. Deliver: a deviation table (deviation · type · evidence · impact · priority · containment action) and the alignment script with {{PATROCINADOR}}. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: Name or identifier of the project under review.
- {{LINEA_BASE_ALCANCE}}: Committed scope (deliverables, acceptance criteria, WBS, assumptions, exclusions) or whatever is available.
- {{TRABAJO_EN_CURSO}}: Actual work in execution, recent requests, and deliverables added since the last baseline.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: Hard constraints (milestone date, effort budget, team capacity). Optional.
- {{PATROCINADOR}}: Role or name of the sponsor to whom critical deviations are escalated. Optional.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-gestion-proyectos_definicion-de-listo:
Act as a senior Agile Delivery Lead and facilitator of team quality agreements, with mastery of Scrum, acceptance criteria, and scope management. I need you to build an actionable and verifiable Definition of Done (DoD) for {{TIPO_ENTREGABLE}}, fitting within {{MARCO_TRABAJO}}, starting from {{MADUREZ_EQUIPO}}, and directly targeting {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}.

Before writing, distinguish three concepts to avoid the most common confusion: Definition of Done (applicable across every increment), acceptance criteria (specific to each story), and Definition of Ready (entry condition for work); explain what belongs to each and where the boundaries are drawn.

Then draft the DoD organized by verifiable categories, prioritizing {{DIMENSIONES}}: code and review, testing (unit, integration, regression), quality and security, documentation, deployment and observability, and business acceptance. For each criterion define three things: binary statement (passes / does not pass), concrete verification method (command, pipeline, checklist, review), and the role that confirms it. Prohibit vague adjectives such as "adequate," "sufficient," or "reasonable": if a criterion cannot be observed, it is rewritten or discarded.

If complexity warrants it, tier the DoD by level (story, sprint, increment/release) indicating what is added at each level. Define governance: who approves changes, how often it is reviewed, and where the document lives. Close with anti-patterns to avoid (aspirational DoD that cannot be met, unmeasurable criteria, confusing DoD with acceptance criteria, silent exceptions) and, for each one, a countermeasure.

Rules: derive criteria backward from {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}; every criterion must be achievable on every increment, not aspirational. Mark as [SUPUESTO] any data you assume and ask for it if it blocks the design. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide standards or prior context. Deliver the document with a criteria table by category (statement / verification / owner), levels section, and governance block, ready to adopt as a team agreement.

Variables: {{TIPO_ENTREGABLE}}, {{MARCO_TRABAJO}}, {{MADUREZ_EQUIPO}}, {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}, {{DIMENSIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_criterios-aceptacio:
Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, specialist in scope management and formal deliverable verification, with experience translating vague client expectations into auditable acceptance conditions. Draft the acceptance criteria for {{ENTREGABLE}} within {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}: the set of objective and binary conditions that {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}} will use to formally accept it and close that portion of the scope. Good criteria unlock the milestone without friction, shield against scope creep, and eliminate the ambiguity that generates claims, rework, and payment disputes.

Use {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}} as the compliance basis and {{PLAZO_REVISION}} as the review window. If {{ENTREGABLE}}, {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, or the milestone the acceptance unlocks are unclear, ask for them before writing; do not invent thresholds or scope.

Deliver a document with: (1) header with deliverable, approver, milestone, and reference standard; (2) between 6 and 12 numbered criteria, each binary passes/does not pass, with a measurable verb and a concrete threshold or evidence, with no subjective adjectives (translate 'fast' to a time, 'intuitive' to an observable test); (3) functional / quality / documentary classification per criterion; (4) verification method per criterion (inspection, demonstration, test, or document analysis) and observable evidence; (5) "Out of scope for this deliverable" exclusion section; (6) acceptance procedure with reviewer, timeline {{PLAZO_REVISION}}, handling of partial rejections, and signature record. Present the criteria as a table (number, description, type, verification method, evidence, pass threshold/criterion). Mark each threshold or assumption not derived from {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}} as [assumption to be confirmed]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs. If two criteria overlap, merge them; if one is not binary or cannot be independently verified, rewrite it.

Variables: {{ENTREGABLE}}, {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}}, {{PLAZO_REVISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_acta-aceptacion-for: Act as a senior PMP-certified Project Manager, specialist in scope management and formal deliverable closure, with expertise in change control and criterion-evidence traceability. Draft a formal acceptance record ready for signature that closes the scope of {{ENTREGABLE}} from project {{PROYECTO}}, leaving an auditable record that it meets the agreed criteria and has been accepted by {{ACEPTANTE}}. A well-constructed record unlocks the associated milestone or payment, initiates the warranty, transfers responsibility or operations, and protects against claims about what has already been accepted. Structure the record in seven sections: (1) Header: {{PROYECTO}}, identifier and version of {{ENTREGABLE}}, phase or milestone, acceptance date, and reference to {{REFERENCIA_CONTRACTUAL}}. (2) Purpose: what deliverable is being accepted and under what documentary scope. (3) Verification matrix: one row per criterion from {{CRITERIOS_ACEPTACION}}, with columns criterion | expected result | compliance evidence (from {{EVIDENCIA}}) | verdict (Meets / Meets with observation / Does not meet). (4) Observations and residual pending items: a numbered list of minor findings conditionally accepted, each with an owner, commitment, and remediation deadline; declare that they do not block acceptance. (5) Acceptance scope and exclusions: what is accepted and what this record does NOT cover. (6) Effects: warranty start, transfer of responsibility or operations, and trigger for the next milestone. (7) Signature block: delivery and acceptance ({{ACEPTANTE}}), with name, role, date, and space for acknowledgment. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as referenced annexes. Verify criterion by criterion, cross-referencing each against its evidence: rigorously distinguish full acceptance, acceptance with observations, and rejection; if a criterion lacks verifiable evidence or is not met, mark it Does not meet and do NOT treat it as accepted. Decide on closure: all met → full acceptance; minor observations → conditional acceptance with dated commitments; unmet criteria → recommend rejection and remediation path. Do not invent criteria or evidence; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before drafting. Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Edge cases: partial or expired evidence is treated as an observation, not as compliance; an ambiguous criterion is interpreted literally and flagged; an unapproved scope change is excluded and redirected to change control. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_priorizacion-moscow: Act as a senior Project Manager specialized in scope management, with expertise in MoSCoW (DSDM) and PMBOK scope planning. I need a MoSCoW prioritization of {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} for {{PROYECTO}} against the milestone {{HITO_FECHA}} that cannot move, with per-requirement justification and a scope health verdict. Context: the dominant constraint is {{RESTRICCION}} and the available capacity through the milestone is {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. First, confirm the objective of {{PROYECTO}}, the date {{HITO_FECHA}}, and {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; if a critical piece of data for classification is missing, ask for it before continuing and do not invent figures. Then evaluate each requirement from {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} on two axes (impact on the milestone and consequence of not delivering it) and assign it exactly one category using strict criteria: MUST if without it {{HITO_FECHA}} fails or something legal, contractual, or security-related is violated (non-negotiable); SHOULD if it is important and painful to omit but a temporary alternative or workaround exists; COULD if it is desirable, the first to be sacrificed when {{RESTRICCION}} tightens; WON'T (this time) if it is out of this cycle, registered to prevent reopening the debate. Estimate the effort proportion per category against {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} and apply the health rule: MUST items should not exceed 60 percent of the effort; if they do, alert and propose what to downgrade and why. Handle three edge cases: requirements tied to an external dependency outside the team's control (flag them and make their category conditional), requirements that are MUST only due to political pressure without a real milestone failure (re-categorize them and explain), and requirements too large that should be split so only the indispensable part is MUST. Deliver a table with columns requirement, category, justification linked to {{HITO_FECHA}}, assumption, and impacted party; below it, the effort breakdown by category with the 60-percent rule verdict, the WON'T list as an explicit agreement, and the decisions requiring sponsor confirmation. Mark with [SUPUESTO] every piece of data that is not confirmed. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_lista-actividades-c:
Act as a senior schedule planner with expertise in the PMBOK guide and WBS decomposition technique. Your assignment is to produce the schedule activity list for {{PROYECTO}}: the unit of work against which durations are later estimated, dependencies sequenced, and the critical path built. Do not include durations or dates; the list is the input prior to estimation.

First, restate in your own words the scope you are about to decompose and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{EDT_O_ALCANCE}}, {{ENTREGABLES}}, {{GRANULARIDAD}}, or {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} are missing or insufficient, ask for them before continuing rather than inventing them.

Proceed as follows: (1) read {{EDT_O_ALCANCE}} and {{ENTREGABLES}} and identify each lowest-level work package; (2) decompose each package into activities named with an infinitive verb (design, configure, validate) that represent work, not deliverables, respecting {{GRANULARIDAD}}; (3) assign each activity a unique hierarchical identifier linked to its WBS package code (e.g. 1.3.2-A10); (4) document the attributes of each activity: scope description, assumptions, owner or role from {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}}, predecessors with their logical relationship type (FS, SS, FF, SF), and associated milestone; (5) define zero-duration milestones in a separate milestone list, covering start, phase end, approvals, and external dependencies; (6) verify the 100-percent rule: the activities cover the entire package and nothing outside it.

Mark with [SUPUESTO] every piece of data you fill in on your own and list ambiguous sequences separately as items pending confirmation. Flag external dependencies or third-party deliverables that are outside the team's control. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver: an activity table (ID, WBS package, name, description, owner or role, predecessors plus relationship type, milestone), the milestone list, and a final block of assumptions and sequences pending confirmation.
pr-gestion-proyectos_estimacion-duracion:
Act as a senior project planner (PMP) specialized in estimation under uncertainty. From {{ACTIVIDADES}} (each with O, M, and P) in a homogeneous {{UNIDAD_TIEMPO}}, produce a complete three-point estimation with a probabilistic schedule. Consider {{CAMINO_CRITICO}}, {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}}, and {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} if available. If any required data is missing, ask for it before calculating and do not invent values.

First, restate what you understand (how many activities, what unit, what optional data you have) and present your calculation plan. Then validate each activity from {{ACTIVIDADES}}: flag inconsistencies such as O greater than M, M greater than P, negative values, or units different from {{UNIDAD_TIEMPO}}, and do not calculate on broken data. Per activity, calculate TE = (O + 4M + P) / 6, σ = (P − O) / 6, and σ² = σ squared, under the beta-PERT distribution assumption. Build the table Activity | O | M | P | TE | σ | σ² and flag those with the largest σ as the highest schedule risk.

If {{CAMINO_CRITICO}} is available: sum the TE values of those activities (expected project duration), sum their variances, and calculate the project σ as the square root of the sum of variances, never as the sum of σ values. If {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} is available: calculate Z = ({{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} − total TE) / project σ and translate it into an approximate probability of meeting the date. Recommend a contingency reserve for {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} (default near 95 percent, factor 1.645): reserve = total TE + factor × project σ, indicating the buffer over the expected duration. Close with [SUPUESTO] assumptions, key operations shown so they are auditable, and two method limits: PERT assumes independence between activities, and the critical path formula ignores near-critical paths that may dominate the actual duration.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_calculo-ruta-critic:
Act as a senior project planner with PMP certification, expert in schedule programming and the Critical Path Method (CPM). I need to identify which activities cannot be delayed without delaying the entire project, how much float each one has, and what the committable delivery date is.

Data:
- Activities, durations, and predecessors: {{ACTIVIDADES}}
- Default dependency type: {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}} (optional; default Finish-to-Start)
- Date convention: {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}} (optional; default day 1)
- Duration unit: {{UNIDAD_DURACION}} (optional; default days)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the network from {{ACTIVIDADES}} as you understand it and declare {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}}, {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}}, and {{UNIDAD_DURACION}} you will assume; present your calculation plan; only then execute. Do not invent durations or dependencies: if a data point is missing, there is ambiguity, or you detect a circular dependency or orphan activity, flag it and ask before calculating.

Proceed as follows: (1) Rebuild the network in an activity-duration-predecessors table from {{ACTIVIDADES}}, applying {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}} unless an activity specifies a different relationship. (2) Forward pass: ES and EF, where EF = ES + duration - 1 and ES = maximum EF of predecessors + 1; the initial activity starts on the base day from {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}}. (3) Backward pass from total duration: LS and LF, where LS = LF - duration + 1 and LF = minimum LS of successors - 1; final activities take LF = total duration. (4) Total Float = LS - ES = LF - EF. (5) Free Float = (minimum ES of successors - 1) - EF; for final activities use total duration. (6) Identify the critical path(s) with zero total float and report the total duration.

Deliverable: complete CPM table + list of critical activities + critical path(s) in sequence + total duration + float note indicating rescheduling margin. Declare each assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Report all critical paths if there are multiple. Neutral, professional English.
pr-gestion-proyectos_compresion-crashing:
Act as a senior Project Director (PMP) specializing in schedule planning and control, with hands-on experience in network analysis (CPM), crashing, and fast-tracking on real projects with finite resources.

Project: {{PROYECTO}} (name, brief scope, reason for compression, and current baseline end date).
Schedule network: {{RED_CRONOGRAMA}} (activities with duration, FS/SS/FF/SF dependencies and lag/lead; indicate duration unit).
Compression data: {{DATOS_COMPRESION}} (per compressible activity: normal duration, minimum accelerated duration, and normal vs. accelerated cost in effort units).
Target date: {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} (date or target reduction and whether it is desirable or non-negotiable).
Risk tolerance: {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (conservative / moderate / aggressive + hard constraints).
Compression budget: {{PRESUPUESTO_COMPRESION}} (additional effort cap and actual resource availability).

Produce five numbered deliverables: (1) critical path table with duration, total float, critical path flag, and compression candidacy, declaring method and baseline end date; (2) crashing table with cost slope = (accelerated cost − normal cost) / (normal duration − accelerated duration), maximum compressible days, sorted from lowest to highest slope, with cumulative days gained and effort, compressing only critical path; (3) fast-tracking table with overlappable pairs, proposed overlap, days gained, and named incremental risk, filtered by {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}; (4) compression sequence up to {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} reverifying the critical path after each step, declaring parallel critical paths and marking the cost/risk threshold; (5) net impact with final duration, total incremental effort, consumption against {{PRESUPUESTO_COMPRESION}}, risk change, and a GO / conditional / NO-GO recommendation with conditions.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Effort always in relative units (FTE-day, hours, slope index), never monetary amounts. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every estimate not provided and do not invent accelerated durations. If {{RED_CRONOGRAMA}} or {{DATOS_COMPRESION}} are incomplete, ask for the data before calculating.
pr-gestion-proyectos_linea-base-cronogra: Act as a PMP Project Director specializing in planning and control through the Critical Path Method (CPM) and PERT estimation, responsible for auditable baselines. Your mission is to freeze the schedule baseline of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: a stable, immutable benchmark against which progress and delays are measured via earned value, subjecting every future change to formal control and converting the schedule from a vague promise into a verifiable hypothesis. Before executing, restate what you understand about the scope and present your plan; if {{EDT_WBS}}, {{CALENDARIO_LABORAL}}, or {{FECHA_LIMITE}} are missing or incomplete, ask for them before continuing rather than inventing them. Adapt the method to {{TIPO_PROYECTO}} (Waterfall: CPM with phase gates; Agile/SAFe: milestones by sprint or PI cadence over successive waves; Kanban: cycle-time-based forecast instead of a fixed baseline; Hybrid: macro milestones with internal cadence). Proceed as follows: (1) derive activities from each terminal work package of {{EDT_WBS}}, ensuring every leaf generates at least one activity and no activity spans two packages; (2) sequence with typed dependencies (FS, SS, FF, SF), each classified as mandatory, discretionary, or external, with every lead or lag justified; (3) estimate durations at three points (O, M, P) and calculate tE=(O+4M+P)/6 and σ=(P-O)/6 per activity, respecting the working days, holidays, and blackouts of {{CALENDARIO_LABORAL}}; flag high-variance activities ((P-O)/M greater than 1.5) as risk hotspots; (4) run the forward pass (ES/EF) and backward pass (LS/LF), identify the critical path (total float zero) and the minimum duration; (5) calculate total and free float for non-critical activities and flag near-critical paths (float less than 5 working days); (6) define at least 5 milestones with target dates and type; (7) generate a Gantt in Mermaid with phases, activities, dependencies, and milestones, highlighting the critical path; (8) formalize the freeze (approval date, version, approver, change-control mechanism) and declare the baseline as the measurement benchmark for SV/SPI; (9) if the critical path exceeds {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, present compression options (fast-tracking and crashing) quantifying cost, risk, and days recovered for each. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Label every assertion with [PLAN], [SCHEDULE], [INFERENCIA], or [SUPUESTO]; unconfirmed data goes as [SUPUESTO] with its buffer. Deliver a document in neutral, professional English with a dependency register, PERT table, CPM table, Gantt in Mermaid, milestone register, versioned freeze document, and, if applicable, compression analysis.
pr-gestion-proyectos_programacion-cadena:
Act as a senior project planner expert in Critical Chain (CCPM) and Theory of Constraints, with hands-on experience applying Goldratt's method in multi-tasking environments with shared resources. Your task: transform the schedule of {{PROYECTO}} into a Critical Chain plan with sized buffers and buffer-consumption control.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the scope, activities, shared resources, and chosen criteria; declare your assumptions as [SUPUESTO] and present your plan; only then execute.

First validate {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}: each activity must include an estimated duration, predecessors (dependencies), and an assigned resource. If any of the three is missing for any activity, ask for it specifically before continuing — do not invent it. If the dependency network has cycles or dangling activities, flag them and stop.

Then execute in six steps:
1. Trim each estimate to an aggressive but achievable duration according to {{CRITERIO_RECORTE}} (by default, median near 50% of the original). Record in a table the original duration, the aggressive duration, and the buffer removed per task. The buffer does not disappear: it is relocated into shared buffers.
2. Identify the critical chain: the longest dependency-constrained sequence adjusted for {{RECURSOS_COMPARTIDOS}} contention (if not specified, infer them from {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}), not the classic critical path. When the same resource appears in two parallel tasks, resolve the conflict by sequencing and explain the criterion used.
3. Size a project buffer at the end of the critical chain and a feeding buffer at each convergence of a non-critical chain to the critical chain, via {{METODO_BUFFER}} (by default SSQ = square root of the sum of the squares of the removed buffers); show the 50% cut-and-paste as a contrast.
4. Schedule the staggered start of feeding chains so they finish just before their convergence point (plus buffer), avoiding harmful multi-tasking on shared resources.
5. Calculate the protected finish date = critical chain length + project buffer, and the start dates for each chain.
6. Define buffer-consumption control with a three-zone fever chart (green: observe; yellow: plan recovery; red: execute recovery) and numerical thresholds based on % of chain completed vs. % of buffer consumed.

Rules: mark unconfirmed items as [SUPUESTO]; distinguish critical chain from critical path; no prices or monetary costs; respect the time unit of the inputs. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.

Final deliverable: activity table (original/aggressive/buffer), critical chain marked with resource rationale, buffers (project and feeding: method + size), staggered-start schedule and protected finish date, and buffer-consumption management guide with three-zone thresholds.

Variables:
- {{PROYECTO}}: name and objective of the project to be planned.
- {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}: activities with duration, predecessors, and resource.
- {{CRITERIO_RECORTE}}: rule for converting safe to aggressive duration (median ~50% or a fixed %).
- {{RECURSOS_COMPARTIDOS}}: resources appearing in multiple tasks with contention risk.
- {{METODO_BUFFER}}: SSQ or 50% cut-and-paste.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or "No attachments".

If any essential data is missing, ask for it before starting.
pr-gestion-proyectos_planificacion-olas-: Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager specializing in adaptive planning and progressive elaboration (PMBOK Rolling Wave). I need a rolling-wave plan for {{PROYECTO}}, ready to execute, avoiding false precision and rework over the long term. The project is currently in {{FASE_ACTUAL}}; we will detail a window of {{VENTANA_DETALLE}} over a total horizon of {{HORIZONTE_TOTAL}}, with this available team: {{EQUIPO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before planning, restate in one or two lines what you understood (project, phase, window, horizon) and present your plan of attack; then proceed. If {{PROYECTO}}, {{FASE_ACTUAL}}, {{VENTANA_DETALLE}}, or {{EQUIPO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Produce: (1) Framing: cut-off point between detail and coarse, justified by uncertainty and scope stability, not by fiscal calendar. (2) The near-term wave ({{VENTANA_DETALLE}}) in work packages: deliverable, named owner from {{EQUIPO}}, dependencies, duration, and verifiable milestone with a binary acceptance criterion. (3) The rest of {{HORIZONTE_TOTAL}} as coarse planning packages, undecomposed, each with an approximate scope, explicit assumptions, effort band (optimistic–pessimistic, no hard dates), and the condition that triggers its detailing. (4) Wave governance: re-planning triggers and refinement cadence that converts each planning package into detailed packages as it enters the near horizon. (5) Wave risks and pending information blocking the long horizon, with owner and target date. Mark unconfirmed estimates as [SUPUESTO] and missing data as {por_confirmar}; never decompose the long horizon into fine tasks; do not invent hard dates for bands; separate internal from external dependencies. Deliver tables (one per wave/horizon) plus a trigger list, ready for the scheduling tool.
pr-gestion-proyectos_simulacion-montecar:
Act as a senior schedule planner (PMP/PMI-SP) expert in quantitative schedule risk analysis per the PMBOK Guide and the Practice Standard for Scheduling. Your task is to produce a Monte Carlo simulation report for the schedule of {{PROYECTO}} and a data-defensible commitment recommendation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Work as follows. First validate {{RED_ACTIVIDADES}}: each activity must have consistent predecessors, a declared relationship (FS/SS/FF/SF), leads/lags if applicable, and a three-point estimate with O <= M <= P. Report inconsistencies, dangling dependencies, activities without successors, and cycles before simulating; if you detect a cycle, stop and ask me to fix the network because CPM does not converge on a cyclic graph. If critical data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it; mark every assumed value as an explicit assumption.

Then configure the simulation with {{DISTRIBUCION}} (PERT-Beta by default: mean = (O+4M+P)/6, deviation = (P-O)/6; triangular if I specify) and {{ITERACIONES}} (10,000 by default), and anchor the calendar on {{FECHA_INICIO}} respecting the working calendar; declare whether you assume 5 or 7 days per week and which holidays. Model correlation between activities only if I provide a basis; otherwise assume independence and say so, warning that this tends to underestimate the high tail due to the path-convergence effect (merge bias).

In each iteration: sample one duration per activity, propagate dependencies with a CPM forward pass, record the finish date and which activities were on the critical path for that run. Build the finish-date distribution (text histogram plus mean, median, deviation, minimum, and maximum), calculate the P50, P80, and P90 percentiles with their calendar dates, and if I provide {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} calculate the probability of meeting it. Derive the recommended contingency reserve as P80 minus P50 in days, and the criticality index for each activity as the percentage of iterations on the critical path. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute the network, calendar, or estimates.

Deliver a report with: flagged assumptions, text histogram, percentile table with dates, compliance probability, contingency reserve with its interpretation, criticality-index table sorted from highest to lowest, and a one-sentence data-defensible commitment recommendation to the sponsor. Close by identifying which activity to attack first to shift the curve and warning that the figures depend on the quality of the input estimates.
pr-gestion-proyectos_analisis-holgura-fl: Act as a senior project planner (PMP, mastery of the Critical Path Method and precedence-diagramming networks). I am managing the schedule of {{PROYECTO}} and need an interpreted float analysis — with CPM rigor — that tells me where to focus attention and how much real margin I have to absorb delays without moving the finish date, in order to enable {{OBJETIVO}}. Before calculating, restate what you understand about {{ACTIVIDADES_DEPENDENCIAS}} and the decision to be enabled, and present your plan. Inputs: network in {{ACTIVIDADES_DEPENDENCIAS}} (activities with duration and precedences with their type), values and constraints in {{DATOS_RED}} (available ES/EF/LS/LF, target finish date, working calendar; note what is missing), near-critical threshold in {{UMBRAL_CASI_CRITICA}} (if not provided, propose and justify one), and {{ADJUNTOS}}. If a data point essential for the network passes is missing, ask for it rather than assuming it; if an assumption is unavoidable, mark it [SUPUESTO] and explain its impact. Proceed as follows: 1) reconstruct or validate the network logic and calculate or confirm ES, EF, LS, and LF via forward and backward passes, declaring the date convention used; 2) TF = LS minus ES (equivalent to LF minus EF); 3) FF = (earliest ES of successors) minus EF, and for activities with no successors, relative to the finish date; 4) identify the critical path (TF = 0, or the project minimum if negative float exists) and near-critical paths per {{UMBRAL_CASI_CRITICA}}; 5) distinguish total float (shared margin) from free float (private margin) and translate each into a decision; 6) prioritize by ascending TF, flagging propagation to the finish date versus local absorption; 7) issue recommendations for {{OBJETIVO}}: what to monitor, where to reallocate resources without penalty, where to apply reserves, fast-tracking, or crashing and at what risk cost. Handle edge cases: negative float, lead/lag, hard date constraints, multiple successors, and parallel paths that share float. Deliver one table per activity with ES, EF, LS, LF, TF, and FF with the formula shown; a critical/near-critical/with-float interpretation; and a prioritized attention and delay-response block. Do not invent missing data or assume that all float is free to consume.
pr-gestion-proyectos_estimacion-analoga-:
Act as a senior project manager and certified cost estimator, expert in the analogous and parametric cost-estimating techniques of the PMBOK. I need a defensible internal cost for {{PROYECTO_NUEVO}} before committing to a budget baseline. A single technique is fragile: analogous estimation brings historical realism but carries context bias, and parametric estimation brings scalability but depends on the quality of the unit rate; triangulating and reconciling both produces an estimate with an explicit range and confidence level.

First restate what you understand of the scope of {{PROYECTO_NUEVO}}, fix {{UNIDAD_MEDIDA}} as the cost driver, validate that {{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}} is measurable, and present your plan before executing. If {{PROYECTOS_REFERENCIA}}, {{TASA_UNITARIA}}, or {{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}} are missing, stop and ask for them rather than inventing them.

Then deliver: (1) analogous method with a table contrasting {{PROYECTOS_REFERENCIA}} against the new project in size, complexity, and context, applying {{FACTORES_AJUSTE}} explicitly with their rationale, through to a derived adjusted analogous cost; (2) parametric method with {{TASA_UNITARIA}}, its source, and the traceable calculation of rate times {{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}}; (3) a reconciliation that, if the difference between both costs exceeds 15 percent, explains the gap and justifies the chosen central value and its weighting; (4) the result as an optimistic / most likely / pessimistic range, with {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} declared and a recommended contingency reserve as a percentage with its calculation basis; (5) an assumption log and the cost drivers that move the cost the most.

Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO] and each inherited data point with its source; do not invent figures. This is an internal effort and cost estimate, never a sale price or commercial commitment. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a report with the analogous table, parametric table, reconciliation, and range with contingency, ready to support the cost baseline.
pr-gestion-proyectos_linea-base-costos-c:
Act as a senior project manager specializing in cost management, with experience in Earned Value Management and building authorized baselines. I need the cost baseline (cumulative cost S-curve) for {{PROYECTO}}: the control reference against which I will measure actual performance with earned value (EV vs PV), variances (CV, SV), and projections (EAC). Without this curve there is no objective threshold for determining whether the project is within or over budget.

Inputs: schedule {{CRONOGRAMA}}, WBS estimates {{ESTIMACIONES_EDT}}, unit/range of periods {{CALENDARIO_PERIODOS}}, criterion for time-phasing spending {{PERFIL_GASTO}}, management reserve {{RESERVA_GESTION}}, contingency reserve {{RESERVA_CONTINGENCIA}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Proceed as follows: (1) Restate the scope, WBS, and time horizon you understand; list missing data and ask for it before proceeding. (2) Aggregate the bottom-up estimates: work packages -> control accounts -> project total, obtaining the baseline before the management reserve. (3) Distribute each control account over {{CALENDARIO_PERIODOS}} using its {{PERFIL_GASTO}} (linear, by milestones, weighted by expected progress, or front-loaded/back-loaded curve); never equally by default without justifying it. (4) Calculate cost per period, cumulative cost, and % of BAC; identify the BAC as the last point of the curve. (5) Separate {{RESERVA_CONTINGENCIA}} (inside the baseline, identified risks) from {{RESERVA_GESTION}} (outside the baseline, inside the total budget, unknown-unknowns). (6) Define control thresholds and the measurement cadence.

Limits: do not invent figures; mark every assumed data point as [SUPUESTO] or leave it parameterized. Verify the aggregation reconciliation (sum of costs per period = BAC) and that the cumulative curve is monotonically increasing with an S-shape. If {{CRONOGRAMA}} lacks dates, state that phasing is blocked and propose a tentative horizon marked as an assumption. Deliver: period-by-period table (period, cost of the period, cumulative cost, % of BAC), S-curve narrative with slope segments, threshold block, and reserves note. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before producing figures.
pr-gestion-proyectos_reservas-contingenc: Act as a senior project manager and specialist in quantitative cost management (PMBOK 7, reserve analysis, expected monetary value). Size the reserves and governance of use for project {{PROYECTO}}, with a base cost without reserves of {{COSTO_BASE}} in {{MONEDA}}, based on the risk register {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}, the risk appetite {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, and the authorization levels {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before calculating, restate the assignment and present your plan; if {{COSTO_BASE}} or {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} are missing, stop and request them (mandatory). Mark as [SUPUESTO] anything you infer from {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}}, or {{MONEDA}} when not provided. Proceed: 1) Bottom-up contingency: for each quantified risk, expected monetary value = probability times cost impact; sum the total showing the calculation per risk. If {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} is only qualitative, also add a top-down value as a percentage of {{COSTO_BASE}} and explain the divergence, recommending a method. 2) Management reserve as a percentage of base cost plus contingency, justified by {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, novelty, and uncertainty; never a loose figure. 3) Layered budget: activities, control accounts, baseline (with contingency), total budget (with management reserve), traceable arithmetic. 4) Governance per reserve: authorizes per {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}} (default: project manager for contingency, sponsor for management reserve), required evidence, log of each consumption, replenishment or escalation threshold, and review cadence. 5) Release of unconsumed balance and link to the cost performance index and cost variance. Verify arithmetic, separation of contingency (inside the baseline) from management reserve (outside the baseline), and traceability. No prices or rates: project monetary units only. Deliver: sizing table, layered budget, and governance protocol for the committee.
pr-gestion-proyectos_seguimiento-presupu:
Act as a senior Project Controls Manager, PMP-certified with mastery of Earned Value Management (EVM) and expert in cost control against a baseline. Convert the cost record of {{PROYECTO}} into a financial health control report as of {{FECHA_CORTE}}, separating committed costs from what has actually been executed and enabling early decisions on reallocation, cuts, or funding requests.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand of {{PROYECTO}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}; present your calculation plan; only then execute. If {{REGISTRO_COSTOS}} is missing the baseline, committed, or actual per line item, or if {{AVANCE_FISICO}} is missing when EVM is required, ask for it before calculating: do not invent figures and mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO]. Work in {{MONEDA}} without conversion.

Deliver:
1. Control table by line item or work package with columns: baseline, committed (firm, not accrued), actual (accrued), and available (= baseline - committed - actual); the sum of available must reconcile.
2. Deviation panel: absolute and percentage deviation of actual vs. baseline and (committed + actual) vs. baseline, with a traffic light per line item based on {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}.
3. EVM block if {{AVANCE_FISICO}} is available: PV, EV, AC, CV = EV - AC, SV = EV - PV, CPI = EV/AC, SPI = EV/PV, EAC = BAC/CPI, ETC = EAC - AC, and VAC = BAC - EAC, at project level and by relevant package; if not, state it and deliver only budget control.
4. Root cause diagnosis for each material deviation, classified as: price variance, volume variance, unbudgeted scope, or accounting reclassification.
5. Close-out projection with overrun risk and confidence level (high/medium/low) based on data quality and progress maturity.
6. Three to five corrective actions prioritized by impact, each with a suggested owner and escalation trigger to the change committee.

Limits: distinguish committed (firm, not accrued) from actual (accrued); do not mix contingency with the baseline unless instructed; flag line items with no movement and underreporting risk.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: project name and phase or period under cost control
- {{REGISTRO_COSTOS}}: cost record by line item/package with baseline, committed, and actual accrued
- {{FECHA_CORTE}}: tracking cut-off date (data date)
- {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}: deviation threshold for traffic light (e.g. green <=5%, amber 5-10%, red >10%)
- {{MONEDA}}: project currency and units, without conversion
- {{AVANCE_FISICO}}: physical progress percentage by line item for earned value (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-gestion-proyectos_business-case-refre: Act as a senior Project Manager with expertise in project value management (PMBOK) and investment financial analysis (ROI, payback, NPV). The business case that approved {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} no longer reflects reality: actual spend, timelines, and captured benefits differ from the original plan, and before the next committee the decision must be made whether the investment is still justified. Rebuild the case with real data and deliver a document ready to present. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate what you understand about the status of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and present your plan before calculating. (2) Consolidate {{CASO_ORIGINAL}}, {{DATOS_REALES}}, and {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}}; if any datum from {{CASO_ORIGINAL}}, {{DATOS_REALES}}, {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} is missing, ask me before calculating — do not invent values. (3) Recalculate with real figures: ROI = total net benefit / total investment; payback based on actual cumulative cash flow; NPV discounting remaining flows at {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} over {{HORIZONTE}}; show the formula and the numbers used for each metric.
