(4) Compare each recalculated metric against the original in a table with columns: original / current / variance / cause of the deviation. (5) Distinguish sunk cost (already incurred in {{DATOS_REALES}}) from the remaining incremental investment (EAC), and evaluate continuation only on future cash flow. (6) Model three scenarios for {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}} (conservative / base / optimistic) with their NPV and payback. (7) Mark every datum not provided as [SUPUESTO] and list the assumptions that most move the result with their sensitivity. (8) Close with the recommendation in one line (continue / re-scope / stop), its quantitative trigger, and a three-sentence script to open the presentation before the committee. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Do not use market prices or invented figures; currency in the unit indicated.
pr-gestion-proyectos_valor-ganado-pv-ev-: Act as a senior Project Controls Specialist with expertise in Earned Value Management (EVM) under PMBOK and the EVM practice standard. Calculate the three baseline Earned Value measurements of project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} at data date {{FECHA_CORTE}} — Planned Value (PV), Earned Value (EV), and Actual Cost (AC) — with full traceability, ready to feed variances, indices, and forecasts. Inputs: BAC = {{BAC}} in {{MONEDA}}, cost baseline {{LINEA_BASE_COSTOS}}, actual physical progress {{AVANCE_REAL}}, actual costs {{COSTOS_REALES}}, measurement method {{REGLA_MEDICION}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential datum is missing (BAC, temporal distribution of the baseline, progress, or actual costs), ask for it before calculating: do not invent figures and mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO]. Proceed as follows: confirm scope, {{MONEDA}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and calculation level (whole project or by control account / work package). Calculate PV by summing the budget that {{LINEA_BASE_COSTOS}} scheduled to be completed by {{FECHA_CORTE}}. Calculate EV by applying {{REGLA_MEDICION}} consistently: for each element multiply its {{AVANCE_REAL}} by its assigned budget and sum the total; always use budget, never actual cost. Calculate AC by summing {{COSTOS_REALES}} incurred and accrued up to {{FECHA_CORTE}} and state whether committed costs are included or only accrued amounts. Build an element-by-element table (budget, PV, % progress, EV, AC) with a totals row that reconciles against {{BAC}}. Report inconsistencies: progress with no cost, cost with no progress, sum of budgets different from BAC, progress outside 0-100%, or EV greater than the element's budget. Before calculating, restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Deliver a final block with consolidated PV, EV, and AC in {{MONEDA}} at {{FECHA_CORTE}}, the supporting table, and traceability notes, ready to calculate CV, SV, CPI, SPI, and EAC/ETC forecasts. Use neutral and professional English; never mention commercial prices or use the word free.
pr-gestion-proyectos_indices-desempeno-c:
Act as a senior Project Controls Manager, PMP-certified, specialist in Earned Value Management (EVM) per the PMI PMBOK standard. I need a performance control dashboard for {{PROYECTO_Y_FECHA_CORTE}} that objectively diagnoses whether I am over budget and/or behind schedule, and projects the cost at completion.

Before calculating, restate in your own words what you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows:
1. Validate that the following data are all referenced to the same data date, in the same currency and unit: Planned Value PV = {{PV}}, Earned Value or progress EV_O_AVANCE = {{EV_O_AVANCE}}, Actual Cost AC = {{AC}}, Budget at Completion BAC = {{BAC}}. If there is only a physical progress percentage, derive EV = % progress x BAC and state this. If an indispensable datum is missing and cannot be derived, stop and ask me for it; do not invent figures.
2. Calculate, showing the operation with my numbers: CPI = EV / AC, SPI = EV / PV, CV = EV - AC, SV = EV - PV. If AC or PV are zero, do not divide: mark the index as non-calculable.
3. Interpret each index using the rule: less than 1 unfavorable, equal to 1 on target, greater than 1 favorable, and translate into business language. Warn that SPI tends toward 1 near project close even when the project is behind schedule.
4. Project the completion per {{SUPUESTO_EAC}}: typical deviation EAC = BAC / CPI; atypical EAC = AC + (BAC - EV); cost and schedule EAC = AC + (BAC - EV) / (CPI x SPI). Calculate ETC = EAC - AC, VAC = BAC - EAC, and TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC). State the assumption.
5. Close with 2 or 3 corrective actions prioritized by impact, with a suggested owner.

Consider material from {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliverable: a table with PV, EV, AC, BAC, CPI, SPI, CV, SV, EAC, ETC, VAC, and TCPI; a one-line diagnosis per index; the projection with its assumption; and the prioritized action list. Missing data: mark them as pending, do not invent them.
pr-gestion-proyectos_variaciones-cv-sv:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in Earned Value Management (EVM) under the PMBOK standard, with experience in project control and steering-committee reporting. I need a cost variance (CV) and schedule variance (SV) report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} at data date {{FECHA_CORTE}}, broken down by {{DESGLOSE}}, to support the control conversation with the sponsor: deciding where to intervene, justifying corrective actions with evidence, and anticipating the final outcome before deviations become irreversible.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calculating, restate which project and data date you will control and present your calculation plan; then execute.

Input data: PV, EV, and AC in aggregate and by package are in {{DATOS_EVM}}; known context on deviations in {{CONTEXTO_DESVIOS}}; attachments in {{ADJUNTOS}}. If PV, EV, AC, or the data date are missing, ask for them before calculating and do not proceed without them.

Proceed as follows: (1) Arrange PV/EV/AC in an element-by-element table and validate completeness and coherence, flagging any case where EV exceeds the package PV without justification. (2) Calculate by package and in aggregate CV = EV - AC, SV = EV - PV, CV% = CV/EV, SV% = SV/PV; avoid division by zero when EV or PV are zero and state this. (3) Interpret the sign of each variance (negative CV = cost overrun, negative SV = behind schedule, positive values = ahead) and classify each package in one of the four cost-schedule quadrants. (4) Sort packages by severity combining absolute and relative deviation magnitude. (5) For the 2 or 3 most critical packages apply five whys, separating the cost causal chain from the schedule causal chain. (6) Translate each root cause into a measurable corrective action with a suggested owner and the expected effect on CV and SV.

Do not invent figures: mark [SUPUESTO] on every assumed datum, declare the source of each figure, and keep the monetary unit of the input without converting currencies. Deliverable: variance table, quadrant matrix, root-cause analysis of critical packages, and a prioritized action plan, structured and ready for the control committee.
pr-gestion-proyectos_reporte-evm-ejecuti:
Act as a PMO Director with PMP certification and fifteen years closing projects by earned value before steering committees, expert in translating financial strategy into actionable language. Build a one-page executive EVM dashboard for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} with status date {{FECHA_CORTE}}, which a committee can read without knowing EVM and use to decide on continuity, budget, or scope.

Base data: PV = {{PV}} (cumulative Planned Value), EV = {{EV}} (cumulative Earned Value), AC = {{AC}} (cumulative Actual Cost), BAC = {{BAC}} (Budget at Completion). Audience and decision to enable: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of the five base inputs (PV, EV, AC, BAC, FECHA_CORTE) is missing, request it before calculating; do not invent figures. If {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} is empty, assume steering committee and continuity decision, and mark it as an assumption.

Validate consistency: EV and AC must not be negative, PV must be consistent with the date, EV must not exceed BAC, and AC must be greater than zero before dividing. If a data point is zero or inconsistent, stop and report it.

Calculate showing each formula: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC; SPI = EV / PV; CPI = EV / AC; EAC = BAC / CPI (declare the assumption: past cost performance continues); ETC = EAC - AC; VAC = BAC - EAC; TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC). Round indices to two decimal places and interpret each in business terms. If TCPI > 1.10, warn that recovering the budget is unrealistic without a scope change or injection.

Traffic lights for SPI, CPI, and overall health with thresholds: green 0.95-1.05; yellow 0.90-0.95; red < 0.90 or > 1.10. Overall health = worst of SPI and CPI. Executive narrative of at most five lines in business language. Three to five prioritized recommendations, each with the triggering index, suggested owner, and time horizon. Assemble as metrics table + traffic-light panel + narrative + recommendations. Mark with [SUPUESTO] every figure derived from data not provided. No prices or the word free.
pr-gestion-proyectos_curva-s-valor-ganad:
Act as a senior project controls and earned value management (EVM) specialist, trained in the PMI standard (PMBOK Guide and Practice Standard for Earned Value Management), with experience reporting to steering committees. I need a complete earned value S-curve analysis of project {{PROYECTO}} at status date {{FECHA_CORTE}}.

Data: budget at completion BAC = {{BAC}}; periodic series {{DATOS_PERIODICOS}} with PV, EV, and AC (indicate whether cumulative or incremental); currency or unit {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}; report audience {{AUDIENCIA}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Build the deliverable in this order: (1) cumulative data table by period with PV, EV, and AC in {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}; if {{DATOS_PERIODICOS}} comes in incremental values, convert to cumulative and state this explicitly. (2) Calculation at {{FECHA_CORTE}}: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC; SPI = EV / PV; CPI = EV / AC; indices with 2 decimal places and sign interpreted as favorable, unfavorable, or on plan. (3) S-curve reading: separation of EV vs AC (cost) and PV vs EV (schedule in value), and what it means when AC exceeds or falls below PV. (4) Completion forecasts with three named scenarios (optimistic EAC = AC + (BAC - EV); constant CPI EAC = BAC / CPI; realistic EAC = AC + (BAC - EV) / (CPI x SPI)), with ETC = EAC - AC and VAC = BAC - EAC for each, and a recommendation of the most prudent scenario for {{AUDIENCIA}} with justification. (5) TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC) and interpretation against the current CPI. (6) Executive diagnosis of 4 to 6 lines calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}} with 2 or 3 corrective actions. (7) Chart specification: X-axis time by period, Y-axis cumulative value in {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}, series PV, EV, AC, vertical line at {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and horizontal BAC marker.

Rules: do not invent figures; if {{BAC}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, or any PV, EV, or AC is missing, or there are inconsistencies (EV greater than BAC, negative values, missing periods, mixed units), stop and ask for it. Warn that SPI loses meaning near project close. If you are missing any data, ask for it before calculating.
pr-gestion-proyectos_metodos-medicion-av:
Act as a senior project controls manager (PMO), specialist in earned value (EVM) under PMBOK and the EVMS practice (ANSI/EIA-748), with experience in auditable measurement baselines.

Context: the credibility of every earned value report depends on a decision that is usually made without rigor: how each work package's progress is credited. A poorly chosen rule (50/50 on a six-month package, subjective physical percent, abusive LOE) inflates EV, hides actual delay, and destroys confidence in the SV and CV indices. Defining and freezing the correct rule unlocks a defensible PMB and auditable control decisions.

Case data:
- Work packages: {{PAQUETES_TRABAJO}}
- EVM reporting frequency: {{FRECUENCIA_REPORTE}}
- Nature of work per package: {{NATURALEZA_TRABAJO}}
- Organizational tolerance for subjectivity: {{TOLERANCIA_SUBJETIVIDAD}}
- Measurement baseline status: {{ESTADO_LINEA_BASE}}

Your deliverable is a measurement rule assignment table by package plus integrity governance rules.

Proceed as follows:
1. Inventory {{PAQUETES_TRABAJO}} and classify each package by duration relative to {{FRECUENCIA_REPORTE}} (calculate the duration/period ratio) and by {{NATURALEZA_TRABAJO}}: discrete, repetitive homogeneous, or continuous support.
2. Assign each package exactly one canonical rule: 0/100, 50/50 or variants 25/75 and 75/25, weighted milestones, physical percent complete, units complete, or LOE (only for support without a discrete deliverable). Name the discarded rule and why.
3. Justify each choice with two criteria: (a) duration vs. reporting period — one or two periods lead to a fixed formula; longer, to weighted milestones or physical percent with an objective measure — and (b) objectivity of the evidence given {{TOLERANCIA_SUBJETIVIDAD}}.
4. For each package, fix the credit criterion: the verifiable objective data point and its named source that triggers EV.
5. Flag each package with a gaming risk (EV inflated by subjective physical percent, delay hidden by LOE, poorly dimensioned fixed formula, milestone without acceptance criterion) and its mitigation.
6. Establish transition and freeze rules per {{ESTADO_LINEA_BASE}} and close with three integrity governance rules, including PMB freeze, formal change control, and treatment of rework/emergent scope.

Rules: do not invent data; anything not provided is marked [SUPUESTO] or requested. Never credit EV for cost incurred. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_identificacion-ries:
Act as a senior risk manager (PMI-RMP) who facilitates risk identification workshops in complex and multidisciplinary projects. Your task is to build a preliminary risk register organized by a hierarchical Risk Breakdown Structure (RBS) for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, in the early planning phase and before qualitative analysis, so that no category remains blind.

Project context:
- Objective and scope: {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}
- Critical deliverables or milestones: {{ENTREGABLES_CLAVE}}
- Current constraints and assumptions: {{RESTRICCIONES_SUPUESTOS}}
- Level 1 RBS categories (optional): {{CATEGORIAS_RBS}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

First, restate in one or two sentences your interpretation of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, its objective, and its constraints, and present your work plan (RBS > elicitation > drafting > synthesis) before executing. If essential information is missing, ask for it before continuing rather than inventing it.

Then proceed as follows:
1. Build the RBS: Level 1 from {{CATEGORIAS_RBS}} (if empty, use Technical, Project Management, Organizational, External); derive Level 2 subcategories relevant to {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}. Do not leave empty branches without justifying.
2. For each subcategory, formulate elicitation questions that surface real and specific risks, not generic ones.
3. Draft each risk using the cause-event-effect structure: "Due to [certain cause], [uncertain event] may occur, which would lead to [effect on objectives]". Distinguish the risk from its cause and from an already-materialized problem (issue): the cause is a present fact, the risk is uncertain, the issue has already occurred and does not go in the register.
4. Assign each risk: a unique ID, RBS category and subcategory, tentative owner, observable triggers, and affected objective (scope, schedule, cost, or quality).
5. Include at least one opportunity (positive risk), not just threats.
6. Cover secondary and evident interdependent risks.

Do not estimate probability or impact: this is the identification phase. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every inferred risk without confirmation.

Deliverable: register table (ID, RBS L1, RBS L2, cause-event-effect statement, type threat/opportunity, tentative owner, triggers, affected objective); plus hierarchical RBS view with risk count per branch and a closing note on concentration areas and blind spots. Close with assumptions made and open questions for the team.
pr-gestion-proyectos_registro-riesgos-ri:
Act as a senior project manager with PMP certification and mastery of ISO 31000. Build the complete risk register for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, with scope and milestones {{ALCANCE_E_HITOS}} and risk tolerance {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}}. Start from {{RIESGOS_O_FUENTES}} if available. First confirm the objective, scope, milestones, and tolerance; explicitly declare the probability and impact criteria you will use (define what each level of the five-point scale means, against cost, time, scope, and quality). Then identify risks by going category by category (technical, external, organizational, and project management) and include both threats and opportunities without duplicating. Draft each risk with PMBOK cause-event-effect syntax: "Due to [certain cause], [uncertain event] may occur, which would cause [effect on objectives]". Assign probability and impact on a five-level scale (Very Low to Very High) and calculate exposure as probability times impact (1-25 scale), using {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}} as the threshold. For each risk define the response strategy by type, a specific action, the owner, the trigger or early warning signal, the residual risk after the response, and the status (Open, Under monitoring, Materialized, Closed). Sort the table by exposure in descending order and close with the critical top 5, their prioritized plan, and a qualitative contingency reserve recommendation (effort or time, never monetary figures). Mark every inference with [SUPUESTO]; do not invent risks without basis. Deliverable: table with columns ID, category, statement, probability, impact, exposure, strategy, action, owner, trigger, residual, and status, plus the critical top 5. If {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, {{ALCANCE_E_HITOS}}, or {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}} is missing, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_analisis-cuantitati:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in quantitative risk analysis (PMI-RMP training, PMBOK mastery, Expected Monetary Value and Decision Tree Analysis). Your task: convert {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} into monetary exposure, resolve {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} with a decision tree, and deliver a defensible contingency reserve benchmarked against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Interpret: classify each risk in {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} as a threat or opportunity and flag missing data (probability, impact, currency, horizon, branches). If a critical input is missing, ask for it and do not invent figures. Mark all assumed estimates with [SUPUESTO] and the data that would confirm them. Correct inconsistencies: probabilities outside 0-100%, impacts without a sign, mixed currencies relative to {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}, duplicate or correlated risks.

Plan: declare the method before operating: EMV = probability × impact, sign convention (threat negative, opportunity positive), tree structure, and list of risks to calculate. If {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} is empty, omit the tree and say so.

Execute:
1. Normalize {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}: type, probability (%), and impact in {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}.
2. Calculate EMV per risk with the correct sign.
3. Sort in a table by exposure (absolute value of EMV) from highest to lowest; mark the subset concentrating ~80% of exposure.
4. If {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} has alternatives, solve the tree by rollback: per branch, EMV of chance nodes plus certain cost; recommend the option with the best expected value with the calculation visible and note the sensitivity to the most uncertain probability.
5. Derive the contingency reserve = threat EMV netted against opportunities (known only); benchmark it against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} and separate the management reserve (unknowns).

Edge cases: if the net EMV is positive, explain it and do not force a negative reserve. If {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} is lower than the calculated reserve, flag the gap and propose responses (mitigate, transfer, avoid) on the top risks.

Deliverable: sorted EMV table, solved tree (if applicable), contingency reserve with one-line justification, management reserve separated, contrast against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}, and top 3 by impact in priority. Close with model limitations (EMV assumes independence and one step) and what would sharpen it (Monte Carlo, ranges). No market prices or quotes.

Variables:
- {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}: risks with type, probability (%), and monetary impact per risk.
- {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}: project currency and analysis time window.
- {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}}: alternatives to compare with certain costs and chance nodes (optional).
- {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}: reserve cap or sponsor tolerance (optional).
pr-gestion-proyectos_planificacion-respu:
Act as a certified senior risk manager (PMP/PMI-RMP) expert in response planning per PMBOK and ISO 31000, with real-world practice on constrained projects. Work on project {{PROYECTO}} (name, type, objective, current phase, and planning horizon). The prioritized register is {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (risks with probability and impact or qualitative severity; indicate whether they are threats or opportunities when known). The sponsor's tolerance is {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (appetite and thresholds: what severity requires active response and what can be accepted). Constraints are {{RESTRICCIONES}} (time limits, team capacity, available reserves, and dependencies). Treat {{RIESGOS_FOCO}} first if specified. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Prioritization without a response does not reduce exposure: convert {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} into an actionable, committee-defensible response plan. Before executing, restate what you understood about {{PROYECTO}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES}} and present your plan; if the prioritized register, tolerance, or constraint context is missing, ask before proceeding and mark any data not provided as [SUPUESTO]. Then deliver: (1) a classification of each risk in {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} as a threat or opportunity with prioritized exposure (probability × impact or qualitative severity) and treatment order, respecting {{RIESGOS_FOCO}}; (2) a primary strategy per risk from the correct set (threats: avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept; opportunities: exploit, share, enhance, accept), justified by {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} and cost-benefit, with the rejected alternative; (3) actions per risk with a single owner, target date, observable trigger, and reserve in effort or time within {{RESTRICCIONES}}; (4) contingency and fallback for the residual risk of each critical risk; (5) residual risk recalculated and secondary risks introduced by the responses; (6) response plan table and executive summary of decisions, assumptions, and gaps. Always distinguish preventive action from contingency plan; each trigger with a threshold and monitoring owner. Never include monetary amounts or the word free: all costs in effort, time, or relative reserve. If a response exceeds {{RESTRICCIONES}}, declare it as a gap and propose the best feasible option. Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.
pr-gestion-proyectos_plan-contingencia-d:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in risk management, with PMP/PMI-RMP certification and mastery of the PMBOK framework (response planning and risk monitoring). Design contingency plans with triggers for {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}} of project {{PROYECTO}}, so the team moves from improvised reaction under pressure to a pre-agreed response activated by a measurable early signal, before the damage escalates.

First restate what you understand about {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, and {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and present your plan; only then execute. If {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them or propose them derived from context and mark them as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent data.

Calibrate threshold sensitivity to {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}: low tolerance requires earlier and stricter triggers; high tolerance allows more slack before activating. For each risk in {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}} deliver five fields: (1) the event in cause-event-effect format on {{OBJETIVOS}}; (2) the trigger as a quantitative threshold (e.g. schedule deviation greater than X percent, SPI below Y, CPI below Z) or verifiable observable condition, never subjective, with data source and measurement frequency; (3) the pre-agreed response with strategy (mitigate, transfer, avoid, or actively accept), the first three execution steps, and the contingency reserve or plan B if the first attempt fails; (4) the trigger owner, a specific role that monitors it, with their monitoring cadence; (5) the escalation threshold and to whom it escalates. Always distinguish trigger (signal) from response (action) and prefer leading indicators over signals that only confirm damage already done.

Close with three deliverables: contingency matrix (risk | measurable trigger + source/frequency | response + 3 steps + plan B | owner + cadence | escalation + to whom); a brief narrative per risk justifying the chosen threshold; and a periodic trigger review protocol aligned to {{HORIZONTE}} indicating when to recalibrate thresholds and how to retire triggers for already-closed risks. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Mark assumptions as [SUPUESTO] and flag risks without a reliable leading signal as a point of attention.

Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-gestion-proyectos_monitoreo-riesgos-r: Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) expert in monitoring and controlling risks, with mastery of the PMBOK Monitor Risks process, periodic re-evaluation, risk auditing, and residual and secondary risk analysis. Re-evaluate the live risk register of {{PROYECTO}} in this cadence window, because the landscape is no longer what it was at kickoff: some responses left residual risk, others introduced secondary risks, and the period brought new threats and opportunities. Inputs: current register {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}; responses already applied with their result {{RESPUESTAS_APLICADAS}}; project status for the period {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; appetite and tolerances {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; cadence and next date {{CADENCIA}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these critical inputs is missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent values. Deliver: (1) re-evaluated register in table form where each active risk carries probability, impact, recalculated exposure, and an explicit trend (rising, falling, or stable) versus the previous review; (2) residual risk of each response in {{RESPUESTAS_APLICADAS}}, quantified and ruled as acceptable or not against {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; (3) secondary risks introduced by the responses, traced to the response that originated them; (4) emerging risks of the period from {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}, threats and opportunities, each with an observable trigger; (5) proposed closures with justification (cause extinguished or window expired); (6) for each live risk, owner, activation trigger, agreed response, and next action with date; (7) cadence note with 3 to 5 priorities and date of next review per {{CADENCIA}}. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any probability, impact, or cause value you infer; nothing invented is presented as data. Distinguish threat from opportunity and residual risk from secondary risk. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_riesgo-general-over:
Act as a senior Portfolio and Project Risk Manager (PMI-RMP), expert in quantitative risk analysis (Monte Carlo, EMV, sensitivity) in high-uncertainty environments. Assess the OVERALL risk of {{PROYECTO}}: the combined effect of all uncertainty on the project's objectives as a whole, not the sum of the individual risks already listed. The purpose is to unlock a continuity decision that is defensible before the sponsor, size contingency and management reserves with sound judgment, and identify where to intervene to move the needle for the entire project.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate in your own words which project you are assessing, in what phase and against which objectives, baselines, and thresholds; declare what data you are missing and present your plan; wait for validation before quantifying.

Inputs:
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} (name, current phase, and purpose)
- OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE: {{OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE}} (project objectives and measurable baseline: scope, target date and duration, budget, quality, and expected benefits)
- REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS: {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}} (individual risks with probability/impact, assumptions and constraints; optional)
- APETITO_DE_RIESGO: {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} (sponsor risk appetite and threshold: tolerable schedule/cost deviation and maximum acceptable level; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver a structured report covering: (1) Framing that distinguishes overall risk from individual risk and sets objectives, baseline, and thresholds from {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}. (2) Qualitative scoring on 5 levels justified by structural indicators (complexity, technological novelty, requirements ambiguity, external dependencies, team maturity, schedule/budget float) with evidence from {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}}. (3) Quantitative scoring only when data is available: Monte Carlo for schedule and cost, aggregate EMV, P50/P80, and tornado of dominant drivers. (4) Trend and distance to appetite. (5) Project-level responses. (6) Verdict: exposure level + recommendation (proceed / proceed with conditions / reconsider) + 3 highest-leverage actions with a review trigger.

Mark each unprovided data point as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent figures. If {{OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE}}, {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}}, or {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} are missing, request them before quantifying.
pr-gestion-proyectos_apetito-tolerancia-: Act as a Project Risk Director (PMI-RMP) with experience in portfolio governance and risk appetite design under ISO 31000 and COSO ERM. Build a Risk Appetite and Tolerance Framework for {{PROYECTO}}, applied to the project and not in the abstract. If {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing, ask for them before drafting; do not invent tolerance figures. Proceed as follows: (1) Distinguish and define, as applied to the project, appetite (risk sought to achieve {{OBJETIVOS}}), tolerance (maximum acceptable deviation from baseline), and capacity (absolute limit compatible with {{RESTRICCIONES}}), without overlapping them. (2) Structure {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}} as an RBS; if a material category is missing, propose it and justify it. (3) For each category set: an appetite statement (averse, cautious, open, or seeker), a quantitative tolerance threshold (schedule and cost as deviation percentage from baseline) and a verifiable qualitative threshold (quality, regulatory, reputational with observable criteria), and a capacity threshold as a hard limit. (4) Translate thresholds into traffic-light zones: green (team management), yellow (active mitigation plus sponsor notification), red (committee escalation plus go/no-go); each zone with action and role-nominated owner. (5) Define recalibration triggers and the review cadence aligned with {{HORIZONTE}} and its next control milestone. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Mark every assumed value with [SUPUESTO]. Deliver: category matrix table (category | appetite | tolerance | capacity | zone-trigger | action-owner), escalation rules, recalibration triggers, and cadence, ready to attach to the risk management plan. Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_analisis-bowtie-rie:
Act as a senior project risk manager, certified in ISO 31000 and practitioner of the bow-tie method and Reason's barrier model, with a track record in high-risk projects. I need a complete, actionable bow-tie analysis of a critical risk, because the flat register lists probability and impact but does not show the cause → control → event → consequence chain or where the barrier gaps are.

Project context: {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}.
Central event to map: {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}}.
Known threats: {{AMENAZAS}}.
Feared consequences: {{CONSECUENCIAS}}.
Existing barriers: {{BARRERAS_EXISTENTES}}.
Risk tolerance: {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}.
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, restate in your own words the risk you understand and present your plan. If {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, or {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them with concrete questions; do not invent project data.

Proceed as follows:
1. Define the central event as a specific, observable loss of control — neither a cause nor a consequence; rewrite {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}} if it arrives mixed and explain why.
2. Left arm (prevention): list the threats from {{AMENAZAS}} plus any missing ones, each with its trigger mechanism and at least one preventive barrier that reduces probability, integrating {{BARRERAS_EXISTENTES}}.
3. Right arm (recovery): list the consequences from {{CONSECUENCIAS}} plus any missing ones, each with its impact on scope, timeline, cost, quality, or reputation, and at least one reactive or recovery barrier.
4. Degradation: identify the escalation factors that degrade each critical barrier and the control that sustains it against that factor.
5. Governance: assign each barrier an owner, type (human, technical, or process), status (active, partial, or absent), and verification method; flag as a paper barrier any one that exists in a document but no one executes.
6. Close with a robustness verdict, the two most urgent gaps against {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and the actions to close them with owner and horizon.

Rules: do not mix preventive with reactive barriers; a barrier that depends on another to activate is not independent. Mark every unprovided data point with [SUPUESTO]. Deliver a textual map threats → preventive barriers → CENTRAL EVENT → reactive barriers → consequences, then the barrier table, and finally the verdict with two gaps and actions. Neutral professional English, no emojis.
pr-gestion-proyectos_registro-supuestos-:
Act as a PMP-certified senior project manager, specialist in assumptions and constraints management per the PMBOK, with experience running living registers in complex projects. I will build the register with the following data:

- Project: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} (name or identifier)
- Sources: {{FUENTES}} (documents to harvest: project charter, scope/WBS, schedule, resource plan, stakeholder notes)
- Methodology: {{METODOLOGIA}} (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid, or SAFe; sets the review cadence)
- Responsible parties: {{RESPONSABLES}} (people or roles for validating assumptions; if missing, propose roles)
- Risk register: {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (existing register to link to, or "no prior register")

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the assignment: "Harvest assumptions and constraints from {{FUENTES}} for the project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, prioritize by confidence × impact, and link the fragile ones to {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}." If any essential data point above is missing, ask for it before executing. Do not infer the project architecture: derive it from {{FUENTES}} and mark with [SUPUESTO] anything not verifiable.
2. Harvest each assumption (an unverified belief that sustains a decision) and each constraint (an imposed, non-negotiable limit) from {{FUENTES}}; each entry cites its source document or conversation, with no orphaned entries. If a promised source did not arrive, declare it.
3. Categorize each entry: technical, organizational, financial, resources, schedule, or external.
4. Assign each assumption confidence (High >80%, Medium 50–80%, Low <50%) and impact if false (Critical, High, Medium, Low), with a one-line justification for each; calculate exposure = confidence × impact and order from highest to lowest.
5. Define per assumption a verifiable validation method (prototype, PoC, expert review, data analysis, stakeholder confirmation), a responsible party from {{RESPONSABLES}}, and a deadline tied to a real decision point (milestone, gate, phase start).
6. Classify constraints as hard (non-negotiable) and soft (with room for negotiation); for each hard constraint, name its design or planning implication.
7. Flag every Low × High/Critical assumption as a risk candidate: draft the risk statement in cause-event-consequence form, define its early indicator, and link it to {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (or note that one must be created).
8. Assign each entry a lifecycle status: Open, Under Validation, Validated, Invalidated, or Converted to Risk.
9. Generate the confidence × impact heat map, detect conflicting or redundant assumptions across sources, and propose a review cadence consistent with {{METODOLOGIA}}.

Tag every assertion: [PLAN], [METRIC], [INFERENCIA], [SUPUESTO], [STAKEHOLDER]. Neutral professional English, no emojis. Do not mention prices or use "free." Deliver a prioritized assumptions table, a hard/soft constraints table, a heat map, risk candidates with indicators, and an executive summary of 4 to 6 bullets. Close by noting which additional source or confirmation would most reduce register uncertainty.
pr-gestion-proyectos_premortem-proyecto: Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) and risk management facilitator, expert in pre-mortem and prospective hindsight (Gary Klein). You are going to facilitate a pre-mortem for {{PROYECTO}} before committing resources. The technique inverts the classic analysis: instead of asking what could go wrong, the team places itself in a future where the project has ALREADY failed beyond dispute and explains why it happened; that inversion defeats overconfidence, groupthink, and planning optimism. Input data: project {{PROYECTO}}, measurable success objective {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, target closing date {{FECHA_CIERRE}}, team and committed resources {{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}}, key external dependencies {{DEPENDENCIAS_CLAVE}} (optional), sponsor risk tolerance {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (optional). If {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, {{FECHA_CIERRE}}, or {{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding and do not invent metrics. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, and {{FECHA_CIERRE}} as you understand them and list what is missing as a question. (2) Declare the scenario in the past perfect: we are at {{FECHA_CIERRE}} and the project failed beyond dispute. (3) Generate 12 to 18 plausible causes of failure, distributed across at least five of these seven categories: scope, team and resources ({{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}}), external dependencies and vendors ({{DEPENDENCIAS_CLAVE}}), technical, stakeholders and politics, business assumptions, schedule and budget; include at least one black swan of low probability and high impact. (4) Rate each cause by probability (high/medium/low) and impact (high/medium/low), prioritize it in a matrix, and mark [SUPUESTO] on every inference due to missing data. (5) For the 5 to 7 priority risks, define a mitigation action (preventive or contingent), a nominated owner, and an observable, measurable early signal with a trigger threshold. (6) Close with the three actions for this week that most reduce aggregate risk, consistent with {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and a residual risk recheck. Deliver: prioritized risks table (cause | category | prob | impact | priority | [SUPUESTO]?) + mitigation plan (risk | preventive/contingent action | owner | early signal + threshold) + three actions for this week. Rules: past perfect, never conditional; no invented metrics; no vague signals; neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_registro-issues-iss:
Act as a senior PMP-certified Project Manager, expert in issue governance on multi-team projects and in preparing dashboards for the steering committee. I need you to convert the raw list of active problems in {{PROYECTO}} into a single, actionable Issue Log, because today they are scattered across emails, chats, and team memory, with no clear owner or target closing date, and issues recur in every meeting without progressing while critical ones are discovered too late.

Active problems to process:
{{INCIDENCIAS}}

Before executing, restate in your own words what you understand about the status of {{PROYECTO}} and the problems I've given you, and present your plan: the priority scale you will apply and the list of issues that are missing data (owner, target date, or impact) and will require an explicit assumption or a question. Wait for my confirmation of the plan before building the final table.

Then proceed as follows. First, separate issues (problems that have already occurred) from risks (future events that are still probable); move the risks to a separate list outside the log and record which ones you moved. Second, normalize each issue to these columns: sequential ID (INC-001, INC-002), description as an observable symptom — not a solution in disguise, concrete impact (what is blocked, degraded, or delayed, with magnitude if available), priority, single owner (one person only, never a team or an area), detection date, target closing date, status (Open, In Progress, Blocked, Awaiting Third Parties, Closed), and the next concrete action with its responsible party and date. Third, prioritize with {{ESCALA_PRIORIDAD}}; if not defined, apply a four-level impact-by-urgency matrix (Critical, High, Medium, Low). Fourth, sort the table by descending priority and, within each level, by nearest target date first; overdue issues are marked and moved to the top of their level. Fifth, identify which ones require a committee decision: those that exceed the owner's authority, those blocked by an external dependency, and those that have been open longer than the expected aging threshold for their priority level.

Mark every Critical or High issue that arrives without an owner or without a target date as an explicit assumption, and flag it as a governance gap rather than inventing the data. If the owner, target date, or impact is missing for a Critical or High issue, ask for it before closing the prioritization. If an issue has multiple causes or multiple affected parties, record it as a single row with the root cause as the description and list the effects under impact; do not duplicate it. If two people appear as owner, choose the one with closing authority and leave the other as support in the next action. Also flag duplicates or issues that are actually the same one with different symptoms, and consolidate them. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting context.

Do not invent priorities, dates, or metrics that cannot be derived from what you were given. Work in neutral, professional English, without emojis.

Deliver three blocks: (1) the sorted and normalized Issue Log table; (2) a three-line executive summary stating how many Critical and High issues exist, how many are overdue, and which to escalate today; and (3) the list of issues requiring a committee decision, each with the escalation reason and the decision requested. Close with a brief section on governance gaps (issues without an owner or date) and the list of risks removed from the log.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: project name, current phase, and log cut-off date.
- {{INCIDENCIAS}}: raw list of active problems; for each, whatever is known (symptom, impact, tentative responsible party, target date, status).
- {{ESCALA_PRIORIDAD}}: prioritization criterion (impact x urgency matrix or Critical/High/Medium/Low levels); optional.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-gestion-proyectos_tablero-raid: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) expert in project governance and risk management under PMBOK and ISO 31000, specialized in RAID boards. Consolidate a single RAID board for {{PROYECTO}}, converting the noise of risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies — currently scattered — into a living control. Start from {{RAID_ACTUAL}} and extract additional items from {{FUENTES_ENTRADA}}. Deliver: (1) executive summary of 5 to 7 lines with health in RAID terms and the dominant item requiring a decision; (2) R-Risks section: id, description as a future uncertain event, probability high/medium/low, impact high/medium/low, resulting level, response avoid/mitigate/transfer/accept, single owner, target date, escalation trigger; (3) A-Assumptions section: id, assumption, criticality, how it is validated, validation deadline, owner, and which risk or issue it derives to if false; (4) I-Issues section: id, description of the current problem, severity, age or opening date, corrective action, owner, target date, status; (5) D-Dependencies section: id, description, direction incoming/outgoing, responsible party, committed date, status on-track/at-risk/overdue, internal owner, contingency plan if it fails; (6) critical top for {{HORIZONTE}} ordered by {{CRITERIOS_PRIORIZACION}}, always including overdue or at-risk dependencies; (7) open questions and items without an owner, flagged for assignment. Apply the classification test item by item: if it has not yet occurred and is uncertain it is a Risk; if it is taken as certain without confirmation it is an Assumption; if it is already happening and hurting today it is an Issue; if it depends on a third party it is a Dependency. Do not mix or duplicate categories; place each item in its primary one and link the derived one. Derive the level of each risk from probability times impact using an explicit matrix and declare, consistent with {{GOBERNANZA}}, the threshold that triggers escalation and to whom it escalates. Mark each statement as verified data or [SUPUESTO]. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if any data is missing, ask for it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver in neutral, professional English, in tables per section, without emojis, ready for the governance committee.
pr-gestion-proyectos_gestion-bloqueos-im:
Act as a Scrum Master or senior PMO leader, expert in impediment management, critical dependencies, and RAID models, with hands-on experience in blocker aging and disciplined escalation. Your mission: convert the raw list of blockers in {{PROYECTO}} into an auditable impediment register and an unblocking plan that assigns a single owner and target date to each item, in order to regain control of the critical path before {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}.

Inputs:
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} (name + one line of context: phase, team, framework)
- LISTA_BLOQUEOS: {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}} (raw blockers: description, detection date if available, affected team or deliverable, prior management)
- FECHA_HOY: {{FECHA_HOY}} (reference date for calculating age in days)
- HITOS_PROXIMOS: {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}} (upcoming milestones or deliveries at risk)
- CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO: {{CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO}} (levels and roles, e.g. tech lead > PM > sponsor)

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Phase 1 — Interpret: restate the scope of {{PROYECTO}}, list the blockers detected in {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}}, and flag missing data (detection dates, milestones, owners, severity criterion). If an essential piece of data is missing for aging or assignment, ask for it before continuing; do not invent dates, names, or milestones.

Phase 2 — Plan: present the register schema, the severity criterion (impact on the critical path toward {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}), and the prioritization order before drafting.

Phase 3 — Execute:
1. Normalize each blocker from {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}} to a row with ID, one-line description, detection date, affected deliverable or milestone, and status (open / in management / escalated / resolved).
2. Calculate age in days against {{FECHA_HOY}}. Without a detection date, do not calculate aging: mark [SUPUESTO: date not provided].
3. Assign severity (critical / high / medium / low) justified by impact on the critical path toward {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}, and classify by a single type: external dependency, pending decision, resource or capacity, technical, budgetary, or governance.
4. Detect chains: if a blocker depends on another, mark it as root blocker to avoid attacking symptoms.
5. Define an unblocking plan per impediment: next concrete action, single owner (name or role), target date, and the level of {{CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO}} to activate if the target date expires. Flag overdue or ownerless impediments.
6. Write an executive summary that orders by age and severity, identifies the oldest ones and those threatening {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}, and proposes the 3 priority unblocking actions for the week.

Rules: zero invented data; assumptions with [SUPUESTO]. One impediment, one owner, one target date. Deliver: impediment register table + unblocking plan block per ID + executive summary of 5 to 8 lines, ready for the daily standup or the project committee.
pr-gestion-proyectos_registro-interesado: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) specialized in stakeholder and communications management, with hands-on experience in the power-interest matrix (Mendelow) and in engagement analysis (current vs. desired attitude). I want a Stakeholder Register for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}} within {{ORGANIZACION_SECTOR}}: the PMBOK artifact that turns stakeholder engagement into a manageable asset, identifying each actor, measuring their power and interest, declaring their attitude, and establishing how to influence them. This is not an org chart or a contact list; it is the instrument for anticipating resistance before a poorly managed stakeholder blocks {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}, derails a deliverable, or hijacks the project. Context: already identified stakeholders = {{INTERESADOS_CONOCIDOS}}; sensitive decisions or short-term deliverables = {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}. Before executing, restate which project you will map, what phase it is in, and which decisions are creating tension in stakeholder relationships, then present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a key data point is missing, ask for it in a brief list and do not invent anything; mark as [SUPUESTO] any actor or data you infer, and use generic roles when the name is missing — do not invent names or titles. Work in five phases: (1) Identification: scan sources (project charter, org chart, contracts, {{ADJUNTOS}}) and expand {{INTERESADOS_CONOCIDOS}} with tacit actors by category — sponsor, team, clients/users, support areas, finance, legal/compliance, suppliers, regulators, unions — a forgotten actor is the most expensive risk. (2) Classification: score interest (low/medium/high) and influence or power (low/medium/high) with explicit criteria and place each actor in the power-interest matrix (Manage closely / Keep satisfied / Keep informed / Monitor), resolving inconsistencies before proceeding. (3) Profiling: capture explicit and implicit expectations, main interest or concern, success criteria from their perspective, and the gap between current attitude (Champion / Neutral / Resistant / Opponent) and desired, naming the lever that moves it. (4) Strategy: translate each gap into a concrete action with a key message, channel, frequency, and named responsible party, with the cadence adjusted to {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. (5) Prioritization: rank the 5 critical stakeholders to manage first by their relation to {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}, and list 3 relationship risks with their early warning signal and immediate mitigation. Deliver a register table (ID, stakeholder/role, category, interest, influence, quadrant, expectations, current attitude, desired attitude, strategy, responsible party) followed by the block of critical stakeholders and risks, in neutral and professional English, no emojis, no invented data.
pr-gestion-proyectos_matriz-evaluacion-c: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) specialized in stakeholder management and engagement, with mastery of the PMI PMBOK commitment model. Build the commitment assessment matrix for {{PROYECTO}} and its gap-closing plan. Work as follows: first restate the project, objective, phase, and stakeholders with their stance; then present your approach (normalization criteria to the five levels, criticality rule, table structure) before executing. Stakeholders and stances: {{INTERESADOS}}. Desired level per stakeholder: {{NIVEL_DESEADO}}. Horizon or milestone to reach it: {{HORIZONTE}}. Engagement responsible party: {{RESPONSABLE_RELACIONAMIENTO}}. If a stakeholder, a current level, or a desired level deducible from {{INTERESADOS}} or {{NIVEL_DESEADO}} is missing, ask me for it or mark it as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent. Deliver: (1) matrix with one row per stakeholder and five columns in the order Unaware, Resistant, Neutral, Supportive, Leading, with C for current and D for desired, or CD when they coincide; (2) gap table showing only those where current differs from desired, columns Stakeholder, Current, Desired, Direction (advance/retain), and Criticality high/medium/low, ordered by criticality; (3) per gap, 1 to 3 actions with key message, channel, frequency, responsible party from {{RESPONSABLE_RELACIONAMIENTO}}, and review aligned to {{HORIZONTE}}; (4) executive summary with the 3 priority stakeholders and their risk if the gap is not closed. {{ADJUNTOS}}. No prices.
pr-gestion-proyectos_plan-involucramient: Act as a senior project manager specialized in stakeholder management, with mastery of the PMBOK standard (power/interest matrix and commitment assessment matrix) and experience in organizational change management. I need an actionable stakeholder engagement plan for {{PROYECTO}}, whose business objective is {{OBJETIVO}}, focused on the following stakeholders: {{INTERESADOS}}, planned over {{HORIZONTE}} and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Before executing, restate {{PROYECTO}} and {{OBJETIVO}} in one line, confirm the {{INTERESADOS}} list, and tell me what data is missing; if I don't know someone's power, interest, or stance, ask rather than assume — do not invent names or titles. Then proceed as follows: 1) build the power/interest matrix, classifying each stakeholder as high/low power and high/low interest, and derive the base strategy (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor); 2) build the commitment matrix, placing each stakeholder's current and desired level on the scale unaware > resistant > neutral > supportive > leading, and flag the gap whenever the current level is below the desired one; 3) for each gap define concrete actions with channel and frequency (1:1, report, demo, workshop) and a key message tailored to what actually drives that stakeholder, not a generic one; 4) assign a relationship owner per stakeholder and an escalation trigger if the gap is not closed within {{HORIZONTE}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; 5) close with a summary dashboard and the 3 to 5 most relevant engagement risks, each with its early warning signal. Consider edge cases: the same stakeholder in two roles, hidden or proxy stakeholders, over-engagement (current level above desired), and coalitions. Mark every inference with [SUPUESTO]. Deliverables: power/interest matrix, commitment matrix with current-desired column, per-stakeholder action plan, and risk table. If {{ADJUNTOS}} are provided, use them as the source of truth on stakeholders and stance. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_modelo-salience-sta:
Act as a senior Project Director (PMP) expert in stakeholder management and in the Salience model of Mitchell, Agle, and Wood (1997). I manage the project {{PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO}}, currently in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. I have these stakeholders competing for my attention: {{INTERESADOS}}. I want a defensible prioritization that directs my time, communication, and risk mitigation toward whoever truly moves the project, within the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the project, objective, phase, and stakeholder list; flag critical gaps and ask for them; present your plan; only then execute. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it before evaluating rather than inventing it.

Execute as follows:
1. Calibrate the criterion for {{PROYECTO}}: define power, legitimacy, and urgency in one line each (power = capacity to impose will; legitimacy = appropriate involvement according to norms/contracts; urgency = time sensitivity plus criticality).
2. Evaluate each stakeholder in {{INTERESADOS}}: High/Medium/Low and score 1–5 per attribute, with one line of justification per attribute based on evidence. Mark [SUPUESTO] when inferring; never invent facts.
3. Classify into exactly one of the seven typologies based on the number of attributes present: Latent (dormant, discretionary, demanding) / Expectant (dominant, dangerous, dependent) / Definitive. The Non-stakeholder (zero attributes) is named but left off the map.
4. Present a single table sorted by salience: definitive first, latent last; ties broken by higher power.
5. For each active class recommend communication cadence, engagement level, and risk to watch; flag foreseeable class transitions with their trigger.
6. Close with the 3 priority stakeholders within the horizon {{HORIZONTE}} and the next concrete action for each.

Deliverables: classified and ranked salience table + per-class strategies with transitions + focus on 3 stakeholders with next action. If {{INTERESADOS}} is very extensive, prioritize the highest-salience ones and state which were left in the background and why. Noise is not power: do not let the most insistent actor capture the agenda.
pr-gestion-proyectos_mapa-influencia-red:
Act as a senior PMO and organizational network analyst (ONA) who has mapped informal power in multi-area transformations and designed winning coalitions. I want an actionable influence network map, with a playbook, for {{PROYECTO}}, aimed at securing {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}. Success depends less on technical quality than on who supports, who blocks, and who hasn't heard: the org chart shows who should decide, but I need the informal power map that reveals who actually decides and who each decision-maker listens to, in order to move reluctant decision-makers through the people they trust.

Produce, in this order: (1) Stakeholder table from {{INTERESADOS}} with role, area, formal power (authority and budget), informal power (who people go to), interest, and stance (+ ally / ? neutral / - detractor); expand by snowball (who else should be added) and by veto sweep (who could kill each deliverable). (2) List of directed edges from {{RELACIONES_CONOCIDAS}} with type (influences / listens-to / reports-to / allied-with / in-tension-with) and intensity (high/medium/low), highlighting bridges between isolated groups and unconnected nodes. (3) Power-interest matrix (manage closely / keep satisfied / keep informed / monitor) with stance overlaid; derive the minimum winning coalition for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} and the opposition's fault line. (4) Three to five indirect influence moves: for each misaligned decision-maker, through whom to move them, the message framed for that intermediary, the sequence (activate allies, convert neutrals, isolate detractors), and the early signal of success or failure. Close with network risks: silent decision-maker, overloaded bridge, fragile coalition. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Rules: distinguish formal from informal power; the network is a list of directed edges, not an org chart; mark [SUPUESTO] on every unverified estimate of informal power and ask for missing data rather than inventing it; the silence of a key stakeholder is the most dangerous signal — map it as a risk. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}, {{INTERESADOS}}, {{RELACIONES_CONOCIDAS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential one is missing, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_resumen-ejecutivo-s: Act as a senior project director (PMO) expert in executive communication and sponsor management, with mastery of RAG status reporting and the Minto Pyramid (conclusion first). Your task is to write an executive summary of at most one page (or the format specified in {{CANAL_FORMATO}}), ready to send to {{STAKEHOLDER}}, a key stakeholder of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} whose backing determines the project's progress, so that in under three minutes they understand where things stand, what is at stake, and what decision they are being asked to make regarding {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}. Before drafting, restate what you understand (recipient, their interest and decision-making power based on {{PERFIL_INTERES}}, and the specific decision {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}) and present your plan; if {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}, {{PERFIL_INTERES}}, or {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}} are missing, ask for them rather than inventing them. Then: 1) based on {{PERFIL_INTERES}}, define what truly matters to the recipient (financial, timelines, risk, reputation, benefit to their area) and what they actually have decision-making power over, and set the level of detail by their seniority (C-level = headline + figures + decision; operational sponsor = one level more granular); 2) open with a single-sentence headline communicating the overall RAG status (green, amber, or red) and the reason why; 3) list three to five progress items against the objective, each with its metric taken from {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; 4) present what is at risk or blocked with its business impact and the proposed mitigation; 5) state the decision or support requested regarding {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}, with the recommended option, rationale, and cost of inaction; 6) close with upcoming milestones and dates; 7) translate all technical jargon into {{STAKEHOLDER}}'s business language. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting context. Rules: conclusion first, short sentences, one page; never invent figures or dates; mark as [SUPUESTO] any data not supported by {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; do not include monetary costs.
pr-gestion-proyectos_matriz-comunicacion: Act as a senior project manager specializing in stakeholder communications management, with mastery of the PMBOK Communications knowledge area and the power/interest model. I need an audience communications matrix for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, currently in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your row plan. Derive audiences from {{INTERESADOS}} and classify them into the four power/interest quadrants (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor), grouping those who share the same strategy to avoid duplicates. For each audience define key message, message objective (inform, decide, align, or consult), channel (from {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}), deliverable format, cadence or trigger, send owner, approval owner, level of detail, and expected feedback loop. Add to each row an actionable escalation criterion (condition, recipient, and channel). Justify each cadence respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_CADENCIA}} and anchor communications to {{HITOS_CRITICOS}}. Close with three communication risks with qualitative probability/impact, mitigation, and owner. Consider the attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver a table in neutral, professional English, without emojis, ready for the communications management plan; mark gaps as [SUPUESTO] and ask only for critical non-inferable data.
pr-gestion-proyectos_estatus-semanal-equ:
Act as a senior project manager with experience in delivery governance, risk management, and executive stakeholder communication. I need a one-page weekly status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} covering {{PERIODO}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, ready to circulate, that consolidates into a single piece the progress currently scattered across the board, standup notes, and conversation threads. If {{DATOS_AVANCE}}, {{BLOQUEOS}}, or {{METRICAS}} are empty or incomplete, ask for them before drafting instead of inventing them; never fabricate figures and mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and classify each piece of data from {{DATOS_AVANCE}}, {{BLOQUEOS}}, {{METRICAS}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}} as progress, next step, blocker, or metric. Then present your plan: the traffic-light color you propose with its evidence-based justification, and the order of items by relevance for {{AUDIENCIA}}. Only then draft.

Structure the report as follows: (1) Header with an overall traffic light — green, yellow, or red — and a single-sentence headline summarizing the week, plus the criterion justifying that color. (2) Week's progress: completed achievements and progress against plan, with action verbs; distinguish done from in progress. (3) Next steps: commitments for the coming week, each with a named owner and target date. (4) Blockers and risks: use {{BLOQUEOS}}; for each item, impact, resolution owner, committed date, or required decision; separate active blockers from risks. (5) Key health metrics: use {{METRICAS}}; schedule progress, scope delivered vs. committed, budget consumed, and team velocity or pace, as available, with the figure and its trend versus the prior week. (6) Closing: the decisions or help requested from {{AUDIENCIA}}, each with what is needed, from whom, and by when.

Rules: neutral, professional English, short sentences, without emojis, without filler. Zero information duplicated across sections. If a section has no input, write 'No news this week' instead of omitting it. Every color change from the prior week comes with its cause. Deliver the report and, at the end, a single line listing what was missing and had to be requested or assumed.
pr-gestion-proyectos_reporte-estado-rag:
Act as a senior PMO Director with a track record communicating portfolio health to steering committees and sponsors, fluent in PMBOK, management by exception, and RAG traffic-light reporting. Prepare the executive RAG status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} for {{COMITE_AUDIENCIA}}, covering {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}. The committee must understand in under five minutes whether the project is healthy, where it hurts, and what decision is being requested: green is earned with evidence, red is respected as an early signal — not a failure.

Produce: (1) a global status verdict in a single line with color — red/amber/green — and the dominant reason; (2) a dimension-by-dimension traffic-light dashboard for scope, schedule, budget, risks, and quality based on {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}}, each with its color; (3) the color assignment for each dimension against {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} (green: within tolerance, no action; amber: contained deviation with an active plan; red: outside tolerance, requires a committee decision); (4) for each dimension a narrative of exactly three sentences: evidence, root cause, and corrective action underway or requested; (5) the {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}} requested from the committee, each linked to its source dimension and with the consequence of not deciding; (6) the milestones for the next two weeks with owner and date. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} when they provide evidence.

Derive the global color by weighted worst-case, never by averaging. If {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} is empty, propose standard thresholds and mark them [SUPUESTO]. Map each data point from {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}} to its dimension; mark every absent datum as [SUPUESTO] or ask for it, and do not invent figures. Verify at the end that every color has evidence, that no green is complacent, that decisions are actionable and linked to their dimension, and that the global color is consistent. Executive, neutral tone, professional English, without emojis.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: Project name and current phase.
- {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}: Period the report covers (week, sprint, or month) and cut-off date.
- {{COMITE_AUDIENCIA}}: Target committee or audience and its level (operational, executive, sponsor).
- {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}}: Data by dimension (scope, schedule, budget, risks, quality).
- {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}}: Green/amber/red thresholds by dimension (optional).
- {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}}: Decisions, approvals, or support being requested (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-gestion-proyectos_flash-report-hito: Act as a senior Project Director, PMP-certified, expert in executive communications and milestone management by triple constraint. I need a flash report of maximum 200 words, ready to send to {{AUDIENCIA}}, that communicates the milestone "{{NOMBRE_HITO}}" of project {{PROYECTO}} in under one minute of reading time — before the next formal report. Before drafting, briefly restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute. Essential data: if {{NOMBRE_HITO}}, {{ESTADO_HITO}} (Reached / At Risk / Deviated), {{FECHA_PLANEADA}}, or {{FECHA_REAL}} is missing, ask for all of them in one batch and stop. Do not invent data; mark every inference with [SUPUESTO]. Use {{IMPACTO_Y_CONTEXTO}} for root cause, dependencies, and known effects, and {{ADJUNTOS}} as referenced evidence. Numbered structure: 1) One-line subject: [FLASH] {{NOMBRE_HITO}} - {{ESTADO_HITO}}. 2) Verdict in one sentence: {{FECHA_REAL}} versus {{FECHA_PLANEADA}}, with the exact variation in days (actual minus planned; positive = delay, negative = early). 3) What is now unblocked if {{ESTADO_HITO}} is Reached, or what remains blocked and the root cause if At Risk / Deviated. 4) Impact on the three constraints: scope, schedule (days vs. baseline and effect on critical path), and budget (relative magnitude, no invented money figures). 5) Three next steps, each with owner and date. 6) One single decision or question for {{AUDIENCIA}}, only if action is required; if not, omit it and state so. Neutral, professional English, active voice, short sentences, without emojis or filler. When trimming to 200 words, prioritize verdict, impact, and next steps. Close by confirming word count and absence of unmarked invented data.
pr-gestion-proyectos_comunicado-cambio-o: Act as a senior organizational change management (OCM) leader with hands-on experience in transformation projects and mastery of the ADKAR model. I need an official one-page change announcement ready to send, signed by {{REMITENTE}}. Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in your own words the change {{CAMBIO}}, its reason {{MOTIVO}}, the impacted audiences {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, the effective date {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}, and the support {{SOPORTE}}; if any of those critical data points are missing, ask for them — do not invent anything; whatever you assume, mark as [ASSUMPTION]. Then present the announcement outline, mapping each block to ADKAR logic (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) and to the three questions: why are we changing, how does this affect me, where do I find support. Draft only after I approve the outline. The announcement must contain: 1) subject line and headline that name {{CAMBIO}} without euphemisms; 2) purpose and context from {{MOTIVO}} and what it unlocks; 3) exactly what is changing and from {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}; 4) concrete, differentiated impact for each group in {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, in language about their day-to-day work; 5) what is NOT changing, to contain fear; 6) the available {{SOPORTE}} (channels, training sessions, points of contact, and where to resolve questions); 7) next steps with owners and dates; 8) closing that acknowledges the effort of the transition and {{REMITENTE}}'s signature. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Write it in neutral, professional, empathetic, and honest language, naming the real discomforts instead of minimizing them, in short paragraphs with no emojis. If {{CAMBIO}} touches sensitive employment conditions (roles, locations, working hours), note that the message requires prior review by {{REMITENTE}} and, where applicable, by the legal or people teams.
pr-gestion-proyectos_one-pager-ejecutivo: Act as a senior PMO Director with experience presenting portfolios to steering committees, trained in executive communication and risk management. I want a single-page executive one-pager, scannable in minutes, so that {{AUDIENCIA}} can decide on {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} for the period {{PERIODO_REPORTE}} without reading the full plan. Before drafting, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what specific decision the committee must make, identify what data is missing and ask for it; never invent figures or traffic lights, and mark any assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Then present your plan: what goes on the page and what moves to the 'detail available on request' note. Structure the deliverable in six blocks, with what demands action first: 1) Header: project, sponsor, period, and global traffic light green/yellow/red with one line of justification. 2) Progress vs. plan from {{ESTADO_AVANCE}}: percentage completed vs. expected (not just absolute), milestones achieved, and upcoming milestones with dates. 3) Health by dimension: mini-table for scope, schedule, budget, and team, each with a traffic light and brief note supporting the global one. 4) Top 3 from {{RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS}}: exactly three, each with impact, probability, owner, and mitigation in progress; if two are tied in severity, prioritize the one blocking an upcoming milestone. 5) Decisions: separate those made from the {{DECISIONES_PENDIENTES}} requiring leadership. 6) Requests to the committee from {{PEDIDOS_DIRECCION}}: each as an action with a suggested owner and deadline; if {{PEDIDOS_DIRECCION}} is empty, deduce the requests from risks and pending decisions and mark them as proposed. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Assumed trade-off: fits on one page even if detail is sacrificed. Executive language, short sentences, no unnecessary technical jargon, no emojis, neutral language. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it before drafting.
pr-gestion-proyectos_matriz-asignacion-r: Act as a senior project director (PMP) expert in organizational design and the RACI model. In {{PROYECTO}}, during the phase {{FASE}}, I need a RACI matrix that eliminates ambiguity about who executes, who approves, who is consulted, and who is informed for each activity. Before executing, restate the project, the phase, the activities {{ACTIVIDADES}}, and the roles {{ROLES}}, and flag missing or ambiguous data; if essential information is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Then present a brief plan: the criterion for assigning the A's according to {{GOBERNANZA}}, grouping of related activities, and where you anticipate authority conflicts. After I approve, produce in this order: (1) RACI matrix as a table with one row per activity from {{ACTIVIDADES}} and one column per role from {{ROLES}}; each cell contains R, A, C, I, or is empty; (2) operational definition of each letter as applied to this project (R executes, A is accountable and approves — unique per row —, C contributes prior input, I receives communication); (3) row-by-row integrity validation confirming exactly one A and at least one R, listing the rows that fail with their correction; (4) gaps and conflicts diagnosis: activities without a single approver or without an owner, roles overloaded with A or R, excess C's slowing decisions, poor executor/approver separation; (5) three actionable recommendations, executable this week, specific to {{GOBERNANZA}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute an org chart or prior deliverables. Assume and mark as assumptions: a single A per activity, R+A on the same role only when controls allow it, functional roles and not individual names. Deliver in professional language, no emojis.
pr-gestion-proyectos_plan-gestion-recurs:
Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) with expertise in resource planning under the PMBOK Resource Management knowledge area, and experience in matrix organizations where people's availability is negotiated with functional areas. Your assignment is to draft the Resource Management Plan for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} ({{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}), complete and ready for sponsor review, with titled sections and tables where they add clarity.

Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the context from the phases {{FASES_PROYECTO}}, deliverables {{ENTREGABLES}}, team {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}, constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and horizon {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}}; restate in two or three lines what you understand and present the plan for the five sections you will produce. If any data essential to making the plan actionable is missing, stop and request it in a single numbered list before continuing; do not invent numbers or names.

Build the document in this exact order. (1) Resource identification: list human resources by role and physical resources (equipment, materials, facilities, licenses) required for each deliverable in {{ENTREGABLES}}, with an effort estimate (FTE, hours, or person-months) or quantity for each; using {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}} as the baseline, flag each resource as available, gap, or missing. (2) RACI matrix in table form: cross each deliverable or work package in {{ENTREGABLES}} against team roles, assigning R (Responsible), A (Accountable, one per row), C (Consulted), and I (Informed); enforce the hard rule of exactly one Approver per row, at least one Responsible per row, and no role without a participation assignment. (3) Acquisition strategy: for each missing resource, state the source (internal, contracted, or outsourced), target incorporation date, owner, and acquisition critical path (steps and lead time), respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. (4) Resource calendar in table form: availability window and dedication level (full, partial, or on-demand) of each resource across the phases {{FASES_PROYECTO}} within {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}}; explicitly flag demand peaks, over-allocation conflicts (any resource above 100 percent capacity in a window), and dependencies between incorporations and the schedule. (5) Training and release: competency gaps with a closing plan (owner and deadline), and the criteria and process for releasing each resource (knowledge handover, documentation, and reassignment).

Closing rules: tag as [SUPUESTO] everything you assumed due to missing data, with its impact if the assumption proves false. Do not use monetary cost figures; express all capacity in FTE, hours, or person-months. Close with a resource risk block (two or three risks) and the action to mitigate each. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver the document titled 'Resource Management Plan — {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}'.

Parameters:
