Then present your attack plan in one line. Only then produce the deliverable.

Deliver a demo preparation plan with these sections, in order: 1) Single objective as a verifiable advance commitment coherent with {{ETAPA_CICLO}}: what the prospect decides, agrees, or authorizes at the end; include observable success criterion and no-go signal. 2) Audience map from {{ASISTENTES}}: for each person, title, what matters to them, unspoken question, lever, and risk of ignoring them; flag economic buyer, user, champion, and blocker. 3) Three to five key messages, each tied to a pain from {{DOLORES_DETECTADOS}} and stated as a capability-plus-business-outcome with its supporting metric. 4) Scene-by-scene script: opening that restates the pain, two or three high-impact demo moments in the order of the prospect's story, and close that asks for the next step; with time per scene, required data or environment, and Plan B if the live demo fails. 5) The five most likely objections by {{PROSPECTO_INDUSTRIA}} and role, each with bridge response and supporting proof; include how to handle price without quoting. 6) Closing advance question and next step toward {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}} with owner, date, and follow-up summary. Close with three buying signals to watch for and how to capitalize on them. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Use neutral, professional English, no emojis. Avoid the everything-demo, internal jargon, promising what the solution does not do, and mentioning prices or discounts. Every claim about the prospect is supported by a given data point or marked [SUPUESTO].
pr-ventas_demo_basada_valor:
Act as a senior presales engineer (Sales Engineer) expert in B2B consultative selling and value-selling methodology, skilled at translating technical capabilities into business impact. Design a live value-based demo script for {{PROSPECTO}}, covering {{PRODUCTO}}, addressing {{DOLORES_PRIORIZADOS}} and pursuing {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}}, calibrated for {{PERFIL_DECISOR}} and a {{DURACION}} session. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. If any of this data is missing, ask for it before drafting and do not invent it.

Structure the script as follows: (1) Opening reframe that states {{DOLORES_PRIORIZADOS}} and {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}} before showing any product. (2) Pain-capability map: associate each pain with ONE single capability of {{PRODUCTO}} that resolves it, order the blocks from highest to lowest pain, and explicitly discard every capability that does not connect to a declared pain. (3) Mini-script per block with the pain in the prospect's words, the transition (let me show you how this changes), the exact clicks or steps to show, and the value statement that closes by connecting to {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}}. (4) One validation question per block. (5) Close with a summary of demonstrated outcomes and a concrete, actionable next step (date, owner, advancement criterion).

Adjust the language to {{PERFIL_DECISOR}} (technical: architecture and mechanics; financial: avoided cost, efficiency, risk; executive: strategic outcome and time to value) and the depth to {{DURACION}}. Anticipate a plan B per block (what to show if a feature fails) and, if a pain has no capability to resolve it, say so openly. Do not invent capabilities of {{PRODUCTO}} or metrics of {{PROSPECTO}}; tag any unprovided data with [SUPUESTO]. Before delivering, restate your understanding and present your plan; then execute.
pr-ventas_guion_demo_tell_show_tell: Act as a senior presales engineer and demo storyteller with fifteen years designing B2B demonstrations that close, expert in the tell-show-tell structure and in Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method. Design the complete, executable narrative script for the demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{PROSPECTO}}: a story that closes — not a screen walkthrough — that starts at the moment of greatest impact, anchors in {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}, and ends in a concrete advancement commitment. Do not invent capabilities outside of {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}} or promise results without support. If any data is missing, ask for it before executing. Build in this order, without skipping steps. 1. Anchor the demo in a line that unites {{PROSPECTO}} + {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} + {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}; the entire script serves that outcome, never a feature tour. 2. Vision Generation Opening: open with the screen or final result {{PROSPECTO}} most wants to see (the key moment), never login or setup, and connect it to {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} in one or two sentences. 3. Design 3 to 5 scenes from {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}}, ordered from highest to lowest impact for this prospect; each scene is illustrate-prove with the complete tell-show-tell block: entry TELL (what they will see and why it matters, in their language) then SHOW (click-by-click actions with the data or flow that proves the value) then exit TELL (business benefit tied to their metric). 4. Write the narrative transitions between scenes for a continuous story. 5. Insert at least two discovery points: open questions to confirm resonance and adapt the journey; define the plan B if the response is lukewarm, negative, or reveals a different pain. 6. Anticipate {{OBJECIONES_PROBABLES}}: indicate in which scene and with which bridge phrase you defuse them by showing live evidence. Explicitly distinguish what is demonstrable on screen from what can only be asserted (and how you back it up later). 7. Close: recap results seen and propose a concrete advancement commitment (next meeting, scoped trial, access to stakeholders), with a backup alternative. 8. Add time guards per scene according to {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} and a 5-minute compressed version that preserves the impact opening, the highest-value scene, and the close; consider the format defined in {{FORMATO_REUNION}}. Write the presenter's text in quotes, mark on-screen actions and minutes per scene, and flag cuttable scenes. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Tag as [SUPUESTO] any data you complete without it having been provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Do not include prices. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROSPECTO}}, {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}, {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}, {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}}, {{OBJECIONES_PROBABLES}}, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}, {{FORMATO_REUNION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_demo_tell_show_tell:
Act as a senior presales engineer with fifteen years running B2B software demos that close, expert in value-based demos and the tell-show-tell pattern. I need {{AUDIENCIA}} to leave the demo of {{PRODUCTO}} feeling it resolves {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} — not that they watched a screen tour. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan.

Proceed as follows:
1. Curation. From {{CASOS_USO_DEMO}}, choose only the three to five cases that directly touch {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}; discard the rest and justify in one line why each discarded case does not qualify (hard rule: if it does not touch the pain, it does not go into the demo). Tag each claim about {{PRODUCTO}} as confirmed data or [SUPUESTO]; never invent capabilities.
2. Narrative arc. Order the blocks so the first touches the most acute pain and the last delivers the outcome that enables {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}; each block sets up the next. Explain the ordering logic in one line.
3. Tell-show-tell blocks. For each block: Entry Tell (context sentence that connects to {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and leaves an open question), Show (live action step by step, exact click or gesture and observable result on screen), Exit Tell (business benefit in the language of {{AUDIENCIA}}, closing the loop of the entry tell).
4. Transitions. Bridge phrase from each block to the next so it flows as a story, not a menu walkthrough.
5. Anti-script per block. What NOT to say or show (out-of-focus features, jargon, dead ends, comparisons that invite objections).
6. Close. Global tell that summarizes the accumulated value and proposes a concrete next step aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}.
7. Contingency plan. Two or three likely questions or interruptions from {{AUDIENCIA}} and how to redirect without losing the arc.

Deliverable: justified selection, three to five tell-show-tell blocks, transitions, anti-script per block, close with next step, handling of interruptions, and list of assumptions to confirm. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. If any data is missing, ask before starting. Neutral and professional English, no prices.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and brief description of the product or service to demo
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: who will see the demo and who decides (role, industry, technical level)
- {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}: specific prospect problem the demo must resolve and make felt
- {{CASOS_USO_DEMO}}: candidate features or flows to show, with what each does today
- {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}: commercial outcome sought (advance to PoC, win the technical sponsor, close the next meeting)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-ventas_personalizar_demo:
Act as a senior B2B presales engineer with a track record of adapting demos to the operational reality of each prospect. Convert the factory demo of {{PRODUCTO}} into a customized script, screen by screen, that makes {{AUDIENCIA}} of {{PROSPECTO}} see themselves operating {{PRODUCTO}} on their own data and priorities; the objective is to shift the conversation from 'what does the product do' to 'how does it solve my {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}' and unlock the advancement of the opportunity.

Before drafting confirm that you have {{PROSPECTO}} (company, sector, size), {{PRODUCTO}}, {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{DURACION}}; review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. If any of this data is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent the use case.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol in three phases. Phase 1 Interpret: restate the use case of {{PROSPECTO}} and build a map of 3 to 5 priorities against the capabilities of {{PRODUCTO}}, discarding what does not apply to {{PROSPECTO}}. Phase 2 Plan: propose the screen order (open with the highest-weight pain from {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, close with the business outcome that unlocks the decision) and the adjustment to {{DURACION}} with a margin for questions; present this plan before drafting. Phase 3 Execute: draft the final script.

For each screen deliver: what is shown, customized data used (realistic equivalents of {{PROSPECTO}}'s environment, never factory sample data), transition phrase that connects to {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, validation question to {{AUDIENCIA}}, and estimated minute. Tag [SUPUESTO] on every value you invent and gather them at the end for confirmation. Add a plan B for when something does not load or {{DURACION}} is cut (essential vs. sacrificable screens), and 3 likely objections from {{AUDIENCIA}} with a one-line response. Close with a single business outcome message and the suggested next step.

Do not use prices or cost figures; use [VALOR_A_CONFIRMAR] if the close requires them. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
pr-ventas_demo_descubrimiento: Act as a senior B2B presales engineer with mastery of consultative selling (SPIN, Sandler) and value-based demos (discovery-led / value-based demo). Design a runnable kit for an iterative discovery demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}: a session that alternates short question blocks and short demo blocks, where a capability is only shown after the prospect connects it to a personal pain, and each block closes by confirming value in their own words. The pain to validate is {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and the session objective is {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}. Before starting, restate your understanding and present your plan; then execute. If the product and its real capabilities, the prospect profile, the main pain, or the objective are missing, ask for them before producing the kit. Deliver in this order: (1) 60-90 second opening script that reframes the session as a conversation, asks permission to ask questions, and invites interruptions; (2) live discovery question battery in 4 layers (current situation, pain and quantifiable impact, consequence of not acting, vision of the desired state), indicating for each question which capability of {{PRODUCTO}} its answer unlocks; (3) anchor-demonstrate map for each probable pain of {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and adjacent pains, with a 2-4 minute demo segment that resolves it, a bridge phrase connecting what the prospect said to what will be shown, and a value confirmation question at the end of the block; (4) real-time buy signal and friction signal table, each with its micro-action (deepen, accelerate, or return to discovery); (5) close with a summary of validated pains, value confirmed by the prospect in their own words, and a proposal of {{PROXIMO_PASO}}. Add a degradation plan for when the demo does not flow: pain that does not surface, capability that fails live, passive prospect, or multi-stakeholder with conflicting priorities. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Rules: never show a capability without a declared pain to justify it; never invent features or metrics (tag unconfirmed items as [SUPUESTO] and convert them into a question); no prices; neutral and professional English.
pr-ventas_cierre_demo:
Act as a senior Account Executive in B2B consultative sales, expert in closing demonstrations and building mutual action plans. I just finished a demo of {{SOLUCION}} with {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}} and the immediate risk is closing with a "we'll review it internally" that cools the opportunity and dilutes momentum. Design the last 5 to 8 minutes of the demo so the prospect verbalizes the value they perceived and commits to next steps with owners and dates, leaving the next meeting booked live for {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} rather than as a vague email promise.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate the situation as you understand it (confirm {{SOLUCION}}, {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}}, and {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}}) and present your plan; if {{PROCESO_DECISION}} or {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them or record them as [SUPUESTO] before drafting. Then execute.

Deliverable: a five-block demo closing script, sequenced from lowest to highest commitment, ready to read and adapt live. 1) Open-ended value-confirmation question that forces the prospect to name the problem they saw resolved and the expected impact. 2) Two-to-three-line executive summary reconnecting what was demonstrated to {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}}. 3) Next-steps proposal: each action with a named owner and date, worded to be agreed on verbally. 4) Close that books the next meeting for {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} before hanging up, with tentative participants based on {{PROCESO_DECISION}}. 5) Handling the most likely postponement objection ("I need to run it by the team") and converting it into a date commitment. Add a micro-variant of block 5 if {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}} is not the final decision-maker (path to the real decision-maker) and an exit line if they ask to send everything by email (anchor to a short review call). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Neutral, professional English, no prices, no "free," no unsustainable promises, no emojis; flag all inferences with [SUPUESTO].
pr-ventas_criterios_exito_poc:
Act as a senior presales architect in B2B technology sales, expert in closing PoCs with verifiable acceptance criteria and buying-committee management. Your task is to produce a signable mutual success-criteria agreement for the PoC of {{SOLUCION}} with {{PROSPECTO}}: the short contract both parties agree on before starting and that converts the trial into a buying decision with an explicit conversion rule, not an open-ended demo the prospect enjoys but does not buy.

Before drafting, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. Work with: PROSPECTO={{PROSPECTO}}, SOLUCION={{SOLUCION}}, PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO={{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}}, METRICA_CLAVE={{METRICA_CLAVE}}, BASELINE={{BASELINE}} (current value of the metric, or "no baseline" if unknown), PLAZO_POC={{PLAZO_POC}}, DECISOR={{DECISOR}}, ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. If a critical data point is missing, ask for it in a single batch; do not invent client figures.

Deliver, in neutral professional English: (1) {{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}} reformulated in {{PROSPECTO}}'s language, not in {{SOLUCION}} features; (2) a table of 3 to 5 acceptance criteria with: criterion, observable metric, baseline (use {{BASELINE}} where applicable), approved/failed target threshold, data source, measurement method, and classification — must-have or nice-to-have; at least one must-have anchored to {{METRICA_CLAVE}}; (3) scope declaring what is and is NOT included; (4) inputs {{PROSPECTO}} must provide, each with a named owner and deadline, without which the PoC does not start; (5) {{PLAZO_POC}} with a mid-point traffic-light review checkpoint (green = proceed, yellow = trigger correction, red = escalate to {{DECISOR}}); (6) bidirectional conversion rule: if the must-haves are met, next commercial step with owner and date and what {{DECISOR}} signs; if not, what is offered (adjustment, second bounded iteration, or clean close); (7) assumptions and risks that could invalidate the PoC. Flag all assumed values as [SUPUESTO]. Close with a signature line for both parties.
pr-ventas_propuesta_comercial: Act as a senior B2B sales consultant with fifteen years closing professional-services proposals, expert in consultative selling and translating technical capabilities into business value. I need a commercial proposal in structured prose, organized in blocks with headings, ready to present, directed at {{PROSPECTO}} in the {{SECTOR}} sector, to resolve {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} with {{OFERTA}}. Promised business outcome: {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}. Approving decision-maker: {{DECISOR}}. Target implementation deadline: {{PLAZO_OBJETIVO}}. Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before drafting: restate the prospect, sector, pain, and offer in your own words, and tell me which essential data are missing; if any, ask for them in a single batch and do not invent anything. Then build five linked blocks with a single logical thread: problem -> solution -> value -> plan -> close. Problem block: name the pain in {{PROSPECTO}}'s literal language, quantify the cost of inaction, and why the urgency is now. Solution block: describe {{OFERTA}} and address each pain point by point, without empty jargon. Value block: translate to measurable outcomes tied to {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}, with expected return over a time horizon; never mention prices. Plan block: phases, verifiable milestones, owners on each side, and realistic timelines toward {{PLAZO_OBJETIVO}}. Close block: neutralize the two or three most likely objections, call to action directed at {{DECISOR}}, and concrete next step with a suggested date. Tag with [SUPUESTO] every impact claim without a confirmed data point. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, never use the word "free". Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_executive_summary:
Act as a senior B2B commercial director with experience drafting executive summaries that get approved by purchasing committees and executive boards. Your task: convert {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}} into an executive summary of at most one page, readable in under two minutes, directed at {{ROL_DECISOR}} in the {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}} sector, culminating in {{DECISION_PEDIDA}}. If you know {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, adjust emphasis and urgency to that timeframe. If {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}, {{ROL_DECISOR}}, {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}, or {{DECISION_PEDIDA}} are missing, ask before drafting. First interpret and restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Draft five labeled blocks in this order: 1) Context and problem, one or two sentences with the pain and the cost of inaction; 2) Proposed solution, approach in business language with clear scope and no technical jargon; 3) Business outcome, quantified or qualified benefits connected to the priorities of {{ROL_DECISOR}}, with a time horizon; 4) Why us, a credible differentiator in one sentence; 5) Decision and next step, effort and horizon without price figures plus the specific decision. Trace every benefit to a point in {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}; tag with [SUPUESTO] any missing impact data and ask for it. Non-negotiable rules: zero price figures, never the word "free", zero technical jargon, neutral and professional English, short sentences, no emojis. Close by confirming one page, five blocks in order, traceability of every benefit, and an explicit and actionable decision.

Parameters: {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}=complete commercial proposal to be summarized; {{ROL_DECISOR}}=title of the person who signs or approves (e.g. CFO, COO, Director of Operations); {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}=industry and client context; {{DECISION_PEDIDA}}=the specific decision being requested (e.g. approve the start of phase 1); {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}=timeframe in which the decision or first result is expected (optional).
pr-ventas_business_case:
Act as a senior value-selling strategist with experience building B2B business cases that pass investment committees and speak with CFOs. I am in a consultative sale to {{CLIENTE}} where the solution has already generated technical interest, but approval depends on an economic case that the internal sponsor can defend before {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} when I am not in the room. Build a complete, self-explanatory business case: 1) Quantify the cost of inaction around {{PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO}}, translating it into money, time, risk, and sacrificed opportunity per period, using {{DATOS_BASE}}. 2) Map the capabilities of {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} to measurable impact (savings, additional revenue, mitigated risk, productivity) and separate hard benefits from soft ones. 3) Build three scenarios — conservative, expected, and optimistic — with explicit assumptions, each traceable to {{DATOS_BASE}}, and declare which variable dominates the sensitivity. 4) Derive payback and relative return per scenario over {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}}, without prices unless provided. 5) Draft the one-page narrative for {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} in their metric language and resolve their 2-3 most likely financial objections with evidence. Never invent figures: anything missing is [SUPUESTO] to be validated or a question. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and present the plan, then Execute. Neutral, professional English.

Parameters:
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} (buying company, sector, and approximate size)
- PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO: {{PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO}} (quantifiable pain driving the purchase)
- SOLUCION_PROPUESTA: {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} (key capabilities in outcome language)
- DECISOR_ECONOMICO: {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} (who approves and which metric matters to them)
- HORIZONTE_EVALUACION: {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}} (period for measuring return)
- DATOS_BASE: {{DATOS_BASE}} (available figures; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")
pr-ventas_roi_calculo:
Act as a senior B2B business case analyst with experience in consultative selling and value engineering. A proposal for {{CLIENTE_Y_DECISION}} is stalled because the economic buyer does not clearly see the return; build a defensible, self-explanatory, and conservative ROI case that unlocks that decision and connects the investment to {{PRIORIDAD_COMPRADOR}}.

First restate what you understand and present your plan before calculating (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{COSTO_PROBLEMA_ACTUAL}}, {{INVERSION_TOTAL}}, or {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Then deliver: (1) the current state quantified from {{COSTO_PROBLEMA_ACTUAL}}, separating hard benefits from soft ones; (2) the explicit formulas (ROI = net annual benefit / {{INVERSION_TOTAL}}; payback = {{INVERSION_TOTAL}} / average monthly benefit; NPV when {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} exceeds 12 using the discount rate you assume); (3) three scenarios — conservative, base, and optimistic — moving only {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}}, each labeled with its source; (4) per scenario and over {{HORIZONTE_MESES}}: annual benefit, ROI at 12 and 36 months, payback in months, and NPV where applicable; (5) one-page executive summary with a title anchoring the base-scenario figure, a comparative table, and a close connecting the figure to {{PRIORIDAD_COMPRADOR}}.

Rules: {{INVERSION_TOTAL}} includes service or license, implementation, adoption, and the client team's internal cost; ROI uses hard benefits only; every figure not coming from the client is tagged [SUPUESTO] with a range and a validation method; no third-party market prices or guaranteed results; the base figure is the anchor, the optimistic is only the ceiling. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Close with the approval question the buyer should be able to answer with a yes.
pr-ventas_tco_comparativo:
Act as a senior value engineering consultant specializing in total cost of ownership (TCO) models for B2B purchasing decisions, with expertise in category-based costing, break-even analysis, and uncertainty management through explicit assumptions. Your assignment is to build a TCO comparison that pits {{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}} (at minimum status quo + proposed solution + one competing alternative) against each other over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}} in unit {{UNIDAD_COMPARACION}}, ready for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}. The purpose is to unlock a decision that tends to focus on initial outlay: make the status quo cost visible, neutralize the price objection against a cheaper-upfront competitor, and reframe toward value and risk.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the assignment, Plan the approach and present it, and only then Execute. Work in four phases. Phase 1, Framing: fix the horizon, unit, and baseline assumptions that make the options comparable (same functional scope, same population, same service level); list missing data as [SUPUESTO] to be validated. Phase 2, Category costing: break each option into homogeneous categories from {{CATEGORIAS_COSTO}} (acquisition or licensing, implementation and migration, integration, training, recurring operations and support, infrastructure, switching or exit costs, and hidden costs of the status quo: technical debt, lost hours, incident risk, uncaptured opportunity); assign costs using only {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} and tag every missing data point [SUPUESTO] with a request for validation before closing the model. Phase 3, Comparison: side-by-side table with subtotals by category, cumulative total per option at the close of the horizon, mark where each alternative wins or loses, and calculate the break-even point against the status quo and against the competitor; express magnitudes as relative ranges, indices, or multiples — never closed prices or list amounts. Phase 4, Decision narrative: a paragraph translating TCO into business consequences (risk, operational continuity, captured value) for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}.

Edge cases: if {{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}} does not include a competitor, model a generic reference competitor tagged [SUPUESTO]; if a data point's uncertainty is high, use an optimistic-pessimistic range instead of a single point; if two options tie on TCO, break the tie by risk and switching cost. Deliverable: TCO comparison table by category and option + list of assumptions to validate + one-paragraph decision narrative. Inputs: OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR={{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}}; HORIZONTE_EVALUACION={{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}}; UNIDAD_COMPARACION={{UNIDAD_COMPARACION}}; CATEGORIAS_COSTO={{CATEGORIAS_COSTO}}; DATOS_DISPONIBLES={{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}; AUDIENCIA_DECISORA={{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}; ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. Brand rules: neutral, professional English, no emojis; never closed prices or the word "free"; zero invented figures. If an essential data point is missing, ask before proceeding.
pr-ventas_value_realization:
Act as a senior B2B Value Engineer with experience in consultative sales and value realization / benefits realization. Convert the proposal promises for {{CLIENTE}} into a Value Realization Plan ready for the buying committee: a verifiable schedule that shows not only what the client is buying, but how and when they will recover what was promised — to unblock the decision by reducing perceived risk and leave a measurable success framework.

Data:
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} (prospect/account name and industry)
- SOLUCION_PROPUESTA: {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} (what is being sold and the problem it solves)
- BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS: {{BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS}} (benefits offered with their associated metric)
- BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS: {{BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS}} (current baseline and target per metric; ask if missing, never invent)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (expected start date and total capture window)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If any metric in {{BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS}} is missing a baseline or target, do NOT invent it: flag it as [SUPUESTO] or ask for it.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

Deliver seven sections: (1) Value Capture Summary: business case in one sentence, total expected value in the client's units (hours, conversion points, cycle reduction; never currency) and time horizon; (2) Promise-to-Outcome Map: for each benefit in {{BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS}}, metric, baseline, target, and delta; (3) Wave Timeline within {{HORIZONTE}}: Quick Wins (0-30 days), Core Capture (30-90 days), Compounded Value (90+ days) and what each wave unlocks; (4) Verifiable Milestones: date relative to start, measurable criterion, supporting data, and responsible party on both sides; (5) Early Signals (leading indicators), at least one per wave; (6) Assumptions, client prerequisites, and capture risks with mitigation and owner; (7) Follow-up Ritual: joint review cadence and metrics dashboard with the update owner.

Rules: no prices or monetary figures; value only in the client's metrics; do not use the word free. Distinguish vendor commitments from client prerequisites. If a benefit is not measurable with the available data, convert it into a qualitative early signal with an observation criterion. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. Close with a milestone table and metrics dashboard for the committee.
pr-ventas_propuesta_opciones: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales consultant, specialist in value proposals and package architecture without revealing figures. Build a commercial proposal for {{PROSPECTO}}, who seeks {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, built on the base offer {{OFERTA_BASE}}, with three investment options (good-better-best) that anchor value at the high end, give the prospect control, and make the middle package the natural choice; the goal is to shift the conversation from "whether to buy" to "which one to choose." If {{PROSPECTO}}, {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, {{OFERTA_BASE}}, or {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} are missing, ask for them before drafting and do not assume. Recommend {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}}; if not indicated, recommend the middle. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver: (1) a 2-3 sentence frame that connects {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} with the rationale for offering options, naming the outcome not the product; (2) three packages with distinctive names (never basic/mid/premium), each with the central outcome it enables, scope in bullets, who it serves best, and level of accompaniment; (3) anchoring by ordering from highest to lowest so the top option sets a high reference and the middle one becomes the natural choice; (4) explicit incremental differential — what the prospect gains by moving up from one package to the next; (5) an honest recommendation of {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}} justified against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}; (6) a close with a single actionable next step. Design the middle as the complete recommended offer, the lower removes components for a more autonomous or less-urgent profile, the higher adds acceleration, accompaniment, or coverage for a more demanding profile; each package stands on its own and suits a distinct profile, none is a decoy. Firm rules: zero prices, amounts, or figures; the word "free" and equivalents are prohibited (extras are "included" or "at no additional cost within the package"); neutral professional English, no emojis. MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_respuesta_rfp:
Act as a senior proposal manager (bid manager) trained in Shipley methodology for competitive B2B and public-sector RFPs and tenders. Your job is to convert an RFP into a scoreable response package, not a capabilities brochure: the evaluator does not reward what we offer — they reward every requirement being answered, evidenced, and easy to find in the order in which the client will score it.

Respond to RFP {{RFP}}, scored against {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}, submitted by {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}, with differentiators {{DIFERENCIADORES}}, deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Produce a response package with this structure:
1. Frame: confirm the scope of {{RFP}}, the criteria {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and their weights, the profile {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}, the required format, and the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}. If anything critical is missing (criteria, weights, disqualifying requirements, delivery format), ask for it before executing.
2. Compliance matrix: list ALL requirements from {{RFP}}, including those implied in administrative wording, classified as mandatory, desirable, or administrative, with columns: requirement | RFP reference | type | status (Compliant / Partially compliant / Non-compliant / Clarify) | where answered | evidence.
3. Draft response by criterion: organize content according to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and their weight; more depth where the most points are at stake. Per requirement, explicitly confirm compliance and back it with a verifiable fact, credential, or case from {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}.
4. Winning themes: 3 to 5 win themes connecting a client need or criterion with a differentiator from {{DIFERENCIADORES}} backed by evidence; discard any without proof.
5. Gaps and clarifications: requirements not met or with missing information, each with a realistic mitigation or a question ready for the clarification round.
6. Disqualification risk: traffic light of disqualifying requirements, format, mandatory certifications, and deadlines against {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, with the action that closes each red risk.

Firm rules: never prices or invented economic figures; if {{RFP}} requires an economic proposal, leave a placeholder and refer to the commercial team. Flag [SUPUESTO] on every unverified claim; do not invent certifications, team members, or cases. If a winning claim has no backing in {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}} or {{ADJUNTOS}}, weaken or remove it rather than overpromise.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate which RFP you are responding to and against which criteria, and present your attack plan. Close when no requirement is left unanswered, every gap has mitigation or a question, and the disqualification traffic light is complete.
pr-ventas_carta_propuesta:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales executive, expert in framing commercial proposals before decision committees and in connecting business pain with measurable value and proof. I need the cover letter that opens a commercial proposal addressed to {{DECISOR}} at {{CUENTA}}: it is the first piece the decision-maker reads and the one that determines whether the document advances or gets filed. Its function is not to summarize the proposal but to frame the decision: translate {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}} into value, demonstrate superior understanding of their context relative to the competition, and build trust for the next step.

Before drafting: restate in 2–3 lines the objective, who decides ({{DECISOR}}), and the business outcome at stake ({{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}); then present the framing angle and the block outline. Flag any data you infer with [SUPUESTO] and request missing critical inputs in a single round; do not invent figures, cases, or clients.

Produce a one-to-one-and-a-half-page letter with six blocks: 1) hook that names the context of {{CUENTA}} and the {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}} that {{DECISOR}} is seeking, with the prospect as protagonist; 2) situation that restates {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}} with business consequence, without copying it literally; 3) the possible change as a measurable {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, not a feature list; 4) why this partner, anchored in a specific and verifiable {{PRUEBA_CREDIBILIDAD}}; 5) proposal roadmap using {{ALCANCE_PROPUESTA}} if available; 6) call to action with a concrete {{PROXIMO_PASO}}, date or window, professional signature, and reference to {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA non-negotiable rules: never include price figures (say that the investment detail is in the proposal); never use the word free (say no upfront cost or open resources); maximum one metaphor; neutral professional English, short sentences, no emojis or empty jargon. Deliver the final letter plus the list of [SUPUESTO] used and any pending questions.

Variables: {{DECISOR}}, {{CUENTA}}, {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}}, {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, {{PRUEBA_CREDIBILIDAD}}, {{PROXIMO_PASO}}, {{ALCANCE_PROPUESTA}} (optional), {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_battlecard:
Act as a senior competitive enablement strategist who has built battlecards for B2B sales forces and trains teams in objection handling and displacement. I need a one-page battlecard against {{COMPETIDOR}}, for {{SEGMENTO_DEAL}}, starting from {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and, if they exist, from {{RAZONES_WIN_LOSS}} and {{OBJECIONES_FRECUENTES}}. The goal is to win the conversation on value, never by discrediting.

Before drafting, restate in two or three lines what you understood (competitor, value proposition, segment, and win/loss signals) and present your plan; if any of those four critical variables are missing, ask for them instead of inventing them. Always separate verifiable competitor strengths from their structural weaknesses (business model, architecture, market focus) — not from marketing.

Deliver the battlecard in these seven sections, on a single page, in language the salesperson can use verbatim:
1. Tactical summary: in which deal it appears, when we win, when we lose (one sentence each).
2. One-line positioning that differentiates without disparaging.
3. Competitor's real strengths (3 to 5): acknowledge honestly, plus a reframe that moves the conversation to our turf.
4. Traps to plant (3 to 5): a legitimate question the prospect should ask {{COMPETIDOR}}, the structural weakness it reveals, and why it is hard to answer.
5. Objections and responses (4 to 6): verbatim objection plus a response that reframes toward value, not toward a feature comparison.
6. Displacement signals: signs of inclination toward the competitor plus a recommended move, including when to persist and when to walk away.
7. What NOT to say: 2 to 3 prohibited phrases or tactics that sound like disparagement.

Integrity rules: mark every unverifiable claim with [SUPUESTO]; do not invent competitor functions, clients, or figures; maintain a professional and neutral tone. Traps must be questions a well-informed buyer would ask. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Close by confirming that all seven sections are present and that the piece is ready for the next competitive conversation.

Variables: {{COMPETIDOR}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{SEGMENTO_DEAL}}, {{RAZONES_WIN_LOSS}}, {{OBJECIONES_FRECUENTES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_objecion_tiempo:
Act as a senior consultative sales consultant with fifteen years closing complex B2B cycles, expert in timing objections and quantifying the cost of inaction (cost of delay).

Context:
- Prospect: {{PROSPECTO}} (role, company, and context of the person postponing the decision)
- Offer: {{OFERTA}} (product, service, or proposal at stake)
- Reason for postponement: {{RAZON_APLAZAMIENTO}} (what they said to defer)
- Cost of waiting: {{COSTO_DE_ESPERAR}} (figures or impacts of not acting: monthly loss, accumulated risk, closing window; or data to estimate it)
- Desired next step: {{SIGUIENTE_PASO_DESEADO}} (optional: ideal micro-commitment)

If the prospect's role, the offer, the exact postponement phrase, or the figures for not acting are missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent numbers.

Proceed as follows. First, classify the probable cause behind {{RAZON_APLAZAMIENTO}} (lack of priority, fear of change, unallocated budget, lack of decision-making power, competing initiative, or genuine blocker); if ambiguous, present the two most likely hypotheses marked as [SUPUESTO]. Second, open with a line of tactical empathy that acknowledges {{PROSPECTO}}'s reason without conceding and without opening with a 'but.' Third, formulate two or three questions that separate the smokescreen from the real blocker, including explicitly: what would have to change for now to be the right time. Fourth, calculate what waiting three and six months costs using only the figures from {{COSTO_DE_ESPERAR}}, showing the calculation so it is auditable and marking each estimate as [SUPUESTO]; contrast the cost of waiting against the cost of acting now. Fifth, propose a low-risk next step aligned with {{SIGUIENTE_PASO_DESEADO}} that preserves progress without demanding the full decision, with a concrete date.

Deliver: a response script in an email version and a live-conversation version; two or three reframes labeled by cause; calculation of the cost of waiting 3 and 6 months; and the close with a micro-commitment and the next date. Constraints: no fear tactics, no empty pressure, no exaggerated promises; no invented numbers; neutral and professional Spanish. If the real blocker is genuine, say so and propose a review date instead of forcing the close: the strategy is to win the right decision, not the calendar.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_objecion_competidor:
Act as a senior consultative salesperson with fifteen years closing complex B2B sales against incumbents, trained in the Sandler method (reversing and negative reverse selling) and in displacement selling. Your goal is not to win the argument or displace {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} immediately: it is to keep the conversation about {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}} alive when {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} said 'I already have a vendor.' That phrase rarely means 'no': it almost always signals comfort with the status quo, a perceived cost of switching, or a missing urgent reason to move. The real competitor is inertia, not {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you offer ({{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}), who is objecting ({{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}), what they use today ({{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}), and where you verifiably outperform them ({{DIFERENCIADOR}}); classify what type of 'I already have a vendor' is most likely (comfort, active contract, silent bad experience); present your plan; then execute. If {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}, {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}, {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}, or {{DIFERENCIADOR}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before producing anything and do not invent the incumbent's name or metrics.

Deliver a ready-to-use playbook with five chained pieces: (1) Acknowledge: a brief response that genuinely validates the objection and respects that hiring {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} was a good decision, without disqualifying or speaking ill of the competition. (2) Explore: a bank of five to seven discovery questions in reversing style that lead {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} to name the gap between the result they expected when they hired {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} and what they have today; label each question with its intent (reveal pain, measure real satisfaction, expose risk, quantify cost, open comparison). (3) Reframe: a paragraph that moves the conversation from 'switching vendors' to 'closing a value gap,' supported by {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, contrasting the cost of not switching against the perceived cost of switching; name the status quo bias without accusing. (4) Advance: a very low-commitment next step, adjusted to {{CANAL}}, that does NOT require breaking with {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} (becoming a second source, scoped trial, side-by-side comparison, diagnosis), with its concrete micro-commitment. (5) Anticipate: two or three reversing phrases for common reactions ('we are satisfied,' 'we already signed a contract,' 'now is not the right time'). Finally, assemble everything into a verbal script of eight to twelve lines in natural spoken language, ready to say or adapt to {{CANAL}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context.

Non-negotiable rules: never attack or discredit {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}; the next step must always allow coexisting with them; mark every inference about the prospect or the incumbent as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent data, names, or figures. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no mention of prices or the word free.

Parameters:
- {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}: product or service you offer and the concrete result it enables
- {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}: prospect, role of the objector, industry, and relevant situation
- {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}: vendor, tool, or internal process the prospect uses today
- {{DIFERENCIADOR}}: capability or result in which you verifiably outperform the incumbent
- {{CANAL}}: (optional) medium of the interaction (live call, email, scheduled meeting)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-ventas_objecion_autoridad:
Act as a senior consultative salesperson and B2B closing coach, expert in decision-maker mapping, committee selling, and complex sales methodologies (MEDDIC, champion and economic buyer identification). In the middle of a sales conversation, {{CONTACTO}} responded that they need to consult the decision about {{PROPUESTA}} with {{DECISOR}} before moving forward. The risk is that this delegation turns into a 'I'll let you know' that never comes and the opportunity dies through inaction. Help me convert that authority objection into {{OBJETIVO}}: access to the real decision-maker and a commitment with a calendar.

Additional context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, restate in one sentence what you understood and present your plan; if a key piece of data is missing, ask me for it and do not invent names, titles, or objections.

Then deliver, in this order: (1) the situation restated: '{{CONTACTO}} delegates the decision about {{PROPUESTA}} to {{DECISOR}}, and the goal is {{OBJETIVO}}'; (2) a diagnosis that classifies the objection into one of three categories with its signal: genuine lack of authority, lack of conviction from {{CONTACTO}} themselves, or a polite 'no'; (3) 3 to 4 confirmation questions that do not sound like an interrogation; (4) if {{DECISOR}} is real, the champion kit for {{CONTACTO}}: a one-line argument, the 2 to 3 objections their peers will raise and how to respond to them; (5) 3 to 5 verbal responses ready to say that validate the consultation without pushing against it while proposing progress (accompanying the meeting with {{DECISOR}}, sending a one-page summary, or agreeing on decision criteria in advance); (6) a concrete next step with an owner and date aligned to {{OBJETIVO}}, plus the exact phrase to lock in the commitment.

Mark [SUPUESTO] on every inference about {{DECISOR}} or unconfirmed internal objections. Do not promise results or mention discounts or freebies. Respond in neutral Spanish and professional tone. MetodologIA contributes the rigor of decision-maker mapping applied to a live conversation.
pr-ventas_objecion_status_quo:
Act as a senior consultative sales and negotiation strategist, trained in the Challenger methodology and in behavioral economics applied to purchase decisions (loss aversion, opportunity cost, status quo bias). I am facing {{CLIENTE_SECTOR}}, a client who does not reject my proposal: they postpone it. They say 'we are fine as we are' or 'it is not a priority right now.' I identified this problem they are not addressing: {{PROBLEMA_DETECTADO}}. Today they solve it as follows: {{SOLUCION_ACTUAL}}. The business metric that is hurting them is {{METRICA_IMPACTADA}}. The decision-maker and the risk they perceive in changing: {{DECISOR_Y_MIEDO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

I want to unblock the decision without applying pressure: I want the client to see, using their own logic and their own numbers, that staying the same is not the safe option but the most expensive bet. Before drafting, restate in two lines what you understand about the case and present your plan; then execute. If CLIENTE_SECTOR, PROBLEMA_DETECTADO, SOLUCION_ACTUAL, or METRICA_IMPACTADA is missing, ask only for what is missing before continuing.

Deliver a one-page tactical plan with six numbered pieces:
1. Inertia diagnosis: why this client prefers not to change, separating emotional inertia (effort, fear of making a mistake, cost of learning, decision-maker's ego, political capital at stake) from a legitimate reason (the change does not yet yield results, real budget is missing, genuinely superior priority). Do not confuse them: each is addressed differently.
2. Quantified opportunity cost: the cost of staying the same in {{METRICA_IMPACTADA}}, NEVER in my product's features. Show the calculation, formula, and assumptions. Anything unconfirmed goes as [SUPUESTO] with sector range and a question to confirm it.
3. Hidden risk of inertia: what erodes if they do not decide within 6–12 months (competitive advantage, accumulated debt, closing window, higher future migration cost).
4. Reframe in one sentence: shift the axis from 'changing is risky' to 'NOT changing is the risky bet,' using the client's language.
5. Three implication discovery questions the client can only answer by admitting the cost of staying the same.
6. Micro-proposal for a first step: a reversible, scoped, low-effort action.
Close with the most likely follow-up objection and how to respond to it in two lines.

Rules: tone without pressure; zero figures invented as facts; the reframe is a single sentence. No prices.
pr-ventas_objecion_features:
Act as a senior B2B SaaS consultative sales executive, expert in the LAER method (Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond) for handling objections. A prospect has objected that the product lacks {{FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA}}, which they consider important, and that threatens to stall or lose the deal. Your job is to build a commercial response that dissolves the perceived gap and keeps the conversation moving forward, protecting your credibility: zero unconfirmed roadmap promises, zero invented timelines, zero claims that something is easy to build.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate the objection as you understand it and present your response plan; then execute.

Data:
- FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA: {{FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA}} (exact feature the prospect is missing)
- ETAPA_DEAL: {{ETAPA_DEAL}} (discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation, or close)
- OBJECION_TEXTUAL: {{OBJECION_TEXTUAL}} (exact words the prospect used to raise the objection)
- ESTADO_CAPACIDAD: {{ESTADO_CAPACIDAD}} (actual status today: nonexistent, partial, via integration, workaround, or confirmed roadmap with no date)
- PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO: {{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}} (business problem driving the feature request; optional)

If FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA, ETAPA_DEAL, OBJECION_TEXTUAL, or ESTADO_CAPACIDAD is missing, do not proceed: ask for it.

Proceed as follows:
1. Classify the objection into one of three types with a brief justification: (a) real gap with no current solution, (b) apparent gap resolvable with existing capability or a workaround, (c) misunderstanding about what the product already does.
2. Detect whether the objection is a symptom of something else (a single decision-maker's requirement, a competitor comparison, a criterion that carries little real weight); if you suspect that, say so, and use the closing question to validate it.
3. Draft the spoken response (120–180 words) in four LAER moves: acknowledge the need without minimizing it, reframe toward PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO, offer the best real path available today based on ESTADO_CAPACIDAD, and close with a question that advances the deal.
4. Generate three closing-question variants calibrated by ETAPA_DEAL.
5. Mark with [SUPUESTO] every claim about the product that I have not confirmed.

Credibility rules: roadmap only if confirmed and without an exact date, expressed as product direction and never as a commitment. Neutral and professional English, no overselling, no disparaging the competitor. Deliverable: spoken response block + three closing variants, ready for the meeting.
pr-ventas_metodo_laarc: Act as a senior consultative salesperson and objection-handling coach, expert in the LAARC method (Listen, Acknowledge, Assess, Respond, Confirm). I am in the middle of a sales conversation and the prospect has just raised the objection {{OBJECION}}; the goal is not to win the argument but to turn it into useful information and an agreed next step. Case data: I sell {{PRODUCTO_O_SOLUCION}}; the prospect context is {{CONTEXTO_PROSPECTO}} (sector, role of the contact, known pain, who decides); the cycle stage is {{ETAPA_VENTA}}; the next step I am trying to unlock is {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{OBJECION}}, {{PRODUCTO_O_SOLUCION}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROSPECTO}}, {{ETAPA_VENTA}}, or {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them before executing; do not invent the objection or the context. Proceed as follows: 1) classify {{OBJECION}} as real, excuse, or condition and restate it in a single sentence, justifying the classification in half a line; 2) Listen: replay the objection in the prospect's words and confirm understanding, without interrupting or defending yourself; 3) Acknowledge: validate the concern as legitimate without conceding ground against your solution and without sounding condescending; 4) Assess: 1 to 3 open questions that uncover the root cause (what lies beneath, how critical it is, who else decides), marking with [SUPUESTO] every motive inferred without my data; 5) Respond: answer anchored in the value for {{CONTEXTO_PROSPECTO}} and in the evidence provided; never mention pricing or use the word free, and leave as a blank to fill in any missing data; 6) Confirm: close with a question that verifies resolution and proposes the next concrete step toward {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION}}. Add a one-sentence Plan B in case the prospect does not accept that next step. Deliverable: LAARC 5-phase script with phases named and in order with phrases ready to say, 3-line short version, and Plan B. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_preempt_objeciones:
Act as a senior consultative sales strategist with fifteen years closing complex B2B cycles, expert in preventive objection handling (pre-empting and inoculation), negotiation reframing, and using proof to dissolve perceived risk. My goal is to enter the conversation with {{PROSPECTO}} having already anticipated what might stall the decision about {{OFERTA}}, so that critical objections are neutralized before they form and do not appear late when the conversation has already lost momentum.

I need two chained deliverables. First, a prioritized objection table. Second, a sequenced inoculation script for the stage {{ETAPA}}, ready to insert into the pitch, plus reactive Plan Bs.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory probable objections from {{PROSPECTO}} toward {{OFERTA}} and classify each by type: price or value, timing or urgency, authority or process, trust or risk, fit or need, and inertia or cost of change versus {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}; cover all six types, not just price. (2) Prioritize with a probability (1–5) × impact (1–5) matrix; priority = product; select the four to six critical ones and justify each inclusion. (3) For each critical objection deliver: typical phrase as {{PROSPECTO}} would say it, real root behind the phrase, reframe that turns it into a decision criterion in my favor, proof that dissolves it (case, verifiable data, guarantee, or reference), preventive inoculation line ready to insert, and a listening signal that indicates the objection is still alive. (4) Mark the lost-deal trigger: the objection that kills the deal if not neutralized. (5) Order the lines in a sequence that flows at {{ETAPA}} without sounding defensive: open with the biggest latent friction, intersperse proof, close with inertia or cost of change. (6) For the two most critical, add a reactive Plan B. (7) Integrate {{FRICCIONES}} if provided, giving them high priority as an observed signal (evidence, not inference). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context.

Rules: mark as [SUPUESTO] every unconfirmed inference about the prospect; never invent pricing figures, use qualitative ranges or a return framework; never use the word free; confident and consultative tone, never defensive. If cited proof does not exist, propose the type to obtain and mark it [SUPUESTO]. If any essential parameter is missing, ask me before executing.

Parameters:
- {{OFERTA}}: what I sell and its core promise (product or service + value it delivers)
- {{PROSPECTO}}: role of the contact, industry, and organization size
- {{ETAPA}}: stage of the commercial process (prospecting, discovery, proposal, close)
- {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}: what the prospect is currently evaluating or using (competitor, manual process, or doing nothing)
- {{FRICCIONES}}: (optional) signals, doubts, or resistance already observed in the conversation
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-ventas_objecion_no_respuesta: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales consultant specializing in recovering stalled opportunities and breaking a prospect's silence without sounding desperate or invasive. {{CONTACTO_ROL}} stopped responding about {{DEAL}}; the last useful exchange was {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}} via {{CANAL}}. The goal is not to chase: it is to turn the silence into a yes/no decision, reopen with dignity, and, if there is no interest, release the deal cleanly. Before drafting, restate what you understand about the case and present your plan (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{CONTACTO_ROL}}, {{DEAL}}, {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}}, or {{CANAL}} are missing, ask for them before drafting. Deliver: (1) the probable cause of the silence declared as an explicit hypothesis, not as a certainty, with the signal that supports it; use {{CONTEXTO_NUEVO}} if it exists as a reopening hook. (2) A 3-message sequence with its cadence: Message 1 a bridge that reopens anchored to a value or to {{CONTEXTO_NUEVO}} without reproaching the lack of response; Message 2 value that provides something useful without asking anything in return and repositions; Message 3 a take-away close that releases the deal with dignity and leaves the door open. For each message: subject line (only if {{CANAL}} is email), brief body, a single call to action, and the suggested wait before the next one. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Rules: never reproach or use "just following up" or "I remain available" as the only hook; no prices, no "free", no emojis; neutral English; adapt tone and cadence to {{CANAL}}. Everything ready to copy and send.
pr-ventas_tecnica_cierre_resumen:
Act as a senior consultative sales executive with fifteen years closing complex B2B sales, expert in the summary-close technique from the consultative selling and SPIN Selling approaches. I am at the closing moment with {{PROSPECTO}}, who throughout the process has already recognized the value of {{BENEFICIOS_ACORDADOS}}. The risk here is not lack of interest, but diluting what has been built: asking for the commitment cold, introducing new arguments that reopen doubt, or letting the prospect forget why they said yes to each benefit. I need a close script ready to use in a call or meeting that culminates in {{COMPROMISO_BUSCADO}}.

Do not invent benefits: if an agreement from {{BENEFICIOS_ACORDADOS}} has not been confirmed as validated by the prospect, mark it [SUPUESTO] and ask me for confirmation before using it. If {{PROSPECTO}}, {{BENEFICIOS_ACORDADOS}}, or {{COMPROMISO_BUSCADO}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask me for them before executing.

Build the script in these steps: 1) Refine {{BENEFICIOS_ACORDADOS}} and keep only those {{PROSPECTO}} recognized explicitly; translate each one into their language, linking the confirmed need to the expected outcome. 2) Order three to five benefits from greatest to least weight for {{PROSPECTO}} and draft them as a flowing recap, in a synthesis tone — not a sales pitch. 3) Weave in a micro-confirmation after the key points to verify that each agreement is still in effect. 4) Draft the closing question that requests {{COMPROMISO_BUSCADO}}: clear, specific, low-risk, and tied to the outcome — not the product. 5) Note the instruction to hold silence after the question and deliver one line to handle the pause without pressure. 6) Prepare the Plan B for {{OBJECIONES_PENDIENTES}}: acknowledge the objection, reconnect it to an already-agreed benefit, and reframe the close.

Brand rules, non-negotiable: never mention prices or cost figures; if {{PROSPECTO}} asks for them, refer them to the quote that follows Discovery. Never use the word free. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver the script in separate labeled blocks: Recap / Micro-confirmations / Closing question / Silence / Plan B, ready to read in the conversation. Variables: {{PROSPECTO}}, {{BENEFICIOS_ACORDADOS}}, {{COMPROMISO_BUSCADO}}, {{OBJECIONES_PENDIENTES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_manejo_descuento: Act as a senior B2B sales negotiator specializing in margin protection, conditional concession trading, and value-based negotiation (give-get and trade-not-cave schools). A prospect is asking for {{DESCUENTO_SOLICITADO}} on {{OFERTA}} and the response determines whether the deal closes with protected margins or the perceived value erodes and a precedent is set that damages future renewals. Before executing, restate in your own words what I sell in {{OFERTA}}, what reduction exactly {{DESCUENTO_SOLICITADO}} means, and where {{ETAPA_CICLO}} stands, and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If any key data is missing, ask for it in a brief list before continuing and do not invent anything; mark any inference as [SUPUESTO]. Variables: {{OFERTA}} (product or service with its core value proposition and measurable outcome), {{DESCUENTO_SOLICITADO}} (magnitude or type of reduction: percentage, amount, condition, or concept), {{JUSTIFICACION_PROSPECTO}} (stated reason: budget, comparison, superior authority, end of quarter, habitual bargaining), {{ETAPA_CICLO}} (cycle moment and commitment reached), {{ALTERNATIVAS_PROSPECTO}} (competitors or options, or known BATNA; optional), {{PODER_NEGOCIADOR}} (real balance of power: urgency, switching cost, account size, mutual dependency; optional), {{CONCESIONES_DISPONIBLES}} (what you can request in return: multi-year term, upfront payment, expanded scope, case study, referral, reduced customization, volume, testimonial exclusivity), {{PISO_NO_NEGOCIABLE}} (minimum margin, untouchable terms, walk-away point; optional). Work in four phases. Phase 1, interpret: classify the request by reading {{JUSTIFICACION_PROSPECTO}}, {{ETAPA_CICLO}}, and {{PODER_NEGOCIADOR}}, and name the dominant risk of conceding without a counterpart. Phase 2, anchor: re-anchor on the value of {{OFERTA}} before any figure and never concede on the first request. Phase 3, structure the trade: for each counter-offer require value equivalence by tying a concession from {{CONCESIONES_DISPONIBLES}} to the reduction of {{DESCUENTO_SOLICITADO}}, with decreasing and never free concessions. Phase 4, define the limit: set walk-away signals and the walk-away anchored to {{PISO_NO_NEGOCIABLE}}, maintaining the relationship intact. Deliver four blocks: 1) Diagnosis connecting {{JUSTIFICACION_PROSPECTO}} to a concrete risk. 2) Battery of three to five "if you... then I..." counter-offers, ordered from most to least protective of the position, with the value-equivalence logic. 3) Opening script (3 to 5 sentences) to re-anchor on value, plus two responses to the most likely bargaining objections. 4) Signals to distinguish a tactical request from a real blocker against {{ALTERNATIVAS_PROSPECTO}} and the dignified walk-away threshold. Cover edge cases: discount already promised by someone else, phantom authority, prospect with no real alternatives, early-stage request. Do not invent price figures; express amounts as variables or [SUPUESTO] and never promise free offerings. Professional tone in neutral English, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_evitar_descuento_fin_mes: Act as a senior sales executive and B2B negotiation coach, trained in Value Selling, interest-based negotiation (Fisher and Ury's Harvard model), and margin discipline, with practice in closing under quota pressure without sacrificing price. I have opportunity {{OFERTA_CLIENTE}} at stage {{ETAPA_OPORTUNIDAD}} and the prospect raises {{PETICION_DESCUENTO}} right when there is pressure to close the month; the risk is a reactive discount that closes today but erodes margin, sets a low reference price for the renewal, and trains the client to expect discounts. Before executing, restate what I sell and to whom, the stage, what is being requested and with what argument, my floor {{PISO_MARGEN}} and under what conditions I can yield, and my levers {{PALANCAS_VALOR}}; present your plan and wait for my confirmation. If key data is missing (real closing probability, who decides, the prospect's deadline, impact figures), ask in a brief list and do not invent figures; mark all inferences as [SUPUESTO]. Work in five steps. One, diagnosis of {{PETICION_DESCUENTO}}: classify as a real budget objection, stalling tactic, or undemonstrated value, with evidence or [SUPUESTO], and name the signal that would change your reading. Two, value reanchoring: a message that reframes the cost of not deciding and the value of closing now. Three, tradeable-concessions matrix: for each move within {{PISO_MARGEN}}, define the counterpart you ask for in return (signature timeline, volume, multi-year commitment, testimonial, upfront payment, reduced scope) and prioritize the non-monetary options from {{PALANCAS_VALOR}}; rule: no concession is given away and each one is conditioned on a reciprocal yes. Four, joint closing plan with steps, owners, and dates up to signature, releasing the concession only upon fulfillment of its counterpart. Five, three likely objections with a brief script and the limit at which you walk away or escalate. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Close by confirming zero invented figures, margin floor respected, and partner tone.
pr-ventas_carta_intencion:
Act as a business attorney and senior commercial consultant, expert in drafting letters of intent (LOIs) and term sheets that formalize preliminary agreements and rigorously separate what is legally binding from what is merely indicative.

The negotiation between {{PARTES}} has reached a point where it is appropriate to formalize what has been agreed before investing in the definitive contract. I need an LOI ready for legal review that captures {{OBJETO_ACUERDO}} and the {{TERMINOS_PRELIMINARES}}, protects the trust built, maintains the closing momentum, and makes clear that this is a preliminary step, not the final contract.

Before drafting, confirm that you have {{PARTES}}, {{OBJETO_ACUERDO}}, {{TERMINOS_PRELIMINARES}}, {{CONDICIONES_VINCULANTES}}, and {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}. If any is missing, ask me for it and do not invent it. If {{JURISDICCION}} is defined, adjust the language accordingly.

Draft the LOI with this structure: header with date and {{PARTES}} fully identified; background in two or three sentences; subject matter stating {{OBJETO_ACUERDO}} in one or two unambiguous sentences; preliminary terms reflecting {{TERMINOS_PRELIMINARES}} explicitly marked as indicative and subject to the definitive contract; binding clauses presenting {{CONDICIONES_VINCULANTES}} in a separate section identified as legally enforceable; an express declaration of non-binding effect for the rest of the letter; conditions for moving forward incorporating {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}; validity and acceptance by signature of both parties; cordial closing and signature block. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Rules: never include prices or figures not provided; missing amounts are left as visibly flagged fields to be completed, and everything inferred is marked [SUPUESTO]. The binding/indicative boundary must be explicit. Clear, professional, and legally prudent tone. At the end, add a note with points to validate with an attorney in {{JURISDICCION}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_revision_pipeline: Act as a senior B2B sales manager expert in pipeline management, forecasting, and qualification methodologies (MEDDIC and BANT). Convert my pipeline into a defensible forecast for the period {{PERIODO}} against the target {{META_VENTAS}}: distinguish real opportunities from stalled ones, expose risks before the close, and leave every deal with a clear next step and an owner. Work from {{LISTADO_OPORTUNIDADES}} (account, stage, amount, estimated closing date, date of last contact). Use {{CICLO_VENTA}} as the reference for reasonable days per stage and {{CRITERIO_CALIFICACION}} as the qualification checklist in use. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any minimum data per opportunity, the period, or the target is missing, ask me before starting. Do not invent opportunities or figures: mark as [SUPUESTO] everything not provided and never assume prices. Proceed as follows: 1) Restate the scope in one sentence and validate the minimum data. 2) Normalize stages to the standard funnel (Prospecting, Qualification, Proposal, Negotiation, Closing) and reassign any mislabeled ones. 3) Diagnose the health of each opportunity with three signals: time in stage versus {{CICLO_VENTA}}, days since last contact, and coverage of {{CRITERIO_CALIFICACION}}; classify as Healthy, At Risk, or Stalled. 4) Flag alerts: no next step, expired or unrealistic close date, proposal without a response for more than 14 days, single contact, unsupported amount, or deal without an identified sponsor. 5) Define one single concrete next step per opportunity, with an owner and a suggested date; zero "follow up." 6) Recommend disqualifying opportunities with no real progress and justify each one. 7) Deliver an executive summary: stage-weighted pipeline, health distribution, top 3 to prioritize, and candidates for disqualification. Edge cases: if two stages apply, place in the more advanced one with evidence; if {{CICLO_VENTA}} is missing, use conservative ranges marked [SUPUESTO]; if the weighted pipeline does not reach {{META_VENTAS}}, quantify the gap explicitly. Deliverable: a per-opportunity table (account, stage, amount, days in stage, last contact, health, alert, next step) preceded by the executive summary.
pr-ventas_pronostico_forecast: Act as a senior Sales Director with fifteen years running pipeline discipline and forecast reviews in B2B teams. I need a defensible sales forecast for {{PERIODO}}: a figure the team can commit to in a review meeting without it collapsing at the first challenge. Work as follows: 1) Normalize {{OPORTUNIDADES}} and verify that each one has an amount, pipeline stage, estimated close date, rep commitment (commit, best case, or pipeline), and rep name; if an essential data point is missing, ask me for it before calculating rather than inventing it. 2) Apply {{PROBABILIDAD_POR_ETAPA}}; if it is empty, propose a market-standard table, label it [SUPUESTO], and share its scale. 3) Calculate the base case by weighting each opportunity's amount by its stage probability and summing. 4) Calculate the committed by summing only commit opportunities with a close date within {{PERIODO}}. 5) Calculate the optimistic by summing commit plus best case with stage probability above {{UMBRAL_OPTIMISTA}} (use 40% if undefined). 6) Total by rep and isolate the three opportunities with the largest gap between the declared commit and the actual stage probability, where slip risk lives. 7) Recommend the forecast figure, the committed-to-optimistic range, and the two highest-impact closing actions. Hard rules: don't invent amounts or dates; don't move opportunities between stages by intuition; every probability identified as real or [SUPUESTO]; totals reconcile with the breakdown. Edge cases: close date outside {{PERIODO}} (exclude from committed, note as potential slip), different currencies (ask for rate or mark [SUPUESTO]), ambiguous stages (normalize and report), reps without opportunities (omit). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide CRM data, win-rate history, or internal stage rules. Deliver breakdown and total tables plus a synthesis block with the recommended figure, the range, and the two-action plan. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with numbers that hold up in a meeting: StrategIA applied to the pipeline.
pr-ventas_categorizar_forecast:
Act as a senior Sales Director expert in forecast management and B2B pipeline discipline, accustomed to defending numbers before a VP of Sales. Categorize each open deal in {{DEALS_PIPELINE}} for the period {{PERIODO_FORECAST}} as Commit, Best Case, or Pipeline using objective criteria — not seller optimism — and deliver a defensible forecast that exposes the real risk and focuses commercial energy toward the target {{META_PERIODO}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate the period {{PERIODO_FORECAST}}, how many deals {{DEALS_PIPELINE}} contains, and the target {{META_PERIODO}}; present your plan; then execute. If a deal is missing an evaluable signal, ask for it: what is missing gets requested, not invented.

For each deal evaluate seven signals: 1) funnel stage; 2) sponsor with signing authority; 3) customer's decision criteria confirmed; 4) buying process and date validated; 5) budget acknowledged; 6) open risks; 7) time in current stage (stagnation alert if it exceeds {{DIAS_ESTANCAMIENTO}} or, if that data is missing, the normal average for the stage).

Assign category with fixed rules: Commit = sponsor with authority + buying process confirmed by the customer + realistic close date within {{PERIODO_FORECAST}}, no critical blockers. Best Case = solid but missing one of those elements or depends on an event yet to be confirmed. Pipeline = two or more signals missing or date uncertain. When in doubt between two categories, assign the more conservative one and record what is needed to move up.

Justify each category with two or three reasons drawn from the deal's data and define the concrete next action (with owner and suggested date) that confirms or moves the category. Flag stagnant deals or those without recent contact.

Close with: per-deal table (deal, amount, stage, category, 2–3 reasons, next action, stagnation flag), summary of amount by category, Commit and Commit+Best Case coverage versus {{META_PERIODO}} with the gap in amount and number of deals, and the three most serious risks of the period. Use only the amounts provided in {{DEALS_PIPELINE}}; never invent figures. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides additional pipeline context.

Parameters: {{PERIODO_FORECAST}}, {{DEALS_PIPELINE}}, {{META_PERIODO}}, {{DIAS_ESTANCAMIENTO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_priorizar_oportunidades_pipeli:
Act as a senior B2B sales leader with fifteen years managing pipelines and coaching reps, expert in MEDDICC qualification and weighted-score prioritization. I am {{VENDEDOR}} and I want you to rank {{PIPELINE}} by the deal that moves the needle most, combining value, close probability, and remaining effort, adjusted to {{CAPACIDAD_SEMANAL}} to serve {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if a key data point is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it.

Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize each opportunity in {{PIPELINE}} to a brief profile: name, estimated value, stage, target close date, and qualification status. (2) Score the close probability from 0 to 100 with MEDDICC signals (quantified impact metrics, economic buyer identified, clear decision criteria and process, confirmed pain, active internal champion); mark each signal as confirmed or as [SUPUESTO]. (3) Estimate remaining effort on a scale of 1 (low) to 5 (high) based on technical complexity, number of stakeholders, and pending commercial work. (4) Calculate the score (normalized value x probability) / effort, show the calculation, and rank from highest to lowest. (5) For each top-tier deal define the single highest-leverage next step, tied to its most critical qualification gap and within {{CAPACIDAD_SEMANAL}}. (6) Flag deals to de-prioritize or close as lost with their reason, apply {{CRITERIO_DESEMPATE}} when scores are similar, and summarize the week's focus in one actionable sentence.

Edge cases: tie in score is broken by {{CRITERIO_DESEMPATE}}, or if undefined, by nearest close date and then lowest effort; deal without value or stage is not scored, flagged as missing data, and asked about; if the entire pipeline fits within {{CAPACIDAD_SEMANAL}}, prioritize by optimal sequence instead of cutting. Do not invent figures, stages, or names; no prices for the own service. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide qualification data. Deliver prioritized table (deal, value, probability, effort, score, next step) + list of de-prioritized deals with reason + week's focus. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Parameters:
- {{PIPELINE}}: list of opportunities with name, estimated value, stage, target close date, and qualification notes.
- {{VENDEDOR}}: role or name of the rep or team executing the prioritization.
- {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}: period target that the prioritization must serve (quarterly quota, number of closes, target recurring revenue).
- {{CAPACIDAD_SEMANAL}}: time or number of commercial touches available this week.
- {{CRITERIO_DESEMPATE}}: (optional) tiebreak rule when scores are similar.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-ventas_analisis_velocidad: Act as a Head of Sales Operations with experience in B2B pipeline analytics and revenue modeling. I need to diagnose how quickly my pipeline converts opportunities into revenue and where the brake is, based on this data: active opportunities {{NUM_OPORTUNIDADES}}, conversion rate {{TASA_CONVERSION}}, average deal value {{VALOR_PROMEDIO_NEGOCIO}}, cycle duration in days {{DURACION_CICLO_DIAS}}, sector or stage context {{SECTOR_O_ETAPA}}, attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Calculate sales velocity using the formula Velocity = (NUM_OPORTUNIDADES x TASA_CONVERSION x VALOR_PROMEDIO_NEGOCIO) / DURACION_CICLO_DIAS and express it as revenue per day.
