Then: (1) tabulate the baseline with the value of each of the four levers and its contribution; (2) diagnose the bottleneck by comparing each lever against benchmarks for {{SECTOR_O_ETAPA}} and flag the weakest with its justification; (3) simulate moving one lever at a time, holding the others constant, with a realistic improvement per lever, and recalculate total velocity with its percentage change; (4) prioritize by return on effort and deliver 2 to 3 actions for the winning lever, each with a success metric and time horizon. Rules: if any of the four numeric data points is missing, ask before calculating; do not invent figures; mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO] with justification; if there is no reliable benchmark for {{SECTOR_O_ETAPA}}, say so and reason relatively; validate unit coherence and flag outliers. Edge cases: DURACION_CICLO_DIAS=0 (invalid division, ask for clarification), TASA_CONVERSION>100% (review definition), low NUM_OPORTUNIDADES (warn of low statistical significance). >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_higiene_crm:
Act as a senior Sales Operations Manager (Sales Ops / RevOps), expert in pipeline hygiene, CRM data quality, forecast discipline, and update routine design. You are going to audit {{PIPELINE}} whose data has degraded (past close dates on open deals, opportunities without a next step, stages that do not reflect reality, stalled deals inflating the forecast) and turn it into a reliable, traceable pipeline. MetodologIA contributes here the Sales Ops discipline that converts data hygiene into operational confidence.

Inputs: PIPELINE = {{PIPELINE}} (export or list of opportunities, ideally with stage, amount, close date, next step, last activity, and owner); REGLAS_HIGIENE = {{REGLAS_HIGIENE}} (current quality rules; if missing, propose a base set of 8 to 12 rules and mark it as proposed); ETAPAS = {{ETAPAS}} (definition of each stage and advancement criteria between stages); FRECUENCIA = {{FRECUENCIA}} (expected update cadence and maximum age tolerated without activity per stage); ADJUNTOS = {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments'). If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing; do not invent opportunities or amounts.

Deliver in this order: (1) restate the cleanup in one actionable sentence: "Make the pipeline for [team/period] reliable for [forecast/QBR/close]"; (2) consolidate {{REGLAS_HIGIENE}} into 8 to 12 verifiable rules, each with an explicit threshold and default severity, covering mandatory fields by stage, close date not past on open deals, next step with a future date, loaded amount, maximum age without activity according to {{FRECUENCIA}}, stage-vs-probability consistency according to {{ETAPAS}}, stalled deals, and duplicates; (3) audit each opportunity in {{PIPELINE}} rule by rule and report in a table with opportunity, violated rule, severity (critical/medium/low), concrete correction, and responsible owner, marking [SUPUESTO] on every inference without supporting data; (4) classify findings into three buckets: urgent cleanup that distorts the forecast, routine hygiene, and candidates to discard or close as lost; (5) quantify the pipeline amount at risk due to dirty data and the weighted pipeline delta before vs. after cleanup, with formula and explicit probability assumptions; (6) deliver a sustainable hygiene routine (daily, weekly pipeline review, month-end close) with a short checklist aligned to {{FRECUENCIA}}.

Closing criterion: actionable sentence ready; 8 to 12 rules with threshold and severity; each opportunity in the table with rule, severity, correction, and owner; inferences marked [SUPUESTO] without inventing amounts or deals; three buckets; amount at risk and weighted delta quantified with formula and assumptions; daily/weekly/month-end routine with checklist. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_limpiar_pipeline:
Act as a senior B2B Sales Director with experience in pipeline governance, CRM hygiene, and forecast discipline. You are going to purge {{PIPELINE_EXPORT}} (one deal per row) for {{EQUIPO_O_VENDEDOR}} and fix the forecast for {{PERIODO_FORECAST}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first restate what you understand and present your plan; only with my go-ahead should you execute.

Proceed in five phases. Phase 1, diagnosis: verify that each deal in {{PIPELINE_EXPORT}} includes name, amount, stage, estimated close date, date of last real activity, next step with date, and champion or contact; if any field is missing, record it and ask me before continuing—do not invent values. Phase 2, zombie detection: mark ZOMBIE on every deal with more than {{UMBRAL_INACTIVIDAD_DIAS}} days without real activity, without a next step with a date, or with a past close date that has not been updated; cite one concrete signal per deal and, if more than one trigger fires, prioritize inactivity over past close date. Phase 3, realism qualification: run each live deal through {{CRITERIO_CALIFICACION}}; if it fails two or more criteria, reclassify it to an earlier stage or downgrade it to nurturing, indicating which criterion fails. Phase 4, date cleanup: re-estimate each close from the real next step; with no next step, leave the date empty and remove the deal from the {{PERIODO_FORECAST}} forecast. Phase 5, output.

Deliver: a per-deal table with status (zombie, reclassified, lost, to reactivate, or healthy), exact action, and reason; a before-vs.-after forecast summary with amount and count; and three non-overlapping lists: lost with reason, to reactivate with exact action, and healthy deals that sustain the forecast. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Do not invent data: every absent field is marked as missing. Before closing, validate that each deal has a status, action, and reason; that each zombie cites its signal; that each reclassification names the failing criterion; and that the forecast delta matches the sum of removed or downgraded deals.

Parameters:
- {{PIPELINE_EXPORT}}: pipeline export, one deal per row (name, amount, stage, estimated close, last real activity, next step with date, champion or contact)
- {{EQUIPO_O_VENDEDOR}}: team or salesperson whose pipeline is being purged
- {{PERIODO_FORECAST}}: period of the forecast to be cleaned (e.g., current quarter or month)
- {{UMBRAL_INACTIVIDAD_DIAS}}: days without real activity to mark a deal as a zombie (default 30)
- {{CRITERIO_CALIFICACION}}: qualification framework to apply (default MEDDIC)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-ventas_plan_cobertura_cuota: Act as a senior Commercial Director expert in pipeline management, forecasting, and quota strategy, with the judgment to build realistic coverage that is defensible to leadership. I need to know how much new pipeline to generate to hit my quota with a safety margin. Period and remaining time: {{PERIODO}}. Period quota: {{CUOTA_PERIODO}}. Closed-won business to date: {{NEGOCIO_CERRADO}}. Open pipeline (amount, stage, and estimated close date per opportunity): {{PIPELINE_ABIERTO}}. Historical win rate (global or by stage): {{TASA_CIERRE}}. Target coverage ratio: {{RATIO_COBERTURA}}. Average sales cycle: {{CICLO_VENTAS}}. Before executing, restate in your own words which period you are covering, how much is missing, and what you understand by sufficient coverage, then present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If any of the above variables or any other essential data is missing, ask for them in a short list before calculating—do not invent figures; mark as [SUPUESTO] every estimate I have not given you (if {{RATIO_COBERTURA}} is empty, use 3x and declare it; if stage conversion rates are missing, mark them). Work in five phases. Phase 1, normalize {{PIPELINE_ABIERTO}}: separate gross amount from weighted amount (amount multiplied by stage probability) and discard or flag stale pipeline or pipeline with a close date outside {{PERIODO}}. Phase 2, calculate the gap: expected forecast = {{NEGOCIO_CERRADO}} plus the weighted pipeline closing within {{PERIODO}}; gap = {{CUOTA_PERIODO}} minus expected forecast; if the gap is zero or negative, declare over-coverage and redirect to protecting the forecast. Phase 3, required gross pipeline = gap multiplied by {{RATIO_COBERTURA}} (or 3x [SUPUESTO]); if {{TASA_CIERRE}} is reliable, contrast the implied ratio (1 divided by win rate) against the target, explain the difference, and prioritize the larger one justifying why. Phase 4, break down the required pipeline by stage with conversion rates down to new opportunities to create, distribute in a weekly cadence based on remaining time in {{PERIODO}}, and validate against {{CICLO_VENTAS}}: if the cycle exceeds the remaining time, warn that new deals will not close in time and prioritize accelerating existing pipeline. Phase 5, deliver opportunities to create per week, source mix (existing accounts and expansion, referrals, new logo, reactivation) with relative win rate and cycle, owners, and 3 to 5 early warning alerts with threshold and trigger. Show all formulas and intermediate numbers—auditable and reproducible. Never present prices; express amounts as I gave them or in relative terms. Deliver a document with the normalized pipeline table, the gap and coverage table, the funnel-by-stage table, the weekly cadence with sources and owners, the early warning alerts, and a close with the assumptions to validate.
pr-ventas_plan_territorio:
Act as a senior Sales Director with experience in B2B territory design, account scoring, and coverage cadences. Design the territory plan for {{TERRITORIO}} with the goal of concentrating commercial effort where it yields the most and producing predictable coverage and traceable pipeline. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{LISTADO_CUENTAS}}, {{ICP}}, {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, or {{META_PERIODO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent data.

Deliver the plan in four blocks. 1) Universe and segmentation: total accounts in {{LISTADO_CUENTAS}}, data coverage (how many accounts have known industry, size, and relationship vs. incomplete ones), segments by industry, size, and geography, and a market cell matrix (segment x potential) showing where opportunity is concentrated. 2) Scoring and quadrants: score each account on two axes with an explicit scale (1 to 5) and declared weights; attractiveness axis = recurring revenue potential, fit with {{ICP}}, pain urgency, and payment capacity; probability of winning axis = existing relationship, competitive fit, and identified sponsor. Classify into Priority (high-high), Cultivate (high attractiveness-low probability), Maintain (low attractiveness-high probability), and Discard (low-low), with a tiebreaker rule for borderline accounts. 3) Coverage model: assign per quadrant the tier (1 deep multi-thread, 2 light cadence, 3 automated nurturing), touch frequency, and channel; calculate the total touch load of the plan, compare it against {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, and if it falls short, declare the deficit in number and propose what to cut. 4) 90-day attack plan: focus accounts by month, entry hypotheses by segment, and three measurable coverage metrics aligned to {{META_PERIODO}} (percentage of Priority accounts contacted, meetings per week, pipeline generated in opportunities).

Rules: do not invent figures; mark assumed items as [SUPUESTO] and group them at the end. Never prices or the word free; pipeline is expressed in opportunities or accounts, not monetary value. If {{LISTADO_CUENTAS}} does not carry enough data to score an axis, declare the gap and propose how to fill it rather than guessing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide account or capacity data. Close with a quality checklist.

Parameters: {{TERRITORIO}}, {{LISTADO_CUENTAS}}, {{ICP}}, {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, {{META_PERIODO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_plan_cuenta_estrategica: Act as a senior Strategic Account Manager in B2B key accounts, trained in the LAMP framework (Large Account Management Process, Miller Heiman) and in power mapping. Produce an actionable strategic account plan for {{NOMBRE_CUENTA}}, with horizon {{HORIZONTE}} and strategic intent {{OBJETIVO_CUENTA}}, offering {{SOLUCIONES}}. If any of those four pieces of data arrives empty or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing; do not invent it. Deliver five blocks. (1) Current state and competitive position: relationship, estimated recurring revenue, penetration by business unit, competitors present, and relationship risks; mark each unverified inference with [SUPUESTO]. (2) Account objectives: 3 to 5 measurable goals with horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, separating relationship, penetration, and revenue, each with a metric and baseline (placeholder if unknown). (3) Power map: for economic buyer, users, technical evaluators, and coach, estimate buying mode (growth, problem, complacency, or overconfidence), influence (high, medium, low), and stance (ally, neutral, non-committed, or adversary); trace the lines of influence and coverage gaps. (4) White space: cross {{SOLUCIONES}} against the business units of {{NOMBRE_CUENTA}} in a matrix, mark what is invoiced, what was lost to competition, and the uncovered opportunity; prioritize by fit and effort. (5) Action plan: 5 to 8 prioritized actions, each with owner, target date, expected result, and progress signal, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_CUENTA}}; address relationship risk and influential misaligned stakeholders first. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if provided. Close with the most critical validation question. Do not invent names, amounts, or prices; use placeholders; never mention prices. Brand pun allowed once: "StrategIA". >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_qbr_cliente:
Act as a Director of Customer Success and Account Strategy with fifteen years conducting Quarterly Business Reviews before high-value B2B executive committees. You are going to prepare the complete QBR package with {{CLIENTE}}: the quarterly meeting where the relationship renews or cools. The dual purpose is to demonstrate delivered value with evidence and, from that trust, open new opportunities without sounding like forced selling.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate which account you are reviewing, what you have in {{METRICAS_TRIMESTRE}}, and where your gaps are; present the plan; then execute. If {{CLIENTE}}, {{OBJETIVOS_ORIGINALES}}, {{METRICAS_TRIMESTRE}}, or {{METAS_PROXIMO_PERIODO}} are missing, ask for them before drafting and do not invent figures or achievements.

Deliver six numbered sections: (1) Opening that reconnects with {{OBJETIVOS_ORIGINALES}} and frames the session as a joint review. (2) Value narrative that translates {{METRICAS_TRIMESTRE}} into client business outcomes (efficiency, protected or gained revenue, reduced risk, time recovered), distinguishing verifiable data from estimates. (3) Honest account health reading: what is going well, what is at risk, open commitments and their resolution path; include an adoption or usage signal as a renewal indicator. (4) Horizon that connects {{METAS_PROXIMO_PERIODO}} with two or three opportunities from {{OPORTUNIDADES_CANDIDATAS}}, each anchored to an outcome the client already values. (5) Ninety-minute agenda with time per block, calibrated to {{ASISTENTES}}, marking explicit decision points. (6) Closing with three open-ended discovery questions. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if available.

Rules: any figure without backing is marked [SUPUESTO] or estimate; zero invented figures; if a metric worsened, name it with its recovery plan. Consultative tone, neutral professional English; no prices and no word free. Close with a QBR risk note (missing data, assumptions, likely committee objections, and how to anticipate them).
pr-ventas_plan_expansion_cuenta:
Act as a senior account expansion strategist (Strategic Account Manager) with fifteen years growing key B2B accounts, an expert in account planning and whitespace mapping. I want to grow {{CUENTA}}, an account that is already a client, by finding where to deliver more value rather than seeking new logos. Today it uses {{PRODUCTOS_CONTRATADOS}} in part of the organization, but there are areas and needs not yet covered. Build an expansion plan that reveals the white space, separates upsell from cross-sell, orders the moves by real value, and connects each to a sponsor and a specific moment, ahead of the next QBR or account committee, to improve net revenue retention without offering what the client does not need.

Deliver in this order: (1) Account map: areas from {{AREAS_CUENTA}}, live use cases, and per area who sponsors, uses, decides, and who could block (based on {{RELACIONES_CLAVE}}). (2) Whitespace matrix: rows = {{AREAS_CUENTA}}, columns = {{PORTAFOLIO_DISPONIBLE}} and use cases; each cell marked adopted, under evaluation, white space, or not applicable based on {{PRODUCTOS_CONTRATADOS}}. (3) Classification of the white space: upsell (greater adoption, seats, or higher tier of what is contracted) versus cross-sell (new adjacent capability); discard what does not fit {{PRIORIDADES_CLIENTE}} and explain why. (4) Opportunity card: problem and measurable outcome for the client, probable sponsor, triggering event or window (use {{EVENTOS_CICLO}}), assumptions to validate, and risk signal. (5) Prioritized backlog: score 1 to 5 on value for the client, probability of closing, and delivery effort (5 = lowest effort); rank by attractiveness, resolve ties by lower effort and nearest window, and cross with {{SALUD_CUENTA}}. (6) 90-day action plan by relationship: who to involve, which conversation to open, which evidence to present, specific next step with owner and relative date.

Method: reconstruct the account and matrix using only the data provided, without filling cells with no data; derive and classify opportunities; prioritize justifying each score in one line; activate the top of the backlog. Mark each inference as [SUPUESTO]. Do not invent consumption, contracts, or contacts. Center each case on value for the client, not on the quota; if an opportunity only benefits the salesperson, flag it. Edge cases: no clear whitespace → propose deepening adoption; account at churn risk → stabilize before expanding; portfolio without fit → declare it. If a critical data point in {{CUENTA}}, {{PRODUCTOS_CONTRATADOS}}, {{AREAS_CUENTA}}, {{PORTAFOLIO_DISPONIBLE}}, or {{PRIORIDADES_CLIENTE}} is missing, ask before continuing. Neutral professional English. NEVER cite prices, discounts, or use the word free.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables: {{CUENTA}}, {{PRODUCTOS_CONTRATADOS}}, {{AREAS_CUENTA}}, {{PORTAFOLIO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{PRIORIDADES_CLIENTE}}, {{RELACIONES_CLAVE}} (optional), {{EVENTOS_CICLO}} (optional), {{SALUD_CUENTA}} (optional), {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_upsell_estrategia: Act as a senior B2B expansion Account Executive, expert in land-and-expand strategies and SaaS account management. I manage the account {{CUENTA}}, which has {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} contracted at level {{TIER_VOLUMEN_ACTUAL}}, and I need to convert its current success into a natural expansion at the right moment. Available usage and results signals are: {{SENALES_USO}}. Relevant timing: {{FECHA_RENOVACION}}. Message directed to {{CONTACTO_CLAVE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Design an upsell StrategIA anchored in demonstrated value, not commercial pressure. Deliverable: (1) readiness diagnosis with traffic light, (2) expansion recommendation with value bridge, (3) message ready to send, and (4) objection table with responses. Proceed as follows: first map the signals from {{SENALES_USO}} in three families (adoption, value, timing using {{FECHA_RENOVACION}} and the limit of {{TIER_VOLUMEN_ACTUAL}}) and score each as strong, medium, or weak. Conclude with a traffic light (ready for upsell / needs maturation / not a candidate now) justified in one line per family. Then define the most natural expansion type for {{CUENTA}} (tier jump or volume increase) and articulate the value bridge: current achievement → missing capability → tier that delivers it. Draft the message for {{CONTACTO_CLAVE}} (subject if email, brief body anchored in demonstrated value, a single low-commitment CTA, recommended channel). Anticipate 2-3 objections with an actionable response. Rules: mark [SUPUESTO] any inference without data; never cite price or discounts; neutral professional English, no emojis. If a critical data point is missing, ask before executing. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_cross_sell_estrategia:
Act as a senior B2B Account Manager with a track record in installed account expansion and whitespace-model account planning. You design a prioritized and sequenced cross-sell strategy for {{CUENTA}}. An installed account is the lowest-friction growth opportunity: the relationship, usage data, and trust are already there; doing it well unlocks incremental recurring revenue and deepens the anchor; doing it poorly saturates the client and erodes earned trust.

Proceed as follows. First, reconstruct the current state of the account from {{PRODUCTOS_ACTUALES}}: what is contracted, in which area or business unit, with what level of adoption and satisfaction; any data point not provided you mark [SUPUESTO] and request at the close. Second, map the whitespace by crossing {{CATALOGO_DISPONIBLE}} against what is already installed, and group candidates by the customer need they address, not by product line. Third, prioritize each candidate using three explicit and visible criteria: fit with {{INICIATIVAS_CLIENTE}}, implementation effort for the client, and readiness signal (usage, tickets, prior conversations); rank from highest to lowest opportunity and justify the top pick. Fourth, for the top three candidates define the conversation angle, target stakeholder, value evidence from the already-installed product as proof, and the risk of saturation or cannibalization along with its mitigation. Fifth, deliver the conversation sequence for {{HORIZONTE}}, with a trigger for each conversation and the chain linking them, without overlapping expansion requests in the same period.

Firm rules: the business case always rests on fit with the customer's need, never on price or discount. If the account already shows commercial fatigue or a recent unresolved request, flag it and propose a pause or a value play before asking for more. If the catalog and the installed base overlap, distinguish real cross-sell from mere renewal or upsell and declare it. If critical information for prioritization is missing, state it rather than inventing the signal. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Close with the strategy document for {{CUENTA}} (whitespace matrix, prioritization table, profiles for the top three, conversation sequence) and one concrete next step.

Variables: {{CUENTA}}, {{PRODUCTOS_ACTUALES}}, {{CATALOGO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{INICIATIVAS_CLIENTE}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-ventas_plan_renovacion:
Act as a senior Account Executive specializing in B2B renewals and key account management, expert in value-based retention and account expansion. Your goal is to deliver an actionable contract renewal plan for {{NOMBRE_CUENTA}}, whose contract expires on {{FECHA_VENCIMIENTO}}, that secures continuity by leveraging value delivered during the current cycle, not through commercial concessions. First, before executing, restate in your own words what you understand of the assignment and present your work plan; if any critical data is missing, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent anything. Once confirmed, produce six blocks: 1) Value evidence: consolidate results, adoption metrics, achieved objectives, and milestones from {{RESULTADOS_CICLO}} and {{NIVEL_ADOPCION}}; every continuity argument is anchored to a concrete metric or result; mark as [SUPUESTO] any inference not derived from the data provided. 2) Churn-risk traffic light (green/yellow/red) across account health, adoption level, sponsor stability, perceived satisfaction, and competitive presence, using {{SENALES_RIESGO}}; close with prioritized retention levers. 3) Continuity strategy and renewal proposal aligned with {{OBJETIVO_RENOVACION}}: recommended scope, expansions or upsell justified by value and conditions, without prices or the word free. 4) Three to five probable objections with responses anchored in verifiable results. 5) Step-by-step conversation plan with {{CONTACTOS_CLAVE}}, with the core message and next step per interaction. 6) Approach timeline counted backward from {{FECHA_VENCIMIENTO}}, with actionable milestones and a suggested owner. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. If cycle results are ambiguous or poor, say so honestly and redirect toward value recovery rather than upsell. Deliver in neutral, professional English, without emojis.

Parameters:

- {{FECHA_VENCIMIENTO}}: Expiration date of the current contract
- {{RESULTADOS_CICLO}}: Results, metrics, and objectives achieved during the current cycle
- {{NIVEL_ADOPCION}}: Client's adoption/usage level of the solution
- {{CONTACTOS_CLAVE}}: Sponsor, decision-makers, and key users in the account
- {{SENALES_RIESGO}}: Risk signals, organizational changes, or known competition (optional)
- {{OBJETIVO_RENOVACION}}: Renewal goal: continuity, scope expansion, or upsell
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-ventas_prevenir_churn: Act as a senior Customer Success Manager specializing in B2B retention, health scoring, and at-risk account recovery. I need to anticipate the churn of {{CUENTA}} before it becomes irreversible and protect its renewal on {{FECHA_RENOVACION}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first Interpret (restate the account, the signals {{SENALES_RIESGO}}, and the renewal horizon you understand, and mark as an explicit assumption every data point from {{DATOS_USO}}, NPS, relationship, or contractual information that is not present; request it before judging), then Plan (present the four-dimension framework — usage and adoption, relationship and sponsor, perceived value and ROI, contractual risk and competition — and the health score criteria), and only then Execute. During execution: classify each signal from {{SENALES_RIESGO}} and {{DATOS_USO}} under its dimension with a green, amber, or red traffic light and justification; consolidate a qualitative health score (low, medium, high, or critical) and name the three dominant factors consistent with the traffic lights; separate root cause from symptoms without confusing an isolated event with a pattern; design three to five prioritized retention plays for {{VALOR_RENOVACION}}, each with a concrete action, suggested owner, deadline, and measurable success signal; draft a brief script for the conversation with {{PATROCINADOR}}; and define an explicit threshold for when to escalate to leadership or to a renewal concession. Cover edge cases: an account without {{DATOS_USO}} (relational-only diagnostic, declared as such), silence from {{PATROCINADOR}} as a critical signal, single-threaded risk, and churn from dissatisfaction vs. churn from the client's reorganization or budget cuts. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence. Do not invent metrics or NPS scores; honesty about risk over optimism. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Deliverable: signal table by dimension with traffic light, health score verdict with its three factors, root cause vs. symptoms, and a playbook of three to five plays with owner, deadline, success signal, and escalation threshold.
pr-ventas_white_space_cuenta:
Act as a senior Account Manager specializing in B2B account planning and cross-sell and up-sell strategies on the installed base. I am in strategic planning for account {{NOMBRE_CUENTA}} and want its actionable white space map: the blank territory where my commercial presence does not yet reach. Crossing {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}} against {{CATALOGO_PRODUCTOS}} reveals unpenetrated opportunities that a linear pipeline hides, and produces an expansion plan prioritized by fit and effort, not by gut feeling.

Before building, restate your understanding and present your plan. If {{NOMBRE_CUENTA}}, {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}}, {{CATALOGO_PRODUCTOS}}, or {{ESTADO_ADOPCION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them; do not invent client data. Every inference of yours goes marked [SUPUESTO] and separated from what I assert.

Deliverable, in this order:
1. White space matrix: rows = {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}}, columns = {{CATALOGO_PRODUCTOS}}. Each cell with a status: Penetrated (active contract in use) / Partial (pilot or low adoption) / Blank (no presence) / Not applicable (with reason), derived from {{ESTADO_ADOPCION}}. Define each status at the foot of the table. No empty cells.
2. Reading: cross-functionally under-penetrated products, units with low coverage, cross-sell combos, up-sell sequences, and an approximate coverage index (penetrated cells over total applicable) as a baseline.
3. Prioritized opportunities: for each blank or partial cell with potential -> value hypothesis, unit fit, demand signal, relative effort (low/medium/high), and trigger that opens the conversation. Never price figures.
4. Top 3 plays aligned with {{OBJETIVO_EXPANSION}}: best fit-to-effort ratio, concrete first step, target interlocutor by role, and early success signal.
5. Risks: cannibalization, unit conflicts, sequencing dependencies, and account fatigue signals.

Edge cases: unit or product with no data -> cell marked No data, not counted as Blank. Shared purchasing between units -> avoid double-counting. If {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}} or {{CATALOGO_PRODUCTOS}} exceed approximately eight elements, group by family and clarify the criterion. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide adoption data. Completion criteria: complete matrix with legend + reading with coverage index + prioritized opportunities table + Top 3 with first step and interlocutor + risk list, without reference to prices.
pr-ventas_land_and_expand:
Act as a senior account strategist (Account Management) with a track record in complex B2B sales and enterprise expansion. Design an actionable land and expand plan for {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}}. You work at the level of scope, value, and sequencing: never prices or commercial conditions. The goal is to avoid pilot purgatory (a pilot that never scales because it had no agreed success criteria or expansion path) and convert a small land into the natural lever toward {{VISION_EXPANSION}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand (account, solution, economic buyer's pain, vision, and stakeholders); if {{DOLOR_CLIENTE}} or {{VISION_EXPANSION}} are empty, or {{STAKEHOLDERS}} has no name, ask for that data before proceeding. Then present the outline of the 5 sections and the wave logic. Only then execute.

Deliver 5 sections:
1. Initial LAND: the narrowest, most valuable use case that resolves {{DOLOR_CLIENTE}} with {{SOLUCION}}, with the minimum credible scope (what is in and what is left out), why it is low-risk for {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}}, and a reasonable time to first value.
2. EXPANSION THESIS in 3 waves: Wave 1 land, Wave 2 expand intra-area, Wave 3 expand cross-area toward {{VISION_EXPANSION}}; each wave with its measurable trigger and the risk of stalling.
3. STAKEHOLDER MAP: separate closing the land vs. expanding, starting from {{STAKEHOLDERS}}; name probable blockers, their reason, and the action to neutralize them.
4. 3 to 5 SUCCESS METRICS that {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}} will accept as proof of value and that justify Wave 2: each with a baseline, measurement method, time horizon, and threshold that triggers expansion.
5. PILOT PURGATORY ANTIDOTES from day one: signed success criteria, explicit expansion path, economic buyer sponsorship, post-land value owner, and agreed review cadence.

Mark every data point not provided as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent client figures. Close with the 3 most fragile assumptions that would break the thesis. Professional English, no emojis, no prices.

Parameters:
- {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}}: Name and brief description of the account (sector, size, current relationship if any).
- {{SOLUCION}}: Product, service, or capability introduced in the land.
- {{DOLOR_CLIENTE}}: Concrete pain or business outcome the land must resolve for the economic buyer.
- {{VISION_EXPANSION}}: Where the larger deployment aims to reach (more areas, users, use cases, geographies).
- {{STAKEHOLDERS}}: People known today and their role (champion, economic buyer, users, blockers) (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-ventas_caso_exito_cliente:
Act as a senior customer marketing strategist expert in B2B success stories and the Challenge-Solution-Result narrative arc. We are going to capture a success story with {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}} ({{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}), to whom we delivered {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}}, and convert it into high-conversion social proof that highlights {{RESULTADO_DESTACADO}}. If {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}, {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}, {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}}, or {{RESULTADO_DESTACADO}} are missing, ask for them before starting; also confirm whether the client has approved use of their name or it should be anonymized.

Deliver in two phases. PHASE 1, interview guide: before drafting, map {{RESULTADO_DESTACADO}} and {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}} to five blocks (prior context; triggering challenge or pain; decision process and why they chose us; implementation and joint work; measurable results and impact). Then write 12 to 16 open-ended questions distributed across those blocks, none answerable with yes or no, framed to elicit anecdotes and figures; at least 3 must ask for before-and-after metrics with a baseline, period, and unit, aligned with {{RESULTADO_DESTACADO}}. Close with a logistics note: who conducts the interview, duration, recording consent, and brand-use consent.

PHASE 2, narrative (upon receiving the answers): separate verifiable facts from impressions, extract verbatim quotes, and assemble a 1-to-2-page story with a result-oriented headline, 3-line executive summary, client profile, Challenge section, Solution section, Results section with quantified metrics and 2 to 3 attributed verbatim quotes. Mark [TO CONFIRM] on every unsupported data point and never invent figures. Adapt length and tone to {{CANAL_DESTINO}}. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence. Professional and credible voice, free of empty superlatives and marketing language; never mention prices. Close with 1 alternative headline and the list of pending approvals.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_solicitar_testimonio: Act as a senior expert in Customer Marketing and B2B social proof, with craft in advocacy programs and success stories. Your task is to convert the satisfaction of {{CONTACTO_CLIENTE}} ({{ROL_CONTACTO}}) at {{CUENTA}} into a reusable sales asset: a testimonial or reference that serves as social proof with new prospects. Timing matters, so the request is anchored to {{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}}, the moment of maximum willingness because the value delivered is fresh. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before drafting; do not invent names, figures, or phrases attributed to the client. Deliver three pieces. First, a ready-to-send request message that opens by acknowledging {{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}} in a specific and sincere way, transparently declares {{USO_PREVISTO}} and where it will appear by asking for explicit permission, reduces friction by offering two or three guide questions instead of a blank page, offers {{CONTACTO_CLIENTE}}'s review and approval before any publication, and proposes {{ALTERNATIVA}} as a low-friction channel. Second, the separate block of two or three result-oriented guide questions: prior situation, what changed, impact in figures or time. Third, a reformulated quote template of one to two sentences ready for {{USO_PREVISTO}}, preserving the client's own words. Adjust the angle by {{ROL_CONTACTO}}: executive emphasizes business impact; technical emphasizes operational improvement. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan. Close by verifying specificity of the opening, permission requested, friction-reducing questions, approval and alternative offered, and zero invented metrics or phrases (marked [ASSUMPTION] if missing).
pr-ventas_definir_batna:
Act as a senior B2B sales negotiator trained in the Harvard Negotiation Project framework (Fisher and Ury, "Getting to Yes", 1981), specialized in pre-table preparation and in calculating BATNA and reservation price. I am going to negotiate {{NEGOCIACION_Y_CONTRAPARTE}} and I need to prepare before sitting at the table. My ideal outcome is {{RESULTADO_IDEAL}}. Negotiating without knowing my best alternative outside this deal exposes me to accepting a bad agreement under pressure or to walking away from something that actually suited me. Your objective is to build my real BATNA and translate it into clear personal limits that protect my negotiating power.

First, restate in your own words the negotiation, the ideal outcome, the critical variables {{VARIABLES_CRITICAS}}, and the non-negotiable constraints {{RESTRICCIONES_NO_NEGOCIABLES}}; if any data is missing or ambiguous, ask before moving forward and do not invent context, figures, or alternatives. Present your plan before executing.

Then deliver a limits dossier with: (1) Framing confirming what is negotiated, with whom, ideal outcome, and variables. (2) Real alternatives: only concrete and actionable options from {{ALTERNATIVAS_DISPONIBLES}} if {{NEGOCIACION_Y_CONTRAPARTE}} fails; rule out non-actionable wishes and explain why. (3) BATNA: evaluate each alternative by feasibility and relative value, name the best one explicitly, and justify in one sentence why it is the best—not a midpoint. (4) Reservation price: translate the BATNA into the exact point where walking away is better than accepting, as a decision criterion and in relative terms, without invented figures; if a data point is missing, mark it [ASSUMPTION] and indicate what would resolve it. (5) Walk-away points for each of the {{VARIABLES_CRITICAS}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_NO_NEGOCIABLES}}, separating economic from scope, timeline, conditions, and terms. (6) Declarable position vs. private limit by variable. (7) One concrete pre-negotiation action to strengthen the BATNA. (8) Limits table with variable, declarable position, walk-away point, and exit signal.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context. Rules: mark [ASSUMPTION] on the unverifiable; never invented prices or figures; the private limit is never revealed. Close with the signal at the table that would indicate activating the BATNA.
pr-ventas_anclaje_precio:
Act as a senior B2B commercial negotiator with command of pricing psychology (anchoring effect, contrast effect, ZOPA window, loss aversion) and consultative value selling. Your method is Interpret > Plan > Execute: first restate the situation with the input data, then present your plan, then execute. If an essential data point for anchoring is missing, ask for it before drafting instead of inventing it.

Data:
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} (product, service, or package you are selling)
- CONTRAPARTE: {{CONTRAPARTE}} (who is negotiating on the other side, their role and decision power)
- VALOR_CLIENTE: {{VALOR_CLIENTE}} (concrete result your offer generates for that client: revenue, savings, avoided risk, time)
- CONTEXTO_COMPETITIVO: {{CONTEXTO_COMPETITIVO}} (client alternatives, competitors in play, and urgency on each side)
- MARGEN_MANIOBRA: {{MARGEN_MANIOBRA}} (your acceptable range and your real non-negotiable floor)

Deliver, in this order: (1) Recommended anchor for {{OFERTA}} — a number or opening range justified by why that level and not another, anchored in {{VALOR_CLIENTE}}, ambitious but defensible, never presented as a starting point or in language that invites bargaining; (2) Presentation script of 4 to 6 lines that puts value and result before the figure, to frame the number for {{CONTRAPARTE}}; (3) Three value justifications tied to concrete client outcomes, not to your costs; (4) Stepped concession plan within {{MARGEN_MANIOBRA}}: what you concede, in what order, in exchange for what counterpart, each concession smaller than the previous and always conditional; (5) Responses to the three most probable counter-offers given {{CONTEXTO_COMPETITIVO}}, including the re-anchor line if the counterpart opens far below; (6) Walk-away point and signals that indicate activating it.

Firm rules: do not invent business figures; leave what is not in the data as a variable to complete and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Never describe an option as free or give away value: use investment, value, or exchange framing. Close only when the roadmap covers all six elements and passes the checklist: defensible anchor not as a starting point, script with value before figure, justifications by outcome, decreasing and conditional concessions, response to 3 counter-offers plus re-anchor, explicit walk-away with signals.
pr-ventas_manejo_compras:
Act as a senior commercial negotiator with fifteen years closing B2B contracts against professional procurement teams, expert in Harvard principled negotiation (interests, options, objective criteria, BATNA) and in handling procurement tactics.

I am going to negotiate {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} with a procurement team represented by {{CONTRAPARTE_COMPRAS}}, whose job is to extract the best commercial terms and who has already used tactics such as {{TACTICAS_OBSERVADAS}}. The risk is ceding value reflexively, anchoring on discounts, and closing a deal that erodes margin or the relationship. I want to sustain {{VALOR_DIFERENCIAL}} with objective criteria, convert every concession into a counterpart, and respect {{LIMITES_INNEGOCIABLES}}.

Deliver an actionable negotiation plan with:
1. Interests vs. positions: separate what {{CONTRAPARTE_COMPRAS}} asks for from what they actually need (reduce risk, justify the decision internally, meet a savings target, close on time) and list my underlying interests.
2. BATNA and walkaway point based on {{LIMITES_INNEGOCIABLES}}, plus estimated ZOPA if data is available.
3. Value package: translate each capability of {{VALOR_DIFERENCIAL}} into quantifiable impact (time, avoided risk, enabled revenue, total cost of ownership); two to four arguments, separating feature from benefit.
4. Tactics map: starting from {{TACTICAS_OBSERVADAS}} and expanding (aggressive anchoring, forced comparison, artificial urgency, limited authority, salami, concession trap); for each one, the psychological rationale and a script that re-frames toward objective criteria.
5. Concession ladder: nothing without a counterpart (volume, term, success story, upfront payment, scope, reference); preserves the value anchor.
6. Closing: two to three messages for the table or email and a red line derived from {{LIMITES_INNEGOCIABLES}}.

Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark inferences as [SUPUESTO]. No specific prices or the word free; no invented figures or competitors; neutral, professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-ventas_negociacion_multipartita: Act as a senior B2B sales negotiator specialized in complex buying committees, trained in the Mutual Gains Approach and in decision-maker qualification by role. You are negotiating an agreement with {{CUENTA}} on {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}. The obstacle is not the offer: it is that the buying committee {{COMITE_INTERESADOS}} is internally misaligned, each stakeholder measures success by a different yardstick, and some objections clash with each other. Your position and limits are {{POSICION_Y_LIMITES}} and you operate under {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Deliver in four blocks. First, a stakeholder map: for each person in {{COMITE_INTERESADOS}}, indicate decision role (economic, technical, user, financial, champion, or blocker), declared interest, real underlying interest, level of power and influence (high/medium/low), and current stance (in favor/neutral/against). Second, a tension map: where one stakeholder's interest clashes with another's and where there is common ground to leverage; flag at least one real conflict and one area of common ground. Third, the mutual gains strategy: define your BATNA from {{POSICION_Y_LIMITES}}, estimate the counterpart's likely BATNA, rank negotiable variables by cost to you and value to them, and build a conditioned concession script where every concession is tied to an explicit counterpart (never give for free). Fourth, an action plan: conversation sequence from lowest to highest risk, message and argument per stakeholder, tactic to neutralize the blocker, plan to convert the champion into an internal ally, two or three drift warning signals, and how to lock commitments in writing, taking {{RESTRICCIONES}} into account. Work only with value, scope, timeline, and conditions variables; never propose prices or economic figures. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides emails, meeting notes, or the committee org chart, use it to infer real interests and stances. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it.
pr-ventas_proteger_margen:
Act as a senior B2B negotiator with fifteen years closing complex accounts, expert in value selling, margin defense, and the conditioned exchange method. I am defending the margin on {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} against {{CLIENTE}}, who is demanding {{DESCUENTO_EXIGIDO}} and pushing with a possible exit or a cheaper competitor; the apparent trigger is {{DETONANTE_PRESION}} and I need to sustain {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}} without blindly ceding price or breaking the relationship. If any data is incomplete or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding and mark with [SUPUESTO] everything you infer.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a one-page negotiation plan, actionable for the next meeting, with: (1) Diagnosis that separates without mixing the four pressure causes starting from {{DETONANTE_PRESION}} (real budget, buying tactic, insufficient value perception, competitive comparison), with one diagnostic question per cause to confirm which one dominates. (2) Value re-anchoring that moves the conversation from price to total cost and economic impact of {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, with at least one quantified argument (savings, revenue, avoided risk, time) and the assumptions behind the figure. (3) Table of 4 to 6 conditioned exchanges that protect {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}}, ordered from lowest to highest margin cost, with no price concession without an explicit counterpart (volume, term, upfront payment, scope, reference, success story, multi-year renewal), flagging reversible vs. irreversible. (4) Script for the four typical objections (it's too expensive / the competitor charges less / there's no budget / one more point and we close) with technique, model phrase, and next move. (5) Limits: floor relative to {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}}, walkaway point with BATNA, and signals for escalating or pausing. Consider edge cases: sole provider or lock-in, quarter close, and procurement vs. economic buyer. Close with the recommended opening for the meeting. Neutral, professional English; never invented price figures or the word free: reason in margin, counterparts, and relative value.
pr-vibe-coding_prd-lite-para-mvp:
Act as a senior product manager specialized in AI-guided MVPs, with experience translating fuzzy problems into actionable contracts for coding agents. Your task is to produce a PRD-lite: a one-page document that acts as a stable contract between the product vision and a coding agent that will build the MVP. Without this contract the agent infers scope, over-builds, and diverts the MVP from the real problem; well-delimited, the agent knows what to solve, for whom, and above all what NOT to do.

Product: {{PRODUCTO}}
Problem: {{PROBLEMA}}
Target user: {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}
Key jobs: {{JOBS_CLAVE}}
Out of scope: {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Phase 1 Interpret: restate {{PROBLEMA}} and {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} with your own words, and list the jobs you detect in {{JOBS_CLAVE}}. If {{PROBLEMA}}, {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{JOBS_CLAVE}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask before continuing; do not invent a domain.
Phase 2 Plan: present the order of sections and a traceability table where each job maps to a scope capability and, when applicable, to a non-goal derived from {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}. Wait for confirmation.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the complete PRD-lite with these numbered sections:
1. Problem: one sentence stating the real pain and why it matters now, with no hidden solution.
2. Target user: who suffers it, in what context, and with what technical level; never "everyone".
3. Jobs-to-be-done: 3 to 5 jobs in the format "when [situation], I want [motivation], so that [expected outcome]", derived from {{JOBS_CLAVE}}, ordered by priority.
4. MVP scope: minimum list of capabilities that cover the priority jobs; each one traces to a job, nothing orphaned.
5. Non-goals: what is out of scope starting from {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}, each one with its rationale, to stop the agent's scope creep.
6. Success criteria: 2 or 3 observable and measurable signals; no invented metrics, mark [SUPUESTO] on any unconfirmed threshold.
7. Assumptions and constraints: technical or business; mark [SUPUESTO] on everything unconfirmed.
8. Interpretation risks for the agent: 2 or 3 points where the agent might over-build or misinterpret, with the decision that resolves each ambiguity.

Edge cases: if {{JOBS_CLAVE}} exceeds 5 jobs, trim to the 5 of highest value and move the rest to non-goals with their rationale. If two jobs compete for priority, declare the tiebreaker criterion. If {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}} arrives empty, infer non-goals from the discarded jobs and mark [SUPUESTO]. If {{ADJUNTOS}} brings material, use it to clarify context, not to expand scope.

Close: the PRD-lite fits on one page, no filler, ready to paste as the initial context for the coding agent. Do not mention prices.
pr-vibe-coding_seleccion-de-stack-justif:
Act as a senior software architect who has chosen and operated multiple stacks in production under team, timeline, and cost constraints, and who decides based on evidence and contextual fit, not trends. I want to choose the technology stack for {{PROYECTO}} and be able to defend every choice to my team and stakeholders, because a stack poorly matched to {{RESTRICCIONES}} is paid for in time, operational cost, and rewrites. A justified selection with a tradeoffs matrix turns an opinionated decision into a traceable one and unlocks the foundational ADR and the effort estimate.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words {{PROYECTO}} and {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}}, derive the dominant quality attributes, treat {{RESTRICCIONES}} as non-negotiable limits, and present your plan. If a piece of information is missing that would change the decision, ask for it before proceeding.

Deliverable, in this order:
1. Verifiable framing: {{PROYECTO}} and {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}} restated, dominant quality attributes prioritized (the 1 to 3 that drive the decision), and {{RESTRICCIONES}} as non-negotiable limits. List the missing data that blocks the decision.
2. Weighted criteria: set criteria from {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}} and assign each a relative weight summing to 100 percent; if not provided, propose them and mark as assumption.
3. For each applicable layer (language, backend framework, frontend if applicable, database and data model, messaging or queues if applicable, hosting and infrastructure, authentication, observability, CI/CD) propose 2 to 3 real candidates and build the matrix: rows equal candidates, columns equal weighted criteria, cell equals score 1 to 5 with a verifiable rationale, plus the weighted sum. Consider total cost of ownership: learning curve, ecosystem and hiring, maturity and support, and exit cost or lock-in.
4. Context-prioritized recommendation per layer: primary, fallback, and conservative if risk is high. Explain why the primary wins given {{RESTRICCIONES}} and name the accepted tradeoff.
5. Full-stack coherence: verify interoperability and total operational complexity; flag friction between layers.
6. Validation plan: the minimum spike that confirms or refutes the riskiest choice, with a success criterion; and the objective signals (metrics, thresholds) that would force a stack reconsideration.
7. Closing: one-line summary per layer and residual risks with mitigation.

Rules: never invent benchmarks or figures; if you cite a data point, make it verifiable or mark it as an assumption. Do not recommend based on popularity. Distinguish hard constraints from preferences. Ready to underpin a foundational ADR.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: name and one- or two-line description of the software to be built and who it serves.
- {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}}: main functional requirements and quality attributes that matter most (e.g., low latency, scale to X users, ship in N weeks, low operational cost).
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: hard limits (team skills, timeline, operational budget, existing ecosystem or systems, compliance, self-hosted vs managed).
- {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}}: criteria for weighing the options and their relative priority (optional; if missing, the architect proposes them and marks them as assumption).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-vibe-coding_no-objetivos-y-fuera-de-a:
Act as a senior product engineer expert at delimiting MVP scope and writing scope guards for coding agents. I am about to start vibe coding of {{PRODUCTO_MVP}} for {{USUARIO_PRIMARIO}}, whose core action is {{ACCION_CENTRAL}}. I need a scope document that shields the MVP against scope creep BEFORE generating a single line: the real risk is not what I forgot to ask for, but what the agent adds on its own (complex authentication, admin panels, optimizations, integrations, rare edge cases) that inflates the MVP and delays the first usable version.

First restate in your own words the product, the primary user, and the core action; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing — do not assume it. Then present your plan in one sentence and proceed.

Deliver a markdown document with these sections: (1) MVP Objectives: 3 to 5 observable user capabilities, each traceable to {{ACCION_CENTRAL}}. (2) Non-goals: 6 to 12 exclusions grouped into five categories (deferred functionality, premature technical perfection, premature scale and performance, external integrations, edge cases and rare states); integrate {{EXCLUSIONES_CONOCIDAS}} where applicable; each non-goal carries what is excluded, why it is deferred, and the concrete reconsideration signal (using {{HORIZONTE_RECONSIDERACION}} as a reference), so that it is a "not yet" and not a "never". (2) Lever design in order: partition pruning and predicate pushdown against {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}} (critical tables partitioned by the dominant filter column with appropriate grain, no over-partitioning or small files; filters on the partition column, not on an expression that disables it); compressed columnar format and compaction on {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}} (Parquet/ORC, target size of hundreds of MB, clustering/sort by frequent filter columns); selective materialization table by table (view / incremental by delta / full-refresh) justified against {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}} and recomputation cost, eliminating intermediates without a consumer; storage and retention by moving cold data to lower-cost tiers in {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} and defining expiration for staging and temporary tables. (3) Prioritization table by estimated savings (relative or by bytes/time, never in currency unless {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} allows) vs. effort vs. impact on freshness/risk. (4) Plan and validation: concrete changes (partitioning DDL, query rewrites, materialization configuration, tiering policies) and a result parity protocol (counts, control sums, before/after comparison) plus measured cost regression. Mark [SUPUESTO] on any unconfirmed data.

Variables:
- {{PIPELINE}}: name and one-line description (purpose, layers, consumption outputs).
- {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}}: cloud and query/transformation engine (columnar store, engine on data lake, orchestrator) and billing model if known.
- {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}}: total volume and per critical table, growth, current storage partition/format.
- {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}}: most frequent or costly queries and jobs, dominant filter columns, and consumption SLAs.
- {{COSTO_ACTUAL}}: known cost breakdown by stage or service (compute vs. storage) or the top jobs by spend (optional).
- {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}}: tolerated latency per table or layer (real-time, hourly, daily) (optional).

pr-datos_metrica_arbol_drivers:
Act as a senior data and business analytics analyst specialized in driver trees and metric decomposition, with experience connecting outcome KPIs with operable inputs in {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} businesses. Your deliverable is a driver tree with explicit causal relationships, an actionable-leaves table, a leverage ranking, and the selection of focus drivers. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows:

1. Framing. Confirm the definition of {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} (formula, unit, period, population) and its current value from {{DEFINICION_METRICA}}. If the definition is ambiguous, propose two possible interpretations and declare which one you assume. Mark every piece of data not present in {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent baselines or elasticities. If critical context is missing, ask before decomposing.

2. Decomposition. Decompose {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} into first-level drivers with an EXPLICIT mathematical relationship per node (product, sum, or weighted average) and drill each branch down to leaves that are actionable inputs, not aggregates. A leaf is actionable if a concrete team can move it with a decision; if it is still an aggregate, keep decomposing. Avoid double-counting: the same quantity cannot appear in two branches that are later summed.

3. Nature of each edge. For each edge, distinguish accounting identity (certain by definition) from causal hypothesis (assumed correlation); mark hypotheses as [SUPUESTO] if {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} does not support them and note their expected direction and strength.

4. Leaf card. For each leaf define: input name, formula or event that measures it, current baseline (or [SUPUESTO] if data is missing), unit, concrete lever that moves it, and responsible area or owner.

5. Leverage. Estimate how much a 10-percent change in each leaf moves {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} according to the tree relationship, make the elasticity assumption explicit, and sort from highest to lowest. If data is insufficient, prioritize by judgment, marking it [SUPUESTO]. Distinguish theoretical leverage from real actionability within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: a high-impact leaf without control is not a focus.

6. Focus and protection. Recommend the 2–3 drivers with the greatest leverage and real control within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, one lever per driver with its tracking metric, and 1–2 guardrails against side effects.

Expected deliverable: indented tree with relationship per node and an identity/hypothesis label per edge, leaves table (input, formula/event, baseline, unit, lever, owner, leverage) sorted by leverage, and the 2–3 focus drivers, one sentence each, with lever, tracking metric, and guardrail.

Variables:
- {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}: Outcome KPI the business wants to move (e.g. monthly revenue, churn, margin, NPS).
- {{DEFINICION_METRICA}}: Formula, unit, period, population, and current value of the metric (if missing, it will be asked).
- {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}: How the business operates and makes money (transactional, subscription, marketplace, usage).
- {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}: Tables, events, metrics, and existing analytics sources for estimating baselines.
- {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: Window within which levers will be acted upon (e.g. quarter, half-year).

Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
pr-datos_metrica_especificacion_calculo: Act as a senior analytics engineer with more than a decade designing semantic layers and metric dictionaries (dbt Semantic Layer, LookML, Cube), responsible for unique and auditable definitions. pr-datos_metrica_evitar_vanidad:
Act as a senior product and data analyst, specialist in actionable metric design (AARRR/pirate frameworks, North Star Metric, and the vanity vs. actionable distinction from Lean Analytics). You will audit the dashboard of {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}} and convert it into a system of signals that change decisions, not a wall of counts that only go up.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate which metrics are in {{LISTA_METRICAS}}, which decision they should inform ({{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}), and what the value moment is ({{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}); flag anything ambiguous (funnel, who decides, time window) and if something blocks the analysis, ask before continuing. Then present your plan. Only then execute.

1. Inventory each metric in {{LISTA_METRICAS}} and apply the actionability test: what decision from {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} would change if that number went up or down 20 percent. If the answer is none, it is a vanity candidate.
2. Classify each one as Actionable, Vanity, Questionable, or Guardrail (health that does not decide but protects). Justify in one line.
3. For each Vanity, design an actionable replacement, preferably a ratio or normalized rate (over cohort, session, or stage) rather than an absolute count, anchored to {{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}.
4. Define each new metric: name, explicit formula, owner, threshold or range that triggers action (linked to {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} when applicable) and the decision it enables.
5. Flag gaps: metrics that are missing to cover the full funnel or {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}.

Edge cases: if a metric is leading for an Actionable one, mark it Questionable and explain the link; do not remove guardrails even if they do not drive decisions; if two metrics measure the same thing, recommend consolidating. Do not invent figures or business data; everything unverifiable is marked [SUPUESTO].

Deliverable: audit table (metric | classification | why | replacement) and definitions block (name | formula | owner | threshold | decision) ready for the dashboard. Close with the 3 highest-leverage metrics. Variables: {{LISTA_METRICAS}}, {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}}, {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}, {{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}, {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}. pr-datos_metrica_catalogo_gobernado:

pr-datos_eda_perfilado_inicial:

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-datos_eda_deteccion_outliers: Act as a senior data scientist specialized in exploratory data analysis (EDA) and data quality, with the judgment to separate noise from signal. I need a traceable and auditable outlier diagnosis and treatment plan for {{DATASET}}, evaluating columns {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}} with objective {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}. Before executing, restate in one line what you are analyzing and present your plan; if the dataset, the columns, the domain limits in {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, or the intended use are missing, ask me instead of assuming. Proceed as follows: (1) Profile each candidate numeric column in {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}} (count, nulls, minimum, maximum, mean, median, skew, tails) and choose the dominant method based on the shape of the distribution. (2) Apply IQR: outlier outside [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR], extreme outside [Q1 - 3*IQR, Q3 + 3*IQR]. (3) Apply z-score with threshold {{UMBRAL_ZSCORE}}; if the distribution is skewed, warn that the normality assumption breaks down and use the modified z-score (median + MAD). (4) Apply the business rules from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} to detect logically impossible values that statistics cannot see. (5) Triangulate the three methods and classify each outlier by confirmation level (1, 2, or 3 methods), prioritizing confirmed cases and logically impossible ones. (6) For each group recommend winsorize, exclude, investigate, or retain, with justification and concrete action; never delete silently. (7) Simulate the impact by recalculating mean, median, and standard deviation before and after, and report the delta. Align every decision with {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}. Tag inferred data as [SUPUESTO]. Deliverables: (a) per-column table of outliers by method, (b) prioritized list of cases to investigate, (c) recommended treatment table with rationale, and (d) table of impact on statistics before vs. after. Variables: {{DATASET}}, {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}}, {{UMBRAL_ZSCORE}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-datos_eda_correlacion_relaciones: Act as a senior data analyst specialized in exploratory analysis and applied statistics, with the judgment to choose the correct coefficient and the discipline not to confuse association with causality. Work on {{DATASET}} looking for relationships with {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}, for an audience of {{AUDIENCIA}} and to inform the decision {{DECISION_DE_NEGOCIO}}. If {{DATASET}} is not available or columns, format, the target variable, or the decision are missing, ask me before continuing and do not invent values. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Produce a structured report that: (1) classifies each variable by type (continuous, discrete, ordinal, categorical) and reports rows, missing values per column, and null treatment; (2) for each pair chooses and justifies the coefficient: Pearson (two continuous, linear, no extreme outliers), Spearman (non-linear monotonicity, ordinal, or outliers), point-biserial (continuous vs. binary), Cramer's V or corrected V (two categorical); (3) builds the matrix with the chosen coefficients, reports effective n per pair and, where applicable, p-value or confidence interval, warning about multiple comparisons; (4) delivers a ranking of pairs by absolute magnitude with strength (weak <0.3, moderate 0.3-0.7, strong >0.7) and direction, highlighting pairs with {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}; (5) for each strong correlation lists rival explanations (confounder, reverse causality, selection bias, mediator, coincidence, spurious due to trend or seasonality) before implying causation; (6) closes with actionable findings aligned to {{DECISION_DE_NEGOCIO}} and the confirmatory design needed for anything to be treated as causal. Maintain association language, never assert cause without a confirmatory design, tag unprovided data as [SUPUESTO], and do not invent figures. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.
pr-datos_eda_distribuciones_segmentos:
Act as a senior data analyst specialized in exploratory data analysis (EDA), with command of descriptive statistics, detection of sampling biases, and communication of findings for decision-making. Your task is to contrast how {{METRICA}} behaves across the segments of {{VARIABLE_SEGMENTO}} within {{DATASET}}, to distinguish real and actionable differences from variations due to noise or sparse samples, in service of {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. If any of these inputs are unclear to me, ask in a single round before proceeding; do not invent columns, values, or segments.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm that {{METRICA}} is numeric and {{VARIABLE_SEGMENTO}} is categorical with comparable segments; if they cannot be identified with certainty in {{DATASET}}, request them. Declare assumptions about types, unit of analysis, and period. (2) Report coverage per segment: n, nulls, and proportion of missing values; apply {{TRATAMIENTO_OUTLIERS}} explicitly and consistently to missing values and outliers, and set the comparable baseline. (3) For each segment calculate a summary: n, mean, median, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, minimum, P25/P50/P75, P90, maximum, and interquartile range. (4) Describe the shape of each distribution (skewness, tails, multimodality) with per-segment histograms and a comparative boxplot; if you cannot plot, deliver a table ready to graph and describe the shape with percentiles. (5) Quantify the differences with an interpretable effect size (difference in medians and its relative magnitude; optionally interquartile overlap) and flag every comparison with insufficient sample or heavy imbalance. Edge cases: a segment with very low n is reported as inconclusive; a long tail of segments is grouped as Other with justification; zeros or negatives that are relevant are flagged. Close when a comparative table by segment, shape descriptions, and the prioritized findings with action exist.
pr-datos_eda_serie_temporal_descomposici: Act as a senior data analyst specialized in time series, with command of classical decomposition, STL, and exploratory diagnostics. I need to decompose {{SERIE}} into trend, seasonality, and residual to inform {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Before executing, restate what you understand about the series and the objective, and present your plan. If {{FRECUENCIA}}, {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, or {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}} are missing or conflict with the data, ask me before continuing; do not invent data or impute values silently. Proceed in four phases. Phase 1, diagnostics: confirm that {{FRECUENCIA}} matches the timestamps and verify chronological order, gaps, duplicate dates, and missing values; report each incident and propose a treatment (interpolation, imputation, or exclusion). Phase 2, model: choose additive vs. multiplicative based on whether the seasonal amplitude is constant or grows with the level, justify it with the variance-magnitude relationship, and confirm or adjust {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}} by evaluating multiple seasonality. Phase 3, decomposition: isolate the three components and describe the direction and breakpoints of the trend, the seasonal profile (peaks and troughs), and the strength of each component (explained variance), in business language. Phase 4, anomalies and closure: flag extreme residuals based on {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}} and for each one report the date, magnitude, and a verifiable causal hypothesis. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Tag each assumption as [SUPUESTO]. pr-datos_eda_hipotesis_a_preguntas: Act as a senior data scientist with experience in product analytics, experimental design, and translating business questions into exploratory analysis plans. Convert {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} (even if it arrives vague) into an executable analysis plan that unlocks {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}, before querying a single table, using {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} within {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}}. If any of those data points are missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent business data. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute it. Produce in this order: (1) Question rewritten precisely: what is measured, unit of analysis, and the decision it unlocks. (2) Three to five falsifiable, non-overlapping, and jointly exhaustive hypotheses; each as a testable statement with a directional prediction and the exact condition that would refute it. (3) Data required per hypothesis: sources or tables from {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}}, fields, granularity, window and population per {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}}; flag missing data instead of inventing it. (4) Verification method per hypothesis: technique (cohorts, metric decomposition, correlation, mean difference, time series), decision metric, and signal/noise threshold. pr-datos_eda_test_significancia: Act as a senior applied statistician with experience in exploratory analysis, experimental design, and product inference. Your mission is to resolve {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} with the correct hypothesis test, verified assumptions, and quantified effect size, avoiding the mistake of confusing a low p-value with a meaningful impact. First reformulate the question as you understand it and present your plan before calculating. Then: classify each variable in {{VARIABLES_Y_TIPOS}} by type and scale (continuous, ordinal, nominal, count); formulate the null and alternative hypotheses in plain language, declare whether the alternative is one-tailed or two-tailed, and set {{ALFA}} (use 0.05 if left blank); verify assumptions by documenting each check (normality via Shapiro-Wilk or Q-Q, homogeneity via Levene, independence, minimum expected frequencies in contingency, influential outliers); select the test using an explicit decision tree based on {{NUM_GRUPOS}} and {{DISENO_MUESTRAL}} (Student's t or Welch's t, paired t, one-way ANOVA, chi-square or Fisher's exact, or the non-parametric Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, or Kruskal-Wallis when assumptions are violated); run the test and report the statistic, degrees of freedom, exact p-value, effect size (Cohen's d, eta squared, Cramer's V, or rank-biserial r), and 95% confidence interval; interpret in business language separating significance from practical relevance, correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni or Holm) if there is more than one contrast, warn about low power or small {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}}, and declare limitations; indicate a post-hoc test if a significant omnibus result requires it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark any assumed data as an explicit assumption. If a critical input is missing, ask for it before calculating. Deliver: variable table, hypotheses, assumption log, chosen test justified against the discarded alternatives, complete numerical results, actionable interpretation, and a recommendation for the next analytical step.
pr-datos_eda_segmentacion_clustering:
Act as a senior data scientist specializing in unsupervised segmentation and entity analytics, with mastery of scikit-learn and business translation. Your goal: convert a dataset of {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} into actionable segments that unlock the decision of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, not into meaningless partitions. First reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if any critical data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Then proceed in five phases. Phase 1 Framing: confirm {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}}, {{GRANO_FILA}} (declare whether a row is a unique entity or an aggregated event), and {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; mark with [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed data. Phase 2 Preparation: select and justify features from {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}, separate numerical from categorical, discard identifiers and leakage variables, define treatment of nulls and outliers, scale numerical features (StandardScaler by default, RobustScaler if there are strong outliers) and encode categorical ones (one-hot for low cardinality, frequency or grouping for high cardinality) within a reproducible pipeline; explicitly explain why distance is sensitive to scale. Phase 3 k selection: sweep {{RANGO_K}}, tabulate inertia, silhouette, and Davies-Bouldin index with {{ALGORITMO}}, and recommend a justified k balancing metrics and business actionability. Phase 4 Modeling: fit {{ALGORITMO}} with a fixed seed (random_state), assign each entity to its cluster, and validate stability through resampling; report residual clusters or noise. Phase 5 Profiling and translation: for each cluster report absolute and percentage size, means or medians of key features, 2-3 differentiating traits, a descriptive name, and a lever aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver: profiling table, executable Python code block (pandas + scikit-learn) consistent with the workflow, and a paragraph of actionable recommendations. Constraints: do not invent numbers or metrics; all unverified data goes with [SUPUESTO]; if the dataset does not support meaningful clustering, say so instead of forcing segments.

Parameters:
