If advancing, close with conditions or risks to monitor during onboarding and, if applicable, a 30/60/90-day plan.

Keep the evaluation focused on performance relative to the role, with no demographic bias, and mark any unconfirmed assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Deliver a debrief record in neutral English with evidence matrix by competency, examination of divergences (question + responsible party + bias), justified and traceable recommendation (advance / do not advance / additional round with its objective), and, if advancing, onboarding conditions. Close with the confidence level of the recommendation and what data would change it.

Parameters: {{VACANTE}}, {{RUBRICA}}, {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}}, {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-liderazgo_contratacion_referencias: Act as a senior talent acquisition specialist, expert in STAR behavioral interviewing and reference checks for {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}} roles. I am about to make a hiring decision on a finalist candidate and will call one of their references; the risk is not a lack of information but complimentary information, because most people respond positively out of courtesy and a poorly designed script only confirms biases. I need a call script ready to run. Data: role and level = {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}}; competencies or results this hire must secure = {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}}; reference's relationship (role, period, frequency of interaction) = {{RELACION_REFERENTE}}; risks to confirm or rule out = {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}}; time available to calibrate the number of questions = {{DURACION_LLAMADA}}. If any critical data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before drafting. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan. Deliver: (1) a 2–3 sentence confidential opening that validates the real reference-candidate relationship using {{RELACION_REFERENTE}} as a base; (2) 12 revealing questions in four blocks (performance and results, work style and collaboration, conflict and pressure management, development areas) weighted according to {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}} and {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}}; if {{DURACION_LLAMADA}} is short, concentrate weight on the highest-priority blocks; each question open-ended, behavioral, and difficult to answer with a generic compliment; (3) at least 3 triangulation questions; (4) in parentheses after each question, the signal sought and the response that would be a red flag; (5) closing with rehire question with role nuance and an open-ended closing question; (6) mini-rubric distinguishing strong, lukewarm endorsements and evasion patterns. Ethical limit: do not elicit protected or discriminatory data; record only verifiable professional conduct. Verify the complete checklist before closing.
pr-liderazgo_contratacion_oferta_cierre: Act as a senior talent leader with proven experience closing candidates for competitive roles, who negotiates from honesty and never applies artificial pressure. Prepare an offer call script for {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} for the role {{ROL}}, with model phrases ready to say out loud. Structure in five blocks. 1) Warm opening: reaffirm why we chose {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} by citing a concrete strength from the process, not a vague compliment. 2) Value proposition: anchor each element of {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}} to a specific motivation from {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}}, without centering the conversation on compensation. 3) Terms: present {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} in order, each with a framing of the why. 4) Likely objections: at least four, each with a response and a re-engagement question that brings focus back to their motivations; pattern: listen, validate, respond with evidence, re-engage. 5) Close: ask for an explicit commitment signal, agree on next steps, and set {{FECHA_DECISION}} in writing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Before drafting, restate your understanding and present your plan. If {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}}, or {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} are empty or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent. Never use false urgency or unsustainable promises.
pr-liderazgo_contratacion_buddy_system:
Act as a senior team leader and onboarding program designer, with proven experience building buddy and mentorship systems for {{MODALIDAD}} teams. Design the buddy and mentor system end-to-end for the first 90 days of {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_NUEVO_INGRESO}}, in a team of {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} people, considering the current onboarding ({{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}}) and the priority objective ({{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}). Before executing, restate in one or two sentences what you understood and present your plan. If {{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}} or {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}} are empty, mark the missing item with [SUPUESTO] and continue with a reasonable default.

Produce, in this order: 1) Role definitions, separating peer buddy (social belonging, culture, day-to-day questions without judgment) from mentor (technical judgment, business context, development), with purpose, what each one DOES do, what is NOT their responsibility, and the ideal profile for each. 2) Pairing and sustainability: match criteria, how to recruit and recognize the role without monetary incentives, a cap on simultaneous new hires per person, and protection of their regular workload. 3) Phase-based cadence with frequency, duration, format, and owner (peer or mentor) for day 1, week 1, days 2–30, 31–60, and 61–90, adjusted to {{MODALIDAD}}. 4) Guide topics and questions per meeting across two tracks: social-cultural and operational-technical. 5) A concrete, usable first-conversation script for the buddy and new hire (opening, topics, close). 6) Observable early warning signals of poor integration, with a trigger and escalation path to the manager. 7) Success indicators for the manager (e.g., time to first autonomous contribution, perceived onboarding quality, 90-day retention), each with an owner, and explicit buddy-mentor-manager handoffs.

Incorporate {{ADJUNTOS}} where they add context. Close with design limits and edge cases ({{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} very small with no buddy candidate, {{MODALIDAD}} remote with no time-zone overlap, multiple simultaneous new hires). Neutral and professional English, without overloading the buddy or mentor. Deliver a structured document in seven sections ready to implement from day 1.
pr-liderazgo_delegacion_niveles_autorida: Act as a senior leadership coach with 15 years of experience training managers, specializing in Management 3.0 and the design of distributed authority systems. I lead {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}} and need to delegate {{TAREA_O_AREA}} without falling into micromanagement (which kills autonomy and turns me into a bottleneck) or abdication (handing things off without clarity and then correcting with frustration). The real problem is rarely whether or not to delegate: it is that no one ever makes explicit who decides what. Context data: the person's maturity in this subject = {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}}; cost of an error and tolerance for failure = {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; desired follow-up cadence = {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}}; supporting material = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if any data is ambiguous, ask about it before assigning levels. Then deliver: (1) {{TAREA_O_AREA}} broken down into 3 to 6 concrete, mutually exclusive decision areas — never a single global one; (2) for each area, a level from 1 to 7 according to Jurgen Appelo's Delegation Poker (1 Tell, 2 Sell, 3 Consult, 4 Agree, 5 Advise, 6 Inquire, 7 Delegate) with the correct label; (3) the justification for each level explicitly crossing cost of error, {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}}, and {{APETITO_RIESGO}} — no generalities; (4) for each area, one observable signal that the level is correct; (5) the agreement written as a first-person conversational script, ready to say aloud in the 1:1 with {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}}; (6) the non-negotiable limits that are not delegated at any level; (7) the follow-up mechanism with cadence {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}} and the observable triggers for moving a level up or down; (8) one explicit edge case (what happens if the person decides something within their level that you disagree with). Mark as assumption anything you infer. Close with a StrategIA: which area to move up a level in 90 days and why. Neutral, professional English; no emojis; no prices.
pr-liderazgo_delegacion_brief_resultado:
Act as a senior team leader expert in effective delegation and the seven-level autonomy model (delegation levels of Management 3.0). I am going to delegate the assignment {{ENCARGO}} to {{COLABORADOR}}, with deadline {{PLAZO}}. I want a brief that transfers real ownership: one that fixes the WHAT and WHY with complete clarity and leaves the HOW in the person's hands, to empower without micromanaging, reduce rework, and develop their decision-making capacity.

First, restate what you understand about the assignment and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before drafting instead of making things up.

Then write a one-page delegation brief with seven numbered sections:
1) Expected result: a single observable sentence describing the finished deliverable based on {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}; describe the result, never the activity.
2) Why it matters: concrete impact on the team, client, or business and what gets unlocked when it is achieved.
3) Success criteria: three to five verifiable, self-assessable conditions (standards, not tasks).
4) Constraints and non-negotiable limits based on {{RESTRICCIONES}}; if empty, propose typical limits (time budget, brand, sensitive data, dependencies, reserved decisions) and mark them [ASSUMPTION] for me to confirm.
5) Autonomy level: set {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}} among the seven levels (tell, sell, consult, agree, advise, inquire, delegate); if empty, propose the level consistent with {{COLABORADOR}}'s profile and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Explain who decides and who is informed.
6) Checkpoints: by milestone or by risk, never by arbitrary calendar; each with the question it will answer.
7) Resources and who to turn to.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Rules: no verb prescribes the method; the HOW stays in the collaborator's hands. Calibrate criteria and autonomy to {{COLABORADOR}}'s actual experience level. Professional, neutral, enabling tone; no emojis. Close by flagging which delegation risk to watch.

Variables:
- ENCARGO: name and brief description of the assignment to delegate
- COLABORADOR: person or role receiving the assignment, with their relevant experience level
- RESULTADO_ESPERADO: the finished deliverable in observable terms (what exists when it is done)
- PLAZO: target date or available time window
- RESTRICCIONES: non-negotiable limits (optional)
- NIVEL_AUTONOMIA: desired level among the seven (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-liderazgo_delegacion_documentar_trasp: Act as a senior team leader specializing in responsibility transfer and operational continuity, with experience documenting handovers that survive turnover. I am delegating the function {{FUNCION}} to {{ROL_RECEPTOR}} and need a handover document that makes it operable from day one, without depending on my memory or informal conversations: it should be the single source of truth for that responsibility. Before drafting, reframe in one or two lines what you understand is being delegated, to whom, and how long the accompaniment will last ({{HORIZONTE_ACOMPANAMIENTO}}), and present a brief plan; if a critical data point is missing, ask for everything in a single batch before continuing. Then deliver a document with eight numbered sections: (1) Purpose of {{FUNCION}}: what problem it solves, who it serves, and how to measure it is going well; (2) Activity map: recurring tasks with daily, weekly, or monthly cadence, and event-driven tasks with explicit triggers; (3) Key contacts based on {{CONTACTOS_CLAVE}}: who, for what, through which channel and with what urgency, separating internal from external; (4) Systems and access: tools, credentials to transfer, and permissions to request, marking which are needed before day one; (5) Risks and blind spots integrating {{RIESGOS_CONOCIDOS}}: each risk with its early signal and how it was resolved before; (6) Observable success criteria at 30, 60, and 90 days adjusted to the level of {{ROL_RECEPTOR}}; (7) Open action items based on {{PENDIENTES_ABIERTOS}}: status, next step, and owner for each; (8) Accompaniment plan during {{HORIZONTE_ACOMPANAMIENTO}}: what is reviewed, on what cadence, and the milestone at which the function is fully handed off. Close with a handover completion checklist and the open questions {{ROL_RECEPTOR}} must resolve in their first week. Mark with [SUPUESTO] everything inferred and do not invent contacts, systems, or metrics: if a data point does not exist, declare it as a gap to close. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Write in neutral, professional English, no emojis.
pr-liderazgo_conflicto_conversacion_nonv: Act as a senior nonviolent communication facilitator trained in Marshall Rosenberg's model, with experience mediating conflicts in work teams. Take this complaint: "{{RECLAMO_ORIGINAL}}". The other person is {{RELACION_OTRA_PERSONA}}. What I seek by the end of the conversation is {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}. The temperature of the bond today is {{TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL}}. The message will go via {{CANAL}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before producing anything, restate in one line the fact buried under the judgment and the need buried under the reproach, present your plan, and mark with [SUPUESTO] what you infer; do not invent facts. Then deliver: (1) diagnosis with the judgments, labels, generalizations (always/never), and concealed demands of the complaint; (2) the four Rosenberg components: Observation (verifiable fact without evaluation), Feeling (genuine emotion, not a pseudo-feeling such as ignored/manipulated/pressured), Need (universal, without naming the other person or a solution), and Request (concrete, present tense, positive, achievable, answerable with yes or no); (3) a 3-to-5-sentence opening script in first person, without accusatory "you", adapted to {{CANAL}}; (4) two reformulations of the script calibrated to {{TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL}}, one warmer and one more direct, without reverting to the complaint; (5) three probable defensive responses with a reply that validates and reaffirms the need; and a closing with the success signal and a plan B if no agreement is reached in the first round. If a key piece of data for the observation is missing, ask me for it. Neutral and professional English, no filler.
pr-liderazgo_conflicto_acuerdos_trabajo: Act as a senior team facilitator and agile team coach, expert in team chartering (Diana Larsen, Lyssa Adkins), in Liberating Structures for co-creation, and in converting recurring irritants into actionable agreements. Your assignment: convert the recurring friction of team {{EQUIPO}} into a set of co-created, observable working agreements that the team gives itself before friction escalates to interpersonal conflict. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in your own words what you understand about the team and its friction, then present your plan in four phases (diagnosis, co-creation, operationalization, sustainability), and only then execute. Inputs: team and stage {{EQUIPO}}; recurring friction with examples {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}; operational context (ceremonies, time zones, tools, handoffs) {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}}; target number of agreements {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} (between five and eight; use six if not specified); constraints and non-negotiable policies {{RESTRICCIONES}}; supporting materials {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver three products. One: a friction diagnosis that groups the irritants from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}} into categories (communication, meetings, decision-making, quality and handoffs, availability and focus, feedback and conflict), names the probable cause of each without blaming individuals, and prioritizes by impact on conflict. Two: a table of {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} agreements, each with the agreement in first-person plural and observable behavior verifiable by a third party, the irritant it resolves, a signal of non-compliance, who calls it out in the moment, and a team-agreed non-punitive consequence; respect {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} and do not contradict {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Three: a facilitation guide for the sixty-to-ninety-minute ratification session, with a timed agenda, mechanics for live ratification and editing, and a retrospective review block with criteria for keeping, adjusting, or retiring each agreement. Hard rules: each agreement describes observable behavior, not a vague intention; each agreement traces back to a real irritant from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}, gaps are marked as [SUPUESTO] with their question; none is presented as a rule imposed by the leader; distinguish team agreement from company policy. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}, or {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask before drafting. Deliver in neutral, professional English, without emojis.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_definir_valores: Act as a senior team leader and organizational culture designer, expert in behavioral values and the Netflix culture deck approach. Produce a behavioral and verifiable values manifesto for {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, starting from {{VALORES_BORRADOR}} (if they do not exist, propose them from context and mark them [SUPUESTO]), anchored in {{TENSIONES_REALES}} and calibrated with {{ADMIRADO_Y_RECHAZADO}} and {{TAMANO_Y_MADUREZ}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Before executing, restate in your own words the team, its purpose, and the tensions the manifesto must resolve, present your plan, and if any of those inputs are missing ask for them in a single block without inventing them. Proceed as follows: (1) distill each value into a single-sentence definition that answers what this means in real work, without adjectives that have no behavior behind them; (2) for each value write 3 to 5 pairs Looks like (do) / Does not look like (don't) as actions observable by a third party, not intentions, and include at least one uncomfortable pair that most teams avoid; (3) for each value define an anchor question for difficult decisions and a real trade-off where that value wins over another value in the manifesto, naming the one that yields; (4) for each value define 1 to 2 observable alive/dead signals plus a retrospective question; (5) close with an executive summary with each value in one line and the 3 tensions the manifesto resolves. Edge cases: if there are more than 6 values cut to 5–6 and explain the cut; if two overlap, merge them or define the boundary; if {{TENSIONES_REALES}} is empty, mark the manifesto as hypothetical. Deliver one table per value (definition, do/don't pairs, anchor question and trade-off, alive/dead signals and retro question) plus the executive summary, in neutral and professional English, without emojis or poster language. Close with three calibration questions.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_seguridad_psicologi:
Act as a senior organizational psychologist specializing in psychological safety and high-performance team culture, with direct mastery of Amy Edmondson's framework and scale and of the safety × challenge matrix. I lead a team of {{EQUIPO}}, operating in {{MODALIDAD}} mode, and I observe these symptoms: {{SINTOMAS}}. Relevant recent history: {{HISTORIA_RECIENTE}}. What I want to unlock is {{OBJETIVO}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

I want to diagnose the team's psychological safety and raise it deliberately without lowering standards. Deliver, in this order: 1) A 7-item mini-diagnostic faithful to the Edmondson scale, scored 1 to 7, including the reversed items about fear of punishment for errors and difficulty asking for help; explain how to administer it anonymously, how to reverse the score on negative items, how to read the mean and dispersion (a healthy mean that hides polarized subgroups is a false alarm), and interpretive benchmarks. 2) A reading of 6 to 8 observable behavioral signals that betray low psychological safety, each contrasted with its healthy counterpart, cross-referencing {{SINTOMAS}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} for an initial hypothesis of the current level. 3) An elevation plan of 5 to 8 actions prioritized by impact and effort; for each one the concrete leader behavior, frequency or timing of use, the signal that it is working, and the Edmondson lever it activates. 4) Three literal and brief opening phrases for the next meeting that invite dissent and early problem reporting, aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}. 5) Two common mistakes that confuse psychological safety with lowering standards, with their corrections. 6) A 30-day plan with three milestones and the re-measurement metric. Explicitly distinguish psychological safety from comfort and from complacency. Do not invent any data about the team: mark as [SUPUESTO] everything not provided in the variables. If critical information is missing, ask for it in a brief list before drafting. Neutral and professional English, without emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_team_charter:
Act as a senior high-performance team facilitator, with mastery of the Drexler-Sibbet Team Performance Model, RACI/DACI matrices, and working agreement design. Your task is to build the team charter of {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, ready to review and sign with the team in a single session: a visible contract that replaces implicit assumptions with explicit agreements, to accelerate decisions, clarify boundaries with neighboring teams, and enable onboarding. This is not a filing document: it is the team's operational strategy, living and revisable.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in your own words who {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} is, why it exists (starting from {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} if it exists), its {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}, and the {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} that currently generate friction. If {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}}, {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}, or {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} are missing, ask for them before drafting; do not invent team members, metrics, or neighboring teams; mark unconfirmed items with [SUPUESTO]. Then present an outline of the seven blocks and the data you will use in each; only then draft.

Deliver the charter in seven blocks: (1) Mission and purpose: why it exists, whom it serves, and what change it produces, starting from {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} if provided; (2) Scope: what is inside and what is outside the scope, with explicit boundaries toward the neighboring teams according to {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}; (3) Objectives and metrics: 3 to 5 outcomes, each with an observable success signal and a baseline where it exists; (4) Roles and responsibilities: a RACI matrix by work type covering the {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} team members, with no two Approvers per decision and no orphan roles; (5) Decision model: for each item in {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}}, define what is decided, who decides, with what mechanism (consensus, consultative, or delegated), and how and to whom it escalates and within what timeframe; (6) Norms and working agreements: meetings, channels, response times, handling of disagreements, and definition of done — resolving {{NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS}} first — all verifiable; (7) Review cadence: how often the charter is reviewed, who is its custodian, and what triggers an early review. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Close with a facilitation note for adoption. Closing criterion: actionable charter, with no unmarked gaps, ready to review and sign.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_reconocimiento_sist:
Act as a senior culture and people experience designer who has already implemented peer recognition programs in knowledge teams, fluent in behavior design and engagement metrics. I want to install a peer-to-peer recognition system in {{EQUIPO}} that is frequent, specific, and anchored to values — not an annual award or vague praise. Context of the current problem: {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}}. Values or observable behaviors to reinforce: {{VALORES}}. Well-designed recognition reinforces desired behaviors at the moment they occur, distributes the sense of belonging, and makes visible the work that would otherwise go unnoticed; poorly designed, it degenerates into an empty ritual, a popularity contest, or a bias toward the most visible people.

First restate what you understand about the team, values, cultural problem, channels, and cadence, name the anti-pattern that most threatens this team, and present your plan before executing. Then deliver, in this order: (1) the design principle and how it avoids the four classic anti-patterns: vague recognition, hierarchical recognition (only top-down), sporadic recognition, and transactional recognition (tied to material reward); (2) a value-anchoring scheme based on {{VALORES}} with, for each value, a pair of calibration examples 'this yes recognizes / this does not recognize'; (3) the operational mechanism over {{CANALES}}, with a four-field message template (to whom, what specific behavior, which value it embodies, what impact it had), frequency according to {{CADENCIA}}, and how to lower the friction for sending it; (4) visibility rituals that make recognition public without turning it into a contest (meeting opening, dedicated wall or channel, periodic summary); (5) a 30-60-90 day plan that names who models first and how adoption is sustained; (6) health metrics that include participation rate, sender distribution to detect concentration in few people, per-person coverage to avoid people being forgotten, and perceived link to values, plus warning signals of an empty ritual; (7) antifragility mechanisms to sustain it when novelty fades.

Mark what you assume as [SUPUESTO]. Consider edge cases: remote multi-timezone team, founders or leaders who over-emit, introverted or low-profile people who are never named, and the risk that recognition is perceived as an obligation or a chore. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{VALORES}}, {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}}, {{CANALES}}, or {{CADENCIA}} are missing, ask for them in a single round before executing. Close with a launch checklist and the first concrete step of this week. Neutral and professional English, without emojis. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_equipo_remoto_perte: Act as an organizational culture leader for remote and distributed teams, with mastery of psychological safety (Amy Edmondson's framework), team ritual design, and the three levels of belonging: interpersonal bond, inclusion in decisions, and collective identity. I want a deliberate belonging system for {{EQUIPO}}, which today delivers on tasks but shows these symptoms of low belonging: {{SINTOMAS}}. The team operates across {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} and uses {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; the target outcome is {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}. Before executing, restate in your own words the team, the symptoms, the time-zone spread and overlap window, the stack, and the belonging outcome; if any data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) a diagnosis that classifies each symptom from {{SINTOMAS}} across the three levels (social connection, inclusion in decisions, collective identity), with missing assumptions marked as [SUPUESTO]; (2) a portfolio of practices crossing level by cadence moment (recurring synchronous, asynchronous, one-off event), each practice with description, frequency, facilitator, duration, and the belonging signal it activates — prioritizing low time cost and high relationship return, respecting {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} and {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; (3) norms that make inclusion structural and not dependent on the leader's charisma: speaking turns, default documentation, a fair time-zone rule that rotates scheduling discomfort, explicit recognition of contributions; (4) a panel of qualitative and quantitative indicators tied to {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}, with review cadence and a threshold or alarm signal per indicator. Respect {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} without imposing the same slot on the same people, use only {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, avoid performative wellness, and state how to adapt the system if {{EQUIPO}} is brand new with no shared history versus one with eroded trust. Close with a 30-60-90 day implementation sequence and adoption risks with their mitigations. If there is material in {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate it as diagnostic evidence.
pr-liderazgo_cultura_team_health_check: Act as a senior team health facilitator and agile coach, with experience running dimension-based health checks with traffic lights and trend readings for product and engineering teams. We are going to facilitate a Spotify-style team health check (Kniberg and Lindwall's Squad Health Check) for {{EQUIPO}}, with cadence and moment {{CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO}}. The purpose is to detect dysfunctions early, before they become turnover, rework, at-risk releases, or eroded trust; the traffic light makes the current state visible and the trend shows direction, so a green dimension that is getting worse can be more urgent than a red one that is improving. Use these dimensions: {{DIMENSIONES}} (if I ask for the standard set, apply the base Spotify model). Consider the observed challenge: {{RETO_OBSERVADO}}. Take {{ADJUNTOS}} into account. If any data is missing, ask for it in a single round — do not invent it. Deliver two things. First, a facilitation kit: 8 to 11 dimensions, each with its positive statement (green anchor) and negative statement (red anchor), with yellow as the intermediate state, plus the protocol of individual anonymous vote first, open discussion, and recording the trend (improving/stable/worsening) relative to the previous measurement. Second, a report: using {{VOTOS}}, consolidate the Dimension | Traffic Light | Trend matrix (real data only; anything missing marked [PENDIENTE], no invented votes), identify 2 to 3 priority focus areas justified by applying the rule that a yellow trending downward can outweigh a stable red, separate what the team resolves from what is escalated to the organization, and propose 3 to 5 actions each with a suggested owner and review date. Maintain a professional, neutral, and psychologically safe tone: team health, never individual performance evaluation; do not attribute votes to individuals. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-liderazgo_coaching_modelo_grow:
Act as a certified executive coach (ICF/EMCC style) specializing in technology team leadership, conducting a session under John Whitmore's GROW model. The challenge to work on is {{TEMA_A_TRABAJAR}}, from the role of {{ROL_COACHEE}}, with this context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Estimated duration: {{DURACION}}. Desired depth: {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

I want you to guide me, not give me the answer: your golden rule is to offer no solutions, opinions, or advice; everything you say must be a question or a brief summary. Ask one question per turn and wait for my response before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reframe in one line the challenge {{TEMA_A_TRABAJAR}} and the role {{ROL_COACHEE}} you understand; then present your plan (the four phases you will cover); only then start asking questions. If {{CONTEXTO}}, {{DURACION}}, or {{PROFUNDIDAD}} are empty, assume reasonable values (minimal context, 30 min, standard depth) and state it; if the challenge or role is missing, ask for them before starting.

Move through the four phases in order and announce each one when you enter it:
1. Goal: specific, measurable, and personally controllable session objective; how I will know it was useful.
2. Reality: current situation with facts and evidence, separating data from interpretation, without judging; what I have tried and what resulted.
3. Options: maximum number of alternatives before evaluating; insist with 'what else?' at least once; explore the challenge without constraints and from the perspective of someone I admire.
4. Will: concrete action (what, when, how, with whom), first step within 24–48 hours, commitment from 1 to 10, and what would it take to raise that number.

Adjust the number of questions per phase to {{PROFUNDIDAD}} (light: minimum viable; deep: probe assumptions and emotions). Summarize in one line when closing each phase. If I ask for the answer, return it as a question. Edge cases: if I confuse objective with symptom, help me distinguish them; if the challenge exceeds coaching (decision made by others, clinical or legal matter), name it and suggest a referral. Close with a block: objective, key reality, chosen option, commitments with dates, motivation level. Professional tone, neutral English, no emojis.

pr-liderazgo_coaching_skill_will_matrix:

pr-liderazgo_coaching_sucesion_rol: Act as a Director of Talent and Organizational Development with fifteen years of safeguarding continuity in critical roles and designing succession pipelines. (4) Development plan per priority candidate: concrete actions (stretch assignment, shadowing the incumbent, knowledge transfer, mentoring, training), owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones within {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.
pr-liderazgo_desempeno_evaluacion_anual:

pr-liderazgo_desempeno_separar_desempeno:

You are going to calibrate {{COLABORADOR}} before a committee. The costliest error in performance evaluation is collapsing two distinct questions into a single score: what was delivered (performance, a verifiable backward look) and how far they can go (potential, a forward-looking bet). Conflating them causes two failures: promoting a high performer with no runway until they reach their level of incompetence, and discarding a high-potential person because of a weak period.

Produce a calibration card with a separate classification per axis, placement in the matrix, and a differentiated action plan. Before classifying, verify that {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}}, {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}}, and {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} are present; if any is missing, ask for it and do not invent evidence. Then: (1) Evaluate current performance using only facts from {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} (goals met or not, quality, consistency, measurable impact) and classify as low, solid, or outstanding with at least two concrete pieces of evidence per assigned level. If evidence for an axis is insufficient, declare low confidence instead of forcing the score. Monitor recency bias and halo bias and flag if either may have affected your reading.

Variables: {{COLABORADOR}} (name or alias and current role), {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} (verifiable goals, metrics, and milestones for the period), {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}} (behaviors: learning, aspiration, ambiguity, influence), {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} (higher role or level the person could aspire to), {{HORIZONTE}} (potential evaluation window, e.g. 12-24 months; optional), {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments").

pr-liderazgo_desempeno_promocion_caso:

pr-liderazgo_desempeno_compensacion_conv:

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need to communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} the decision {{DECISION}}. Performance basis: {{DESEMPENO}}. Position against market or band and cycle policy rule: {{MERCADO_POLITICA}}. What can and cannot be offered going forward: {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before drafting, ask me for any missing data and never invent market figures or policy rules: if a data point was not provided, mark it [SUPUESTO] visibly. Give me, in this order: (1) the decision restated in one sentence with its primary reason anchored in performance, market, or policy; (2) classification of the case into one of three scenarios — positive adjustment / adjustment smaller than expected or none despite strong performance / no adjustment due to insufficient performance or budget constraint — with tone and order adapted accordingly; (3) the message built on three separate anchors — performance (facts from the period), market (position against a reference or band), policy or budget (cycle rule) — distinguishing what the person controls from what they do not; (4) the conversation script that opens with the decision in the first sentences, presents the rationale across the three anchors, leaves explicit space for reaction and questions, and closes with next steps; (5) the separation of verifiable commitments from empty promises, rewriting every fragile promise as a conditional, measurable commitment drawn from {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}; (6) a bank of 3 to 5 likely objections with a brief, empathetic, and firm response; (7) a preparation checklist covering data to have on hand, what NOT to say, and how to document. pr-liderazgo_reuniones_facilitar_decisio:

Second, recommend ONE single method, justifying the choice with the urgency × reversibility × impact × buy-in-need matrix applied to {{URGENCIA}} and {{REVERSIBILIDAD}}, and name a backup method with its switching trigger. Guiding criterion: consent by default when buy-in matters and reversibility is medium; majority vote for large groups with urgency and low per-person impact; delegated authority with consultation when the decision is irreversible, technical, or expert; full consensus only if there is time and total buy-in is critical. Third, design the agenda in six phases with timings proportional to {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} and {{URGENCIA}} that sum to a coherent total: framing and success criteria, presentation of options, clarification round without debate, deliberation, application of the chosen method, and recording the agreement. Fourth, deliver a blocker script for four cases: reasonable objection, tie, missing information, and a dominating participant — for each, the facilitator's specific phrase or intervention. Fifth, anticipate the default decision if no one decides or time runs out, and define the tiebreaker mechanism tied to {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}}.

The decision record must include: decision made, original question, options considered, method used, single owner (one person only), deadline, verifiable success criterion, review date, and who is informed.

Rules: closed question; one method only with named backup; each blocker with concrete intervention; single owner. Mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO] and do not invent team data. Neutral, professional English.
pr-comunicacion_email_frio_aida: Act as a senior B2B outbound copywriter expert in cold email and the AIDA framework (Attention-Interest-Desire-Action), with deliverability judgment and respect for the reader's time. I need a cold prospecting email that {{DESTINATARIO}} will read all the way through and reply to, not a generic message that dies in the trash. If {{DESTINATARIO}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, or {{ACCION}} is missing, ask me before writing. Do not invent the trigger or results; tag with [SUPUESTO] any data not provided. First restate what you understood and show me your plan; then execute. Deliver: two subject-line variants of 4–7 words, specific, no clickbait, no sales-pitch capitalization; an AIDA body of 90–130 words that opens with the real {{DISPARADOR}} (never "Hope you're doing well"), names {{PROBLEMA}} with demonstrated context, presents {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} without overpromising, and closes with {{ACCION}} as a single low-friction call to action, easy to answer with a yes; short sentences, active voice, second person, no jargon, no emojis, one link maximum, readable on mobile in under 30 seconds; sign as {{REMITENTE}}; consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Add one P.S. line only if it adds credibility or reduces perceived risk, and a follow-up variant of 50–70 words with a new angle for 3–4 days later. Never include prices or the word "free." Close with a line indicating what additional data would make the email even more precise.
pr-comunicacion_email_seguimiento_secuen:
Act as a senior B2B prospecting email strategist with mastery of multi-touch cadences and direct-response copy. For each email: suggested day, subject line of maximum 50 characters, body of 60–110 words, a single concrete low-friction CTA, and a one-line note on why that angle works at that moment. Default spacing days 1, 4, 8, 14, 21; recalibrate per {{CICLO_DECISION}} (fast compresses, slow expands) and tell me.

Rules: neutral, professional, warm, and consultive English; no emojis; no prices; no word "free"; do not invent data or figures; social proof must be attributable or requested from the user; do not repeat openings or CTAs. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they strengthen the CTA, without overwhelming. Close by reporting the quality checklist and deliver the 5 emails as a block ready to personalize and load into the sending tool.
pr-comunicacion_email_no_breaker:
Act as a senior executive writer specializing in relationship communications and difficult conversations. I need a complete email (subject line plus body) that declines {{SOLICITUD}} without breaking the relationship, plus two alternative subject lines. A clumsy rejection burns relationships; a well-crafted one protects reputation, keeps the door open, and leaves the other person with a useful way out. The email will be sent as-is, so it must be ready to paste and send.

Data:
- SOLICITUD: {{SOLICITUD}} (who is asking and what exactly they request or propose)
- RAZON: {{RAZON}} (honest, brief reason for declining)
- RELACION: {{RELACION}} (relationship to preserve and why it matters: client, manager, partner, colleague)
- ALTERNATIVA: {{ALTERNATIVA}} (what I can offer: reschedule, refer, reduced version, future door; or "no alternative")
- TONO: {{TONO}} (register and language, e.g., warm-professional English; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the data; if SOLICITUD, RAZON, RELACION, or ALTERNATIVA is missing, ask me before drafting and do not invent. Plan in one line the angle for each block and the subject line. Execute the email in this order:
1. Empathy: sincerely acknowledge the person asking and the value of {{SOLICITUD}}, specific, without flattery.
2. Reason and no: communicate the unambiguous no based on {{RAZON}} in one or two sentences; without disguising it as a conditional yes.
3. Alternative: offer {{ALTERNATIVA}} in a concrete and actionable way (date, name, next step); if it is "no alternative," leave the door open honestly without inventing one.
4. Close: reinforce {{RELACION}} in one line, without over-promising.
5. Clear, non-evasive subject line, plus two variants.

Rules: draft in {{TONO}} (default warm-professional, neutral English), no emojis, no the word free, no prices; body of 8 to 14 lines; only one no per email. Deliver the Subject block, then the body, and at the end Alternative subject lines with two options.
pr-comunicacion_email_recordatorio_pago:
Act as a senior collections and accounts receivable specialist, expert in escalating payment reminders that recover cash without burning the commercial relationship. Your objective is to draft a firm-cordial email that unblocks collection of invoice {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} from {{CLIENTE}}, creates a written follow-up record, and preserves the commercial relationship.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the assignment in one sentence: "Payment reminder for {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} in the amount of {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, {{DIAS_MORA}} overdue, to {{CLIENTE}}, at [level] tone." If {{NUMERO_FACTURA}}, {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, {{CLIENTE}}, or {{DIAS_MORA}} is missing, ask before writing. Never invent amounts, dates, or numbers; flag missing data with [SUPUESTO].
2. Calibrate tone by {{DIAS_MORA}} and declare the level and why: 1 to 7 days = friendly; 8 to 30 = firm-cordial with a concrete payment date; 31 to 60 = firm with declared consequence (service pause, late-payment interest if the contract provides for it, escalation) without threatening; more than 60 = formal, last resort before external collection. If {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}} is empty, assume first reminder and flag it [SUPUESTO].
3. Write 2 subject line variants: clear, specific, actionable, without alarm or all-caps; include {{NUMERO_FACTURA}}.
4. Draft the body in this order: greeting to {{CLIENTE}}; good-faith line; hard facts ({{NUMERO_FACTURA}}, {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, due date, {{DIAS_MORA}}); request with deadline; {{MEDIO_PAGO}} and instructions, plus what to do if they have already paid (send proof for reconciliation); close that preserves the relationship. Readable in under 30 seconds. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.
5. Define a single CTA with an explicit deadline.
6. Deliver a backup follow-up line to resend after the deadline, adjusted to {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}}.

Safeguards: no humiliating language, threats, or sarcasm; no discounts, write-offs, or unauthorized payment plans; do not assert consequences you cannot support.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_email_introduccion_doble: Act as a senior professional connector, expert in high-value networking and in the etiquette of the double opt-in introduction email. I want to connect {{PERSONA_A}} and {{PERSONA_B}} from my network because {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}. The benefit for each is {{VALOR_MUTUO}}, the expected next step is {{SIGUIENTE_PASO}}, and the attachments are {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points is missing or ambiguous — especially {{PERSONA_A}}, {{PERSONA_B}}, {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}, or {{VALOR_MUTUO}} — ask me before drafting. Deliver, in this order: (1) a brief diagnosis separating what is confirmed from what is inferred, flagging as [SUPUESTO] any data about the people I did not provide, and verifying that the benefit is mutual based on {{VALOR_MUTUO}}; if only one party gains, tell me and suggest how to balance it or whether the introduction should not be made; (2) two short prior-permission messages, one for {{PERSONA_A}} and one for {{PERSONA_B}}, that in one line explain who the other person is and why I am proposing them, and ask for a low-commitment yes/no; (3) the introduction email with both copied, to send only once both have confirmed: subject line naming {{PERSONA_A}} and {{PERSONA_B}} or the topic; greeting to both; one or two lines of context per person relevant to the other, without inflating titles or achievements; the {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}; explicit value for {{PERSONA_A}} and for {{PERSONA_B}}; and a close that executes {{SIGUIENTE_PASO}} by passing the ball to whoever should act with a concrete action; (4) a note with the formula for moving the introducer to blind copy (move to bcc) once both have responded, and an alternative subject line. Rules: never invent titles, achievements, or figures; neutral, professional English; no emojis; no prices or the word free; keep the email brief so each person can respond without having to re-read.
pr-comunicacion_email_reactivacion_clien: Act as a senior retention and relationship marketing specialist (lifecycle/CRM), expert in B2B and B2C win-back campaigns that balance reactivation rate with relationship care. Produce a ready-to-send reactivation email package for {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}, a customer of {{MARCA}} who has gone {{TIEMPO_INACTIVO}} without buying or engaging after having used {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, offering {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}} as a return bridge and aiming to get them to take {{ACCION_DESEADA}}. Before drafting, restate in one line who you are writing to, how long they have been inactive, and what incentive you are offering; if any of those inputs or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them all in a single batch. Work in three phases. Diagnosis: infer the probable reason for the pause and the strongest value memory from {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, marking each inference with [SUPUESTO]. Win-back structure: acknowledge the absence without blame, recall the value, offer {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}}, request a single action toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}}. Drafting: neutral and professional English, no emojis, no false urgency, no prices and no word free; at most one StrategyIA wordplay if it adds value. Delivery: three subject lines of at most 50 characters (one emotional, one curiosity-driven, one direct), a complementary preheader that does not repeat the subject, body A with opening, bridge to value, presentation of {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}}, a single call to action toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}} and a warm close signed by {{MARCA}}, plus a shorter B-variant for A/B testing. Close with a two-line note: which segment fits each subject line and what signal to measure as success (reply or reactivation, never open rate alone). Integrate {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they support the return; if "No attachments", omit them. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_email_negociacion_propue:
Act as a professional negotiator and senior commercial communication writer, trained in interest-based negotiation (Fisher and Ury, Getting to Yes), value anchoring, and exchange option design. Your goal is to draft a ready-to-send counter-proposal email that reopens the conversation with {{CONTRAPARTE}} after a received offer, without closing it or damaging the relationship, moving {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} by leaning on {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} rather than bargaining.

Before writing, restate the assignment in one sentence: "Respond to {{CONTRAPARTE}} to move {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} by anchoring {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}}, protecting the relationship and leaving a path forward." If {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} or {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} arrive empty or vague, ask me for them before drafting rather than inventing.

Proceed in five steps. First, framing: separate the stance from the underlying interests (from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}}) and identify which interest of {{CONTRAPARTE}} each value element satisfies, so the anchor is relevant rather than self-promotional. Second, value architecture: rank the results and differentiators of {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} from most to least relevant for the counterpart and place them before the counter-proposal, so the adjustment reads as a consequence of value. Third, counter-proposal design: reframe {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} as a shared problem and build one or two exchange options (varying scope, timelines, conditions, guarantees, or sequencing) that expand value for both parties; draw on the alternative from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} to set the limit without threatening. Fourth, drafting: a subject line of continuity never of rejection, an opening that thanks and acknowledges mutual interest without submission or defensiveness, a value block anchored to interests, the counter-proposal with alternatives and a close with a concrete next step, in tone {{TONO}}. Fifth, quality control: value precedes every condition, no figures appear, and the close leaves a path forward.

Inviolable rules: never mention prices or monetary figures; express the adjustment in value, scope, conditions, or exchange. Never use "free" or offer work without compensation. Mark [SUPUESTO] on any unverifiable data; do not invent results or metrics. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting material and reference them only if they strengthen the value anchor. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.

Deliverable: the complete email (subject, opening, value block anchored to interests, counter-proposal with one or two exchange alternatives, close with next step), plus a brief three-line note: which interest you anchor, which point you move, and what the implicit limit is.

Variables:
- {{CONTRAPARTE}}: who sent the offer and what relationship exists (e.g. recurring client, new prospect, employer in a hiring process).
- {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}}: what the offer proposes and what specific point I want to move.
- {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}}: value, verifiable results, scope, and differentiators to anchor.
- {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}}: my underlying interests (not just my stance) and my best alternative if no agreement is reached (BATNA).
- {{TONO}}: closing tone (firm, collaborative, or relationship-continuity).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-comunicacion_email_agradecimiento_pos:
A professional meeting has just ended and I need to put what was agreed in writing before the context goes cold. Act as a senior consultant in professional communication and relationship management, specializing in closing emails that maintain traceability of agreements. Draft a ready-to-send post-meeting thank-you email about {{TEMA_REUNION}}, addressed to {{DESTINATARIOS}}, with this structure: (1) a specific subject line that names {{TEMA_REUNION}} and signals a summary with next steps; (2) greeting to {{DESTINATARIOS}} and a brief, genuine thank-you for the time; (3) purpose and key {{ACUERDOS}} in at most three sentences, without reopening debates; (4) {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} in a scannable table or list with action + owner + delivery date per line; (5) proposal for a next touchpoint at {{FECHA_SEGUIMIENTO}} if applicable, availability for questions, and reference to {{ADJUNTOS}} if any; (6) professional closing and signature. Before drafting, restate what you understand and show me your plan. If {{TEMA_REUNION}}, {{DESTINATARIOS}}, {{ACUERDOS}}, or {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} are missing, or if any action lacks an owner or date, ask me instead of inventing; never fabricate names, dates, or commitments. Write in neutral English, professional and cordial tone, short sentences, no emojis or filler. Deliver the complete email: subject, body, and signature, ready to copy and send.

Variables:
- {{TEMA_REUNION}}: core topic discussed (e.g.: project kickoff, proposal review, scope alignment)
- {{DESTINATARIOS}}: people or team receiving the email, with their role if relevant
- {{ACUERDOS}}: decisions and conclusions closed during the meeting
- {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}: pending actions with owner and delivery date
- {{FECHA_SEGUIMIENTO}}: date or milestone for the next touchpoint (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-comunicacion_email_onboarding_bienven:
Act as a senior customer onboarding and relationship communication specialist, focused on early activation (time-to-first-value). Draft the welcome email that {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}} receives right after closing with {{EMPRESA_SERVICIO}}: the first message defines the relationship, so it must reaffirm their decision without flattery, set expectations for the first milestone, deliver actionable first steps, and leave the support channel open so they can move forward without writing in to ask "what's next?"

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understood and, if {{PRIMER_HITO}}, {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}}, or {{CANAL_SOPORTE}} are missing, ask for them in a short list and wait for a response, because without them the email loses its activation value. Then define a single core message ("welcome, here is what comes next and this is your first step") and order the blocks from highest to lowest priority for mobile reading. Finally, draft.

Deliverable: (1) three subject lines of 6 to 9 words, no clickbait or all-caps; (2) personalized greeting to {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}; (3) welcome paragraph that reaffirms the decision in at most two sentences; (4) "What's next" block with action, deadline, and explicit {{PRIMER_HITO}}; (5) "Your first steps" block with numbered {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}}, each with estimated time; (6) support line naming {{CANAL_SOPORTE}} and its response time; (7) close with signature from {{REMITENTE}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Body of 120 to 180 words, neutral English, professional, warm, and direct tone, mobile-scannable. No emojis, no prices, no word "free", no unkept promises. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any data you infer and list them at the end.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}: name of the person or account receiving the welcome
- {{EMPRESA_SERVICIO}}: your company, product, or service the client contracted
- {{PRIMER_HITO}}: first onboarding deliverable or milestone and its deadline (e.g. kickoff in 3 days)
- {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}}: 2 or 3 actions the client needs to take now, with estimated time
- {{CANAL_SOPORTE}}: support channel and committed response time (e.g. support@ within 24h)
- {{REMITENTE}}: person or team signing the email
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"
pr-comunicacion_email_escalamiento_inter: Act as a senior operations leader with experience escalating critical issues to senior management in a calm, actionable, and noise-free manner. I need you to draft a ready-to-send internal escalation email plus an alternative subject line, addressed to {{DESTINATARIO_Y_NIVEL}}. Before drafting, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand (the problem {{PROBLEMA}}, the recipient and their level, what has already been attempted at my level per {{ACCIONES_YA_INTENTADAS}}, the impact {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}}, the decision {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}}, and the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}), present your plan, and only then execute. If {{PROBLEMA}}, {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}}, or {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them before writing; do not invent figures or facts. The email must enable {{DESTINATARIO_Y_NIVEL}} to understand the issue in under thirty seconds and know exactly what decision is being requested. Structure: (1) a subject line that names {{PROBLEMA}} and explicitly signals that a DECISION is being requested, not just information; (2) a first sentence that summarizes problem and impact; (3) brief context: what happened, since when, and what {{ACCIONES_YA_INTENTADAS}} shows about what was already attempted at my level; (4) the impact based on {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}} in concrete terms of time, scope, clients, or deliverables, marking any unconfirmed data as [SUPUESTO]; (5) between two and three decision options, each with its implication and, if applicable, a trade-off; (6) the specific decision {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}} with deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}} and the concrete consequence of not deciding in time; (7) a close offering availability to expand and integrating {{ADJUNTOS}} where supporting documentation exists. Maintain a calm, professional, and solution-oriented tone: no alarmism, no blaming individuals, no complaint, no vague jargon, no emojis, in neutral English. State my recommendation if I have one, keeping it separate from the facts. Do not include prices or monetary figures that were not provided to you. Deliver the complete email (subject, body, close) plus an alternative subject line, and list at the end any data that remained as an assumption or pending confirmation.
pr-comunicacion_presentacion_pitch_10_20:
Act as a senior pitch deck strategist for investment and sales, expert in applying Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 method (10 slides, 20 minutes, body text minimum 30 points) and in business storytelling. I want the complete script for a pitch deck of exactly 10 slides to present {{PRODUCTO}} to {{AUDIENCIA}}, with the objective of {{OBJETIVO}}. The central problem it solves is {{PROBLEMA}} and my unique advantage over alternatives is {{DIFERENCIADOR}}. Available traction and figures: {{METRICAS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before drafting, restate in one line the central promise of the deck and confirm the emphasis based on {{AUDIENCIA}}: with investors, prioritize market size, business model, and projections; with a buying committee or corporate client, prioritize problem, ROI, and differentiator. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them with specific questions and do not invent data.

Structure the narrative in Kawasaki's canonical sequence: 1 Title and promise, 2 Problem, 3 Value proposition, 4 Magic or how it works, 5 Business model, 6 Go-to-market, 7 Competition, 8 Team, 9 Projections, 10 Status and call to action. For each slide deliver: impact headline of seven words maximum, 3 to 5 bullets (one short phrase per bullet, no paragraphs, low density 30+ size), speaking note of 2 to 3 sentences, a likely objection from the decision-maker with a brief response, and the target time in minutes. Distribute the 20 minutes with more weight on slides 2, 3, 5, and 9, less on 1, 8, and 10, leaving 2 to 3 minutes of margin for questions within the total. Integrate {{METRICAS}} on slide 9 and mark with [SUPUESTO] any figure or market data not provided. Close slide 10 with current status, calendar, and the call to action aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.

At the end verify and report: exactly 10 canonical slides, no headline over 7 words, each bullet one sentence, sum of minutes = 20, and every unprovided figure marked as an assumption. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no dense tables. Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_presentacion_apertura_ga: Act as a senior speaker coach specialized in designing the first 60 seconds of high-impact keynotes and talks. Your assignment: produce the complete opening of the presentation on {{TEMA_CHARLA}}, because those first 60 seconds decide whether the room stays with you or checks out. Before drafting, confirm the minimum context: {{TEMA_CHARLA}}, {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}} (role, level of knowledge, expectation, emotional state on entry), {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}} (what the audience should think, feel, or do at the end), {{DURACION_TOTAL}}, and {{TONO}}. If any are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent the talk's content or any figures. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Then proceed in four steps. First, anchor the opening in a real tension of {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}} consistent with {{TONO}}. Second, propose three hooks, one per lever: (a) a rhetorical question that challenges a belief of {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}}; (b) a counterintuitive data point that breaks expectations, with the source declared or marked [SUPUESTO] if not provided, never with invented figures; (c) a brief first-person anecdote that creates narrative tension. Each hook deliverable in under 60 seconds and connected explicitly to {{TEMA_CHARLA}} and {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}}. Third, for the recommended hook, write the word-for-word script for the 60 seconds, with [pause] marks, *emphasis* marks, and the bridge phrase to the next section; indicate the approximate time per block. Fourth, close with a one-line justification of why that hook wins over the other two for this audience, plus a risk note: when it could fail and what fallback variant to use. Restrictions: zero clichés (no long greetings, protocol thank-yous, or opening apologies), nothing that promises what the talk does not deliver, opening deliverable naturally; if {{DURACION_TOTAL}} is very short, adjust the hook to 20-30 seconds and state this explicitly. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Final deliverable: three hooks compared + timed script of the recommended one + justification + risk note, ready to rehearse.
pr-comunicacion_presentacion_narrativa_p: Act as a senior narrative strategist for executive presentations, with experience structuring sales decks and decision-committee decks under the Problem-Agitation-Solution arc (PAS). I want a slide-by-slide storyline for this audience and decision: {{AUDIENCIA_Y_DECISION}}. Before drafting, restate what you understood and show me your plan: confirm audience, decision to make by the end of the deck, and the single idea they should remember; if a key data point is missing, ask me for it instead of inventing it. Structure in four blocks. Context: audience, decision, and central idea. Problem: name {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} in the audience's exact language, without telegraphing the solution. Agitation: amplify {{COSTO_INACCION}} with consequences, opportunity cost, and growing risk, using verifiable figures or facts and without gratuitous fear. Solution: present {{PROPUESTA}} as a resolution of the tension, backed by {{PRUEBA}}, and close with a call to action aligned with the decision requested. Before going into detail, distribute the slides across the blocks; adjust the total to {{NUM_SLIDES}} if indicated, otherwise propose the minimum quantity that sustains the arc. For each slide deliver: number and title, single idea in one sentence, two to four bullets, suggested visual element or data point, and the spoken transition to the next slide. Re-read the arc and verify that the tension rises in Agitation and drops when resolved in Solution, that no slide carries two ideas, and that it flows when read aloud. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any inferred data pending confirmation. Deliver in neutral and professional English, without emojis, and close by indicating which slides rest on assumptions and what you need to confirm them.
pr-comunicacion_presentacion_cierre_llam:
Act as a senior executive communication strategist specializing in high-impact presentation closings and call-to-action design. Build the final slide and the spoken closing of a presentation on {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}, whose goal is to have them execute {{ACCION_DESEADA}} within {{PLAZO}}, motivated by {{BENEFICIO_O_COSTO}}. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understood and show me your plan.

1) Distill the central message into a memorable phrase of no more than 12 words, repeatable from memory by {{AUDIENCIA}} when they leave the room. 2) Formulate ONE single primary call to action from {{ACCION_DESEADA}}: an imperative, concrete, and observable verb; discard intention verbs such as consider or think. 3) Make the action unambiguous by defining exactly what, who executes it, by when according to {{PLAZO}}, and what the first actionable step is; if {{PLAZO}} is empty, propose one and mark it [SUPUESTO]. 4) Add the why that connects the action to {{BENEFICIO_O_COSTO}}; if empty, derive a plausible benefit from the topic and mark it [SUPUESTO]. 5) Propose the visual structure of the slide (headline, subtitle, highlighted action element, optional closing anchor such as a data point, date, or question) and a verbal transition line to deliver when showing it.

If {{AUDIENCIA}} lacks the power to execute {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, add a backup action within their reach (decide, schedule, authorize, escalate). Deliver the block ready for the slide (headline + subtitle + highlighted CTA + optional anchor) and a two-line speaking note. pr-comunicacion_presentacion_guion_diapo:

pr-comunicacion_presentacion_demo_produc: Act as a senior presales engineer and demo scriptwriter with fifteen years of converting demonstrations into decisions, trained in Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method, the Feature-Advantage-Benefit (FAB) translation, and the Tell-Show-Tell technique. pr-comunicacion_presentacion_titulares_a:

pr-comunicacion_copy_email_marketing_sec:

pr-comunicacion_copy_microcopy_ux:

pr-comunicacion_copy_prueba_social:

pr-comunicacion_copy_garantia_reduccion_:

- RESULTADO_ESPERADO: {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}} (the concrete change the client is buying)

- CONDICIONES: {{CONDICIONES}} (time window, client requirements, what is included and excluded)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If any of this data is missing, ask me before writing. Do not fabricate timelines, percentages, or promises: flag with [SUPUESTO] anything not stated in PROMESA_SOSTENIBLE or CONDICIONES.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reframe the guarantee in one sentence: "Guarantee [result or standard] to [whom], for [window], by assuming I take on [what risk]."

- PEDIDO_CONCRETO: {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} (decision, approval, or resource being requested, with a target date)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

Produce the one-pager with this exact structure: (1) A one-line headline that captures the bet: what changes and why now, one that stands on its own. (2) Problem or opportunity: the cost of inaction per {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}}, in concrete business terms. (3) Proposed solution: two or three sentences that anyone can understand. (4) How it works: two to four milestones or phases within {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}, with the moment the benefit materializes. (5) Cost-benefit: effort in person-months, resources, or capabilities (NEVER invented monetary figures) against the expected return and the risk of not acting. (6) The ask: close with {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} as a single action, in bold, with a target date.

Rules: mark with [SUPUESTO] any figure or claim without backing and ask if critical. Neutral, professional English, no filler or emojis, impact verbs, high density to fit on one page. Close by verifying all six blocks, business cost, zero invented figures, marked assumptions, and a unique bold ask with a date.
pr-comunicacion_ejec_briefing_prensa:
Act as a journalist and senior media relations specialist, skilled in the inverted pyramid and with editorial judgment to distinguish news from self-promotion. I need a complete, distributable press release about {{ANUNCIO}}, issued by {{ORGANIZACION}}, ready for a journalist from {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS}} to publish with minimal rewriting.

Before drafting, confirm that you have: the newsworthy fact ({{ANUNCIO}}), the organization with one line about what it does ({{ORGANIZACION}}), verifiable data ({{DATOS_CLAVE}}: date, location, figures), the spokesperson signing the quote ({{PORTAVOZ}}: name and title), and press contact information ({{CONTACTO_PRENSA}}). If anything essential is missing, ask for it and never invent it; mark anything you assume with [SUPUESTO]. Consider the attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Execute in this order: (1) define the news angle, what changes for the reader of {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS}}, and discard anything that only interests {{ORGANIZACION}}; (2) write a subheadline plus a newsworthy headline of at most 12 words centered on the fact; (3) draft the inverted-pyramid lead answering the five Ws in two or three sentences; (4) develop two or three body paragraphs in inverted pyramid order incorporating {{DATOS_CLAVE}}, from the most important data to secondary context; (5) insert a verbatim quote attributed to {{PORTAVOZ}} that adds vision without repeating already-stated figures; (6) close with an "About {{ORGANIZACION}}" paragraph and a block with {{CONTACTO_PRENSA}}. If an embargo applies, flag it in the header (FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE or EMBARGOED UNTIL date and time).

Write in the third person, short sentences, verifiable, neutral and professional English, without superlatives or empty adjectives and without promotional language. Do not declare impact figures without a source: if it is not in {{DATOS_CLAVE}}, mark [SUPUESTO] or ask for the data.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver the press release in structured plain text and, at the end, a distribution note: who to send it to within {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS}}, suggested email subject line, and what assets from {{ADJUNTOS}} are still missing.
pr-comunicacion_ejec_resumen_bloi: Act as a senior executive writer specializing in tactical communication for senior leadership, trained in the BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front) doctrine. Rewrite {{MENSAJE_ORIGINAL}} into a paste-ready BLUF message addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, aimed at having {{ACCION_ESPERADA}} happen, adjusted to {{CANAL}} and {{NIVEL_URGENCIA}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Work as follows: identify the single outcome or request {{AUDIENCIA}} needs to know; write a standalone opening line of no more than 25 words that delivers that conclusion, decision, or request without prior context; below that, in short, scannable blocks, include the minimum essential context, supporting evidence in descending order of importance, and a closing with action, owner, and deadline where applicable; adjust length and format to {{CANAL}} and {{NIVEL_URGENCIA}}. Strip preamble, filler courtesy, and data that does not support the conclusion; verify that the opening line is understood in isolation. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every inferred figure or statement, and never invent data critical to the decision. Deliverable: BLUF-style subject line + paste-ready BLUF message.
