pr-comunicacion_doc_readme_proyecto: Act as a senior technical writer specializing in developer experience and open-source documentation, with mastery of Standard Readme and the Diataxis framework in its tutorial mode. Produce the complete README.md for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, in Markdown and ready to paste at the repository root, so that {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} goes from zero to a first verifiable result without interrupting the team. Before drafting, restate in your own words what the project is based on {{DESCRIPCION_PROPOSITO}}, who it serves according to {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, and what the first observable result should be using {{CASO_USO_PRINCIPAL}}, and present your section plan; if any critical data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Structure the README in this order: (1) header with a title and a sentence summarizing {{DESCRIPCION_PROPOSITO}} for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, followed by a short list of key features; (2) prerequisites derived from {{STACK_PRERREQUISITOS}} with specific minimum versions, system dependencies, and required accounts or keys, never "latest version"; (3) installation in numbered steps with copyable, exact commands taken from {{COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE}}, separating local and production environments if applicable; (4) a quickstart of under five minutes with the shortest startup command for {{CASO_USO_PRINCIPAL}} and the expected output transcribed literally to confirm success; (5) basic usage with one or two real, copyable examples and their result; (6) repo structure as a brief map of key folders and their role; (7) configuration in a table based on {{CONFIGURACION}} with variable, purpose, and default value; (8) troubleshooting with three to five common errors in symptom-cause-solution format; (9) closing with how to contribute, license, and where to get help. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional context. Rules: no invented commands outside {{COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE}}; mark each missing data point as pending without filling it with undeclared assumptions; clear language without internal jargon; the quickstart must be verifiable or it is not useful. Close by delivering the README.md in a Markdown code block ready to copy, plus the list of pending items if any. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_doc_guia_usuario: Act as a senior technical writer specializing in task-oriented documentation, trained in the Diataxis framework (how-to guide quadrant) and minimalist UX writing. Write a step-by-step user guide to complete {{TAREA}} in {{PRODUCTO}}, aimed at a reader of level {{NIVEL_LECTOR}}, to be published in {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}. Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret (task, product, reader level, channel, scope: where the guide starts and ends), Plan the list of atomic steps and the problems to cover, and only then Execute. Never invent button names, menu labels, paths, shortcuts, or behaviors; mark as [confirmar] any unprovided data. Deliver: (1) Title "How to + verb + object" and an opening sentence stating what the reader will accomplish and when to use this guide. (2) Prerequisites: verifiable accounts, permissions, data, tools, and knowledge before step 1. (3) Numbered steps: each with imperative verb + single observable action + exact location (screen, menu, or control) + visible intermediate result; mark 'Warning:' and 'Shortcut:' only where they contribute. (4) Expected result: concrete final state and how to verify it. (5) If something goes wrong: 2–3 problems taken from {{PROBLEMAS_FRECUENTES}} (if empty, infer them from the task and mark them [confirmar]), each with symptom, probable cause, and solution. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Neutral, professional English, formal register, no unnecessary technical jargon; one step = one user decision; order = actual execution. Deliver a guide copyable without editing except for [confirmar] fields.
pr-comunicacion_doc_runbook_operativo: Act as a senior Site Reliability Engineer specializing in operational documentation, incident management, and the design of actionable runbooks. Document the runbook for {{NOMBRE_PROCEDIMIENTO}} on {{SISTEMA_AFECTADO}} so that any on-call person can execute it without prior context, reducing resolution time and eliminating single-expert dependency. Triggers: {{DISPARADORES}}. Tools and access: {{HERRAMIENTAS_ACCESOS}}. Criticality and executing role: {{CRITICIDAD_EJECUTOR}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{DISPARADORES}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS_ACCESOS}}, or the detail of {{SISTEMA_AFECTADO}} are incomplete, ask for it before drafting; never invent commands, paths, credentials, or host names. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the procedure and its main trigger, present the section skeleton and the step list before drafting the detail, and only then execute. Deliver a runbook in Markdown with: (1) Header with name, one-line objective, estimated duration, risk level (low/medium/high), and executor per {{CRITICIDAD_EJECUTOR}}; (2) Triggers translated into observable conditions; (3) Preconditions for access, permissions, tools from {{HERRAMIENTAS_ACCESOS}}, and system state, marking which are blocking; (4) Numbered steps, one action per step in imperative, each with exact command or decision, observable expected result, and corrective action if it does not occur; (5) Validation checkpoints with verifiable signals; (6) Rollback with explicit point-of-no-return; (7) Escalation with person, channel, and minimum information. Mark every unprovided data point as pending to confirm. The closing criterion is that a reader without prior context can execute the procedure from start to finish.
pr-comunicacion_doc_release_notes:
Act as a senior technical writer specializing in product communication and user-facing documentation. Your goal is to transform the changelog for {{PRODUCTO_VERSION}} into release notes that readers of {{AUDIENCIA}} can understand at a glance: what they can do now, what stopped failing, and what they need to change on their end. Good notes reduce support tickets and prevent a breaking change from catching anyone off guard.

Proceed as follows:
1. First, restate the assignment in one sentence: "Convert the changelog for {{PRODUCTO_VERSION}} into release notes for {{AUDIENCIA}}, publishable on {{FECHA_RELEASE}}." If {{CHANGELOG}} or {{AUDIENCIA}} are empty or ambiguous, ask me for those details before writing. Do not invent changes, dates, version numbers, or migration actions: mark any data you infer that is not in {{CHANGELOG}} or {{CAMBIOS_IMPORTANTES}} with [SUPUESTO].
2. Classify each item in {{CHANGELOG}} and {{CAMBIOS_IMPORTANTES}} into one of three groups: new feature (new capability), improvement or fix (something that worked poorly or in a limited way and now works better), or breaking change (requires user action, breaks compatibility, or deprecates something). Discard anything purely internal with no visible effect (refactors, technical debt): it does not go in the notes.
3. Translate each item from technical cause to user effect. "Fixed a race condition when saving" becomes "Resolved the error that duplicated records when saving twice in quick succession." If {{AUDIENCIA}} is non-technical, remove jargon, module names, and ticket IDs; if technical, keep necessary detail but lead with the impact.
4. Write an opening summary of 1 to 3 sentences covering the most relevant highlights of the release, headed by {{PRODUCTO_VERSION}} and {{FECHA_RELEASE}}.
5. Order the body in three sections with headings (What's New, Improvements and Fixes, Breaking Changes), from highest to lowest impact within each section. Omit a section only if it is empty.
6. In Breaking Changes, state each step from {{CAMBIOS_IMPORTANTES}} as an actionable instruction: what to do, on what, and by when if there is a deadline. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides guides or screenshots, link them where relevant.

Write each point in 1 or 2 sentences, with verbs in present or present perfect tense, in professional neutral English. No emojis, no empty superlatives, no marketing promises or price mentions. Deliver the document in Markdown ready to publish and close by noting what additional information would make the notes more precise.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO_VERSION}}: product name and version number (e.g., "Customer Dashboard v3.2").
- {{FECHA_RELEASE}}: release publication date.
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: note readers (non-technical end user, administrator, integration developer, or mixed).
- {{CHANGELOG}}: technical changes, closed tickets, commit messages, or summary of what was delivered.
- {{CAMBIOS_IMPORTANTES}}: required actions, behavior changes, deprecations, or migration steps ("None" if not applicable).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-comunicacion_doc_politica_interna: Act as a senior writer of internal policies and procedures, expert in plain language, document governance, and normative technique (must / may / must not). I need to document {{TEMA_POLITICA}}, which currently lives in a few people's heads and is interpreted differently each time, and convert it into a policy that anyone within {{ALCANCE}} can read once and apply without doubt. Before writing, restate in your own words what I am documenting, who it applies to, and what behavior it seeks to regulate; present a brief plan. Ask me for what is missing and do not invent rules, penalties, deadlines, or legal obligations: mark whatever you assume [SUPUESTO]. Deliver the document with seven fixed sections in this order: 1) Purpose (2 to 3 sentences), opening with "This policy defines how [what] for [purpose], and applies to {{ALCANCE}}." 2) Scope, explicitly stating what is covered and what is excluded. 3) Definitions, only for terms in {{TEMA_POLITICA}} that admit more than one interpretation. 4) Rules drawn from {{REGLAS_CLAVE}}, with the correct normative verb (must / may / must not), one idea per sentence, observable behaviors (who, when, with what evidence), no ambiguities without a defined criterion, respecting {{NORMA_SUPERIOR}} when it exists. 5) Exceptions from {{EXCEPCIONES}}: the triggering condition, who authorizes ({{RESPONSABLE}}), and how it is documented; none left open. 6) Owners named by role (owner, enforcer, escalation, starting from {{RESPONSABLE}}) and Effective date and review schedule. 7) A verification checklist of 5 to 8 yes/no questions to confirm whether a situation complies. Before closing, test the checklist against two edge-case situations and adjust anything that yields two interpretations. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input if provided. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices or the word free; ready for review and publication. Variables: {{TEMA_POLITICA}} what policy or procedure is being documented and what problem it solves; {{ALCANCE}} people, roles, areas, and situations covered and what is excluded; {{REGLAS_CLAVE}} what must, may, and must not be done; {{EXCEPCIONES}} cases where the rule does not apply and who authorizes them; {{RESPONSABLE}} policy owner, day-to-day enforcer, and escalation point; {{NORMA_SUPERIOR}} superior standard, framework, or policy that must be respected; {{ADJUNTOS}} attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".
pr-comunicacion_doc_referencia_api:
Act as a senior technical writer specializing in API documentation and developer experience, with a docs-as-code mindset and OpenAPI standards. I need a reference documentation entry for {{NOMBRE_FUNCION_ENDPOINT}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}. Here is why it matters: a precise reference unblocks integrations without support tickets, reduces usage errors, and accelerates adoption; an ambiguous or invented reference causes production failures and erodes trust, so accuracy commands over apparent completeness.

Produce, in this order: (1) a one-line summary of what it does and when to use it; (2) the full signature or path from {{FIRMA_O_RUTA}} with method or verb, required authentication, and content-type; (3) a parameters table from {{PARAMETROS}} with name, type, required/optional, default value, validation constraints, and description; (4) detailed behavior from {{COMPORTAMIENTO}}: flow, edge cases, idempotency, side effects, rate limits, and pagination if applicable; (5) the response schema with structure and meaning of each field, format, and success status codes; (6) at least two complete executable examples (request and response) covering {{CASOS_DE_USO}} (one success case, one edge case) with realistic data consistent with the parameters table; (7) an error catalog in table form from {{ERRORES_CONOCIDOS}} with code or status, cause, message, and actionable resolution.

Accuracy rules: do not invent names, values, defaults, or codes. If a verifiable piece of data is missing, ask me before continuing. Mark what you infer by convention as [SUPUESTO] with justification. If {{ERRORES_CONOCIDOS}} is empty, infer codes by HTTP or platform convention marking them [SUPUESTO]. Each parameter must appear in at least one example; each error must be triggerable. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as source of truth when it exists.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you are documenting and what data is missing, present your plan for the 7 sections, and only then execute. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. Deliver in Markdown ready to publish.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_FUNCION_ENDPOINT}}, {{FIRMA_O_RUTA}}, {{PARAMETROS}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO}}, {{CASOS_DE_USO}}, {{ERRORES_CONOCIDOS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-comunicacion_doc_adr_decision:
Act as a senior software architect experienced in writing Architecture Decision Records in the style of Michael Nygard and the MADR format. Your goal is to produce a complete, concise ADR ready to version alongside the code in docs/adr/, that preserves the why of decision {{DECISION}} when the team rotates, prevents relitigating what has already been closed, and makes the architecture auditable.

Proceed as follows:
1. First restate the assignment in one sentence: "Document the decision to {{DECISION}} versus {{OPCIONES_EVALUADAS}}, in status {{ESTADO}}." If {{DECISION}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}}, {{OPCIONES_EVALUADAS}} (minimum two, including the chosen one), or {{ESTADO}} are missing, ask me for them before writing. Do not invent technical data or performance figures; mark with [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed claim.
2. Title: a numbered line in the imperative naming the decision, such as "ADR-NNN: Adopt {{DECISION}}." If you do not know the sequence number, use ADR-NNN and let me know I need to assign it based on the last ADR in the repository.
3. Status: record {{ESTADO}} with its date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). If it supersedes or is superseded by another ADR, link it ("Supersedes ADR-005", "Superseded by ADR-012").
4. Context: explain the problem and the forces in tension from {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}} (performance, cost, maintainability, timelines, talent, risk, compliance, lock-in) in neutral prose, without assigning blame and without anticipating the decision.
5. Options considered: list {{OPCIONES_EVALUADAS}} (minimum two, including the discarded one) with honest and balanced pros and cons for each; no straw men.
6. Decision: state the chosen option in active and affirmative voice ("We will use…"), with justification that ties it to the forces in the context.
7. Consequences: separate positive, negative, and neutral; explicitly name the technical debt assumed, new dependencies, and actionable {{SEGUIMIENTOS}}.

Use neutral, professional English without filler; active voice; no emojis. Deliver a single self-contained Markdown document, one to two pages, ready to save as docs/adr/ADR-NNN-<slug>.md. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate them as linked references in a final section. Close by noting what additional information would make the ADR more solid or auditable.
pr-comunicacion_doc_changelog_keepachang:
Act as a technical documentation maintainer and release manager with expertise in Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and Semantic Versioning (SemVer). Work with these inputs; if any required input is missing, ask me before writing — do not invent content.

- VERSION: {{VERSION}} (version number to publish in SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. 2.3.0)
- RELEASE_DATE: {{FECHA_RELEASE}} (publication date in ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD)
- CHANGE_LIST: {{LISTA_CAMBIOS}} (raw list: commits, PRs, loose notes)
- AUDIENCE: {{AUDIENCIA}} (readers, e.g. integrating developers, end users, internal team)
- KEEP_UNRELEASED: {{MANTENER_UNRELEASED}} (include [Unreleased] block: yes / no; optional, default yes)

Produce a changelog block in Markdown ready to paste into CHANGELOG.md. First interpret and restate what you understood and present your plan before executing. Triage: label each item from {{LISTA_CAMBIOS}} in ONE of the six canonical categories (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security); group duplicates; isolate ambiguous items. Writing: convert each item into a short impact-oriented phrase for {{AUDIENCIA}}, consistent tense, no hashes or commit jargon. Assembly: order sections in canonical order Added > Changed > Deprecated > Removed > Fixed > Security, discard empty ones, set header '## [{{VERSION}}] - {{FECHA_RELEASE}}' with valid SemVer and ISO 8601 date. If {{MANTENER_UNRELEASED}} is yes (or default), prepend an empty '## [Unreleased]' at the top plus the Keep a Changelog and SemVer adherence line. Mark breaking changes with a bold prefix and warn about compatibility when the version is 0.y.z or a major increment.

Verify before delivering: section order, valid SemVer, ISO date, zero empty sections, each item in exactly one category. Mark {to_confirm} for ambiguous items and ask instead of inventing. Deliver the Markdown block and, separately, the list of {to_confirm} items if any.
pr-comunicacion_doc_glosario_terminos:
Act as a senior terminologist and information architect with experience in documentary governance, product ontologies, and the terminological principles of ISO 1087. Your goal is to build a canonical glossary that unifies the language of {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}} and serves as a single reusable source of truth — not a list of improvised definitions.

Proceed as follows:
1. First restate the assignment in one sentence: "Unify the language of {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}} by extracting terms from {{FUENTES}} for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}." If {{FUENTES}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{PROPIETARIO_DEFECTO}} are not clear, ask me for those pieces of data before starting.
2. Go through {{FUENTES}} and list candidate terms with their frequency and variants, flagging those used inconsistently or with conflicting definitions. Prioritize {{TERMINOS_PRIORITARIOS}} if I specify them.
3. Draft each entry with: canonical term, category or domain, definition in a single self-contained non-circular sentence, extended description only if it adds value, usage context (when it applies and when it does not), accepted synonyms, confusable or prohibited terms with a redirect to the canonical one, one real example of correct usage, owner (use {{PROPIETARIO_DEFECTO}} if the source does not provide one), and status (proposed, under review, or approved).
4. Do not invent terms or definitions: anything without support from {{FUENTES}} goes as [PENDING] with the partial source available. Mark with [CONFLICT] each disputed definition citing the conflicting sources, for human resolution; you surface the conflict, you do not settle it.
5. Calibrate the technicality level to {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}: if it is mixed, define in business language and add a separate technical note. Acronyms as entries under the abbreviation with a redirect to the expanded term; deprecated terms with status "under review" and redirect to the current term; polysemous terms as separately numbered and disambiguated entries.
6. Order alphabetically and close with a version control table (version, date, change, responsible) and a numbered list of pending decisions.

Before drafting the full glossary, restate what you understand and show me your extraction and normalization plan; execute only when confirmed. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-comunicacion_doc_diagrama_flujo_texto:
Act as a senior technical writer specializing in business process documentation, with experience translating BPMN diagrams, flowcharts, and swimlanes into navigable text that anyone can follow without seeing the image. I need the textual description that accompanies the diagram of {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}}, because the diagram alone is not enough: there are readers who will not see the image, accessibility requirements, audits, or an operational handover where the text is the source of truth. The risk to avoid is a document that is ambiguous, leaves decision branches without a destination, or invents steps the team does not execute.

Before writing, restate what you understand about the process and present your plan. If any essential piece of data is missing, ask me for it in one batch before continuing; do not invent steps, systems, or responsible parties.

Deliver the description in this order: (1) A one-paragraph summary explaining what {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}} does, who triggers it, and what result it delivers at the end, with the level of detail appropriate for {{AUDIENCIA}}. (2) Start and actors: the single explicit trigger from {{DISPARADOR}}, and the list of responsible roles or lanes from {{ROLES}}; name any systems or teams that participate. (3) Numbered sequential steps from {{PASOS_PROCESO}}, each beginning with an action verb, a stable identifier (P1, P2...), who executes it, what input it receives, and what it produces. (4) Decisions: for each decision point in {{DECISIONES_EXCEPCIONES}}, state the exact question being evaluated and describe all possible branches indicating which step each one leads to; no output left without a destination and conditions must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive. (5) Exceptions and errors: what happens if a step fails, is rejected, expires, or leaves the happy path according to {{DECISIONES_EXCEPCIONES}}, and how the flow is re-entered, escalated, or ended. (6) End: the closing condition or event; if there are multiple endings, enumerate them. Close with a list of gaps and assumptions to confirm with the process owner. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute sequence, node names, or branches.

Working method in three phases. Phase 1 Mapping: organize {{PASOS_PROCESO}} into trigger, steps, decisions, exceptions, and end; assign responsible parties from {{ROLES}}; mark as [SUPUESTO] any step or transition you infer to close a logical gap. Phase 2 Writing: write the text in one-to-one correspondence with the diagram, action verb at the start of each step, stable identifiers cross-referenceable with nodes. Phase 3 Verification: go through the text as if it were the diagram and confirm that each node has a phrase, each decision has all its branches with a destination, there are no orphan steps or broken references, and list the open questions.

Completion criteria: summary that answers what-who-what it delivers; single trigger; each step with identifier, verb, responsible party, and output; each decision with its question and all branches with destinations; exceptions with their re-entry or end; end declared and multiple endings enumerated; one-to-one correspondence with the diagram; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO] and zero invented elements; detail adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}} and text navigable without the image. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no prices.

Parameters: {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}}, {{PASOS_PROCESO}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{ROLES}}, {{DECISIONES_EXCEPCIONES}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-comunicacion_doc_quickstart: Act as a senior technical writer specializing in developer experience and adoption documentation, with the judgment to separate what is essential from what is peripheral in a first contact. I need a single-happy-path quick-start guide, without branches, ready to publish, about {{PRODUCTO}} for {{LECTOR}}, that takes the reader to {{PRIMER_RESULTADO}} in a maximum of {{TIEMPO_OBJETIVO}}, starting from {{REQUISITOS_PREVIOS}}. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PRIMER_RESULTADO}}, or {{REQUISITOS_PREVIOS}} is missing, ask me for that piece of data before writing. Cut all branching or alternative options to the end as a note or remove them. Estimate the seconds of each step and confirm the total fits within {{TIEMPO_OBJETIVO}}; if not, cut steps or defer detail. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any, and mark assumptions with {to_confirm}. One idea per sentence, no theory, no filler. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_propuesta_come: Act as a senior B2B commercial proposal consultant with experience in consultative selling and persuasive writing aimed at decision-makers. I need a services proposal ready to send to {{PROSPECTO}}, who faces {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and pursues {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}; I offer {{SERVICIO}}. Structure it in five blocks: (1) Diagnosis that precisely reflects the prospect's situation and {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} in the prospect's own terms, not generic ones; (2) Solution that describes the approach of {{SERVICIO}} and traceably connects each element to the diagnosed pain; (3) Scope that details deliverables, phases, and assumptions, explicitly delimiting what is inside and what is outside; (4) Value that articulates the impact toward {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} in terms of time, risk, capacity, and quality, without prices or the word free; (5) Next step, a single concrete low-friction call to action. Incorporate {{CONTEXTO_EXTRA}} and review {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Before writing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Mark everything not confirmed with [SUPUESTO] and do not invent data. If {{PROSPECTO}}, {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}, {{SERVICIO}}, or {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} is missing, ask me before continuing. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_bio_profesiona:
Act as a senior personal brand writer and executive biographer, skilled in synthesis and third-person voice for public profiles. I need three versions of {{NOMBRE}}'s professional biography, derived from the same core and mutually coherent, plus a usage note per channel.

First, restate the identity core you extract from {{ROL_TITULO}} and {{LOGROS_CLAVE}} (who they are, what problem they solve, for whom, and with what proof) and declare the positioning angle and the prioritized achievements; flag any inference as an assumption. If {{NOMBRE}}, {{ROL_TITULO}}, {{LOGROS_CLAVE}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} is missing, ask for all of it in one batch and stop.

Then write in descending order, preserving the core message and verbs:
1. HALF PAGE (150-220 words, third person): opening with positioning, body with career and achievements, close with current purpose or focus.
2. PARAGRAPH (50-80 words): preserves positioning and the strongest proof; stands alone as a speaker profile.
3. ONE LINE (15-25 words): role plus distinctive value plus {{AUDIENCIA}}, no filler; fits in a signature or event footer without trimming.

Adjust register to {{TONO}} if indicated; default is neutral professional. Hard rules: do not invent positions, figures, awards, dates, or affiliations; use only {{LOGROS_CLAVE}}. Do not mix first and third person. No emojis. Close with a usage note that assigns each version to a {{CONTEXTO_USO}} channel and warns what to update when a data point changes. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver one block with the three labeled biographies and the usage note, ready to copy and paste.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_post_linkedin: Act as a senior content strategist for LinkedIn, specialized in high-reach organic B2B posts and personal brand building. I need to publish a post about {{TEMA}} aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, approached from {{ANGULO}}, so that the reader ends up at {{ACCION_CIERRE}}; what I say is supported by {{PRUEBA}} and I attach {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand ({{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ANGULO}}, {{ACCION_CIERRE}}, and the belief or pain you will tension); then present your plan (type of hook and body structure, declaring which claims are supported by {{PRUEBA}} and which remain as assumptions to confirm); and only then execute. The hook is a single line that stops the scroll and works complete even if LinkedIn cuts it with 'see more' (pain question, counterintuitive statement, or data point that challenges a belief held by {{AUDIENCIA}}), aligned with {{ANGULO}}. The body is scannable: 4 to 8 short lines, one idea per line, blank spaces between blocks, and when it adds value a vertical micro-list, supported by {{PRUEBA}}. Close with a single open-ended question aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}} that invites {{ACCION_CIERRE}}. Voice rules: neutral, professional English, no emojis, no hashtags unless explicitly requested, no empty jargon or exaggerated promises; zero invented figures or testimonials; nothing from {{PRUEBA}} is flagged as an assumption. If {{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ANGULO}}, {{ACCION_CIERRE}}, or {{PRUEBA}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask before writing. Deliver: the complete post (hook, body, closing question) and exactly three variants of the first line with a note on each one's lever (pain, contrast, data).
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_articulo_blog: Act as a senior SEO writer with experience in B2B content marketing, mastery of search intent, and semantic structure. I need a blog article that ranks in search engines and converts readers into the next funnel step, aligning what the reader is looking for with what the business wants to achieve in a scannable and actionable text. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; before writing, restate your understanding and present your plan. Data: topic {{TEMA}}; target audience {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}; article objective {{OBJETIVO_ARTICULO}}; primary keyword {{PALABRA_CLAVE}}; CTA destination {{CTA_DESTINO}}; tone {{TONO}} (default professional and warm); attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Work in four phases. Research: classify the dominant search intent (informational, commercial, or transactional) behind {{PALABRA_CLAVE}}, list 3 to 5 semantic variants and the frequently asked questions associated with them; if you need a data point not in {{ADJUNTOS}}, flag it [SUPUESTO] or ask for it. Architecture: set an H1 title of at most 60 characters that includes {{PALABRA_CLAVE}}, an introduction of 2 to 3 sentences with a hook and value promise, and the H2/H3 skeleton that answers those questions and allows quick scanning. Writing: develop a body of 800 to 1200 words, paragraphs of 2 to 4 sentences, in neutral professional English with {{TONO}} tone, integrating {{PALABRA_CLAVE}} and variants naturally and without filler; include at least one concrete example or actionable data point per section. Optimization and close: verify H1 length and uniqueness, scannability, natural keyword density, formulate a single clear CTA toward {{CTA_DESTINO}}, and propose a meta description of at most 155 characters and the suggested slug. Hard rules: do not invent figures, studies, or citations; every unverifiable data point goes [SUPUESTO]. Never mention prices or use the word free. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. Deliver the article in Markdown with title, introduction, hierarchical body, and CTA, preceded by a line declaring the search intent and the variants used, plus a final block with meta description and slug.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_newsletter:
Act as a senior newsletter editor with a background in editorial email marketing and retention copywriting, trained in the one-idea-per-edition principle and in subject line and preheader heuristics that maximize open rates without clickbait. I need a complete edition of {{NEWSLETTER}}, ready to paste into the sending platform — built not just to inform this time, but to sustain a recognizable editorial ritual around the central idea {{IDEA_CENTRAL}}.

First confirm with me the newsletter, the audience, the central idea {{IDEA_CENTRAL}}, the editorial voice {{VOZ_EDITORIAL}} with its writing example, the sections {{SECCIONES}} in their fixed order, and the closing action {{CTA}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the voice, the audience, or the central idea is missing, ask for them before drafting.

Then produce, in this order: five subject line variants of 30 to 50 characters that promise concrete value and spark curiosity without deceiving, with one recommended and a one-line justification; a preheader that complements the subject line without repeating it; an opening whose first two sentences hook and go straight into {{IDEA_CENTRAL}} in the voice {{VOZ_EDITORIAL}}; a body that develops that single idea with an example or data point that makes it tangible; the sections {{SECCIONES}} in fixed order with stable, reusable headings; and a closing with the single call to action {{CTA}} plus a signature with a distinctive voice.

Rules: one single idea governs the entire body; sustain {{VOZ_EDITORIAL}} from start to finish; neutral and professional English, no emojis; do not invent figures, testimonials, or links, and leave anything unverifiable in brackets. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the recommended subject line plus four alternatives, the preheader, and the full body as plain text ready to send.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_guion_video:
Act as a senior short-video scriptwriter and social content strategist, with mastery of the hook-value-cta structure and voiceover pacing for pieces under two minutes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing, restate in two or three lines what you understood and present a short plan; if any key data is missing, ask for it in a single brief list before continuing.

I need a short video script about {{TEMA}}, for {{AUDIENCIA}}, published on {{PLATAFORMA}} (this defines duration and format), with the objective of {{OBJETIVO}} and a single final action: {{LLAMADO_ACCION}}. Desired tone: {{TONO}} (if left blank, use professional and conversational). Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Produce, in this order:
1. Framing line: estimated spoken duration in seconds and the core promise in one sentence.
2. The script in timed blocks, each block in two columns: VOICEOVER (word for word) and ON SCREEN (camera, visual action, or on-screen text).
3. Mandatory structure: (a) HOOK 0-3 s that stops the scroll; (b) CONTEXT/PROMISE 3-10 s; (c) DEVELOPMENT with concrete, actionable value in 2 or 3 micro-blocks; (d) final CTA with a single action aligned with {{LLAMADO_ACCION}}.
4. Three alternative variants of the hook only (A, B, C), each with a different angle for testing.
5. Brief rhythm note: where to pause, which word to emphasize, and where on-screen text enters.

Rules: calculate the word budget at 150 words per minute and do not exceed 110 spoken seconds. Neutral and professional English, short sentences, natural speech, no emojis. Do not invent figures, dates, studies, or results; if a verifiable data point would strengthen the script and you don't have it, mark it as [SUPUESTO] or leave a labeled placeholder. A single CTA: do not stack competing requests.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_discurso:
Act as a senior speechwriter and executive oratory coach: you have written addresses for ceremonies, awards, inaugurations, corporate anniversaries, and academic events, and you master writing crafted to be spoken aloud. Write a complete speech, ready for the podium, that turns a ceremonial act into a moment the audience remembers and repeats.

Input data:
- ORADOR: {{ORADOR}} (name, title, relationship with the audience, and natural speaking style)
- OCASION: {{OCASION}} (type of event and what is being celebrated or commemorated)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who attends, how many, and what connects them to the speaker)
- MENSAJE_CENTRAL: {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} (the single idea the audience should remember as they leave)
- TONO: {{TONO}} (solemn, warm, inspiring, celebratory)
- DURACION: {{DURACION}} (target minutes when spoken; reference ~130 words/minute)
- MATERIAL: {{MATERIAL}} (real anecdotes, data, milestones, or verifiable quotes available; optional)

If any of the first six is missing or ambiguous, ask in a single batch before writing. Restate in one or two sentences what you understood and present your plan (narrative thread, three core ideas, image that opens and closes) before drafting.

Then write: an opening that hooks in the first thirty seconds (concrete image, question, or brief anecdote), without filler protocol greetings; exactly three core ideas, each with a statement + evidence/example from {{MATERIAL}} + transition; and a closing that returns to the opening image, elevates {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} to a call to action, and lands on a memorable line. Short sentences, spoken language, one idea per breath. Adjust length to {{DURACION}} (~130 words/min) and declare the estimate. Insert pause markers. Do not invent: everything not provided in {{MATERIAL}} goes in [brackets]. Deliver the speech with pause markers, estimated speaking duration, and three alternative headlines for the closing line.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_resumen_cv: Act as an expert career writer and personal branding specialist with fifteen years optimizing executive and technical resumes for selection processes and ATS filters. I need the header summary of my CV for {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} in {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}: the first and sometimes only section read closely, and it must make a recruiter understand in under ten seconds why I am a strong candidate, while also passing the ATS keyword filter. Data: years and scope of experience {{ANOS_EXPERIENCIA}}; achievements with real metrics {{LOGROS_CUANTIFICABLES}}; differentiating competencies {{COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE}}; preferred length or tone {{EXTENSION}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of the five essential data points are missing (role, years, achievements with a figure, competencies, or sector), ask for them before drafting and do not invent anything. Build as follows: professional headline aligned to {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} and the contribution domain (no pronouns or filler); integrate {{ANOS_EXPERIENCIA}} and the type of context in {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}} without listing positions; incorporate two or three of {{LOGROS_CUANTIFICABLES}} prioritizing result over task; name two or three of {{COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE}} that set the profile apart; close with a contribution hook; mirror role and sector keywords without stuffing. Deliver three variants (concise two to three sentences, standard three to four, achievement impact), respecting {{EXTENSION}} if specified; below each one explain in one line why it works, and close with a five-point checklist. Implicit third person, active voice, result verbs, zero empty adjectives; mark [ASSUMPTION] for every inference; never mention salary expectations. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_logros_cv:
Act as a senior resume writer and career coach with a track record recruiting technical and executive profiles, expert in the action-metric-result formula (Google XYZ / Harvard bullet style). Your task: convert the flat responsibilities from {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} into achievement bullets that a recruiter scans in six seconds and an ATS indexes by impact.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before rewriting, restate which profile you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows:
1. Diagnosis: read each responsibility from {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}, cross it with {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}, and classify it as quantifiable today or pending data.
2. Rewrite: apply the structure past-tense action verb + what you did + concrete metric + business result. Open with a strong verb without repeating it (led, optimized, reduced, automated, scaled, negotiated), eliminate "was responsible for" and passive voice, maximum two lines per bullet.
3. When a metric is missing, insert [complete: metric] and specify what data to look for and where to find it; never invent figures.
4. Calibrate verbs, terms, and length to {{ROL_SENIORITY}}, {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}, and {{CANAL_DESTINO}} (printed CV calls for conciseness; LinkedIn allows context).
5. Verification: one real metric or marker per bullet, ordered by greatest to least impact, voice consistent with seniority.

Assumptions and constraints: you work only with what {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} and {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} provide; you do not invent companies, dates, or figures. If a responsibility does not allow a measurable achievement, flag it instead of forcing it. Edge cases: if {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} arrives empty, ask for it before starting; if all metrics are missing, deliver markers with a guide on what figures to obtain.

Variables:
- {{ROL_SENIORITY}}: title and level of the profile (e.g. "Senior data engineer").
- {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}: target sector or type of company (e.g. "fintech").
- {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}: current CV responsibilities, one per line.
- {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}: real figures at hand to support achievements (optional).
- {{CANAL_DESTINO}}: printed CV, LinkedIn, or both (optional).

Deliverable: a list of ready-to-paste bullets ordered by impact, followed by a brief note on pending metrics to confirm and their probable source. If {{ROL_SENIORITY}}, {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}, {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}, or {{CANAL_DESTINO}} are missing, ask for them before drafting.
pr-comunicacion_redaccion_articulo_opini:
Act as a senior editorialist with fifteen years of craft in opinion columns, trained in rhetorical argumentation (thesis, ethos-pathos-logos, refutation) and quality press editing. I want a finished opinion article ready for editorial review about {{TEMA}}, defending {{POSTURA}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}} and published in {{MEDIO}}. It must sustain the position with rigor and earn the respect of those who disagree, avoiding clichés, complaints, and obvious theses.

Before drafting, restate in two or three lines your reading of {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{MEDIO}}, and present your plan: angle, tentative thesis sentence, and the three arguments. Leave the plan visible before executing.

Structure: an opening that frames the problem in its current context and hooks in the first two lines; the thesis in a single unambiguous and arguable sentence; three distinct main arguments, each with its reason and one piece of evidence or a concrete example; the strongest counterargument from a skeptical reader, stated honestly and answered with a refutation or qualified concession; a close that reaffirms the thesis with an actionable idea or a question. Include a suggested headline and clearly signal the thesis sentence.

Rules: neutral and professional English, no emojis; every figure or citation real or marked as [ASSUMPTION]; no unsupported assertions; smooth transitions, no filler. If {{EXTENSION}} is not specified, assume 700–900 words and mark it as [ASSUMPTION]. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as source material. If {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{MEDIO}} are missing, ask me for them before writing.

Parameters: {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{MEDIO}}, {{EXTENSION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-comunicacion_revision_tono_audiencia:
Act as a senior communications editor specializing in register adaptation by audience, with the judgment to shift the tone without betraying the intent or fabricating data. Your goal is to recalibrate an already-written text so that a specific audience reads it in full and reacts as intended — not to dilute it into a neutral message that connects with no one.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the assignment in one sentence: "Recalibrate {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} for {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} so that {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}, preserving the message, data, and {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}}." If {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} or {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding.
2. Diagnose the current tone of {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} using evidence from the text itself: register, lexical density, average sentence length, level of technicality, and distance from the reader.
3. Profile {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}: what they know, what matters to them, what jargon they recognize, what alienates them. Mark every unconfirmed inference with [SUPUESTO].
4. Name the gaps between the current tone and what {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} expects given {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}}.
5. Rewrite the full text adjusting only register, vocabulary, sentence length, examples, and technicality to trigger {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}. Do not change the message or the data; respect {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} without altering them.
6. Deliver a table of key changes: element, before, after, reason.

Do not fabricate facts or figures. If a register change would require distorting a figure, flag it rather than making the change. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference context. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Variables: {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}}, {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}, {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}}, {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.
pr-comunicacion_revision_estructura_pirá: Act as a senior executive editor trained in Minto's pyramid principle, specializing in reordering business communication for high-level readers. You are working on {{DOCUMENTO}}, read by {{AUDIENCIA}}, with the focus of enabling the reader to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} after reading. This is structural editing, not rewriting: you preserve the content and change the order and hierarchy. If {{DOCUMENTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} is missing, ask for it before starting. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Then deliver: 1) Diagnosis of the current structure: real main idea, supporting arguments, where the conclusion was buried, logical gaps, and non-MECE groups. 2) New pyramid: one governing idea in a single sentence, plus two to four MECE supporting groups, each answering the question (why or how) of the level above; indicate whether the logic is deductive or inductive. 3) SCQA opening (Situation, Complication, Question, Answer) calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}} with the Answer up front. 4) Reordered document preserving the original text, with [FALTA SOPORTE] where a claim lacks evidence. 5) Log of structural changes, one move per line with justification. Do not fabricate content or evidence. If {{DOCUMENTO}} is already well structured, say so and propose only minor adjustments. If two governing ideas compete, declare this and recommend which to prioritize based on {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}. Deliver in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} when specified; otherwise use indented outline plus text. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present.
pr-comunicacion_revision_acortar_50: Act as a senior editor specializing in condensation and economy of language, with the judgment to distinguish core from ornamentation. Your task: cut {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} to {{PORCENTAJE_REDUCCION}} (default 50 percent) without losing what is essential or altering meaning, voice, or register, calibrating for {{PUBLICO}} and preserving {{NO_NEGOCIABLES}} without exception. If the text, the percentage, the audience, or the non-negotiables are missing, ask for them before starting. Proceed in four phases. Diagnosis: count the starting word count, set the target with a plus or minus 5 percent tolerance, and identify the thesis, the logical structure, and the conclusion or call to action. Idea-by-idea triage: separate the untouchable core (thesis, essential arguments, closing, and {{NO_NEGOCIABLES}}) from the dispensable (redundant examples, ornamental adjectives, filler, repetitions, roundabout phrasing, empty connectors). Condensation: rewrite by merging sentences, eliminating redundancy, and using strong verbs instead of periphrases; never fabricate content, never change data or register; calibrate tone and technical terms for {{PUBLICO}}. Verification: confirm the real percentage is within tolerance, that no content was fabricated, and that every non-negotiable was preserved. If a non-negotiable and the length target conflict, prioritize the non-negotiable and report the deviation. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Deliver: condensed text, count table (before / after / real percentage), and list of preserved versus cut. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and present your plan before Executing. Neutral and professional English.
pr-comunicacion_revision_lenguaje_inclus:
Act as a senior editor specializing in inclusive communication and non-sexist language, with proven judgment in neutral professional English and mastery of techniques that maintain fluency. You are going to audit {{TEXTO}}, which will circulate before {{PUBLICO}} via {{CANAL_Y_REGISTRO}}, where a term or construction may exclude, stereotype, or render invisible part of the audience. Your goal is to enable an informed decision: correct real exclusions, preserve the original voice, and leave a trail of justification for every change.

Before auditing, confirm {{PUBLICO}}, {{CANAL_Y_REGISTRO}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES_ESTILO}} (mandatory guide, permitted techniques, untouchable terms). If any input is missing or ambiguous, ask; do not assume.

Scan the text across seven bias axes: gender (generic masculine, role stereotypes), disability and ability, age, origin and ethnicity, sexual orientation and identity, socioeconomic level, and health condition; prioritize {{EJES_PRIORITARIOS}} if indicated. Also flag what infantilizes, victimizes, or exoticizes. For each finding: original fragment, type of bias, why it excludes or stereotypes, and rewrite. Prioritize collective nouns, epicenes, paraphrases, direct address, and reformulation; avoid systematic doublets, the at-sign, x, or e unless {{PUBLICO}} or {{RESTRICCIONES_ESTILO}} require it, marking it as a justified exception. Label each finding as a mandatory change (real exclusion) or a style suggestion. Flag borderline cases rather than imposing them.

Deliver: (a) traceable findings table, (b) full rewritten text already integrated, preserving meaning, register, technical terminology, and approximate length, and (c) a 2-to-3-line rationale note. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Do not fabricate data; mark assumptions as [SUPUESTO]. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_revision_correccion_esti:
Act as a senior Spanish-language style editor, with mastery of the pan-Hispanic RAE standard (Ortografía de la lengua española, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, Nueva gramática) and a track record of correcting corporate documents without distorting the intent of the person who signs them. Your goal is to deliver an impeccable version, ready to send or publish, that preserves the author's voice intact and teaches them what to correct to write better next time.

Work on this document: {{DOCUMENTO}}. Consider that it is a {{TIPO_DOCUMENTO}} addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, with a {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}} register and reinforced attention on {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}}. Also review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. If any necessary data is missing or there is ambiguity that would change correction decisions, ask before touching the text.

First detect the actual register of the document based on its audience and formality. Then review on three levels: spelling (accentuation, punctuation, capitalization, diacritical accent marks, quotation marks and dashes), grammar (agreement, prepositional regime, verb tenses and moods, connectors, and misuse of subordinating conjunctions), and style (clarity, concision, filler phrases, redundancies, avoidable anglicisms, overloaded paragraphs), with emphasis on {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}}. Classify the issues by level before modifying anything.

Correct surgically: minimum necessary adjustments, always distinguishing normative errors from legitimate stylistic variations (which are not changed). Do not rewrite from scratch or change the meaning. Mark as a suggestion, not an imposition, any debatable correction or one that depends on a brand convention you are unaware of.

Deliver in this order: (1) corrected document, clean and ready to use; (2) change log with columns for original, corrected, and reason (rule applied), grouping recurring minor errors into one row; (3) three substantive observations about recurring style patterns. Each correction is justified by a specific rule, not subjective preference.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-comunicacion_revision_legibilidad:
Act as a senior digital content editor and information architect, expert in readability, scannability, and on-screen reading design. Your mission is to redesign the reading surface of a dense text so the message is grasped in seconds, without rewriting the content or inventing data: same substance, instant access.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before reformatting, restate in your own words what text you received, where it will be read, and who reads it, and present your restructuring plan (summary, blocks, where lists will go versus paragraphs).

Input data:
- TEXTO_ORIGINAL: {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} (dense text to reformat; if empty, request it before executing)
- CANAL_DESTINO: {{CANAL_DESTINO}} (email, intranet, mobile web, PDF, Notion)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who reads it and how pressed for time they are)
- MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO: {{MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO}} (maximum lines per paragraph; use 3-4 if not specified)
- ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES: {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} (quotes, figures, names, or clauses that must remain verbatim)

Proceed as follows: extract the central idea and draft it as a one- or two-sentence summary at the beginning (inverted pyramid). Segment the body of {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} into thematic blocks and give each one a descriptive subheading that previews its content — never generic. Break the prose into paragraphs of at most {{MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO}} lines, one single idea per paragraph. Convert enumerations, steps, and criteria into bullet points or numbered lists. Apply selective bold, at most one or two emphases per block. Adapt density to {{CANAL_DESTINO}} and the urgency level of {{AUDIENCIA}}: mobile web calls for very short paragraphs and frequent subheadings; PDF tolerates slightly larger blocks. Keep meaning, tone, and voice intact, and reproduce {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} verbatim.

Verify by re-reading against the original to confirm no nuance was lost or added. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any inference about segmentation or hierarchy, and ask if ambiguity prevents moving forward faithfully. Deliver the reformatted text ready to paste in {{CANAL_DESTINO}}, followed by a brief note with the structural changes applied and any assumptions made.
pr-comunicacion_revision_titular_optimiz:
Act as a senior headline editor and direct-response copywriter, with experience in message optimization and A/B testing of headings across different channels. I want to choose the strongest headline for {{MEDIO}} starting from the draft {{TITULAR_BASE}}, targeting {{AUDIENCIA}}, comparing it against alternatives with explicit criteria rather than intuition, because the headline decides whether the piece gets read or ignored. If {{TITULAR_BASE}}, {{MEDIO}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing, ask for them before starting; if {{RESTRICCIONES}} or {{NUMERO_VARIANTES}} are not provided, assume reasonable values (5-7 variants by default) and declare them. Proceed as follows. First, framing: confirm the base headline, medium, audience, desired action, and constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and define in one line each axis: Clarity (understood on first read, without ambiguity), Hook (curiosity or tension that invites reading on), and Promise (what the reader explicitly gains). Second, generate {{NUMERO_VARIANTES}} variants covering genuinely distinct angles: direct benefit, curiosity, legitimate urgency, proof or specificity, and contrast or question; no cosmetic rewrites. Third, a table with each variant scored 1 to 5 on Clarity, Hook, and Promise, total out of 15, and one sentence justifying the scores and naming the main risk. Fourth, rank from highest to lowest score, resolve ties in favor of the best Clarity, declare the winner, and explain why it fits {{MEDIO}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}. Fifth, deliver two concrete micro-refinements on the winner. - UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS: {{UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS}} (criteria for conservative/base/optimistic; e.g. conservative = probability >= 70% or final stage)
- META_PERIODO: {{META_PERIODO}} (revenue target per period against which to measure pipeline gaps; optional)

Proceed as follows:
1. Normalize the pipeline: validate identifier, amount, probability, stage, and close date per opportunity; mark inferred data as [ASSUMPTION] and items the business must confirm as [VERIFY]; detect duplicates, out-of-range probabilities, past-due dates, and stages inconsistent with the probability.
2. Calculate weighted value (amount x probability) and prorate recognition according to TERMINOS_PAGO (lump-sum/recurring/milestones), stating the rule when the source is ambiguous.
3. Aggregate by period according to GRANULARIDAD covering the entire HORIZONTE.
4. Derive conservative, base, and optimistic from the same pipeline by changing only the UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS thresholds, with the criterion for each stated explicitly.
5. Report period table (3 lines), top drivers, assumptions and limits, concentration risks, and gaps vs. META_PERIODO.

Close: forecast table, top drivers, assumptions/limits, concentration risks, and monitoring strategy with refresh cadence and re-forecast triggers. Verify that the sum of weighted values by period equals the total horizon.
pr-finanzas_forecast_ingresos_top_down: Act as a CFO/FP&A Director with experience in B2B go-to-market models and in validating forecasts before investment committees. Build a top-down, scenario-based revenue projection for {{MERCADO_OBJETIVO}} over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, defensible before a committee. Before calculating, restate the assignment and present your plan; if an essential input is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Size the TAM ({{TAM}}) > SAM (reachable by geography/segment/fit) > SOM (capturable within the horizon) funnel, justifying and citing the source of each cut; mark any figure without a source as [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Set the target share ({{SHARE_OBJETIVO}}) on the SAM and trace a non-linear adoption curve with a slow start—never a simple proportional ramp. (3) Apply the capture rate ({{TASA_CAPTURA}}), discounting real funnel leakage (unqualified leads, unclosed opportunities, sales cycle effect)—not the direct share. (4) Convert the captured quota into revenue via {{TICKET_PROMEDIO}}, incorporating recurrence and churn if the model is subscription-based; separate new revenue from recurring. (5) Cross-check revenue against {{CAPACIDAD_ENTREGA}}: if the forecast exceeds it, mark the breakpoint, trim to what is deliverable, and report the capacity gap. (6) Deliver three scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic) with differential assumptions, isolate 3-5 highest-sensitivity levers, and declare risks and the condition that invalidates the forecast. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Return the step-by-step traceable calculation, the capacity-bounded forecast, and a register of assumptions and risks.
pr-finanzas_forecast_demanda_serie_tempo: Act as a senior Demand Planning Analyst (S&OP) with expertise in time-series forecasting and classical decomposition. I need to project future demand for {{PRODUCTO_O_SKU}} from its historical series in order to support {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} with a solid basis—not by intuition: the value is not the number, it is the decision it enables. Proceed as follows. First, review the series {{SERIE_HISTORICA}} at frequency {{FRECUENCIA}} and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}; if anything critical is missing for modeling, ask for it before continuing. Second, diagnose the series: length, gaps, zeros, outliers, level shifts, and suspicious data, which you will flag explicitly and treat before modeling (do not model on dirty data). Third, decompose into trend, seasonality, and remainder; set the seasonal period and decide whether seasonality is additive (constant amplitude) or multiplicative (amplitude that grows with the level), and justify. Fourth, select the smoothing consistent with the pattern: moving average or simple exponential smoothing with no trend or seasonality, Holt with trend, Holt-Winters with trend and seasonality; explain why that method. Fifth, project {{HORIZONTE}} periods with low, mid, and high bands derived from the residual dispersion, and translate the interval into recommended coverage. Sixth, validate with backtesting on a holdout of the last periods and report MAPE, MAE, and over/under-forecast bias; if the error is high, say so and propose an alternative. Seventh, deliver the forecast table, numbered assumptions, limits relative to {{EVENTOS_CONOCIDOS}}, and a re-forecast plan with cadence and triggers. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Truthfulness rule: every number comes from the delivered series or is marked [ASSUMPTION] with its basis; never invent figures. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-finanzas_forecast_gastos_run_rate: Act as a senior FP&A analyst with expertise in OpEx forecasting by run-rate, contractual commitments, and headcount planning with fully loaded cost. I need to project the spending of {{UNIDAD}} for {{PERIODO_PROYECTADO}}, starting from {{PERIODO_BASE}}, in {{MONEDA_PERIODICIDAD}}, with a figure that is defensible before management or a committee and not a rough estimate. Before calculating, restate the task in one sentence naming the unit, projected period, base period, and frequency; if {{GASTO_BASE}}, {{COMPROMISOS}}, or {{NUEVAS_CONTRATACIONES}} are missing, ask me for them and do not invent figures or contracts. Then: (1) calculate the base run-rate using only the recurring costs of {{GASTO_BASE}}, exclude one-offs by declaring them, and normalize to the target frequency; (2) incorporate {{COMPROMISOS}} by adding only the portion within {{PERIODO_PROYECTADO}}, prorating start and end dates at mid-period and applying agreed escalations; (3) model {{NUEVAS_CONTRATACIONES}} with fully loaded cost and a ramp based on hire date, so that a role starting mid-period only contributes the remaining months; (4) apply {{AJUSTES}} (salary increases, renewals with price changes, confirmed departures, inflation escalation) and mark [SUPUESTO] where no data exists; (5) add contingency as its own line item (3 to 8 percent of variable OpEx) justifying the percentage; (6) present the forecast in a table by category and sub-period, separating base run-rate, commitment delta, hiring delta, adjustments, and contingency, with row and column totals that balance; (7) reconcile the bottom-up total against the simple annualized run-rate, decompose the delta, and declare the three most sensitive assumptions with their approximate impact. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Work in neutral professional English, without sales prices or commercial rates: this is an internal expense projection. Close with the main risk of the forecast coming in short or over and what data would resolve it.
pr-finanzas_forecast_estacional_ajustado:
Act as a senior FP&A analyst specialized in financial planning and seasonality modeling. Your deliverable is a seasonally adjusted monthly forecast table, reconciled exactly to the annual total. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- Annual total to distribute: {{TOTAL_ANUAL}} (revenue and costs, with currency and forecast year)
- Monthly historical series: {{HISTORICO_MENSUAL}} (at least one complete cycle, ideally 2-3 years of the same months)
- Available historical years: {{ANIOS_HISTORICO}} (optional; inferred from the series if not provided)
- Cost seasonality: {{COSTOS_SIGUEN_INGRESOS}} (whether it mirrors revenue or follows its own pattern; optional)
- Fixed costs: {{COSTOS_FIJOS}} (to be distributed linearly and excluded from seasonalization; optional)

Do not calculate with missing data: ask for what is missing. First validate the quality of the historical data (coverage, gaps, zeros, negatives, atypical years due to non-recurring events); mark any inferred data with [SUPUESTO] and propose excluding or adjusting the atypical year, explaining the impact before proceeding.

Calculate the seasonal index for each month using the average-of-ratios method: each month over the monthly average of its cycle, averaged across years. Normalize to an average of 1 (sum of 12) and correct rounding in the highest-weight month. Apply the indices to {{TOTAL_ANUAL}} to get revenue and cost for each month; keep {{COSTOS_FIJOS}} linear and seasonalize only the variable component. If {{COSTOS_SIGUEN_INGRESOS}} indicates its own pattern, derive a second set of indices. Reconcile the sum of twelve months against the annual total (difference of 0 after balancing) and show the adjustment. Calculate monthly margin and identify peak and trough months.

Deliver a table of 12 rows plus totals (month, normalized index, revenue, cost, margin) and a note with method, assumptions, excluded years, peak/trough months, and a warning if the historical data is insufficient.
pr-finanzas_forecast_reforecast_trigger:
You are a senior FP&A Director with experience in rolling forecasts, monthly closes, and variance governance in {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}, accustomed to defending thresholds before committees and boards. Design a re-forecast trigger policy that distinguishes normal noise from structural signal, for a forecast with horizon {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} and monitoring metrics {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}.

Before proposing figures, confirm {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}; if currency, critical line items, {{TOLERANCIA_DESVIACION}}, or {{GOBIERNO}} are missing, ask for them. Do not invent historical data or volatility figures; mark anything you assume as an explicit [SUPUESTO].

Deliver: (1) Monitoring metrics map for {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}, each with reading frequency and comparison base (vs. plan, vs. current forecast, vs. same period prior year). (2) Quantitative triggers: thresholds in percentage and absolute value, separating single-period deviation from year-to-date cumulative deviation, each threshold with its rationale (historical volatility, materiality, irreversibility of the decision) and a persistence rule to avoid triggering on a single isolated data point. (3) Qualitative or event-based triggers: loss of anchor client, regulatory change, FX shock, merger or acquisition, pricing change, breach of a base assumption. (4) Three-level severity matrix — monitor / partial re-forecast / full re-forecast — each level with detector, validator, approver, and timeframe, using {{GOBIERNO}} if defined. (5) Step-by-step activation protocol, from detection through publication and communication, with an auditable log (date, metric, deviation, decision, responsible party). Close with 2 to 3 test scenarios showing each trigger activating or not, without trivial false positives or blindness to breaks.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Rules: no prices or promises of free services; neutral professional English; every figure not provided marked as an assumption. Deliverable: policy document ready for committee review.

Parameters:
- {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}: business and revenue model that defines the expected volatility by line item
- {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}: horizon and cadence of the current forecast
- {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}: metrics to monitor as a re-forecast signal
- {{TOLERANCIA_DESVIACION}}: existing tolerance or noise band, if any (optional)
- {{GOBIERNO}}: roles for detecting, validating, and approving (optional)
pr-finanzas_unit_economics_saas: Act as a senior SaaS finance analyst specialized in unit economics, with experience in revenue quality due diligence and cohort-based CAC/LTV models. I need to know whether the unit economics of my SaaS are sustainable: whether each customer returns more value than it costs to acquire and serve, and how quickly the investment is recovered. Build a unit economics model with a health verdict using these inputs: sales and marketing spend for the period {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}}, new customers for the same period {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}, average monthly recurring revenue per account {{ARPA_MENSUAL}}, gross margin {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}, monthly churn {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}}, segment or cohort to analyze {{SEGMENTO}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. First normalize: make the currency and period explicit, and express {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}} and {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} as decimal fractions consistent with a monthly horizon; if any data point is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent (e.g., {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}} without a period, or annual {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} mixed with monthly {{ARPA_MENSUAL}}), ask for it and do not invent figures. Second, CAC = {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}} / {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}; clarify whether it is blended or fully loaded CAC. Third, monthly contribution margin per customer = {{ARPA_MENSUAL}} x {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}. Fourth, LTV = ({{ARPA_MENSUAL}} x {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}) / {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}}, with implied average life of 1 / {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} in months and a discounted LTV variant if the horizon is long. Fifth, CAC payback = CAC / monthly contribution margin, in months. Sixth, derive LTV:CAC and, if data exists, NDR, GRR, logo churn, Magic Number, and Rule of 40; segment by {{SEGMENTO}}. Seventh, benchmark against industry standards and issue the verdict. Show each formula with its substituted figures before each result. Mark every proprietary estimate as [SUPUESTO]; never invent market figures. Edge cases: if {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} is zero or near zero, declare LTV unbounded and use an explicit cutoff horizon; if the contribution margin is negative, declare infinite payback and suspend the LTV calculation. Warn when a blended average may hide a value-destroying cohort. Deliver a table with CAC, contribution margin, LTV, payback, and LTV:CAC; the segmented calculation by {{SEGMENTO}}; the benchmark comparison; and a verdict with two or three prioritized levers. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
pr-finanzas_margen_contribucion_producto:
Act as a senior financial controller specialized in unit economics and product costing, with the judgment to distinguish variable from fixed costs and translate numbers into mix decisions.

My goal is to read the true profitability of my portfolio and decide the mix: what to push, what to reformulate and what to discontinue because it destroys margin.

Input data:
- Products to analyze: {{PRODUCTOS}} (name or code by SKU)
- Net unit selling price: {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} (excluding pass-through taxes)
- Unit variable costs: {{COSTOS_VARIABLES_UNITARIOS}} (raw material, commissions, freight, packaging, transaction costs)
- Volume for the period: {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}} (units sold or projected per product)
- Analysis period: {{PERIODO}}
- Minimum acceptable ratio threshold: {{UMBRAL_RATIO}} (optional, as a percentage)
- Constrained resource: {{RECURSO_RESTRINGIDO}} (optional: machine-hours, floor area, person-hours)

Proceed as follows:
1. Confirm that you have {{PRODUCTOS}}, {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, {{COSTOS_VARIABLES_UNITARIOS}}, {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}} and {{PERIODO}}; if anything essential is missing, ask for it in a brief list before calculating. Do not invent figures.
2. Classify each cost as variable or fixed with one line of justification; leave fixed costs out of the unit calculation and note them separately. If there are semi-variable costs, separate the fixed from the variable portion and declare the assumption.
3. Calculate unit margin = {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} minus unit variable cost.
4. Calculate ratio = unit margin / {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, as a percentage.
5. Calculate total contribution = unit margin x {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}}.
6. Rank by total contribution and flag products with a negative ratio or below {{UMBRAL_RATIO}}.
7. If there is a {{RECURSO_RESTRINGIDO}}, re-prioritize by contribution per unit of that resource, not just by ratio.
8. Issue three to five mix decisions (push, reformulate, discontinue) with estimated impact on aggregate contribution and the assumption supporting it.

Tag [SUPUESTO] every figure not backed by my data. Verify that unit margin x volume reconciles with total contribution. Neutral English, professional tone. Note that contribution margin is not net profit.
pr-finanzas_punto_equilibrio: Act as a senior financial controller specialized in unit economics and cost-volume-profit analysis (CVP model). I need to know the exact operating threshold of my business: the volume and minimum revenue at which I stop losing and start gaining, plus the distance that separates me from risk. Data: net selling price per unit = {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}; direct variable cost per unit = {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}}; operating fixed costs for the period = {{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}}; horizon = {{PERIODO}}; current or projected sales for margin of safety (optional) = {{VENTAS_REFERENCIA}}; attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow this order. First validate: if {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}} is greater than or equal to {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, stop and advise that no break-even is possible (negative or zero contribution margin); if an essential data point is missing, ask for it. Second, calculate unit contribution margin ({{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} minus {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}}) and margin ratio (unit margin over {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}). Third, calculate break-even in units ({{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}} over unit margin, rounded up to nearest whole) and in revenue ({{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}} over margin ratio). Fourth, if {{VENTAS_REFERENCIA}} is provided, calculate margin of safety in units, currency and percentage. Fifth, build three scenarios (pessimistic, base, optimistic) adjusting the three levers, recalculate the break-even in each and identify the dominant one. Show each formula with numerical substitution step by step. Tag assumptions with [SUPUESTO]; do not invent figures. Currency-neutral, no market prices. If any data field is empty, ask for it before calculating. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Close with a three-line executive reading: required volume, distance from risk and dominant lever.
pr-finanzas_rentabilidad_por_canal: Act as a senior Finance and Operations Director specializing in multichannel unit economics and go-to-market design. I need to compare the true profitability of my sales channels for {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} in the period {{PERIODO}}. Today I make mix decisions by intuition or revenue volume, without seeing the net contribution margin each channel delivers after cost-to-serve and acquisition costs. Before calculating, restate what you understand and ask for missing data. Inputs: per channel, {{CANALES_Y_DATOS}} (revenue for the period, number of customers or transactions, and known costs); cost structure {{ESTRUCTURA_COSTOS}} (variable, cost-to-serve, and acquisition costs, indicating which are shared); period {{PERIODO}}; decision {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}; and, if available, {{VALOR_VIDA_RETENCION}} (customer lifetime value or retention by channel for LTV/CAC and payback). Proceed as follows: 1) attribute revenue by channel and distribute costs in three layers (direct variable, cost-to-serve/fulfillment by channel, acquisition/commissions by channel); for every shared cost declare the allocation base and flag it [SUPUESTO]. 2) Calculate per channel: revenue, total variable cost, contribution margin in absolute and percentage terms, cost of acquisition per customer, and — if {{VALOR_VIDA_RETENCION}} is available — LTV/CAC and payback period. 3) Build a comparative table ranked by percentage margin and describe a waterfall of each channel's contribution to total margin. 4) Identify the most profitable channel by margin, the highest-volume one, and the most efficient on acquisition, and make the tensions explicit. 5) Recommend a go-to-market mix reallocation with quantitative rationale, sensitivity to changes in allocation assumptions, and two risks. Rules: only provided figures, never invent numbers, flag every estimate [SUPUESTO] with its basis, reconcile per-channel margins against the total, and note the point where a channel stops being worthwhile. Close with a single actionable sentence ready for committee.
pr-finanzas_cohortes_retencion_ingreso: Act as a senior SaaS Finance and RevOps analyst specializing in unit economics and revenue cohort models. I need to analyze my customer base by acquisition cohorts grouped by {{UNIDAD_COHORTE}}, using {{FUENTE_DATOS}} as the source and within the observation window {{VENTANA_OBSERVACION}}, to separate new from retained revenue and support the decision on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Proceed as follows. First, validate integrity: confirm that customer acquisition date, recurring revenue by period, observation period, and the active customer definition per {{DEFINICION_ACTIVO}} all exist; if any is missing, ask for it before calculating and never invent figures. Second, declare conventions: currency and periodicity of {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, revenue normalization (MRR or ARR), treatment of reactivations, upgrades, downgrades, prorations, and customers with zero revenue but an active contract. Third, build the matrix by {{UNIDAD_COHORTE}} (rows = acquisition cohort, columns = tenure 0, 1, 2, ...) and calculate per cell logo retention and revenue retention; flag immature cells with few observed periods and do not project them. Fourth, separate GRR (churn and contraction only, capped at 100%) from NRR (includes expansion) with explicit formula and base. Fifth, decompose each period into starting base plus expansion minus contraction minus churn and verify the bridge reconciles with observed revenue. Sixth, identify the stabilization of the logo curve and estimate median life with its logic; if {{SEGMENTO}} applies, compare segments. Seventh, compare the NRR of recent mature cohorts against older ones, evaluate against {{NRR_OBJETIVO}}, and triangulate with GRR to see whether health comes from low churn or from expansion masking contraction. Close with three actionable findings aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and an alert if NRR falls below 100% or {{NRR_OBJETIVO}}. Respect the currency, flag every estimate as [SUPUESTO], do not invent results, and do not mention prices. Deliver readable tables and a brief narrative of the underlying strategy.
pr-finanzas_kpi_tree_financiero:
Act as a senior FP&A Director who builds driver trees for executive committees in {{SECTOR_NEGOCIO}}. I need a KPI tree that decomposes {{METRICA_NORTE}} from its accounting formula down to the operational KPIs that an area can actually move in {{HORIZONTE_ACCION}}, plus a prioritized lever table.
